prs.title: feat(bulk): DataTable bulk actions — delete, duplicate, export, update, archive, assign
prs.body:
## Summary

Extends the DataTable system with bulk actions across 8 resources. Builds on the PR #192 bulk-import foundation: every bulk endpoint routes per-ID through the singular service methods via a shared `BulkService` primitive, so events / ACL / cascade behave exactly like single-resource operations.

Selected rows can now be **deleted**, **duplicated**, **exported**, **updated** (status / owner / custom field), **archived / activated** (isActive toggle), **assigned** (leads → owner), or have their **IDs copied** — with cross-page selection + "Selecionar todos os N filtrados" badge (Linear/HubSpot style).

### Non-negotiables
- **Tenant isolation**: every bulk endpoint pre-filters IDs through the same `getVisibleUserIds()` scope used by singular endpoints. IDs outside the caller's hierarchy land in `skipped[]` with `code: 'forbidden'`. Never distinguishes "not yours" from "not found" so we don't leak existence cross-tenant.
- **Critical bug fix**: `DataTableToolbar.tsx:137` was calling `action.onClick([])` instead of passing `selectedIds`. Every bulk action prior to this PR was a NO-OP.

## What ships

**Shared backend primitive** (`common/bulk/`)
- `BulkService.{deleteMany, duplicateMany, updateMany}` + `runPerId` primitive
- `BulkSelectorDto` / `BulkUpdateDto` (accepts `ids` OR `allFiltered + filters + search`)
- `BulkOperationResult<T>` with merged `skipped` from ACL + per-ID failures
- Hard cap of 500 IDs/request; larger → 400 (async path tracked as tech debt)
- p-limit(5) concurrency, same pattern as `importRows`

**Backend endpoints per module** (8 resources)
- Leads: bulk-delete / bulk-update (routes `{ assignedToId }` patches through `assign()`) / export accepts `?ids=`
- Workflows: bulk-delete / bulk-duplicate / bulk-update
- Agents: bulk-delete / bulk-duplicate / bulk-update
- Users: bulk-delete / bulk-update (drops caller's own ID before ACL to prevent self-delete)
- WhatsApp Devices: bulk-delete (forwards JWT for BB dispatcher cleanup) / bulk-update
- Custom Actions: bulk-delete / bulk-update
- Lead Types: bulk-delete / bulk-update (dependency errors when type in use)
- Capture Links: bulk-delete / bulk-update

**Shared frontend components** (`components/data-table/bulk/`)
- `BulkActionConfirmDialog` — type-DELETE gate for destructive ops + preview of 5 affected rows
- `BulkUpdateFieldModal` — curated single-field editor (prevents bulk-update foot-gun of silently overwriting heterogeneous rows)
- `BulkActionResultToast` + `BulkResultErrorsModal` — surfaces succeeded / skipped / failed + error table with typed codes
- `useBulkActions(config)` — declarative hook returning ready-to-use `BulkAction[]` for `<DataTable>`

**Cross-page selection** (`useDataTable`)
- `selectedIds` now persists across pagination changes (was replaced)
- `selectAllFiltered` virtual mode + `selectedTotalCount`
- Auto-drops the virtual mode when filters/search change so stale scopes can't silently delete the wrong rows
- "Selecionar todos os N filtrados" CTA appears in the toolbar when selection covers the current page and more filtered rows exist

**8 pages wired**: Leads, Workflows, Agents, Users, WhatsAppDevices, LeadTypes, CustomActions, CaptureLinks.

## Verified before this PR

- [x] **Backend unit tests: 376 pass in 14 suites** (`cd apps/painel-cliente-api && npx jest src/common/bulk src/modules/leads src/modules/workflows/workflows.service.spec.ts src/modules/agents src/modules/users src/modules/custom-actions src/modules/whatsapp-devices src/modules/capture-links src/modules/lead-types`)
- [x] **13 new BulkService tests** — success, partial failure, ACL-skipped merging, NestJS exception classification, 500-ID cap
- [x] **7 new ACL isolation tests on LeadsService** — master-sees-own, sub-user-cannot-reach-stranger, assign-routing-fires-richer-ACL, empty-patch-rejected, cap-enforced
- [x] **TypeScript clean** on both frontend (`apps/painel-cliente && npx tsc --noEmit`) and new backend code (pre-existing cross-workspace errors are unrelated)
- [x] **Manual API smoke against live Postgres + Redis** (dev API on port 8114):
  - 3 real + 1 fake bulk-delete → `{total:4, succeeded:3, skipped:1, failed:0}` with `code:'forbidden'` on the fake
  - Deleted IDs return 404 after the call
  - Bulk-update `{status: 'CONTACTED'}` persists in DB
  - Empty patch → 400; 501-ID request → 400
  - Workflows bulk-duplicate produces `name (cópia)` copies

## What reviewers should exercise (NOT yet verified by me)

- [ ] **UI smoke on the Leads page** — select 3 rows → Excluir → type EXCLUIR → confirm → toast + table refresh
- [ ] **UI smoke for bulk-update** — select 2 leads → Atualizar → pick Status → verify badge updates inline
- [ ] **UI smoke for cross-page selection** — select rows on page 1, navigate to page 2, verify the selection persists; exercise the "Selecionar todos os N filtrados" CTA when more pages exist
- [ ] **E2E Playwright suite** — `npx playwright test tests/painel-cliente/bulk-actions.spec.ts --project=painel-cliente-ci` (requires full dev stack up — I wrote the spec but didn't run it)
- [ ] **Real sub-user attempt** — log in as a sub-user under a different master, try bulk-delete of another master's IDs via devtools → confirm all land in `skipped` with `forbidden` (unit-test-covered but worth a live check)

## Tech debt registered

`docs/tech-debt/bulk-actions-async.md` — the 500-ID sync cap is fine for typical UX but hard-stops a handful of scenarios (large filtered deletes, high-fanout per-row ops). Plan is a BullMQ queue + SSE progress for selections ≥ 500 or `allFiltered === true`. Out of scope for this PR.

prs.title: feat(ai): expose provider/model in chat + OpenAI prompt caching
prs.body:
## Summary

- Expose active LLM **provider/model** in AI Assistant response + SSE events; render a color-coded badge next to the "Beta" chip so users can see when their own OpenAI token is actually being used.
- Add OpenAI **prompt caching** via `prompt_cache_key` (stable sha256 of system prompt + sorted tool names) and extract `cached_tokens` from the usage payload, bringing OpenAI to Claude's level for repeated prefixes.
- Pull in two small pre-existing fixes caught while typechecking: model-alias 404 when `OpenAIProvider` is constructed without an explicit model, and `percent is possibly undefined` in `WhatsAppStats.tsx`.

## Why

In prod a user set a per-tenant OpenAI key and assumed the switch hadn't taken effect because replies kept claiming to be Claude. Logs showed OpenAI was in fact being called — the model was hallucinating its identity from prior turns and the UI had no signal. Same session shows Claude paying ~1.7k tokens (cache hit) vs OpenAI paying ~6.6k (no caching). Prompt caching closes the cost gap; the badge removes the ambiguity.

## Changes

**Backend (`apps/painel-cliente-api`)**
- `dto/chat-response.dto.ts`: `provider?`, `model?`
- `dto/stream-event.dto.ts`: `CompleteEvent.aiMetadata?`
- `ai-assistant.service.ts`: returns `provider: provider.name, model`
- `ai-assistant-stream.service.ts`: populates `request.aiMetadata` at each `getProvider` call and includes it in `response` + `complete` SSE events (7 emit sites)
- `ai-core/providers/base/openai-compatible.provider.ts`:
  - `supportsPromptCaching()` hook (default `false`)
  - `buildPromptCacheKey()` → `pc_<sha256 first 24>`
  - `extractCachedTokens()` from `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`
  - Cache-hit log parity with `ClaudeProvider`
  - Fixed `resolveModel()` to also translate aliases that come from `config.defaultModel`
- `ai-core/providers/openai/openai.provider.ts`: `supportsPromptCaching() → true`
- `ai-core/providers/llm-provider.interface.ts`: `usage.cachedTokens?`

**SDK (`apps/panel-sdk`)**
- `schemas/ai-assistant.schema.ts`: `ChatResponseSchema` gains `provider`, `model`; `TokenUsageSchema` gains `cachedTokens`; `StreamEventSchema` gains `aiMetadata`

**Frontend (`apps/painel-cliente`)**
- `types/index.ts`: `AIChatResponse` mirrors the backend
- `stores/ai-assistant/{types,sessionsSlice,streamingSlice}.ts`: `activeProvider` / `activeModel` state, updated from REST response and SSE `complete` event
- `components/ai-assistant/AIAssistant.tsx`: `Badge` next to "Beta" using existing `getModelDisplayName` / `getProviderColor` helpers, Tooltip with full `provider · model` id

## Summary

- Transforma o agente monolítico VTEX do PR #202 numa **experiência de compra orquestrada** via workflow multi-agente com **6 agentes especializados** (~94% economia de token vs 1 agente com 23 tools)
- **Cart abandonment demo-friendly 5min** (só dispara em add_to_cart/view_cart, nunca após checkout)
- Infraestrutura genérica adicionada: `{{CREDENTIAL:slug}}` substitution no install + `dto.credentialIds` + `E_COMMERCE` enum + Dockerfile copia `sales-agent-knowledge/`

## Arquitetura

```
trigger: messages.upsert (fromMe:false, sem filtro de status)
  ↓
[0] triage (Haiku, temp 0.1) → JSON intent classifier
  ↓
[1] AI_EXTRACT_DATA_AI → { intent, productQuery, skuId, orderId, confidence }
  ↓
[2] intentRouter (CONDITIONAL, 5 branches: account/search/cart/order/concierge)
  ↓
[3a-e] RUN_AGENT em paralelo (só um bate por execução)
  ↓
[4] SEND_MESSAGE (dependencyBehavior:any, $coalesce sobre 5 outputs)
  ↓
[5] cartAbandonmentGate (se intent in [add_to_cart, view_cart])
  ↓
[6] WAIT_FOR_REPLY 5min

[7] abandonmentNudge (só dispara no :timeout edge)
```

| Slug | Modelo | temp | Tools | RAG |

prs.title: feat(ux): Wave 1/A2 — variable chips + live preview + typed picker
prs.body:
## Summary

Wave 1 / Agent A2 of the Actions+Modais UX refactor (plan:
`.claude/plans/algumas-actions-e-modais-cozy-garden.md`, sections *Fase 0.2*
and *Estratégia de execução paralela*).

All changes are **additive** — no existing consumer of `VariableAutocompleteInput`
or `VariablePicker` is touched. The new primitives live under
`apps/painel-cliente/src/components/variables/`.

### v2 vision behind these primitives

Today the workflow forms show `{{lead.name}}` raw tokens to non-technical
operators. v2 replaces that with:

- A friendly **chip** (`👤 Nome do Lead`) color-coded by category (Trigger /
  Lead / Action / Global).
- A **live preview** (`🔍 Prévia: Olá João`) directly below inputs so users
  see exactly what will be sent at runtime.
- A **type-filtered picker** so a phone field only offers phone variables,
  etc. — reduces accidental mismatches for non-technical users.
- A **chip-editable composite input** (`ChipEditableText`) where `{{...}}`
  tokens render as chips and text between them stays inline-editable,
  round-tripping cleanly to the raw template string on `onChange`.

### What's in this PR

- `VariableChip.tsx` — pill component (icon + friendly name + optional ✕).
- `useVariableResolver.ts` — memoized hook + pure helpers for template
  substitution. Handles dotted paths, `items[0]`, `map["sku-1"]`, and missing
  keys (silently collapses to empty string — never leaks `undefined`).
- `LivePreview.tsx` — renders the resolved string below an input; auto-hides
  when empty.
- `VariablePicker.tsx` — extended with optional `filterByType` prop
  (`'string' | 'number' | 'boolean' | 'phone' | 'email' | 'date'`). Default
  behavior unchanged — consumers without the prop see the exact same picker.
- `ChipEditableText.tsx` — composite input. Raw value stays `{{...}}`-based;
  UI renders chips + inline-editable text segments with a `+ Inserir dado`
  button that opens the existing picker, plus a raw-mode toggle escape hatch.

### Wave 2 consumers

These primitives will be consumed in Wave 2 by the per-modal agents
(`WebRequestForm`, `DispatchEventForm`, `DataTransformForm`, etc.). The
`filterByType` hook on the picker is specifically what makes the typed-field
work in those modals tractable.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 193/193 passing (22 files; 31 new tests cover chip
      rendering, resolver semantics, live-preview auto-hide, and

      integration and raw-mode toggle).
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds (pre-existing dynamic-import warnings only)
- [ ] Manual smoke test: run `npm run dev` (port 8100), open any workflow
      that uses `VariableAutocompleteInput` (e.g. SendMessage, WebRequest)
      and confirm the existing UX is unchanged.
- [ ] Once Wave 2 starts wiring the new primitives into a real form, revisit
      accessibility (focus order of chip ✕ buttons, keyboard nav between
      chip and adjacent text segments).

prs.title: feat(onboarding): Meta multi-tenant import + standalone device mode
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the broken \"choose any Meta App + paste appSecret\" onboarding flow that always failed with Meta error #190 (\"Invalid OAuth access token signature\") when the picked app didn't issue the stored token. Two paths now:

- **Mode A (import existing Meta account)**: DTO no longer accepts \`newAppId\` / \`newAppSecret\`. BB resolves and auto-links the \`wppBizApp\` via \`/debug_token\` on every create/update.
- **Mode B (standalone device)**: new \`StandaloneDeviceModal\` — user pastes \`accessToken\` + \`phoneNumberId\` and the API calls \`POST /devices/standalone\`, which trusts BB to infer WABA, business, and \`wppBizApp\` from the token.

When BB returns \`APP_NOT_REGISTERED\`, \`AppSecretInlinePrompt\` surfaces inline in the current modal, lets the tenant admin paste the secret, registers the app via the existing MetaApps route, and retries the original action — no navigation, no context loss.

## Companion BB change

prs.title: fix(agents): strip leaked tool-call XML + allow hyphen in agent slug
prs.body:
## Summary

Dois bugs detectados no smoke staging do PR #204 (VTEX Commerce Workflow):

1. **XML de tool call vazando na mensagem WhatsApp** — agente enviou mensagem ao cliente com `<function_calls><invoke>...<function_result>...</function_result>` literal.
2. **Slug com hyphen criado pelo install rejeitado ao editar via UI** — install gera `vtex-commerce-whatsapp-vtex-triage` mas o validator regex só aceita `[a-z0-9_]`.

## Fix 1 — XML leak (dupla trava)

### Causa raiz
Claude (Sonnet 4.x) tem prior forte de treinamento pro formato Claude Code harness (`<function_calls><invoke name="X"><parameter name="Y">...</parameter></invoke></function_calls><function_result>...</function_result>`). Quando system prompts descrevem tools usando pseudocódigo em backticks (ex: `` `execute_custom_action({ slug: "X", input: {...} })` ``), o modelo ativa esse prior e narra a chamada AS TEXT além de usar o tool_use nativo. O texto contendo XML entra em um bloco `text` legítimo, passa por `extractTextContent`, e vai pro usuário.

### Solução
- **Prompts**: reescritos 6 system prompts em `vtex-commerce-workflow.ts` — removido pseudocódigo, usada linguagem natural ("use a ferramenta X passando Y"), adicionado guardrail explícito "## Formato de resposta" proibindo XML/pseudocódigo.
- **Sanitização**: `claude.provider.ts#extractTextContent` agora strip-a com regex qualquer `<function_calls>`, `<function_result>`, `<invoke>`, `<parameter>` que escape. Cobre TODOS os agentes (VTEX + futuros).
- **Spec**: novo `claude.provider.spec.ts` (8 testes) cobrindo strip cases.

## Fix 2 — slug aceitar hyphen

- Install flow gera slug kebab-case mas `agentsService.create()` via service layer bypassa class-validator, permitindo criação. Edit via UI re-valida e falha.
- Hyphens já são padrão em workflow/agent template slugs. Amplia regex backend+frontend pra aceitar ambos.

**Arquivos**:
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/agents/dto/create-agent.dto.ts` — `/^[a-z0-9_]+$/` → `/^[a-z0-9_-]+$/`
- `apps/painel-cliente/src/components/AgentModal.tsx` — mesmo
- `apps/painel-cliente/src/components/agents/AgentWizardModal.tsx` — mesmo

## Verificação

- 8/8 novos em `claude.provider.spec.ts`
- 58/58 tests do escopo (claude.provider + vtex-commerce-workflow + workflow-templates.spec + knowledge-router)
- Frontend TSC: 0 erros
- **Sem regressões** — 11 erros TSC + 10 testes falhando são todos pré-existentes (tools-executor `.data`/`.pagination`, OAUTH2/ML enum, bullmq missing, ollama integration, IAM guard spec) e já estavam presentes no master merge do PR #204.

## Referência criada

`memory/reference_iam_jwt_format.md` — documenta que JWT pra panel-cliente-api requer `sub=IAM_UUID`, não cuid local. Self-signed JWTs criam phantom users sem acesso a device/credencial. Descoberto ao debugar smoke staging (erro obscuro de SEND_MESSAGE era conseqüência de workflow criado sob phantom).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit: `npx jest claude.provider` (8/8)
- [x] Unit: `npx jest vtex-commerce-workflow` (14/14)
- [x] Unit: `npx jest workflow-templates.spec` (29/29)
- [x] Frontend typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors)
- [ ] Staging smoke: deploy + re-seed workflow-templates + re-install via UI + edit um agent (deve salvar) + mandar "Oi" no 3414 (texto puro, sem XML)
- [ ] Prod: após OK staging

- Implementa refresh silencioso de token JWT no interceptor axios do painel
- Ao receber 401, tenta renovar via `POST /auth/refresh` e retenta a request original automaticamente
- Padrão mutex + fila: múltiplos 401 simultâneos disparam apenas 1 refresh, todas as requests ficam em fila e são retentadas juntas
- Logout forçado apenas quando o `refreshToken` também é inválido/ausente
- Guards de segurança: anti-loop em `/auth/refresh`, exclusão de endpoints WhatsApp e billing
- Adiciona `authStore.updateTokens()` para rotacionar tokens sem limpar sessão do usuário

## Testes (30 casos)

- `authStore.updateTokens` — 6 testes (tokens, user, isAuthenticated, clearAuth, setAuth)
- Interceptor happy path — refresh OK, header correto, fallback de refreshToken
- Interceptor failure — clearAuth + redirect, não chama updateTokens
- Sem refreshToken — logout imediato sem tentar refresh
- Anti-loop — 401 em `/auth/refresh` não tenta refresh de novo
- Endpoints excluídos — WhatsApp, billing, mensagem "API token" não disparam refresh
- Concorrência — 1 só refresh para N requests simultâneos, todas resolvem/rejeitam juntas

## Test plan

- [ ] Build passa: `cd apps/painel-cliente && npm run build`
- [ ] Testes passam: `npx vitest run src/stores/__tests__/authStore.test.ts src/services/__tests__/api.interceptor.test.ts`
- [ ] Smoke: login no painel → forçar token expirado no localStorage → próxima ação renova silenciosamente

prs.title: feat(ai): AI Intelligence Layer + bubble UI
prs.body:
## Summary

Ships three backend pillars for smarter AI assistant behaviour and restores the floating bubble trigger that was replaced with a thin docked strip users found hard to discover.

### Backend — AI Intelligence Layer (\`ai-core\`)

- **Knowledge Base** — \`KnowledgeContributor\` plugin interface + \`CoreKnowledgeContributor\` with 7 embedded entries (workflow patterns, agent creation, entity relationships, anti-patterns). Relevant entries are injected into the system prompt based on user message keywords + active skills, capped at ~800 tokens.
- **Verification Contracts** — post-execution verification of mutating tool calls (\`create_lead\`, \`create_workflow\`, \`add_workflow_trigger\`, \`create_agent\`, \`add_agent_tool\`, \`update_lead\`, \`create_custom_action\`, \`finalize_workflow_diagram\`). A verify tool (\`get_*\`) is dispatched automatically and the outcome is appended to the tool result so the LLM can course-correct.
- **Session Compression** — triggers when estimated message tokens cross 8 000. Compresses everything except the last 5 turns into a 2-message summary (user + assistant) via the fast model. Live-tested drop: 22 681 → 8 201 prompt tokens on a long conversation (-63%).

### Backend — four silent bugs surfaced during live validation, now fixed

1. \`contracts.ts\` \`idField\` was used for both \"read id from tool result\" and \"param name for verify tool\". Split into \`resultIdField\` + \`verifyParamField\` — without this, verification of \`create_lead\`/\`create_agent\`/\`create_workflow\`/\`update_lead\` never ran end-to-end.
2. Tool results come wrapped as \`{ success, data }\` from the Panel SDK. The service read \`toolResult.id\` instead of \`toolResult.data.id\`, so every contract fell to the \"id not returned\" branch. Now unwraps explicitly.
3. \`onVerifyTool\` was only wired on the Claude provider. Added to \`OpenAICompatibleProvider\` so OpenAI / OpenRouter / Qwen / Ollama all get verification too.
4. \`toolResultsToOpenAI\` / \`toolResultsToAnthropic\` dropped \`verificationMessage\` during serialization, so the LLM never saw the outcome. Now appended.

### Frontend — AI Assistant bubble

- \`DashboardLayout\`: when collapsed, render \`<AIPanel />\` directly (no 44px docked container).
- \`AIPanel\`: collapsed state is now a circular FAB (purple, \`MdSmartToy\`) fixed bottom-right with tooltip + hover scale. Expanded state unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit: **4 632 passing / 0 failing / 55 skipped** (48 external-API integration, 4 Ollama-dependent, 3 other legacy — all pre-existing, unrelated to this PR)
- [x] New specs: \`KnowledgeBaseService\` (10 tests), \`VerificationService\` (13), \`SessionCompressorService\` (11) = 34 new tests, 100% green
- [x] Live smoke: verification runs end-to-end — log shows \`🔍 Running verification for create_lead → get_lead\` + \`PASSED (id=...)\` after a real lead creation via \`POST /ai/chat\`
- [x] Live smoke: compression fires at threshold — \`Session compression triggered: ~8 095 tokens > threshold 8 000\` → \`Compressed 10 messages → 2 summary messages (kept 5 recent)\`
- [x] Live smoke: KB injection fires on keyword match — \`Injecting KB context: 3 entries (~337 tokens) [workflow-ai-agent, agent-creation-pattern, entity-relationships]\`
- [x] UI smoke: bubble visible bottom-right when collapsed, opens panel on click, tooltip appears on hover
- [ ] Staging smoke after ship (pending)

## Known gap — not addressed in this PR

Baseline token usage for trivial prompts (\"oi\") is still ~5.5k because the three pillars attack *growth* and *confidence*, not baseline. The \`SkillDetectorService\` is loading 5 skills for inputs that shouldn't match any — this is a **fourth pillar** that needs its own plan. Tracked separately.

prs.title: docs(ai): plan for Intent Router v2 (4th pillar)
prs.body:
## Summary

Self-contained plan for the 4th pillar of the AI Intelligence Layer: **Intent Router v2 + Skill Catalog via KB**.

The previous pillars (KB, Verification, Compression) attack token growth and confidence but do not reduce baseline. Live measurement after PR #225 showed \"oi\" still costs 6 749 input tokens — because \`SkillDetectorService\` always falls back to 2 default skills (22 + 15 tools) when keywords don't match.

This plan evolves the existing \`IntentRouterService\` (already LLM-based in the codebase but under-utilized) to:

- Allow returning \`skills: []\` + \`mode: \"chitchat\"\` → zero tools loaded for greetings/thanks/small-talk
- Read the skill catalog from the Knowledge Base instead of a hardcoded file (so adding a skill auto-registers it)
- Preserve expert quality when queries require skills (no regression for single/multi-skill paths)

Targets:
- Chitchat P50: 6 749 → ≤ 1 500 tokens (-77%)
- Single-skill P50: 6 749 → ≤ 3 500 tokens (-48%)
- Multi-skill P50: sem regressão
- Router overhead: ≤ 400 tokens por request

## Delivery

- **No code changes** in this PR — only the plan document
- Three implementation waves described with exact file paths, specs, validation steps, critérios de aceite quantitativos
- No feature flag — direct rollout with stg smoke + user approval before prod
- Self-contained: a fresh Claude session can execute without prior context

## Next step after merge

Open new worktree \`.worktrees/feat-ai-intent-router-v2\`, branch \`feat/ai-intent-router-v2\` from master. First commit: Wave 0 (bench tool + baseline CSV).

prs.body:
## Summary

Implements the 4th pillar of the AI Intelligence Layer (plan: `docs/plans/2026-04-19-ai-intent-router-v2.md`). Reduces AI Assistant baseline tokens by **-88.7%** on chitchat ("oi", "obrigado", etc.) and introduces a configurable per-mode skill cap for plan orchestration.

**Headline numbers** (local bench, OpenAI fast, 30-query corpus × 3 runs):

| Categoria | Baseline | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| chitchat | 6 750 | **762** | **-88.7%** |
| ambiguous | 5 903 | 764 | -87.1% |
| single-skill | 12 856 | 10 974 | -14.6% |
| multi-skill | 8 370 | 9 345 | +11.6% * |

*\* See "Bug latente" in the case study — baseline measured a broken router falling into keyword fallback; Wave 1 fixes that, so +11.6% reflects the router now actually selecting relevant skills.*

## Waves

- **Wave 0** (`ab980d9a`) — Reproducible bench tooling: `scripts/ai-token-bench.ts`, `corpus.json`, baseline CSV.
- **Wave 1** (`046f7260`) — Chitchat mode: router returns `mode: "chitchat"` + empty skills; assistant bypasses skill loading entirely; providers short-circuit on `tools=[]`. Critical secondary fix: pass `userCredential` to router so it uses the caller's provider (the router was silently failing on every request due to a `AI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=claude` / factory enum `anthropic` mismatch).
- **Wave 2** (`cda07580`) — Skill catalog lives in `KnowledgeBase` via `SkillCatalogContributor` (no more hardcoded `skill-catalog.ts`); new configurable `AI_ROUTER_PLAN_SKILL_CAP` env (default 6) with per-mode caps (chitchat=0, action=2, plan=configurable).
- **Wave 3** (`083290a5`) — Telemetry: `mode` + `routerCost: {inputTokens, outputTokens, latencyMs}` in `/ai/chat` response body. Before/after comparison doc in `docs/benches/`.
- **Docs + bump** (`2e03621e`) — pitch-ready case study at `docs/case-studies/2026-04-20-ai-intent-router-efficiency.md`; painel-cliente-api 1.5.0 → 1.6.0.

## Cap sweep evidence (Wave 2)

| Cap plan | chitchat | single-skill | multi-skill |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 (default) | 762 | 10 974 | 9 345 |
| 8 | 762 | 10 974 | 9 345 |
| 15 | 762 | 10 974 | 9 345 |

Router self-regulates — raising the cap doesn't inflate token usage in typical traffic. Justifies keeping default at 6 and making the flag available for edge cases (verified: mega-complex 5-resource query needs cap=15 to get complete outcome).

## Verification

- Jest: **4 649 passing, 0 failing, 55 skipped** (+17 new specs across Wave 1 router + Wave 2 contributor).
- Bench CSVs committed: baseline, post-W1, post-W2 (cap=6/8/15), post-W3.
- Smoke manual: "oi" ("chitchat"), "quantos leads" ("action"), "crie workflow + webhook" ("plan") — todos com `mode` + `routerCost` no response.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (jest + e2e)
- [ ] Smoke stg (after deploy): 1 chitchat query, 1 action, 1 plan — check `mode` + `routerCost` in response body
- [ ] Verify no provider drift (router + main use same userCredential)
- [ ] Verify `AI_ROUTER_PLAN_SKILL_CAP` bumps plan-mode skill count on demand

## Rollout

**Default is safe** — `AI_ROUTER_PLAN_SKILL_CAP` ausent → 6. No breaking change.
No feature flag; mudanças são mais restritivas (menos tools), não mais permissivas.
Rollback via `git revert` se regressão detectada em prod.

## Stop before prod

Per `feedback_stg_then_ask_before_prod`: depois de smoke stg OK, **parar e pedir confirmação explícita** antes de `ship:prod`.

- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-04-19-ai-intent-router-v2.md`
- Case study: `docs/case-studies/2026-04-20-ai-intent-router-efficiency.md`
- Comparison: `docs/benches/ai-tokens-comparison-wave-2026-04-19.md`

prs.title: fix(ai-prompt): generic guards against silent substitution + destructive ops
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #227 (merged). During post-deploy validation in staging, the quality test surfaced a pattern where OpenAI would silently substitute a user-requested resource by a "similar-enough" existing one (e.g. user asks for a lead tipo "médico", AI uses CLIENTE because MEDICO doesn't exist). Anthropic handled the same case correctly (asks first).

This is a generic pattern — not lead-specific — so the mitigation lives in BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT where it benefits every skill, every tool, every provider.

## Changes

- `base-prompt.ts` — two rule tightenings:
  1. **Novo bullet em "REGRA CRÍTICA"**: "NUNCA substitua um recurso pedido pelo usuário por outro parecido." Aplica a leads, tipos, agentes, workflows, webhooks, custom actions, capture links, devices, credenciais.
  2. **Rule #2 "Confirme ações destrutivas"** reforçada com regras concretas: listar itens afetados com contagem, pedir confirmação explícita, não inferir de ambíguo, em bulk >10 itens o número tem que aparecer no texto da pergunta.

Cost: ~80 extra tokens/request para o main completion (router não usa esse prompt).
Chitchat: 760 → ~820 input tokens.

- `scripts/ai-token-bench.ts` — agora dumpa um `.jsonl` paralelo ao `.csv` com request+response completos por call, para feedback loop offline.

## Validation — same quality suite against stg pre/post

| Provider | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | 14/14 (100%) | 14/14 (100%) | ceiling (no change) |
| OpenAI | 10/14 (71%) | **14/14 (100%)** | **+29 points** |

Q6 ("adiciona um médico" — MEDICO type doesn't exist) now gets the right behaviour in OpenAI too:
> "Como não temos um tipo de lead específico para médicos..." (lists existing, asks to create)

Before the fix OpenAI silently used CLIENTE. After the fix it pauses and asks.

## Follow-up flagged (not blocking)

Noticed OpenAI Q7 turn 1 entered a 10x loop on `list_available_agent_tools` before aborting with "operação muito complexa" (109k input tokens on that single turn). Turn 2 recovered → overall PASS. Likely a prompt interaction to investigate separately.

## Test plan

- [x] Deployed to stg (service `wpp-staging_painel-cliente-api` updated)
- [x] Smoke test Q6 manually: `"adiciona um médico..."` → asked before substituting
- [x] Re-ran full 7-test quality suite, both providers → both 14/14
- [x] Full fullRecords JSON saved for offline inspection (input + output per turn)
- [ ] Monitor for 24h in stg for any regression in normal flows (manual)

## Rollback

`git revert 7d21e90f 4a5a2883 && git push && npm run ship:staging painel-cliente-api`

prs.title: fix(ai): generic tool-call loop guard + max-iter hardening
prs.body:
## Summary

Generic per-turn loop guard for LLM tool-calling, applied uniformly to both `ClaudeProvider` and `OpenAICompatibleProvider`. Resolves the Q7 OpenAI postfix regression where the LLM looped 10× on `list_available_agent_tools({})` and burned 109 069 input tokens in a single turn.

- **Helper:** `ToolCallDedup` compares `(name, canonicalHash(args))` of the current tool call against the immediately previous call. Match ⇒ skip the executor and return a `TOOL_CALL_LOOP_DETECTED` synthetic result so the LLM can recover (try a different tool, ask for context, or finalize with text).
- **Providers:** Both `Claude` + `OpenAI-compatible` integrate the dedup per-turn (one instance per `completeWithTools`).
- **MAX_ITERATIONS:** 10 → 6 in both providers.
- **Max-iter message:** now lists tools used (via `summarizeToolCalls`, e.g. \`list_x×3, create_y\`) instead of the generic "operação ficou muito complexa".

Plan B (Map+threshold for hypothetical ping-pong A→B→A→B) is documented in the master plan as upgrade path — not built upfront (YAGNI).

## Bench evidence — Q7 (`Q7-multiturn-missing-type-then-confirm`, turn 1)

| Cenário | toolCalls | inputTokens | Diagnóstico |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI **pré-fix** | 0 | 4 322 | correto (texto pedindo clarificação) |
| OpenAI **post-fix** (sem loop-guard) | 10× same | **109 069** | regressão observada |
| Anthropic pré/post-fix | 1 | ~9 400 | intocado |
| OpenAI **com loop-guard** (esperado smoke) | ≤ 3 | < 30 000 | a validar em stg |

Diagnóstico Fase 1 (H1–H4) appendado ao master plan no commit \`8b0682c5\`. Conclusão: H3 + H4 confirmadas (provider quirk + prompt novo); H1 refutada → router hygiene SKIP.

## What changed

prs.body:
## Motivação

A tabela de Consumo (`/billing/usage`) exibia apenas a coluna **Quantidade**, sem o cap do meter (`includedUnits`). Quando o `BillingLimitGuard` bloqueia novas operações ao bater o limite do plano, os valores ficam "congelados" exatamente em `includedUnits` (ex.: Workflow=50, Action=200, WhatsApp=100 no plano Gratuito). Como a coluna não mostrava o limite, o usuário interpretava *"tá pendente 50, nada faturado"* como *"nada foi consumido"*, quando na verdade era *"estourou o cap"*.

O campo `includedUnits` **já vem no response do BB** (`/api/v1/usage/summary`) — a UI apenas descartava.

## O que mudou (apenas front)

- **Coluna "Quantidade" → "Consumo"** no formato `X / Y`
  - Planos Enterprise (`includedUnits ≥ 999999999`) mostram `X / ∞`
- **Nova coluna "Progresso"** com `<Progress>` do Chakra, cor por faixa (`green` <80%, `yellow` 80–99%, `red` ≥ cap) e % ao lado
- **Badge vermelho sólido "LIMITE ATINGIDO"** ao lado do nome do meter quando `quantity ≥ includedUnits`
- Colunas Faturado e Pendente mantidas como estavam

## Escopo — o que NÃO mudou (proposital)

- ❌ Nada em `BillingLimitGuard`
- ❌ Nada em `UsageMeterService`, `BillingClientService`, controller
- ❌ Nenhuma env var (`BILLING_ENFORCE_LIMITS` continua `true` em stg/prod)
- ❌ Nenhum schema / migration
- ❌ Nenhuma alteração de contrato de API

Bloqueios por cota continuam funcionando como esperado — essa PR só deixa visível pro usuário o *motivo* do bloqueio.

## Antes / Depois (mental)

```
ANTES                                  DEPOIS
Recurso           Qtde   Fat  Pend     Recurso                      Consumo        Progresso        Fat  Pend
Workflow Exec.    50     0    50       Workflow Exec. [LIMITE...]   50 / 50        ██████ 100%  🔴  0    50
WhatsApp Msg      100    0    100      WhatsApp Msg   [LIMITE...]   100 / 100      ██████ 100%  🔴  0    100
AI Tokens Plat.   286    0    286      AI Tokens Plat.              286 / 20.000   ▓░░░░░ 1%    🟢  0    286
```

- [ ] Navegar como user com plano Enterprise (se houver) e confirmar `X / ∞` + "Ilimitado"

prs.title: fix(billing): recalibrate plan includedUnits — kilotoken bug + worst-case margins
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Bug**: `seed-billing.ts` wrote `includedUnits` for `ai-tokens-*` as raw tokens (e.g. 50000), but the meter records `Math.ceil(rawTokens / 1000)` in agents/ai-assistant services. Free plan had effectively 50M real tokens instead of 50K — a **1000x gap** that silences the billing guard.
- **Fix**: recalibrate all plan limits to kilotokens with worst-case-balanced COGS (Sonnet R\$0,06/kilo + WhatsApp 30% marketing R\$0,12/msg). Margin target: Free ≥ −R\$5, paid plans ≥ 40%.
- **Professional**: price raised R\$497 → R\$997 to preserve WA 3000 quota and hit 47% margin at worst case.

### Before vs After

| Plan | Price | AI-Act (kilos) | AI-Plat (kilos) | WA msgs | Margin worst |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Free | R\$0 | 50000 → **20** | 20000 → **10** | 100 → **20** | −R\$4 |
| Starter | R\$149 | 300000 → **300** | 100000 → **80** | 750 → **400** | 52% |
| Growth | R\$297 | 800000 → **800** | 250000 → **200** | 1500 → **800** | 45% |
| Professional | **R\$997** (was R\$497) | 2000000 → **2000** | 500000 → **400** | 3000 (kept) | 47% |

## Wave 1 scope (this PR)

- Seed recalibrated + explicit unit comment in `PLAN_DEFINITIONS`
- Regression tests: 3 kilotoken contract tests in `usage-meter.service.spec.ts`, 1 quota breach test (Free 21 kilos → 402) in `billing-limit.guard.spec.ts`
- Full plan + rollout waves + curl/DB update strategy: `docs/plans/2026-04-21-billing-quotas-recalibration.md`

## Wave 2 (NOT in this PR — needs manual coordination)

Seed idempotency skips existing plans in BB. After deploy, stg/prod plan items need manual update via:
1. curl PATCH to BB (if endpoint exists)
2. UPDATE SQL on `subscription_plan_items` + Redis flush (fallback)
3. BB admin UI (last resort)

See §2.3 of plan doc for full commands. Shadow mode 7 days recommended if \`BILLING_ENFORCE_LIMITS=true\` in prod.

prs.title: feat(chats): persist outbound WhatsApp messages in chat history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Outbound messages now visible**: CRM chat `sendMessage`/`sendMedia` persist to `Message` table immediately after BB send with `correlationId` placeholder + `deliveryStatus='pending'` — frontend's existing `fetchMessages` call shows the pending row on send.
- **Echo reconciliation**: when BB echoes back with the real `wamid` (fromMe=true), `MessageProcessor` finds the pending placeholder (by `chatId + fromMe + pending` FIFO within 60s), swaps `messageId → wamid`, flips status to `'sent'`. Single row, no duplicates.
- **Sub-second latency**: `BbEventsController` now calls `EventProcessorService.processEventNow` inline (fire-and-forget) so messages land in the DB within seconds instead of up to 60s cron lag. Cron remains as a fallback.
- **No double-billing**: `MessageProcessor` skips meter for `fromMe=true` (OutboundMessagePersistence already metered at send time with `idempotencyHint='outbound-<correlationId>'`).

## Why

Before this change, `ChatsService.sendMessage/sendMedia` only called BB WPP Business and returned the `correlationId` — nothing was written to `Message`. Users sent messages in the CRM chat UI but the message never appeared until the next refresh, and only if the 1-minute `EventProcessor` cron had picked up the BB echo (`messages.upsert` with `fromMe=true`). This broke the "conversas salvam mensagens outgoing" UX.

## Schema

New column `Message.correlationId String? @unique` + index on `deliveryStatus`. Migration `20260421233617_message_outbound_correlation`.

## Deferred to follow-up PRs

- **Workflow `SEND_MESSAGE`/`SEND_MEDIA` direct-save** — avoided the chat-resolution race with `MessageProcessor`. Sync echo processing (this PR) already eliminates the lag for workflow-sent messages via the echo path.
- **Frontend status indicator** (pending/sent/delivered/read checkmarks) — `chatsStore.sendMessage` already does `fetchMessages` after send, so placeholder shows immediately; transition to `'sent'` is UX polish.
- **Playwright e2e** — needs live BB + WhatsApp device. Unit coverage (4752 passed) exercises persistence + reconciliation.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: 4752 passed, 0 failed (includes 12 new tests in `outbound-message-persistence.service.spec.ts` + `message-processor.spec.ts`; +4 tests in `chats.service.spec.ts`; updated `bb-events.controller.spec.ts` with `EventProcessorService` mock).

prs.title: fix(workflows): scope $lead lookup by tenant to prevent cross-tenant leak
prs.body:
## Summary
- **Bug crítico de segurança**: `ContextEnrichmentService.loadLeadByPhone/loadLeadById/enrichWithLead` consultava leads sem filtro de `ownerId`, retornando o lead mais recente de QUALQUER tenant. Workflow do tenant operacao-investimentos resolvia `{{$lead.name}}` pra um lead da Catalisa quando ambos tinham leads com o mesmo phone.
- **Fix mínimo + cirúrgico**: assinaturas exigem `ownerId` (TS-enforced), filtro `ownerId IN (tenantUserIds)` via `TenantHierarchyService.getTenantUserIds()` que já existe e é a mesma semântica do hardening cross-tenant de 2026-04-13. PANEL_ADMIN preserva cross-tenant intencional.
- **Cobre TODOS os trigger paths**: manual canvas, BB inbound webhook, scheduled, sub-workflow — todos convergem em `execute()`.

## Evidência (produção)

```
[22:27, 21/04/2026] K.: oi
[22:31, 21/04/2026] operacao-investimentos 0481: Olá Prospect VTEX Day, eu sou o Tom da operacao-investimentos!
                                A C6 Seg solicitou o contato com você...
```

Branding "Tom da operacao-investimentos" (correto, tenant operacao-investimentos) + nome "Prospect VTEX Day" (lead da Catalisa, **tenant errado**).

## Root cause

`apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/workflows/services/context-enrichment.service.ts:95-104` (pré-fix):
```ts
const lead = await this.prisma.lead.findFirst({
  where: { phone: normalizedPhone },   // ← sem ownerId
  orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },
});
```

Hardening cross-tenant de 2026-04-13 cobriu `LeadsService.findAll/findOne/update` (REST). Caminho de enrichment do workflow é "lazy/interno" e ficou sem revisão.

## Files changed

- `context-enrichment.service.ts` — assinaturas + queries + helper `buildTenantOwnerWhere`
- `execution.service.ts:172` — propaga `workflow.userId` em `enrichWithLead`
- `context-enrichment.service.spec.ts` — 13 novos casos
- `package.json` — bump 1.15.0 → 1.15.1

`workflows.module.ts` NÃO precisou mudar (`UsersModule` já importado, `TenantHierarchyService` já exportado).

## Test plan

### Unit (já verde local)
- [x] 27/27 testes passam (`npm run test -- context-enrichment.service.spec`)
- [x] 13 casos novos cobrem: tenant isolation A/B, hierarquia master+sub-users, PANEL_ADMIN passthrough, defense-in-depth, plumbing

### Smoke real em staging (próximo passo)
- [ ] Deploy via `npm run ship:staging painel-cliente-api`
- [ ] Reproduzir cenário: 2 tenants em stg com lead de mesmo phone, executar workflow tenant A do canvas → deve interpolar lead A (não B)
- [ ] Workflow disparado por BB webhook real (mensagem inbound) — confirmar lead correto
- [ ] Workflow sem lead no tenant correto → `$lead === null`, mensagem interpola vazio (não vaza outro tenant)

### Adjacent audit (clean)
- [x] `opt-out-detection.service.ts:28` — JÁ filtra por `ownerId`
- [x] `follow-up-scheduler.service.ts:84` — `lead.id` vem de query escopada upstream

## Plan B (follow-up separado, não bloqueia esta PR)

Tolerância a formato de phone (`+55...` vs `55...` vs format) — `loadLeadByPhone` ainda faz match exato. Padrão correto está em `lead-lookup.util.ts:65-74`. Trigger pra ativar: se algum workflow legítimo passar a falhar com `$lead === null` quando o lead existe no tenant correto mas com prefixo diferente.

## Risk register

- **Falsos negativos**: workflow legítimo deixa de achar lead → sintoma visível (`{{$lead.name}}` vira vazio), Plan B cobre
- **Performance**: índices `Lead(ownerId)` + `Lead(phone)` já existem; bitmap intersection do Postgres é eficiente
- **Edge case "user deletado"**: ELIMINADO — `Workflow.userId` é NOT NULL com `onDelete: Cascade` (verificado no schema)

prs.title: fix(admin-clients): include Masters only (parentId=null), drop STAFF_ROLES gate
prs.body:
## Summary
- Replace \`role: { notIn: [PANEL_ADMIN] }\` with \`parentId: null\` on \`listClients()\` — the real invariant is "Master owns org + billing", which only Masters satisfy.
- \`assertIsClient()\` now rejects sub-users (parentId != null) with \`BadRequestException\` instead of rejecting staff roles. Admins are free to operate on themselves.
- Specs updated: \`admin-clients.service.spec.ts\` + \`admin-billing-override.service.spec.ts\` (50+ green).

## Why
Two bugs in one filter:
1. **Admin invisible to themselves** — PANEL_ADMINs own organizations and billing accounts like everyone else, so there's no reason to hide them from the admin client management UI. Today the admin has to force plan changes via direct BB API calls.
2. **Sub-users leaking into the list** — \`parentId != null\` users inherit billing from their Master, have no \`bbBillingAccountId\`, and any admin action on them 500s in the billing flow. They were polluting the UI with rows the admin couldn't meaningfully act on.

The new filter captures the structural invariant (hierarchy) instead of the fragile proxy (role).

## Test plan
- [ ] \`cd apps/painel-cliente-api && npx jest src/modules/admin-clients\` → 50/50 green locally
- [ ] Ship to stg, open \`/admin/clients\` as admin: your own row appears, no PANEL_MEMBER rows
- [ ] Change plan on yourself via the UI → payment link returns (uses the payments fix from PR #246)
- [ ] Override scenarios on yourself work (billing-override endpoints accept your userId)
- [ ] Try to operate an override on a sub-user → 400 with clear "Target user is a sub-user" message

## Out of scope
Pre-existing TS errors in \`ai-core\`, \`ai-assistant\`, \`agents/ollama-provider.spec.ts\`, \`workflows/variable.validator.spec.ts\`, and \`ai-core/compression/session-compressor.service.spec.ts\` are unrelated — they do not touch admin-clients.

prs.title: fix(ai-assistant): eliminate "vou começar / um momento" narration — 47%→100% exec rate
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the \"theoretical assistant\" regression where the AI Assistant would reply with text like \"Vou começar agora, um momento\" without emitting any `tool_use`, leaving users waiting forever. Confirmed by user as affecting multiple users in production logs.

Four layered defenses, each attacking a different failure mode:

1. **Plan-mode prompt + base prompt** (`ai-assistant.service.ts:198-204`, `prompts/base-prompt.ts`) — PROIBIDO list of 13 transition phrases (\"vou começar\", \"um momento\", \"aguarde\", …). Rule: \"PRIMEIRO bloco DEVE ser um `tool_use`\" forbids text-only responses when executing.

2. **Confirmation detector** extracted to `confirmation-detector.ts` with 5 regex families (affirmative/imperative/agreement/english/emoji) + Signal B (implicit confirmation when previous assistant msg ends with \"?\" and user reply is short non-negation). Catches \"beleza\", \"isso\", \"👍\", \"bora\" etc. that the old prefix-match missed.

3. **Narration guard** in `claude.provider.ts:241-284` — when iter 1 returns text matching narration regex while tools are available, inject a `[SISTEMA]` rebuke and re-iterate once. Telemetry logs every trigger.

4. **Mid-task chitchat hydration** (`ai-assistant.service.ts:154-186`) — when router flags confirmation as chitchat but `sessionSkillsCache` has skills, promote to action mode and re-hydrate tools. Fixes the silent empty-response bug when user says \"pode\" after a plan presentation.

## Baseline A/B against local `admin@catalisa.app` (Haiku default)

| Metric | master (prefix) | all 4 fixes (postfix) | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `bugRate` (narration phrases) | 0.0% | 0.0% | — |
| `executionSuccessRate` | 46.7% | **100.0%** | **+53.3pp** |
| `noExecRate` | 53.3% | **0.0%** | **−53.3pp** |

Evidence: `docs/benches/ai-execution-baseline-{prefix,postfix}-LOCAL-2026-04-23.json` (15-case corpus, same session ids, same user, same model).

Fix #4 was the decisive change — Fixes 1-3 alone didn't improve exec rate because the router kept stripping tools on confirmations. The hydration fix reopens the tools cache for confirmations, at which point Fixes 1-3 ensure the model calls them instead of narrating.

## Files changed

- `apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/ai-assistant/ai-assistant.service.ts` — plan-mode prompt + confirmation branch + Fix #4 hydration
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/ai-assistant/prompts/base-prompt.ts` — global no-narration rule
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/ai-assistant/confirmation-detector.ts` — new, extracted pure function
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/ai-core/providers/claude/claude.provider.ts` — narration guard retry
- 3 new spec files (50 new tests, all green)
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/scripts/ai-execution-bench.ts` + `docs/benches/corpus-execution.json` — A/B harness for future regression detection
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/package.json` — 1.15.2 → 1.15.3

## Tests

- ✅ 50/50 new unit tests (confirmation-detector, narration-guard, plan-mode-prompt specs)
- ✅ 4797/4797 existing tests — zero regression
- ✅ A/B bench LOCAL: 47% → 100% execution rate
- ❌ `tsc` build fails on `variable.validator.spec.ts` (pre-existing on master since commit `24c0e8f2`, unrelated to this fix — `actionNames: new Set<string>()` vs `string[]`). Dev server + tests are unaffected (ts-node-dev + ts-jest).

## Summary

Every WhatsApp message write (inbound webhook, manual UI send, workflow action, agent tool, AI Assistant tool) now flows through a single entry point `MessagesService.recordMessage(...)`. Each `Message` row carries polymorphic source attribution (`sourceType`, `sourceRefId`, `sourceLabel`, `sourceMetadata`) and outbound device attribution (`deviceId`); `Chat.lastDeviceId` tracks the last device for UI default.

- **Fixes:** outbound messages (manual UI / workflow / agent / AI) were **never persisted** before because BB WPP Business doesn't echo our own sends — the panel had blind spots in 4 of 5 production paths.
- **Fixes multi-tenant bug:** `Chat.@unique(remoteJid)` globally allowed two owners to share a Chat row. Swapped for `@@unique([ownerId, remoteJid])` gated by a pre-check script.
- **Adds UI device switcher:** operators pick which WhatsApp number to reply from per chat; default is the last device used/received.

prs.title: feat(agents): wall-clock budget + retry + circuit breaker for RUN_AGENT
prs.body:
## Context

Agents executados em workflows (ação `RUN_AGENT`) estavam estourando tempo em produção sem corte determinístico. O único teto em jogo era o timeout do SDK Anthropic (30s), aplicado por request HTTP — não pelo loop inteiro. Uma execução com 15 iterações de tool call podia pendurar o worker por 3-5 minutos sem nada cortar.

Esse PR adiciona **4 camadas de proteção** herdadas automaticamente por qualquer agente (sem opt-in):

1. **Wall-clock budget** com cascata `action > agent > env (60s default)` + AbortController até o SDK
2. **Per-tool timeout** (30s default) — tool travada retorna `TOOL_TIMEOUT` sintético, LLM continua
3. **Error classifier + retry seletivo** — só timeout/network/5xx, nunca 4xx, uma vez com 50% do budget
4. **Circuit breaker** por `(agentId, workflowId)` em Redis — 5 falhas em 10min → open por 5min

## Summary

- Per-agent budget: `Agent.executionBudgetMs` (nullable, 10000–600000ms, range validado no DTO)
- Per-action override: `config.timeoutMs` + `config.retryOnTimeout` na RUN_AGENT action
- 38 unit tests novos, **4858 total passing (0 failures)**
- Smoke manual end-to-end: CREATE/UPDATE/validation/clear/DELETE todos verificados via curl
- Migration aditiva (ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) — safe em shared DB
- Frontend: form do agente + node do canvas + badges de status (timeout/breaker_open) + histórico

## Technical highlights

- **Cooperative cancel até o SDK**: AbortSignal propagado pelo `LLMCompletionOptions.signal` → `this.client.messages.create(req, { signal })`. Interrompe socket em trânsito, não só boundaries.
- **`executeWithRetry` aborta durante backoff**: antes segurava 60s mesmo com signal abortado; agora cancela o sleep via `signal.addEventListener('abort')`.
- **Distinção `null` vs `undefined` em PATCH**: `executionBudgetMs: null` limpa override, `undefined` não toca.
- **Breaker fail-open**: se Redis cair, retorna `{open: false}` — perder proteção temporária é melhor que bloquear todos os agentes.
- **Bug achado pelo próprio teste**: `recordSuccess` não limpava counters parciais quando estado ainda era `closed` — 4 falhas ao longo de 10h + 1 sucesso + 1 falha abriria breaker errado. Fix + teste.

## Files (22 changed, +1232 / -44)

**Backend (9 files, 3 new):**
- `prisma/schema.prisma` + migration SQL (aditiva)
- `run-agent.handler.ts` — budget cascade, AbortController, retry seletivo, breaker gate
- `agent-executor.service.ts` — aceita `signal`/`traceId`, persist `status='timeout'` com `timedOutStage`
- `claude.provider.ts` — SDK honra signal, per-tool `Promise.race`, abort durante backoff
- `llm-provider.interface.ts` — `signal` + `traceId` em `LLMCompletionOptions`
- `agents.module.ts` — registra `AgentCircuitBreakerService`
- `agents.service.ts` + `create-agent.dto.ts` — persistir/validar `executionBudgetMs`
- **NEW** `agent-circuit-breaker.service.ts` + spec
- **NEW** `error-classifier.ts` + spec
- **NEW** `run-agent.handler.spec.ts`

**Frontend (6 files):**
- `AgentWizardModal.tsx` — slider "Tempo máximo por execução"
- `RunAgentForm.tsx` — timeout + retry-on-timeout inputs no node do canvas
- `NodeExecutionBadge.tsx` — badges para `timeout` (laranja) / `breaker_open` (vermelho)
- `execution-utils.tsx` — novos status configs
- `AgentHistoryTab.tsx` — UI distinta por status (mostra `timedOutStage`)
- `types/index.ts` — tipos estendidos

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy staging: `npm run ship:staging painel-cliente-api painel-cliente`
- [ ] Aplicar migration em stg: `docker exec \$(docker ps -q -f name=wpp_painel-cliente-api) npx prisma migrate deploy`
- [ ] Smoke na UI de stg: criar agente com budget de 30s, rodar workflow que chama RUN_AGENT, ver `AgentExecution.status`
- [ ] Verificar 24h de métricas: distribuição de status em `AgentExecution`, P95 de `durationMs` por agente
- [ ] Se P95 > 45s em algum agente, ajustar `agent.executionBudgetMs` individualmente antes de prod
- [ ] **Parar aqui** — confirmar com @klederson antes de prod (feedback [Stg-then-ask])

## Breaking changes

Nenhum. Todas mudanças são aditivas:
- Campos novos em schema são `nullable`
- Default 60s só aplica quando `executionBudgetMs` é null
- Status novos em `AgentExecution.status` coexistem com os antigos (frontend e backend lidam com os dois)

## Rollback

1. `docker service update --rollback wpp_painel-cliente-api wpp_painel-cliente`
2. Migration não precisa ser revertida (colunas nullable, não quebram v1.15.9)

prs.title: fix(agents): make MAX_ITERATIONS dynamic + uniform default 15
prs.body:
## Context

Em prod, o agent **Atendimento Catalisa** (provider=openai) bateu no cap de 6 iterações ao tentar processar *"atualize meu nome pra João Bueno"* — chamou `update_lead, get_lead×4, create_lead` (6 tools, args diferentes em cada `get_lead` então `ToolCallDedup` não cortou) e disparou o fallback "Tentei várias abordagens...".

**Causa raiz** (confirmada com 100% de certeza via logs prod + audit cruzado):

1. Cada provider tinha seu próprio `MAX_ITERATIONS` hardcoded local: Claude=15, OpenAI/Qwen/Gemini/OpenRouter=6, Ollama=10.
2. `agent.maxIterations` (default 10 no DB) era **dead code** — nunca propagado pra `provider.completeWithTools()`.
3. Mesmo agent com mesmas tools rodava diferente dependendo de qual provider estivesse plugado.

prs.title: fix(workflows): async dispatch via BullMQ + AI_HUB_AGENT non-text skip + subscriber resilience
prs.body:
## Summary

Three coordinated fixes for the production timeout reports on agent flows and bulk-import-driven workflows.

### Frente A — BullMQ workflow-execution queue (impacto principal)

`EventListenerService` used to `await WorkflowExecutionService.execute()` inline inside the Redis Pub/Sub `pmessage` callback. With one api replica that drained one workflow at a time per tenant — bulk imports of N leads fanned out into N `LEAD_CREATED` events processed serially. Last leads appeared to time out because their workflow only started minutes after the import.

New \`WorkflowExecutionQueueService\` registers a BullMQ \`Queue\` + \`Worker\` in the same NestJS process. Producer adds a lightweight \`{ workflowId, payload, triggerId }\` job; worker re-fetches the workflow from Prisma and delegates to \`WorkflowExecutionService.execute()\`. Subscriber returns immediately — backpressure on Pub/Sub gone.

Behind \`WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_VIA_QUEUE\` flag (default OFF) for safe rollout. Concurrency tunable via \`WORKFLOW_WORKER_CONCURRENCY\` (default 5). Defense in depth: if \`queue.add()\` throws, listener falls back to inline execution so events are never lost.

### Frente B — AI_HUB_AGENT skip on empty message

Audio/image/sticker inbound messages interpolate \`$helpers.getMessageText(...)\` to empty string, making the handler return \`success:false\` with \`'AI_HUB_AGENT requires message in config'\`. The CORRETOR tenant logs were full of these. Handler now returns \`success:true, data:{skipped:true, reason:'non-text-message'}\`. Downstream actions can branch on \`output.skipped\`.

### Frente C — Subscriber Redis resilience

\`EventListenerService\` raw \`new Redis()\` didn't match \`createResilientRedis\` factory used elsewhere. Added \`createResilientRedisSubscriber\` (psubscribe-friendly: \`enableOfflineQueue:true\`, \`maxRetriesPerRequest:null\`) and migrated listener to it.

## Tests

- 4 new spec files, 20 unit tests covering producer enqueue, consumer execute, missing-workflow no-op, AI_HUB_AGENT skip path (empty/null/undefined), inline fallback when queue throws, legacy synchronous path
- Full painel-cliente-api jest run on touched modules: 2911 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed across 107 suites

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests passing (workflows + ai-assistant + agents + leads + billing/guards): ✅ 2911/2911
- [ ] Local boot validates DI graph (no module load errors)
- [ ] Stg deploy with \`WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_VIA_QUEUE=true\`
- [ ] Smoke: bulk import 50 leads → all workflows execute via queue
- [ ] Smoke: send audio to CORRETOR device → workflow does not fail (skip log visible)
- [ ] Smoke: \`docker service logs wpp_painel-cliente-api\` shows \`📥 Enqueued workflow\` and EventListener latency drops to <5ms
- [ ] No new \`Reconnecting\` cascades that drop requests

prs.title: fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe)
prs.body:
## Summary

Builds on top of PR #260. With a single \`wpp_painel-cliente-api\` replica the queue path works perfectly. Once we scale to 2+ replicas, every replica spins up its own EventListener subscriber and Pub/Sub fans every message to all of them. Without a deterministic jobId each replica would enqueue an independent BullMQ job per matched trigger — the workflow runs N times for the same event.

This passes \`jobId = \"\${eventId}:\${triggerId}\"\` so BullMQ collapses concurrent enqueues into a single job (BullMQ rejects duplicate jobIds across all states).

## Tests

- 3 new specs in \`event-listener.service.spec.ts\`:
  - jobId derived from \`event.id\` + triggerId
  - hash fallback when event has no id (synthetic publishes)

The 27-line stub is now an 865-line production-grade driver covering the full `IWhatsAppDriver` surface: connect/disconnect/logout, QR + pairing code, send (text/image/video/audio/document/sticker), reaction, location, contact, group ops (create/metadata/subject/description/participants/leave), event normalization (`messages.upsert/update/delete/reaction`, `groups.*`, `contacts.*`, `chats.*`, `connection.update`), dedupe by `key.id` with LRU(5k), v7 `remoteJidAlt`/`participantAlt` handling, disconnect classification via Boom `statusCode`. `sendTemplate` returns `BadRequest` (templates are a Cloud API feature owned by `wpp-business`).
- **Encrypted credential storage.** New AES-256-GCM cipher (`src/wpp/lib/baileys-auth-cipher.ts`) keyed by `WPP_BAILEYS_MASTER_KEY` (64 hex / 32 bytes). New `BaileysAuthStateProvider` persists Baileys auth state on `WppWaAuth`, encrypts at rest, supports v7 `SignalDataTypeMap` (incl. `lid-mapping`, `device-list`, `tctoken`). Serialization via Baileys' `BufferJSON` so `Buffer` round-trips cleanly. Provider registered in TypeDI (`src/shared/container/modules/wpp.ts`).
- **Existing wpp infra reused as-is**: `SessionManager` (lifecycle + reconnect with backoff), Redis Streams consumer (14 job types), SSE handler. The driver only emits — no reconnection logic is in the driver itself.

prs.title: feat(wpp): bridge driver message events to repos and SSE
prs.body:
## Summary

Today \`BaileysDriver\` emits 11 message-domain events but only \`connection.update\` and \`creds.update\` have listeners. Result: \`wpp_messages\`, \`wpp_chats\`, \`wpp_contacts\`, \`wpp_groups\`, \`wpp_group_participants\` and \`wpp_message_reactions\` stay empty in production, and SSE clients on \`/wpp/events/:organizationId\` never see anything after pairing.

This PR wires the driver event stream into the rest of the WPP module:

1. **Persistence** — each event is written to its matching repository (fire-and-forget; failures warn-log and never crash the driver socket).
2. **SSE pub/sub** — each event is published as a JSON envelope on Redis channel \`wpp-events:{organizationId}\`, which \`SseHandler\` already subscribes to.

### Events handled (all 11)

| Event | Persistence | SSE envelope type |
|---|---|---|
| \`messages.upsert\` | \`MessageRepository.upsertByKeyId\` + \`ChatRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.message.upsert\` |
| \`messages.update\` | \`MessageRepository.update\` (status/ack) | \`wpp.message.update\` |
| \`messages.delete\` | \`MessageRepository.update({deletedAt})\` (soft-delete) | \`wpp.message.delete\` |
| \`messages.reaction\` | \`MessageReactionRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.message.reaction\` |
| \`chats.upsert\` / \`chats.update\` | \`ChatRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.chat.upsert\` / \`wpp.chat.update\` |
| \`contacts.upsert\` / \`contacts.update\` | \`ContactRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.contact.upsert\` / \`wpp.contact.update\` |
| \`groups.upsert\` | chat upsert + group create/update + participants upsert | \`wpp.group.upsert\` |
| \`groups.update\` | \`GroupRepository.update\` (skips when group unknown) | \`wpp.group.update\` |
| \`group-participants.update\` | \`GroupParticipantRepository.upsert\` (add/promote/demote) or \`markLeft\` (remove) | \`wpp.group.participants.update\` |

### Architecture

- **\`src/wpp/services/message-event-mapper.ts\`** — pure functions that translate driver event payloads into repo inputs and SSE envelopes. No I/O, no \`await\`, easy to unit-test (21 tests).
- **\`src/wpp/services/session-manager.ts\`** — new private \`wireMessageEventListeners(driver, orgId, deviceId)\` called from the existing \`wireEventListeners\`. Each handler is wrapped in \`try/catch\` so a thrown mapper or repo cannot kill the driver event loop.
- **Container** (\`src/shared/container/modules/wpp.ts\`) — \`SessionManager\` now receives the six message-domain repos. Constructor params are optional (default undefined), so existing unit tests don't have to change.

### Tests

- \`tests/unit/wpp/services/message-event-mapper.test.ts\` — 21 mapper unit tests
- \`tests/unit/wpp/services/session-manager-bridge.test.ts\` — 24 listener wiring tests, one per event type plus skip/fault-tolerance paths
- \`tests/unit/wpp/integration/baileys-pipeline.test.ts\` — extended with 1 new assertion proving the full chain (mocked socket -> real BaileysDriver -> real SessionManager -> mocked repo + Redis publish)

WPP suite total: **410 passing** (was 364, +46 new).

### Out-of-scope (not done here)

- No new repositories, no schema changes.
- No driver code touched.
- No PATCH/DELETE endpoints, no replay/DLQ for failed persists.
- The persisted-row events (\`MESSAGE_RECEIVED\`/etc.) on the existing \`EventPublisher\` Redis Streams topic are NOT republished; the SSE channel is the only fan-out, since SSE uses raw \`subscribe\`/\`message\` and the streams topic has no SSE consumer.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`bun run test:unit\` (wpp suite passes locally)
- [ ] After merge, run smoke script (\`scripts/smoke-baileys-qr.ts\`) and verify rows appear in \`wpp_messages\` / \`wpp_chats\` and an SSE client connected to \`/wpp/events/:organizationId\` receives \`wpp.message.upsert\` events
- [ ] Confirm \`wpp_groups\` and \`wpp_group_participants\` populate when the device is added to a group

prs.title: feat(wpp): media download via file-storage + roadmap fixes
prs.body:
## Summary

Lazy media download via file-storage BB + 4 architectural fixes uncovered along the way. Builds on the message-bridge that landed in PR #117.

## Highlights

### 1. Lazy media download (commits 1–10)
Operator hits `GET /wpp/api/v1/messages/media/:messageId`. On cache miss, route enqueues `wpp:download-media`. Worker consumer pulls bytes via `driver.downloadMedia` (Baileys `downloadMediaMessage` against the persisted protobuf), uploads via the new `IFileStorageFacade` (Local + Remote impls — same pattern as webhooks-engine/decision-engine facades), persists the resulting `mediaFileId`, completes the operation. Cache hit on subsequent calls = synchronous 302 redirect to a presigned download URL — no Baileys round-trip, no ban risk in scale. Validated E2E live against a paired device + operacao-investimentos bot: 770ms cold → 13ms warm, byte-for-byte MP4.

Schema: `wpp_messages` gets nullable `deviceId` and `mediaFileId` plus an index on `(organizationId, deviceId, timestamp)`. The bridge's `serializeMessage` now preserves the encrypted Baileys protobuf via `serializeProtoForStorage` (round-trips `Uint8Array`/`Date`/`bigint` through jsonb) **only** for media types — text/reactions/status stay lean.

### 2. Architectural fixes (commits 11–19, parallelized via worktree-isolated agents)

### 3. Tooling

prs.title: fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions actually re-establishes driver sessions
prs.body:
## Summary
`restoreActiveSessions` was a no-op. It only wrote a `reconnect_attempt` row to `wpp_connection_logs` and returned — no driver instantiated, no Baileys socket opened. Workers booted "running" with an empty in-memory sessions Map while DB still showed devices as `open`. Every worker restart silently dropped every previously-paired session until someone hit `POST /devices/:id/reconnect` manually.

PR #122 (`fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions queries devices across all orgs`) fixed the query side, but the actual restore step has been a no-op since the very first wpp commit (`f9fbd92`).

## Fix
Each restored row now goes through `getOrCreateSession` after the log is written. That fires `wireEventListeners`, opens the Baileys socket, and registers the driver in `this.sessions` for the running worker process. The driver's `connection.update` event then flips `wpp_devices.status` back to `open` on success, or to `closed` with an error code if auth was revoked remotely.

Per-device errors are caught and warn-logged — one stale auth (`LoggedOut`/401) does not block the rest from restoring.

## Local validation
Cold-booted the worker against a paired local device:

```
[INFO] Restoring active WPP sessions count: 1
[INFO] WPP session restored
state_change → connecting   (driver wired)
state_change → connecting
state_change → open         ← real Baileys socket
```

`wpp_devices.updatedAt` advanced. `wpp_connection_logs` shows the full state-change sequence. Time from boot to `open` was ~2.3s.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run vitest run tests/unit/wpp/services/session-manager.test.ts` — 33/33 pass (+2 new: driver actually invoked, per-device error isolation).
- [ ] Deploy to staging, watch `wpp_devices.updatedAt` of any pre-existing `status=open` row advance after worker boot. If existing staging devices fail with 401 (auth removed via WhatsApp UI), pair a fresh device and re-validate.

prs.title: feat(wpp): distribute restoreActiveSessions via Redis Streams across replicas
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Coordinator-elect** (`SET NX EX wpp:restore-coordinator`, 60s TTL) so exactly ONE replica reads the DB and fans out one `SESSION_RESTORE` job per device into the existing Redis Stream — eliminating the duplicate `reconnect_attempt` log rows + duplicate Baileys socket attempts that occur when N>1 worker replicas all run the restore loop in parallel.
- **Stream-driven distribution** via the existing `WppQueues.SESSION_RESTORE` consumer group (`wpp-consumers`) — each device job is delivered to exactly one worker, splitting reconnect load across the replica fleet instead of every replica fighting over every device.
- **Per-device idempotency** preserved via `wpp:reconnect-lock:{org}:{device}` (SET NX EX, 30s) inside the new `restoreSessionFromStream` path, so consumer-side stream redelivery (consumer crash before XACK) is safe — the lock + the in-memory `this.sessions.has` short-circuit guarantee no duplicate sockets even under worst-case race.
- New `RedisService.setIfAbsent(key, value, ttl)` helper wrapping `SET NX EX`.

## Why not the previous "lock per device only" design

With N replicas each running their own restore loop, even with the per-device lock the losers still did the DB scan and wrote the `reconnect_attempt` log row before observing the lock. The coordinator-elect cuts this to one DB scan and one set of log rows total, regardless of replica count.

## Local validation (3 real devices, 2 workers)

Validated end-to-end against the 3 devices we have paired in local Postgres (real Baileys auth) with 2 worker replicas booting simultaneously:

```
T0 = 1777468356

Reconnect attempts after T0:  3   (expected 3 — pre-fix would be 6)
Devices restored:             3 / 3
Worker A claimed:             3 devices via stream
Worker B claimed:             0 devices via stream
Coordinator-elect:            Worker A WON
Distribution check:           PASS (sum = 3)
```

Worker A logs:
```
[10:12:43] INFO: Restoring active WPP sessions  count: 3
[10:12:43] INFO: WPP session restored via stream
[10:12:43] INFO: WPP session restored via stream
[10:12:43] INFO: WPP session restored via stream
```

Worker B logs:
```
[10:12:44] INFO: Restore coordinator role already taken, skipping enqueue
[10:12:44] INFO: WPP sessions restored
```

DB final state — all 3 devices flipped back to `status='open'` after restore:
```
claude-multi-a-1777464537 | open | 13:12:44.262
claude-restore-1777463791 | open | 13:12:44.782
claude-multi-b-1777464537 | open | 13:12:44.984
```

The 3-0 split across workers is timing — Worker A registered its consumer in the group ~150ms before Worker B was ready, so it grabbed all three jobs from `XREADGROUP` before B's consumer joined. With more devices or longer per-device handshake time the round-robin would naturally split. The critical invariant (sum = 3, no duplicates) holds.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `RedisService.setIfAbsent` (NX EX semantics, both branches)
- [x] Unit tests for `restoreActiveSessions` coordinator-elect: winner enqueues N jobs to stream, loser short-circuits with `ok(0)` and never touches DB or stream
- [x] Unit tests for `restoreSessionFromStream` per-device lock: skip when lock held, skip when already wired in-process, real driver creation when lock acquired
- [x] Unit test for consumer dispatch: `handleSessionRestore` calls `restoreSessionFromStream`, NOT `getOrCreateSession` directly
- [x] Local end-to-end with 2 workers + 3 real devices (validation above)
- [ ] Staging deploy: `npm run ship:staging wpp-session-worker` — staging has no devices with live auth (revoked yesterday), so behavior is observable only in worker boot logs ("Restoring active WPP sessions count: 0" — no errors)

prs.title: fix(ai-providers): PR A — cache always-on + parallel tool exec (Claude/OpenAI/Ollama)
prs.body:
## Summary

PR A from the [Phase 0 emergency roadmap](../blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md). Targets the **8-10s latency regression** (was 2-3s) reported in prod after PRs #256-#259.

Three fixes shipped together — no behavior changes for callers, only structural improvements to the LLM provider tool-loop.

## Changes

### A1 — Claude prompt cache on EVERY iteration
- `claude.provider.ts:238` was `enableCaching && iteration === 1` — gated cache to iter 1 only
- For AI Assistant (152 tools, ~45k tokens) with 3-5 iterations, this forced 3-5× re-tokenization
- Fix: drop the iteration gate. Anthropic's 5-min ephemeral TTL covers a full multi-turn flow, so iter 2+ hits the prefix written on iter 1

### A2 — ONE cache_control on the LAST tool (prefix breakpoint)
- Was setting cache_control on the **last 3 tools** (~880 lines), leaving the first N-3 uncached
- `cache_control` is a **prefix breakpoint** in Anthropic's API — a single one on the last tool caches the entire tools block
- For AI Assistant: 152 tools cached vs 3 before

### A3 — Cross-provider parallel tool execution (helper extraction)
- New `providers/utils/tool-batch-runner.ts`:
  - **Pre-pass (sync):** record fatigue + check dedup in input order
  - **Parallel pass:** `Promise.all` with per-branch try/catch + cancellation + optional per-tool wall-clock timeout
  - **Post-pass (serial, in input order):** record dedup with actual result, run `onVerifyTool` (must stay serial — stateful), apply optional smart-truncation
- Applied to **all 3 providers** (`claude.provider.ts`, `openai-compatible.provider.ts`, `ollama.provider.ts`)
- Anthropic and OpenAI both emit multiple `tool_use` per turn explicitly because they're independent — running them serially turned 5×2s into 10s wall-time when 2s would do
- Net **-210 lines** across the 3 providers (DRY win)

## Tests

- **13 new** in `tool-batch-runner.spec.ts`: parallelism (`maxInflight=3`), order preservation, fatigue/dedup short-circuit, cancellation, per-tool timeout, `onVerifyTool` stays serial, smart-truncate flag, error isolation, callbacks
- **9 new** in `claude.provider.cache-strategy.spec.ts`:
  - cache_control on system on EVERY iteration including **iter 2 regression test**
  - exactly 1 cache_control on the last tool (not 3, not N)
  - parallel execution wiring with `maxInflight=3` + structured savings log
- **All 154 ai-core tests pass** (12 pre-existing suites + 2 new), including `cross-provider-parity.spec.ts`

## Pre-existing build issues (NOT introduced by this PR)

These also fail on `master` — flagging for visibility, NOT in scope here:

- `workflows.service.ts` implicit-any params + missing prisma fields (`workflowActionLog`, `workflow`)
- `chats.service.ts` / `messages.service.ts` missing prisma columns (`ownerId_remoteJid`, `deviceId`, `lastDeviceId`) — looks like Prisma client lag
- `run-agent.handler.ts` missing `executionBudgetMs` field on `Agent` (PR #256 schema not in client?)
- `claude.provider.ts:202` / `openai-compatible.provider.ts:213-215` `response.usage` possibly undefined (strict mode)
- `claude.provider.spec.ts:19` passes `ConfigService` where `ClaudeProviderConfig` expected
- `claude.provider.loop-guard.spec.ts` + `claude.provider.narration-guard.spec.ts` — fixtures missing required `systemPrompt` field

## Expected impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| AI Assistant turn1 P50 | 8-10s | **4-5s** |
| Atendimento Catalisa median | 6-8s | **3-4s** |
| Cache hit ratio iter 2+ | <5% | **>85%** |
| Multi-tool wall (5 tools, parallel) | ~10s | **~2s** |

## Test plan

- [ ] Stg deploy, then run `ai-execution-bench.ts` with `AI_BENCH_RUN_NAME=postfix-PR-A-STG-anthropic-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)`
- [ ] Diff vs `docs/benches/ai-execution-postfix-STG-anthropic-2026-04-23.json` baseline

- [ ] User OK gate before prod deploy

prs.title: fix(ai-providers): PR B — cross-provider narration guard + Claude tool_choice
prs.body:
## Summary

PR B from the [Phase 0 emergency roadmap](../blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md). Eliminates the **gerundio regression** (model says "vou começar / um momento / vou tentar" without emitting `tool_use`) across **Claude / openai-compatible / Ollama / Gemini** via a shared helper. Also adds explicit `tool_choice` to Claude, mirroring the pattern OpenAI-compat and Gemini already use.

## Changes

### B1-3 — Shared `narration-guard.ts` helper
Lives in `providers/utils/narration-guard.ts`. Pure-function decision: `shouldRetryForNarration({ iteration, finalText, hasTools, messages, retriesUsed }) → { retry, reason, systemMessage, routerMiss }`.

**Three failure modes of the original Claude-only guard fixed:**

1. **Was iter 1 only** — narration on iter 2+ (after the model received tool_results) slipped through. Now fires on EVERY iteration with a per-session retry cap (default 2).
2. **Required `hasTools`** — when the upstream skill router returned an empty tools array on a clearly action-demanding prompt ("cria um lead pra mim"), the guard skipped silently. Now `isActionIntentMessage(userText)` fires the guard with a different system message AND emits a `routerMiss` log.error for upstream observability.
3. **Regex narrow** — the original 5 verbs missed 11 prod variants. Widened to: `vou (começar/criar/fazer/chamar/iniciar/tentar/precisar/buscar/listar/verificar/consultar/preparar/enviar/montar/configurar/atualizar/cadastrar)`, `primeiro vou`, `preciso primeiro`, `um (momento/instante/segundinho/segundo/minutinho/minuto)`, `só um (instante/momento/...)`, `aguarde`, `já vou`, `começando`, `iniciando`, `estou começando`, `deixa (só) eu`, `agora vou X`, `agora mesmo`. Verb-anchored to avoid false positives on past tense ("comecei ontem") or unrelated phrases ("vou ali").

**Applied to:**
- `claude.provider.ts` (replacing inline guard)
- `openai-compatible.provider.ts` (Gemini inherits — `getToolChoiceOverride` was forcing required on iter 1, now also catches narration on iter 2+ from text-only fallbacks)
- `ollama.provider.ts`

Same regex + same decision logic across all providers — `cross-provider-parity.spec.ts` passes.

### B4 — Claude `tool_choice` (mirroring openai-compatible:135,252 + Gemini)

New private `getToolChoiceForIteration(options, iteration, forceAnyOnLater)`:
- Iter 1 with tools: `{ type: 'auto', disable_parallel_tool_use: false }`
- Iter ≥ 2 with tools: `{ type: 'any', disable_parallel_tool_use: false }` when `AI_FORCE_TOOL_CHOICE_ANY=true`, else `'auto'`
- Without tools: omit entirely

Gated behind env flag (default OFF) so first prod rollout preserves legacy. Plan: turn on in stg, validate via bench, ramp prod.

## Tests

- **61 new** in `narration-guard.spec.ts`: NARRATION_RE variant matrix (24 must-match + 9 must-NOT-match), `isActionIntentMessage` (11 actions + 5 non-actions + undefined), `getLastUserText` (string/array content/skip non-user/empty), `shouldRetryForNarration` (8 scenarios incl. retry caps + iter 2+ + routerMiss + chitchat passthrough)
- **6 new** in `claude.provider.tool-choice.spec.ts`: default off → auto everywhere, flag on → auto iter 1 + any iter 2/3, no tool_choice when no tools
- **1 updated** in `claude.provider.narration-guard.spec.ts`: regression test "TRIGGERS retry on iter 2 when narration appears AFTER tool_use" — was validating the bug, now validates the fix
- **All 199 ai-core tests pass** (17 suites)

## Pre-existing build issues NOT introduced by this PR

Same as PR #262 — flagged for tracking, not in scope here:
- `workflows.service.ts`, `chats.service.ts`, `messages.service.ts`, `run-agent.handler.ts` — Prisma client lag and implicit-any issues
- `claude.provider.spec.ts:19` ConfigService vs ClaudeProviderConfig
- `narration-guard.spec.ts` and `loop-guard.spec.ts` fixtures missing required `systemPrompt` (pre-existing)

## Expected impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gerundio responses / 100 sessions (estimated) | ~12 | **<1** |
| iter 2+ narration coverage | 0% | **100% (all 4 providers)** |
| skill-router miss observability | silent | **logger.error w/ routerMiss flag** |

## Test plan

- [ ] Stg deploy on integration branch, then `ai-quality-test.ts` for narration regressions
- [ ] Smoke: AI Assistant + Atendimento Catalisa with action prompts ("cria um lead", "manda mensagem"), watch logs for `Narration detected` warns
- [ ] User OK gate before prod
- [ ] Set `AI_FORCE_TOOL_CHOICE_ANY=true` in stg env, re-run bench, compare
- [ ] Ramp `AI_FORCE_TOOL_CHOICE_ANY=true` in prod 0→10→50→100% over 24h

## Rollback

Each fix is localized. `git revert` the commit; helper file deletion is one `rm`.
Feature flag `AI_FORCE_TOOL_CHOICE_ANY=false` reverts B4 in <1min without code change.

## Combined testing with PR A

Will be merged into `integration/ai-perf-and-gerundio` along with PR #262 for combined stg testing before master merge.

## Summary

PR C from the [Phase 0 emergency roadmap](../blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md). Minimal observability win: replace unparseable emoji-string cache logs with **JSON lines** so log aggregators (Loki / CloudWatch) can extract fields like `cacheHitRatio`, `provider`, `model`, `iteration`.
