commits.title: revert: rollback Parte B multi-tenancy (X-Target-Organization-Id) (#243)
commits.body:
revert: rollback Parte B multi-tenancy (X-Target-Organization-Id) (#243)

The Parte B change was based on a misread of the design. Catalisa's BB
billing model is intentionally provider-scoped: every tenant's billing
account lives under the provider's org (today always Catalisa platform
org). The shared `bbOrganizationId` was not a bug — it was the design.

My fix introduced X-Target-Organization-Id to give each tenant its own
BB org, which broke subscription creation (plans live in platform org
under the old model; with tenant-org scoping, `createSubscription`
couldn't resolve the plan).

Reverts:
- billing-client.service.ts: getAuthHeaders() back to no-arg
- auth.service.ts register(): pass CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID as bbOrgId again
- organizations.service.ts getBBIds: remove iamOrganizationId fallback

feat(admin-clients): Phase 6 — meter limit overrides + aditive BillingLimitGuard

The final phase of docs/plans/2026-04-21-admin-client-management.md.
Lets staff raise or remove per-client limits independently of the plan
(e.g. Starter has 5 devices, this one partner can use 20). The only
happy-path modification in the whole plan — mitigated by a fallback
guarantee: when the override table is empty, guard behavior is identical
to pre-Phase-6, and the regression is covered by a spec.

Backend
- New Prisma model `ClientMeterOverride` (applied via `prisma db push`):
  targetUserId + meterKey unique, limitOverride (Int; -1 = unlimited),
  reason (≥10 chars), expiresAt (nullable; non-expired check in guard),
  createdBy/createdByEmail snapshots.
- CRUD on AdminClientsController:

  - POST   /admin/clients/:userId/meter-overrides
  - PATCH  /admin/clients/:userId/meter-overrides/:overrideId
  - DELETE /admin/clients/:userId/meter-overrides/:overrideId
- BillingLimitGuard: aditive lookup in a new `resolveMeterOverride` helper
  AFTER `resolveIncludedUnits` so the existing Redis mock ordering stays
  intact. Short 15s Redis cache in front of the DB read. Defensive:
  when the DB lookup throws, we fall back to the plan limit (guard keeps
  the "when in doubt defer to the plan" discipline).

Regression gate
- `billing-limit.guard.spec.ts`: 19/19 green (16 existing + 3 new).
  Existing "should throw BillingQuotaExceededException when hard-limit
  plan is over quota" now acts as the empty-table regression guarantee —
  when no row matches, the aditive lookup is a no-op. Also tested:
  active override overrides the plan limit; limitOverride=-1 unblocks
  usage above the plan limit; DB lookup failure falls back to plan.
- Full suite across admin-clients + billing: 212/212 green.

Frontend
- `MeterOverridesPanel` — new "Limites" tab with table + create/edit/
  delete modal. Value `-1` is surfaced as a green "ilimitado" badge.
  `expiresAt` is a date picker (ISO yyyy-mm-dd). meterKey is immutable

fix(workflows): scope $lead lookup by tenant to prevent cross-tenant leak

ContextEnrichmentService.loadLeadByPhone/loadLeadById/enrichWithLead
queried leads with no ownerId filter, returning the most recent lead
across ALL tenants. A workflow on tenant A could resolve {{$lead.name}}
to a lead from tenant B if both shared the same phone.

canvas sent WhatsApp with correct branding but with the lead name from
tenant Catalisa (same phone existed in both tenants).

  positional arg (TS-enforced). Plumbed from workflow.userId in
  WorkflowExecutionService.execute().
- Lookups filter by ownerId IN (tenantUserIds) using
  TenantHierarchyService.getTenantUserIds — same semantics adopted by
  the 2026-04-13 cross-tenant hardening (PANEL_ADMIN keeps cross-tenant
  visibility via null tenant set).
- 13 new unit tests covering: tenant isolation in both directions,
  master/sub-user hierarchy, PANEL_ADMIN passthrough, defense-in-depth
  early returns for empty inputs, signature plumbing in enrichWithLead.

Affects all workflow trigger paths (manual canvas, BB inbound webhook,
scheduled, sub-workflow) — all converge on execute().

commits.title: feat(chats): persist outbound WhatsApp messages in chat history
commits.body:
feat(chats): persist outbound WhatsApp messages in chat history

Outgoing messages sent from the CRM chat UI are now persisted immediately
in the Message table with a correlationId placeholder and deliveryStatus
'pending'. When the BB echo (messages.upsert with fromMe=true) arrives,
MessageProcessor reconciles by swapping the placeholder messageId for the
real wamid and flipping status to 'sent'.

Why: before this, ChatsService.sendMessage/sendMedia only called BB and
returned the correlationId — nothing was written to the Message table.
The row only materialized when the 1-minute EventProcessor cron processed
the BB echo, so outgoing messages disappeared from the chat view. Now the
frontend's existing fetchMessages-after-send call immediately picks up the
pending placeholder, and the reconciled wamid lands seconds later via the
sync echo processing added to BbEventsController.

Key changes:
- Message.correlationId column + index on deliveryStatus (migration)
- OutboundMessagePersistenceService: shared persistence for CRM + future
  workflow paths; emits CHAT_MESSAGE_SENT webhook; meters via
  UsageMeterService with idempotencyHint='outbound-<correlationId>'
- MessageProcessor: reconcile pending placeholders by chatId+fromMe+pending
  (FIFO within 60s window); skip meter for fromMe=true to avoid
  double-billing with the direct save
- BbEventsController: fire-and-forget EventProcessorService.processEventNow
  inline so messages land in DB within seconds instead of 1-minute cron

Unit tests: 4697 passed, 0 failed (includes 12 new tests for
OutboundMessagePersistence + MessageProcessor reconciliation + 4 new
ChatsService send tests).

Deferred to follow-up PRs:
- Workflow SendMessage/SendMedia handlers direct-save (avoids chat
  resolution race with MessageProcessor; sync echo processing already
  eliminates the lag for the current echo path)
- Frontend status indicator (pending/sent/delivered/read checkmarks)
- Playwright e2e (needs live BB + WhatsApp device)

commits.body:
feat(admin-clients): Phase 5 — billing overrides (waived) + audit trail

Admin-only WAIVED billing operations with immutable audit. Three override
types shipped (plan §14 Phase 5), all gated by @Roles(PANEL_ADMIN):

Backend
- New Prisma model BillingOverrideAudit + enums OverrideType +
  OverrideCategory (applied via `prisma db push` — migration file to be
  generated when the repo's shadow-DB history is cleaned; table exists
  in local dev DB already).
- New submodule admin-clients/admin-billing-override.{controller,service,
  dto}.ts + AdminBillingOverrideController registered alongside
  AdminClientsController.

Endpoints
- POST /admin/clients/:userId/billing/overrides/plan-change
    → voids open invoices (fail-open, non-fatal) + deactivates ACTIVE
      payment links (fail-open) + cancels current sub (FATAL) + creates
      new sub (FATAL) + writes audit with partialFailures[] if any.
    Returns { auditLogId, subscription, previousSubscriptionId,
    voidedInvoiceIds, cancelledPaymentLinkIds, partialFailures }.
- POST /admin/clients/:userId/billing/overrides/new-subscription
    → 409 if client already has ACTIVE/TRIAL/PAUSED sub. Creates sub
      with skipTrial derived from trialDays payload.
- POST /admin/clients/:userId/billing/overrides/renewal
    → AUDIT-ONLY: records the grace-period intent (additionalDays,
      periodEndBefore, periodEndAfter, approver, reason). BB has no
      subscription-period-update endpoint yet — plan §8.1 acknowledged
      this fallback. Operators enforce manually until BB ships the
      endpoint; response includes an explicit `note` so the UI surfaces it.
- GET /admin/billing/overrides (global) + GET /admin/clients/:userId

  usage, activity
- Gated with `@Roles(PANEL_ADMIN)` via existing RolesGuard (the only role
  that carries PANEL_CROSS_TENANT today). Staff targets are rejected 403
  by `assertIsClient` so admin tools cannot operate on other staff.
- 18 Jest cases covering staff rejection, listing filters, fail-open BB
  lookups, empty-billing fallbacks, BB JSON:API param translation, etc.

* feat(admin-clients): Phase 2 — edit cadastro + organization billing metadata

Adds two admin-scoped PATCH endpoints and the corresponding UI forms so
staff can fix a client's name/phone and organization billing details
without going to SQL.

Deferred by design (will land as a Phase 2.5 sub-plan):
- Role change — needs a proper IAM association-update flow. Writing
  directly to the local DB violates `feedback_iam_source_of_truth` and
  gets overwritten on next login by iam-jwt.strategy's role sync.
- Email change — email is the IAM login identifier; changing it locally
  creates drift with IAM.

Backend
- `PATCH /admin/clients/:userId` with AdminUpdateClientDto (name, phone).
  Delegates to UsersService.update. E.164 phone validation.
- `PATCH /admin/clients/:userId/organization` with
  AdminUpdateClientOrganizationDto (name, billingEmail, billingName,
  document). Writes via prisma directly — bypassing
  OrganizationsService.update which scopes to the caller's own org.
  slug, bbOrganizationId, bbBillingAccountId, iamOrganizationId are
  deliberately immutable.
- 9 new Jest cases (27 total) covering staff rejection, empty-body 400,
  missing-org 404, field stripping, and the slug/BB-IDs immutability
  invariant.

- adminClientsApi: updateClient + updateOrganization

  and role shown as IAM-managed (read-only)

  and BB IDs shown as read-only with a warning banner
- ClientDetail.tsx: "Cadastro" section + "Editar" buttons on both
  sections + refetch on save so the UI reflects the new state

attempting to set slug/bbOrganizationId via the PATCH was stripped by
class-validator, so the payload became empty and the service returned

* feat(admin-clients): Phase 3 — pause / resume / cancel subscription + fix BB 4xx mapping

- 7 new Jest cases (34 total): staff rejection, no-billing-account 404,
  no-active-sub 404, BB delegation with correct IDs, PAUSED→resume,
  default cancel flag, explicit immediate-cancel flag.

- The controller's safeCall was blanket-mapping every BillingApiError to
  503. That masked BB's 4xx business rules (e.g. "Cannot resume in ACTIVE
  status") as if the service were down. Fixed to preserve BB semantics:
  404→NotFoundException, 400→BadRequestException, 409→ConflictException,
  5xx→ServiceUnavailableException, anything else→HttpException(status).

  UI can show a meaningful toast instead of a generic "billing down".

* feat(admin-clients): Phase 6 — meter limit overrides + aditive BillingLimitGuard

The final phase of docs/plans/2026-04-21-admin-client-management.md.

(e.g. Starter has 5 devices, this one partner can use 20). The only
happy-path modification in the whole plan — mitigated by a fallback
guarantee: when the override table is empty, guard behavior is identical
to pre-Phase-6, and the regression is covered by a spec.

- New Prisma model `ClientMeterOverride` (applied via `prisma db push`):
  targetUserId + meterKey unique, limitOverride (Int; -1 = unlimited),
  reason (≥10 chars), expiresAt (nullable; non-expired check in guard),
  createdBy/createdByEmail snapshots.

  AFTER `resolveIncludedUnits` so the existing Redis mock ordering stays
  intact. Short 15s Redis cache in front of the DB read. Defensive:
  when the DB lookup throws, we fall back to the plan limit (guard keeps
  the "when in doubt defer to the plan" discipline).

- `billing-limit.guard.spec.ts`: 19/19 green (16 existing + 3 new).
  Existing "should throw BillingQuotaExceededException when hard-limit
  plan is over quota" now acts as the empty-table regression guarantee —
  when no row matches, the aditive lookup is a no-op. Also tested:
  active override overrides the plan limit; limitOverride=-1 unblocks
  usage above the plan limit; DB lookup failure falls back to plan.
- Full suite across admin-clients + billing: 212/212 green.

* docs(plans): BB X-Target-Organization-Id override + admin-clients prod rollout

Two-part plan for fresh-context execution:

Part A: Deploy admin-clients (PR #239) to prod — mirrors the stg rollout
already done in the prior session. Zero code changes; pure ops.

Part B: Fix the bbOrganizationId multi-tenancy bug where all tenants
share the same BB organization (currently b0000000-...-02 because
CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID is the api-key scope).

The bug is a pre-existing design gap, NOT introduced by PR #239. Phase 1-6
surfaced it via the admin detail UI. Fix requires:
- BB: add X-Target-Organization-Id header in auth.middleware.ts, gated
  by PANEL_CROSS_TENANT permission (which already exists in BB Permission
  enum at src/iam/types/index.ts:339)
- Panel: BillingClientService.getAuthHeaders(targetOrgId?) forwards the
  header when targetOrgId differs from the platform org. Every ~20
  BillingClientService methods that already accept bbOrgId as 1st arg
  start honoring it (they ignored it before).
- Panel register(): use iamOrg.id as bbOrganizationId instead of the
  platform client id.
- Migration: backfill existing organizations to set bbOrganizationId =
  iamOrganizationId where they currently point at the platform id.

Plan includes full smoke matrices, rollback procedures, and explicit
stop-and-ask gates between phases per feedback_stg_then_ask_before_prod.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(billing): X-Target-Organization-Id + per-tenant bbOrgId

Panel side of the multi-tenancy fix (matched by BB auth middleware change
in feat/x-target-organization-id on building-blocks-v2).

Before: auth.service.register() passed CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID as bbOrgId, so
every tenant got bbOrganizationId = shared platform id. BB billing accounts
were all collapsed under the platform org.

After: register() passes iamOrg.id as the tenant's bbOrgId and BillingClient's
getAuthHeaders() appends X-Target-Organization-Id when the target differs
from the service's platform bbOrgId. BB validates PANEL_CROSS_TENANT on the
api key's user and routes the request to the target org.

Changes:
- billing-client.service.ts
  - getAuthHeaders(targetOrgId?) appends X-Target-Organization-Id when needed
  - getBaseAuthHeaders() extracted for the 401 retry path (preserves header
    from the original config.headers)
  - all ~30 methods that take bbOrgId as first arg now forward it to
    getAuthHeaders(bbOrgId)
- auth.service.ts register(): tenantBbOrgId = iamOrgId (not platform id)
- organizations.service.ts getBBIds: defensive fallback to iamOrganizationId
  when bbOrganizationId is null post-migration

Tests: 287 passed (includes new spec cases for header presence/absence +
regression test proving tenant iam org id is used, not platform id).

Simplify plan-change flow end-to-end to eliminate pro-rata math that
was the root cause of confusion and complicated the 4-call BB upstream

commits.body:
fix(bb-calendar): use IAM client_credentials service token instead of user JWT

Root cause of staging 500: user JWTs from panel client-orgs don't carry
CALENDAR_READ/WRITE perms (those are new BB IAM perms, not in the 'ALL
perms' seed for client orgs). Forwarding the user JWT to BB Calendar
triggered 403 'Insufficient permissions', which the panel-api mapped to
500 for the frontend.

Also: the X-Target-Organization-Id header we were injecting is a no-op
on BB today (Part B pending in project_bb_target_org_override_plan). So
the 'shared provider model' needed a different mechanism.

Fix: BbCalendarClientFactory.createForService() — fetches a service token
via IAM OAuth 'client_credentials' grant using CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID +
CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_SECRET (already available in all envs, already used by
BillingClientService). In-memory caching with 60s buffer before expiry +
cache invalidation on 401. All 4 consumers swapped from createWithToken
to createForService:
  - CalendarIntegrationsService (4 call-sites)
  - AdminCalendarProvidersService (1)
  - 6 workflow handlers (6)

Specs updated accordingly. 4818/4818 calendar-related tests pass.

Provider-configs had to be re-registered under the painel-service org
(b0000000-...-000002 in stg) — service token resolves to that org, not
root Catalisa. Legacy configs in root org (c0ff6afd-... + 30c89764-...)
kept temporarily; delete after full validation.

Also relaxed isDefault filter in startOAuth: BB flips isDefault cross-
provider when creating multiple — fallback to first active matching
providerType if no isDefault. Fixes the 'Google is default but user
wants Outlook' case.

Runbook for prod rollout added in docs/ops/bb-calendar-prod-rollout.md
with exact manual steps (OAuth apps verification, service token probe,
provider-config POST order, env vars to set in /root/.env).

commits.title: fix(credentials): skip OAUTH2 field validation for BB Calendar proxied creds
commits.body:
fix(credentials): skip OAUTH2 field validation for BB Calendar proxied creds

BB Calendar credentials are a proxied shape: the OAuth app (clientId,
clientSecret, redirectUri, authorizationUrl, tokenUrl) lives in
building-blocks-v2 `CalendarProviderConfig`, not in painel. Painel
only persists the `connectionId` that references BB's `CalendarConnection`.

The generic `OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE` field validator was designed for
ML/VTEX (where painel owns the OAuth app) and required those 5 fields.
That caused `completeOAuth` to fail with "Field 'clientId' is required
for OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE credentials" right after the user consented
at Google/Microsoft — breaking the calendar connect flow in staging.

Fix: `CredentialStorageService.create` and `update` now skip the schema
field check when `serviceName === CALENDAR_BB_SERVICE_NAME`. The BB
shape is still structurally validated by its TypeScript interface
(`CalendarBbCredentialConfig`) and by BB Calendar itself when painel
later calls `listConnections()` / `deleteConnection()`.

- Moved `CALENDAR_BB_SERVICE_NAME` to `shared/bb-calendar/constants.ts`
  to avoid a circular import (calendar-integrations → credentials →
  storage → calendar-integrations).
- +3 unit tests: BB-calendar skip on create, ML still errors without
  clientId (regression guard), BB-calendar skip on update.

Alternatives rejected:
- Placeholder values like `bb-calendar-managed-outlook` (commit
  c832ef80, later reverted in f71a30aa): pollutes DB rows with fake
  fields that imply an OAuth flow painel doesn't run.
- New credential type enum (e.g. `EXTERNAL_OAUTH_CONNECTION`):
  disproportionate for a one-field validator gap; would require
  Prisma schema + UI form updates.

Wave-A follow-up to PR #249. Three additional fixes that together get
complex multi-tool workflows (conditional + N branches + N sends/generates)
to 100% success rate on local bench:

1. **Mandatory closing summary** — plan-mode prompt + base-prompt now

   × 2 actions each + finalize = 8-10 tool calls) need headroom above 6.

4. **[BUG FIX] add_workflow_action: first action order=0 → order=1** —
   pre-existing bug in tools-executor.service.ts:1255. Used
   `existingActions.length` which yields 0 for the first action, but the
   service validates `order >= 1`, so every first action silently failed.

commits.title: fix(ai-assistant): 4 workflow-construction bugs found by stg deep tests
commits.body:
fix(ai-assistant): 4 workflow-construction bugs found by stg deep tests

Bug sweep uncovered by the 6-scenario deep-test battery on stg 1.15.5.
All 4 were pre-existing behaviors, not introduced by PR #249 — they
just become visible once the assistant is actually executing complex
workflows successfully.

1. **DUPLICATE_ACTION_NAME guard** (tools-executor.service.ts)
   Split-turn construction (turn 1 hits MAX_ITERATIONS mid-build, turn 2
   continues) used to silently duplicate actions because the model had
   no visibility of DB state between turns. Stg scenario C produced 12
   actions where 6 were expected (2×RUN_AGENT, 2×UPDATE_LEAD, 3×DELAY).
   Fix: reject when `stepName` matches an existing action; return the
   existing action's metadata + full list, so the model can either skip
   or pick a different name. Adds regression test.

2. **toggle_workflow required by default** (plan-mode prompt rule 7)
   Stg scenarios B and C left workflows at `active=false` because the
   model forgot to activate after `finalize_workflow_diagram`. User
   tests and sees "it doesn't work" — worse than any error. Rule now
   mandates `toggle_workflow(id, active=true)` unless user asked to
   keep inactive.

3. **Pre-check on continuation turns** (plan-mode prompt rule 8)
   In turn-2+ of a workflow-building session, model must call
   `list_workflow_actions(workflowId)` BEFORE `add_workflow_action`.
   Combined with fix #1 this turns silent duplication into a fast,
   deterministic retry loop.

4. **CONDITIONAL nested-actions pattern** (plan-mode prompt rule 9)
   Model was producing two semantically-different patterns: (a) actions
   INSIDE branches[].actions (correct routing), (b) actions top-level
   with dependsOn referencing conditional name (runs ALL branches in
   parallel, not gated). Stg scenario B exhibited (b). Explicit rule
   + reason makes pattern (a) the default.

Also: agent-executor.service.ts gained a "resource-discovery rule" in
its built system prompt — when the user asks for data that could come
from multiple sources and a list_* tool exists, LIST first, don't ask
the user to disambiguate preemptively. Fixes stg scenario E where the
calendar agent asked for an integration ID instead of calling
list_calendar_events.

4804/4804 tests passing, including new dedup + prompt rule assertions.

commits.body:
fix(ai-assistant): eliminate "vou começar / um momento" narration without tool_use

Four layered defenses against the "theoretical assistant" regression that hit
multiple users after AI Intelligence Layer landed:

1. Plan-mode prompt + base prompt: explicitly PROIBIDO list of 13 transition
   phrases ("vou começar", "um momento", "aguarde", …). Rule "PRIMEIRO bloco
   DEVE ser um tool_use" forbids text-only responses when executing.

2. Confirmation detector extracted to confirmation-detector.ts with 5 regex
   families (affirmative/imperative/agreement/english/emoji) + Signal B
   (implicit confirmation when previous assistant msg ends with "?" and user
   reply is short non-negation). Catches "beleza", "isso", "👍", "bora" etc
   that the old prefix-match missed.

3. Narration guard in claude.provider.ts: when iter 1 returns text matching
   the narration regex while tools are available, inject a [SISTEMA]
   rebuke and re-iterate once. Logs every trigger for telemetry.

4. Mid-task chitchat hydration: when router flags confirmation as chitchat
   but sessionSkillsCache has skills, promote to action mode and re-hydrate
   tools from cache. Fixes the silent "empty response" when user says
   "pode/beleza/👍" after a plan presentation.

Adds ai-execution-bench.ts + corpus-execution.json (15-case A/B harness)

commits.title: fix(calendar): OAuth return — derive connectionId via listConnections diff
commits.body:
fix(calendar): OAuth return — derive connectionId via listConnections diff

BB Calendar does NOT append any identifiers to the redirect URL (see
building-blocks-v2/src/calendar/services/connection.service.ts#handleCallback
— returns the state-stored redirectUrl as-is). So Agent B/E's flow expecting
?connectionId= in the query param was broken: user got 'Parâmetro
connectionId ausente' on return.

connection by diffing listConnections() (via service token) against local
Credentials already claiming a connectionId. Picks newest unclaimed ACTIVE.
Race window (two users finishing OAuth within the same millisecond) is
negligible — human consent takes seconds.

  run listConnections + local findAll in parallel, filter out claimed,
  sort by createdAt desc, take first
- Controller GET /oauth/callback-return: drop @Query('connectionId')

- Service calendarIntegrationsApi.completeOAuthReturn: single-arg

commits.title: fix(agents): hotfix 4 bugs surfaced after PR #258 deploy
commits.body:
fix(agents): hotfix 4 bugs surfaced after PR #258 deploy

Live test of agent atendimento-catalisa via WhatsApp ("Mude meu nome para João da
Silva") still produced "Operação cancelada pelo usuário." after 60s, with 8 tool
calls (update_lead, get_lead, create_lead, get_lead×5). Root-cause analysis
exposed 4 distinct bugs:

1. **fatigue.record() ran AFTER dedup.shouldShortCircuit** in claude.provider
   and openai-compatible.provider. When LLM looped on identical (name, args),
   dedup absorbed every retry and the fatigue counter never moved → loop ran
   until the budget timeout. Fix: swap the order so fatigue records on EVERY
   tool attempt, regardless of whether dedup will short-circuit it.

2. **"Operação cancelada pelo usuário."** wrongly accused the user when the
   abort actually came from RunAgentHandler's wall-clock budget timeout (the
   only producer of signal.aborted in production). Replaced in 6 sites across
   3 providers with: "Não consegui completar a tarefa no tempo disponível.
   Por favor, reformule sua solicitação de forma mais simples ou peça em
   partes menores."

3. **dedup synthetic message was too soft** for gpt-4o-mini, which kept
   retrying the same call after seeing TOOL_CALL_LOOP_DETECTED. Strengthened
   to start with "PARE." and use "EXATAMENTE" / "NÃO retente" — explicit
   imperatives the model actually obeys.

4. **list_leads / list_chats did NOT normalize phone** (only mutating tools
   create_lead / update_lead / send_whatsapp_message did). LLM filtering by
   '+55 11 99999-9999' missed leads stored as '5511999999999' E.164, then
   retried with phone variations until MAX_ITERATIONS. Added per-tool
   normalization for the SEARCH-tool allowlist; mutating tools keep their
   per-case logic to preserve INVALID_PHONE vs MISSING_DESTINATION
   distinction (covered by existing ai-conversation-whatsapp-messaging spec).

Tests: 4959 passing (4 new specs covering each bug). Build prod: exit 0.

perf(whatsapp): 5-min cache for template definitions (not interpolated results)

commits.title: feat(agents): wall-clock budget + retry + circuit breaker for RUN_AGENT
commits.body:
feat(agents): wall-clock budget + retry + circuit breaker for RUN_AGENT

Hardens AI agent executions (invoked from workflows or ad-hoc) against
runaway loops, silent timeouts, and provider degradation. All guard-rails
are inherited by every agent — no per-agent opt-in needed.

**Budget cascade (action > agent > env, default 60s)**
- New `Agent.executionBudgetMs` column (nullable, 10000–600000ms)
- New `config.timeoutMs` on RUN_AGENT actions (same range, per-action override)
- Env `AGENT_DEFAULT_EXECUTION_BUDGET_MS` as fallback
- AbortController wired into agent chat → Claude SDK → tool loop
  so wall-clock exhaustion interrupts in-flight HTTP requests, not just
  next-iteration boundaries

**Per-tool timeout**
- `TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 30s) wraps each tool in claude.provider
- Returns synthetic `{__toolTimeout: true}` result so LLM can recover
  (pick another tool, respond with partial info) instead of killing the loop

**Error classification + selective retry**
- New `error-classifier.ts`: timeout / rate_limit / network / provider_5xx / client_error
- RUN_AGENT retries once at 50% budget for transient categories only
- 4xx never retries (caller's fault); rate_limit handled inside provider

**Circuit breaker per (agentId, workflowId)**
- Redis-backed state machine (closed / open / half_open)
- Opens after 5 failures in 10min, fast-fails for 5min, then probe
- Fails open on Redis errors (doesn't block agent execution)
- Client errors don't count — only transient categories trip it

**Observability**
- New `AgentExecution.status` values: 'timeout' | 'cancelled' | 'breaker_open'
- `timedOutStage` ('budget' | 'llm_call' | 'tool') + `timedOutAt`
- `traceId` field for joining agent exec → workflow exec → provider logs
- Index on traceId for fast correlation

**Frontend**
- AgentWizardModal: "Tempo maximo por execucao" slider (0–600s, 0 = herda)
- RunAgentForm: timeout override input + retry-on-timeout checkbox
- NodeExecutionBadge + execution-utils: new badge states for timeout/breaker
- AgentHistoryTab: distinct UI for timeout vs provider_error vs breaker_open

**Tests**
- 38 new unit tests (error-classifier, circuit-breaker, run-agent handler)
- Found and fixed real bug in breaker: recordSuccess wasn't clearing
  partial failure counters when state was still 'closed'
- Full suite: 4858 passed, 0 failed

**Migration**
- Aditivos only: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS
- Safe for shared DBs (feedback: never `prisma db push` in shared)

commits.title: fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe) (#261)
commits.body:
fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe) (#261)

PR #260 added the BullMQ workflow-execution queue but didn't pass a
deterministic jobId. With a single api replica that's fine — there's
exactly one Pub/Sub subscriber. Once we scale `wpp_painel-cliente-api`
to 2+ replicas every replica spins up its own EventListener subscriber,
Pub/Sub fans every message out to all of them, and without a stable
jobId each replica enqueues an independent job per matched trigger —
the workflow runs N times.

Fix: pass `jobId = "${eventId}:${triggerId}"` when enqueueing.

- `eventId` comes from the publisher (`event.id`/`event.eventId` set by
  WebhookEventsService.emit, which uuidv4s every emit). For synthetic
  publishes that don't carry an id we fall back to a sha256 hash of
  channel + type + userId + payload — same input on each replica yields
  the same hash, so dedup still holds.
- BullMQ rejects duplicate jobIds across all states (waiting/active/
  completed/failed), so the second enqueue is a cheap no-op and the
  workflow runs exactly once even when N replicas race to add it.

This unlocks horizontal scaling of `wpp_painel-cliente-api` without
risking duplicate workflow execution for tenants with active LEAD_*

commits.title: fix(workflows): async dispatch via BullMQ + AI_HUB_AGENT non-text skip + subscriber resilience (#260)
commits.body:
fix(workflows): async dispatch via BullMQ + AI_HUB_AGENT non-text skip + subscriber resilience (#260)

Three coordinated fixes for the production timeout reports on agent flows
and bulk-import-driven workflows.

1. **BullMQ workflow-execution queue (Frente A)** — `EventListenerService`
   used to `await WorkflowExecutionService.execute()` inline inside the
   Redis Pub/Sub `pmessage` callback. With one api replica, that drained
   one workflow at a time per tenant. Bulk imports of N leads fanned out
   into N `LEAD_CREATED` events that the subscriber processed serially —
   later leads appeared to "time out" because their workflow only started
   minutes after the import.

   New `WorkflowExecutionQueueService` registers a BullMQ `Queue` + `Worker`
   in the same NestJS process. The producer adds a lightweight
   `{ workflowId, payload, triggerId }` job; the worker re-fetches the
   workflow from Prisma (picks up any state change between enqueue and
   execute) and delegates to `WorkflowExecutionService.execute()`. The
   subscriber returns immediately, so backpressure on Pub/Sub is gone.

   Behind the `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_VIA_QUEUE` flag — defaulting OFF for
   now — so prod can flip it on, observe, and roll back via env in seconds
   if anything misbehaves. Concurrency tunable via
   `WORKFLOW_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` (default 5).

   Defense in depth: if `queue.add()` itself throws (e.g. Redis
   unavailable), the listener falls back to inline execution so events
   are never silently dropped.

2. **AI_HUB_AGENT skip on empty message (Frente B)** — Audio, image,
   sticker and other non-text inbound messages interpolate
   `$helpers.getMessageText(...)` to an empty string, which was making
   the handler return `success: false` with
   `'AI_HUB_AGENT requires message in config'`. That bubbled up as a
   workflow failure and polluted Sentry. The CORRETOR tenant logs were
   full of these.

   The handler now returns `success: true` with
   `data: { skipped: true, reason: 'non-text-message' }` when message is
   empty. Downstream actions can branch on `output.skipped` if they need
   non-text-specific behavior; otherwise the workflow keeps running.

3. **Subscriber Redis resilience (Frente C)** — `EventListenerService`'s
   raw `new Redis(...)` call did not match the
   `createResilientRedis` factory used elsewhere, so it didn't recover
   gracefully from DigitalOcean managed Redis ECONNRESET cycles. We
   added a sibling `createResilientRedisSubscriber` (psubscribe-friendly:
   keeps `enableOfflineQueue: true` and `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` so
   the long-running subscribe survives reconnect, while still applying
   `retryStrategy` and `reconnectOnError`) and migrated the listener
   onto it.

Tests: 4 new spec files, 20 unit tests covering producer enqueue,
consumer execute, missing-workflow no-op, AI_HUB_AGENT skip path
(empty/null/undefined), inline fallback when queue throws, legacy
synchronous path. Full painel-cliente-api jest run on touched modules:
2911 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed across 107 suites.

Bumps painel-cliente-api 1.15.13 → 1.15.14.

commits.title: fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe)
commits.body:
fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe)

PR #260 added the BullMQ workflow-execution queue but didn't pass a
deterministic jobId. With a single api replica that's fine — there's
exactly one Pub/Sub subscriber. Once we scale `wpp_painel-cliente-api`
to 2+ replicas every replica spins up its own EventListener subscriber,
Pub/Sub fans every message out to all of them, and without a stable
jobId each replica enqueues an independent job per matched trigger —
the workflow runs N times.

Fix: pass `jobId = "${eventId}:${triggerId}"` when enqueueing.

- `eventId` comes from the publisher (`event.id`/`event.eventId` set by
  WebhookEventsService.emit, which uuidv4s every emit). For synthetic
  publishes that don't carry an id we fall back to a sha256 hash of
  channel + type + userId + payload — same input on each replica yields
  the same hash, so dedup still holds.
- BullMQ rejects duplicate jobIds across all states (waiting/active/
  completed/failed), so the second enqueue is a cheap no-op and the
  workflow runs exactly once even when N replicas race to add it.

This unlocks horizontal scaling of `wpp_painel-cliente-api` without
risking duplicate workflow execution for tenants with active LEAD_*
or workflow.* triggers.

Tests: 3 new specs in event-listener.service.spec.ts cover the
event.id-derived jobId, the hash fallback for synthetic events,
and idempotency across re-deliveries. All 11/11 spec cases pass.

Bumps painel-cliente-api 1.15.14 → 1.15.15.

feat(shared): IFileStorageFacade with Local + Remote implementations

Spelled exactly like the existing webhooks-engine and decision-engine
facades: an interface + Token, a Local impl that delegates to the in-
process FileService when running monolith, and a Remote impl that
talks to file-storage over HTTP via ModuleClient when standalone (the
production path for wpp). Internal JWT signed with a fixed sub +
FILES_CREATE/FILES_READ permissions.

Lets cross-BB consumers (wpp first) register/confirm uploads and
fetch presigned download URLs without taking a static dependency on
the file-storage module.

Local registration is best-effort: the FileService isn't always
present in every monolith entry point (e.g. an IAM-only standalone),
so the registry warns and skips instead of crashing.

20 unit tests cover both impls (delegation, header propagation,
URL/body shape).

mapMessagesUpsert now takes deviceId and writes it into CreateMessageData
so persisted rows carry the device that received/sent each message.
SessionManager.wireMessageEventListeners passes deviceId through.

serializeMessage was previously dropping rawPayload entirely for every
message type. Now it keeps rawPayload — encoded via

commits.title: feat(wpp): GET /messages/media/:messageId — lazy materialize via file-storage
commits.body:
feat(wpp): GET /messages/media/:messageId — lazy materialize via file-storage

First call: looks up the WppMessage, fetches the live driver session
for the device that received it, calls driver.downloadMedia which
rehydrates the persisted protobuf and pulls bytes from the WhatsApp
CDN, then registers the file in the file-storage BB (via facade),
PUTs the bytes to the presigned upload URL, confirms the upload,
caches the resulting fileId in WppMessage.mediaFileId, and 302s
to the file-storage download URL.

Subsequent calls: cache hit on mediaFileId — straight 302 to a fresh
presigned URL, no driver round-trip, no re-download from the
WhatsApp CDN. Validated end-to-end: 770ms cold, 13ms warm.

If the cached download URL ever fails, falls through to re-
materialize rather than 500ing.

Error mapping:
- 404 if message not found / wrong org
- 400 if message has no media body (text/reaction/etc)
- 409 if legacy row predates deviceId / preserved protobuf
- 503 if device offline (operator reconnects + retries)
- 502 if WhatsApp CDN failed / media expired

file-storage's MimeType allowlist is narrow (PDF/PNG/JPEG/octet-stream)
because it inherits from a Smithy schema designed for KYC docs. WhatsApp
covers video/audio/sticker too, so we tell file-storage application/
octet-stream for those and keep the real mimetype on the persisted
WppMessage.payload for downstream consumers. Bytes are unchanged.

commits.title: fix(wpp): per-device Redis lock in restoreActiveSessions for replica safety
commits.body:
fix(wpp): per-device Redis lock in restoreActiveSessions for replica safety

The previous restoreActiveSessions fix (PR #124) made the worker actually
re-establish driver sessions on cold start, but had no cross-process
coordination: with replicas>1 — or during a rolling deploy where the new
worker boots before the old one shuts down — every replica would query
the same `status='open'` rows and race on each device. Multiple Baileys
sockets would attempt to bind to the same WhatsApp linked device,
producing 401/conflict disconnects (Meta enforces a single live socket
per linked device).

This change introduces atomic SETNX semantics on RedisService
(`setIfAbsent(key, value, ttlSeconds)`, backed by `SET key value NX EX`)
and uses it inside `restoreActiveSessions` to claim a per-device restore
lock at `wpp:reconnect-lock:{orgId}:{deviceId}` (30s TTL, same prefix as
the existing post-disconnect reconnect lock) before doing any work.
First replica to call SETNX wins and reconnects; the rest see the lock
held and skip.

Recovery characteristic: if a worker dies mid-restore (crash, OOM, etc.),
the lock survives until its 30s TTL elapses. The next boot will pick the
device up. Single-replica deploys are unchanged (lock always acquired).

Validated locally: a clean boot acquires the lock and reaches
`state_change → open` in ~2s; an immediate second boot (lock still
held from prior process) cleanly logs "Restore lock held by another
process, skipping" without spawning a duplicate driver.

Bumps to 1.0.7.

commits.title: fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions queries devices across all orgs
commits.body:
fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions queries devices across all orgs

The session-worker boot path called `deviceRepository.findAll('', { status: 'open' })`,
passing an empty string as `organizationId`. The repo's `findAll` filters by
`WHERE organizationId = $1`, so the query effectively became
`organizationId = '' AND status = 'open'`, returning zero rows in production.
Net effect: no device was ever resurrected on session-worker boot — every restart
left previously connected WhatsApp sessions dead until a manual reconnect request.

Changes:
- Add `DeviceRepository.findAllAcrossOrgs({ status?, driver? })`: cross-org lookup
  that returns `DeviceEntity[]` directly (no pagination wrapper). It is intentionally
  not exposed via the public router/service layer — it exists only for boot-time
  reconciliation.
- `SessionManager.restoreActiveSessions` now calls `findAllAcrossOrgs` and treats
  the result as a flat array.

Why cross-org (and not "loop per org"): the current deployment runs a single shared
session-worker process that owns sockets for every tenant. Boot-time recovery has
to enumerate devices regardless of organizationId. If we ever shard the worker per
tenant, the call site changes (caller already has the orgId), but the repository
method stays useful for ops/diagnostics.

Tests:
- New repo tests cover no-filter (multi-org rows), status filter, driver filter.
- Session-manager `restoreActiveSessions` suite migrated to the new method and a
  regression test was added: two devices in distinct orgs, both `status: 'open'`,
  both must produce `reconnect_attempt` log entries.

commits.title: fix(wpp): coordinator waits 10s before XADD to let other replicas join group
commits.body:
fix(wpp): coordinator waits 10s before XADD to let other replicas join group

The previous Option C implementation worked correctly (1 SETNX winner
enqueues, no duplication, devices restored end-to-end) but local 3-worker
test showed 3-0-0 distribution: worker A's first XREADGROUP COUNT=10
drained the entire stream before workers B/C registered their consumers
in the group. Redis Streams delivers a whole batch to whichever consumer
asks first; round-robin only happens between consumers actively blocked
on XREADGROUP.

Adding a 10s delay between SETNX win and XADD gives Docker Swarm rolling
update the typical 5-15s window it needs to spawn the next replica and
have its consumer register in the group. Worst case: a slow replica
(>10s boot) misses the burst and still gets nothing. Defensive option
(XINFO-poll for consumer count) documented in
docs/wpp/auto-restore-and-distribution.md for future reference.

commits.title: feat(wpp): distribute restoreActiveSessions via Redis Streams across replicas
commits.body:
feat(wpp): distribute restoreActiveSessions via Redis Streams across replicas

Coordinator-elect (`SET NX EX wpp:restore-coordinator`, 60s) ensures exactly
one worker queries the DB and XADDs one SESSION_RESTORE job per device into
the existing stream; the consumer group then round-robins each device to
exactly one replica. Per-device idempotency is preserved via the existing
`wpp:reconnect-lock:{org}:{device}` SET NX EX lock plus an in-memory
`this.sessions.has` short-circuit, so stream redelivery is safe.

Why not the previous "lock per device only" design: with N replicas each
running their own restore loop they would each enqueue duplicate
`reconnect_attempt` log rows and fight over the same Baileys socket — even
with the per-device lock, the losers still did the DB scan and the log
write. The coordinator-elect cuts that to one DB scan and one set of log
rows total, regardless of replica count.

chore(wpp): default WPP_SESSION_WORKER_ENABLED to true

Devs running `bun run src/wpp/main-session-worker.ts` locally without
setting `WPP_SESSION_WORKER_ENABLED=true` saw the worker boot with
`WPP consumer is disabled (WPP_SESSION_WORKER_ENABLED=false)` and
silently no-op, since the previous default was false. Production
(swarm.yml/.env) always sets the flag explicitly, so flipping the
default does not regress prod. Anyone wanting the worker process to
run without the Redis stream consumer (e.g. main-only debug) can still
opt out by setting `WPP_SESSION_WORKER_ENABLED=false` explicitly.

The flag is consumed in two places (src/main.ts, src/wpp/consumers/index.ts)
and both already read from the validated `config.WPP_SESSION_WORKER_ENABLED`,
so no other call sites needed normalization.

commits.title: fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions actually re-establishes driver sessions
commits.body:
fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions actually re-establishes driver sessions

Pre-bug: restoreActiveSessions only wrote a `reconnect_attempt` row in
wpp_connection_logs and returned. No driver was instantiated, no socket
opened — workers came up "running" with the in-memory sessions Map empty
while DB still showed devices as `open`. Effective behaviour: every
worker restart silently dropped every previously-paired session until
someone hit POST /devices/:id/reconnect manually.

The earlier PR #122 fix (`findAllAcrossOrgs`) made the query work, but
the actual restore step was a no-op all along (visible in git history
since the first wpp commit f9fbd92).

Now: each restored row goes through `getOrCreateSession` after the log
is written. wireEventListeners fires, the Baileys socket opens, and the
driver's `connection.update` event flips `wpp_devices.status` back to
`open` (or `closed` if auth was revoked remotely). Per-device errors
are caught and logged at warn — one stale auth doesn't block the others.

Validated end-to-end locally: a paired device went from cold boot to
state_change=open in ~2.3s without any manual reconnect call.

Also bumps to 1.0.6.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.title: fix(ai): cap leadtype context + block 'status' keyword from lead-management
commits.body:
fix(ai): cap leadtype context + block 'status' keyword from lead-management

URGENT FIX for the 130x token inflation bug detected in stg bench
2026-05-02. Documented in docs/analysis/2026-05-02-phase0-bench-results.md.

Bug chain (2 bugs in series):

1. lead-management/index.ts:92 listed 'status' as a keyword. Workflow
   prompts mentioning "status do usuario" matched lead-management with
   score=6, putting it in the top-3 of the keyword detector.

2. lead-type-context.service.ts:28 fetched up to 200 active LeadTypes
   with EVERY field listed verbosely. Stg DB grew from ~50 to 200+
   types in 9 days, ballooning the injected context from ~500 tokens
   to ~30k tokens. workflow-status-periodic bench case went from
   in=222 (2026-04-23) to in=29494 (2026-05-02) — 132x growth.

3. (Latent) DEFAULT_SKILLS = ['lead-management', 'whatsapp-messaging']
   means LLM router failures (rate-limit, timeout) silently inject
   30k tokens. Same defensive caps now bound that blast radius.

Fixes:

A. lead-management/index.ts
   - Remove 'status' and 'novo' from keywords (too generic, matched
     workflow/user/account contexts). Lead-status semantics still
     covered by 'qualificado', 'convertido', 'perdido', 'lead novo'.
   - Add `negativeKeywords: ['workflow', 'automacao', 'automação',
     'trigger', 'gatilho', 'agente', 'agent', 'template']` so
     workflow/automation prompts can never trigger lead-management
     even if a positive keyword sneaks back in. Schema and detector
     logic for negativeKeywords already existed (skill-detector.service.ts:129-137)
     — just was never used.

B. lead-type-context.service.ts
   - Cap MAX_TYPES_IN_CONTEXT=30 (was 200) — single cacheable block
     of ~3-5k tokens is enough for AI to know which custom fields
     exist; model can call list_lead_types for the rest on demand.
   - Cap MAX_FIELDS_PER_TYPE=5 with "+N campos" overflow line.
   - Add structured log `evt:ai.leadtype.context.size` so future
     regressions are visible to log aggregator (Phase 1 dashboard).
   - Fix totalActive read to support both old `result.total` and new
     `result.pagination.total` shape.

Tests:
- New lead-management-status-keyword-bug.spec.ts with 5 tests:
  * workflow-status-periodic prompt → does NOT load lead-management
  * automacao/trigger/gatilho prompts → do NOT load lead-management
  * lead-focused prompts (liste/crie/quantos leads) → STILL load
  * Schema sanity: negativeKeywords present + 'status' removed
- All 1328 ai-assistant + ai-core tests pass

Expected impact (post-deploy):
- workflow-status-periodic: in=29494 → ~5000-8000 tokens (-75%)
- All workflow/automation prompts: same drop
- All AI Assistant turns under throttle/rate-limit fallback: same drop
- Latency turn1 should return to ~8s baseline (was 21s+)

chore(ai-providers): structured cache.metrics logs for observability

PR C from docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md.
Replaces unparseable emoji-string cache logs with JSON lines so log
aggregators (Loki / CloudWatch) can extract fields. Phase 1 Grafana
dashboard reads `evt: 'ai.cache.metrics'` to alert on cacheHitRatio
regressions in <30min instead of waiting for prod incident reports.

Schema (uniform across providers):
  { evt: 'ai.cache.metrics', provider, model, [iteration],
    inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheHitRatio }

Claude (logCacheMetrics):
  - cacheHitRatio = cacheRead / (input + cacheRead) — Anthropic accounts
    cacheRead separately from input, hence the denominator
  - Keeps the human-readable "Cache hit: X tokens" line for live tail

OpenAI-compatible (per-iteration in completeWithTools):
  - cacheHitRatio = cachedTokens / promptTokens (OpenAI counts cached
    inside prompt_tokens, hence different denominator)
  - Includes `iteration` for per-loop tracking

Note: PR #260 already bumped 1.15.14 → 1.15.15, so the planned PR C
version-bump step is moot. Container in prod likely already at 1.15.15
(SSH check pending user OK).

commits.title: fix(ai-tools): cap list_* tool results to prevent context inflation
commits.body:
fix(ai-tools): cap list_* tool results to prevent context inflation

URGENT FIX continuation. Bench 2026-05-02 after fixing leadtype context
showed 3 cases REGRESSING (+44k tokens) because they call list_*
tools (list_whatsapp_devices, list_workflows, list_leads, list_agents)
that returned ALL of the user's resources unbounded into the next
LLM call's input tokens.

Smoking gun from bench JSON:
- broadcast-message t1 tools: [list_leads, list_whatsapp_devices, suggest_navigation] → 35193 tokens
- workflow-update-status t1 tools: [list_whatsapp_devices] → 44615 tokens
- workflow-followup t1 tools: [list_whatsapp_devices, request_resource_selection] → 47639 tokens
- agent-create-basic (control, no list_*): 9880 tokens, latency 10s ⭐

The 3 worsened cases all call list_whatsapp_devices. Stg has dozens of
test devices accumulated; each device serialized with CUID + name + phone
≈ 50 tokens. 100 devices = 5000 tokens injected after EVERY list call.
Same pattern for list_workflows, list_leads, list_agents.

Fix: new `capListResult<T>(items, cap, label, summary?)` helper that
returns top-N items + total + truncatedHint instructing the AI to use
request_resource_selection or specific filters when total > shown.

Caps applied (chosen empirically from typical user limits):

test(ai-providers): standalone real-API harnesses for Phase 0 validation

Two scripts that validate the Phase 0 fixes against the REAL Anthropic
API without needing the full app (no DB, no Redis). Tools are mocked so
provider behavior can be isolated from Panel SDK.

scripts/test-providers-real-api.ts
  Runs 4 scenarios against each enabled provider (Anthropic by default;
  OpenAI / Gemini if their keys are set in env — in prod the creds live
  in the DB and ai-core auto-loads them):
    [1] Single-tool: "lista meus leads" → expect 1 tool call
    [2] Multi-tool parallel: "overview leads/workflows/chats" →
        verifies maxInflight=3 + parallel_savings_ms > 0 (PR A3)
    [3] Multi-turn: 3 messages, validates iteration count + tool sequencing
    [4] Narration trigger: vague prompt, validates guard fires or model
        asks for params instead

scripts/test-cache-real-api.ts
  Forces the cacheable block above Anthropic's threshold (51 synthetic
  tools = ~4k tokens of cacheable content, well above the 1024 Haiku /
  2048 Sonnet minimum) and runs 2 turns:
    Turn 1 iter 1: cache_creation > 0 (cache WRITTEN)
    Turn 1 iter 2 + Turn 2 iter 1+2: cache_read > 0 (cache HIT)

  token savings — proves PR A1 + A2 work end-to-end with real API.

the iteration===1 gate suppressed cache_control.

commits.body:
feat(ai-orchestrator): truth footer — list real IDs created in turn (anti-confabulation)

Combined with PR-pending fatigue threshold bump (15 floor), this addresses
the user's barbershop cyberpunk session where the model:
1. Hit fatigue mid-construction
2. Confabulated completion ("✅ Fase 2 executada com sucesso!")
3. Invented FAKE IDs (wfl_01jg... and agt_01jg... — non-cuid prefix)
4. User had to manually catch the lie and force multi-turn recovery

Fix: executor now tracks REAL resources created/updated during the turn
by inspecting tool results for cuid-shaped IDs, classifies by tool name
(create_workflow → Workflow, create_agent → Agent, etc.), and appends a
"truth footer" to the response:

  ---
  **Recursos REAIS criados/atualizados neste turno** (use só estes IDs — não invente):
  - Workflow: \`cmorzkfvt000u119bv5hu1le9\`
  - Agent: \`cmoqp5yxu0001thl8w...\`

The footer is the authoritative source of truth. If the model writes a
fake ID in the response body, it's instantly contradicted by the footer
listing only real ones. Confabulation becomes obvious to both user and
the model itself in subsequent turns (when history is replayed).

Empty map → empty footer (no noise when read-only chat).

commits.title: fix(ai-orchestrator): truth footer ID extraction — deep-search robust
commits.body:
fix(ai-orchestrator): truth footer ID extraction — deep-search robust

Stg smoke test revealed truth footer wasn't appearing despite tool calls
creating real workflows. Cause: extractIdsFromResult used a hardcoded path
list (result.id, result.workflow.id, etc.) but real tool results vary in
shape (sometimes nested under data, success wrappers, etc.).

Replace with deep-search up to depth 3 looking for any field named "id"
or "*Id" containing a cuid. Recurse only through likely-container keys
(workflow, agent, lead, trigger, action, data, result, customaction) to
avoid scanning massive payloads.

This makes the truth footer resilient to tool result shape changes and
catches IDs the old path list missed.

fix for hallucination), it skipped the planner phase where examples were being
injected. Result: the user's curated examples weren't being used for chat
build intents.

and injects them into the system prompt before the LLM call. Type detection
via simple keyword scan (agente/agent → agent type, custom action → custom-action,
default → workflow). Falls back gracefully when retriever isn't available or
examplesScope is unset.

SystemAssistantOrchestratedService now resolves user's organizationId via
OrganizationsService.getOrgId() and sets config.examplesScope so retrieval
fires per-org. Solo users without OrganizationMember fall back to userId
as scope (personal library).

End-to-end flow now:
1. User saves a working workflow as example via UI ("Salvar como exemplo")
2. Embedder generates 1536-dim float32 vector via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small
3. User asks chat for similar workflow
4. Executor's single-shot path retrieves top-3 by cosine similarity
5. Injector formats the examples into system prompt as markdown few-shot block
6. LLM sees the patterns and copies the structure (not the literals)

commits.title: fix(ai-assistant): hydrate cached skills on implicit selection turns
commits.body:
fix(ai-assistant): hydrate cached skills on implicit selection turns

Bug seen in prod 2026-05-04:
  Turn 1: "Quero workflow para minha adega..." → 2 tools called ✓
  Turn 2: "vamos usar o 3414"             → 0 tools called, AI fabricated
                                            "Instalado! ID: wfl_cmlz..."

Root cause (ai-assistant.service.ts:152-197):
- Intent router classifies short follow-ups without explicit confirmation
  tokens as chitchat (rawIsChitchat=true).
- Previous Fix #4 hydration block only re-hydrated cached skills when
  detectConfirmation matched ("sim", "ok", "pode", emoji, ...).
- "vamos usar o 3414" is a SELECTION, not a confirmation → fails the
  pattern → hydratedFromCache=false → toolsToUse=[] → LLM has no real
  tools but conversation context says it should install/create something
  → hallucinates success.

Fix:
- Extract a static helper `isImplicitContinuation(message)` that returns
  true for short messages (<80 chars) that aren't standalone greetings
  and don't contain negation/cancellation tokens.
- Try the helper first in the Fix #4 block; fall back to the existing
  detectConfirmation path. Behavior is strictly more permissive — every
  prior confirmation still hydrates, plus selection/continuation turns.
- Static so it's testable without the full DI graph.

Tests: 52 cases covering implicit continuations ("vamos usar o 3414",
"esse aí", "o 11999..."), explicit confirmations ("sim", "ok", emoji),
negations ("não, cancela", "esquece"), standalone greetings ("oi", "bom
dia"), boundary cases (length 79/80, case-insensitive), and the exact
prod transcript turn that broke.

Full ai-assistant suite: 1515 passed / 1515.

Context: docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md (continuation
of Phase 0 hardening, post PRs #262 #263 #264).

commits.title: fix(ai-orchestrator): bump ToolFatigueGuard threshold floor to 15
commits.body:
fix(ai-orchestrator): bump ToolFatigueGuard threshold floor to 15

User reported a barbershop cyberpunk demo where the model built a workflow
with 5+ actions but stopped at action 3 due to ToolFatigueGuard blocking
add_workflow_action after 3 invocations. Model then confabulated completion
("Fase 2 executada com sucesso!" + FAKE IDs like wfl_01jg... and agt_01jg...
that don't match cuid2 prefix). Multi-turn recovery worked manually but UX
is bad — user has to nudge "execute oq faltou".

Root cause: AGENT_TOOL_FATIGUE_THRESHOLD defaults to 3 in ai-core. That's
appropriate for short conversational agents but too tight for orchestrator
workflow construction where add_workflow_action is legitimately called
N times for an N-action workflow.

Fix: AIOrchestratorModule.onModuleInit() bumps the env var floor to 15
on startup if not already set higher. Operators can still override via env
to a higher value; we only bump UP, never override an operator-set ceiling.

This was Phase 2.4 fix #3 documented as pending. Provider-level per-call
override would be cleaner long-term, but the env bump is non-invasive,
ships immediately, and resolves the user's UX bug.

commits.body:
feat(ai-examples): Phase 3 — Examples Library backend

User-curated examples of well-formed workflows / agents / custom-actions that
the orchestrator's planner phase retrieves at runtime as few-shot context.
This is the user-requested feature ("área pra subir exemplos / treinar").

Data model (assistant_examples):
- type: 'workflow' | 'agent' | 'custom-action'
- title + intentDescription (free text) + tags[]
- payload Json: snapshot of the config at save time
- embedding Bytes: float32 (1536 dims, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small)
- isCurated: admin-marked "good"; weighted +0.05 in retrieval ranking
- per-org scope + optional per-agent narrowing
- usageCount + lastUsedAt telemetry

Module ai-examples/:
- ai-examples.controller.ts: REST CRUD (POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /ai-examples)
- ai-examples.service.ts: per-org ACL, embedding refresh on title/intent/tags change
- embedder.service.ts: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small via fetch (graceful null on failure)
- retriever.service.ts: tag prefilter + cosine in Node, +0.05 curated boost,
  fire-and-forget telemetry bump on returned rows
- injector.service.ts: formats top-K into markdown system-prompt block with
  "Por que funciona" reasoning so the LLM picks up patterns, not just JSON

Wired into orchestrator: planner.service.ts injects @Optional() retriever +
injector. When config.examplesScope is set, retrieves top-3 and prepends the
formatted block to REPL_SYSTEM_PROMPT before the planner LLM call.

Personal scope fallback: solo users without an OrganizationMember row use
their userId as organizationId — same isolation guarantees, no data migration
needed when they later join an org.

Migration: hand-written idempotent SQL with PG bytea + DO $$ FK guards.
Pattern matches Phase 1.4 schema migration. Safe to run repeatedly.

No pgvector — Float32 in bytea is fine until >500 examples per org.

commits.body:
feat(ai-orchestrator): Phase 2.3 — preview-before-mutate pseudo-tools

Three pseudo-tools the LLM can call BEFORE mutating to validate proposed
workflows / agents / custom-actions:

  workflow_dry_run({ trigger, actions })
    → { mermaid, validationResult, dependencyGraph }

  agent_preview({ name, systemPrompt, tools, ... })
    → { formattedSystemPrompt, validationResult }

  custom_action_preview(actionConfig)
    → { schemaPreview, validationResult }

OrchestratorPreviewService:
- Pure validation + render; no DB writes.
- Tool definitions (CanonicalToolDefinition[]) exposed as static constant
  so wrappers append to config.tools.
- tryHandle() dispatcher returns null for non-preview tools so the
  executor falls through to config.toolExecutor as usual.

Executor wiring:
- New dispatchTool helper intercepts preview tool calls before
  config.toolExecutor; both single-shot and multi-task paths use it.

Wrapper updates:
- SystemAssistantOrchestratedService appends preview tools to TOOLS_REGISTRY.
- BuilderExecutionService appends preview tools to skillContext.tools.

Combined with Phase 2.2 post-execution validators and Phase 4.2 system
prompt enrichment, the orchestrated path now defends against the broken
patterns at THREE layers: (1) generation guidance via prompt + examples,
(2) preview-before-mutate via pseudo-tools, (3) post-mutation validation
on finalize.

commits.body:
fix(ai-assistant): remove hydration gates on mid-task chitchat (Fix #4c)

Cache presence IS the mid-task signal. Previous gates (isImplicitContinuation
length<80 OR detectConfirmation pattern match) were too narrow — they missed
complaints/questions about prior turns, meta-comments, and recreation requests
>80 chars. Those messages reached LLM with tools=[] and the model
hallucinated past-tense success ("Workflow criado") with fabricated cuid IDs.

Bug seen in prod 2026-05-04 15:27-15:35 BRT (admin@catalisa.app adega
workflow recreation flow):
  Turn 1: 21 tool calls, real workflow created (action mode)
  Turn 4: "pode recriar entao" (17 chars, would pass gate, didn't trigger)
  Turn 5: "voce nao recriou apenas disse que recriou..." (95 chars, GATE
          BLOCKED - length>80) → tools=[] → hallucination

Affects all providers (Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama) — bug is at service
classification layer, not provider response layer.

Trade-off: stray "oi" mid-task now loads ~5K extra tokens. Acceptable
because: (a) cache TTL 30min auto-expires when task done, (b) loaded
tools != tools called, (c) hallucination cost (churn, support) >> tokens.

feat(ai-assistant): add hallucination guard for fake tool execution claims (Fix C)

Adds shouldRetryForFakeAction sibling guard alongside shouldRetryForNarration.
Detects pretérito-perfeito execution claims ("Adicionei", "✅ criei id: act_xxx")
without tool_use this iteration. Bug observed in prod 2026-05-04 where Sonnet
fabricated cuid-style IDs across 4 turns.

Patterns (≥2 must match to fire):
- FAKE_ACTION_VERBS: criei, adicionei, atualizei, enviei, deletei, removi,
  ativei, desativei, inseri, configurei, conectei, montei, finalizei, registrei
- FAKE_ACTION_ID_REF: /\bid:\s*[a-z0-9_]{8,}/i
- FAKE_ACTION_PREFIX: /\b(act_|wf_|wfl_|cm[a-z0-9]{20,})/i
- FAKE_ACTION_CHECKMARK: /(?:^|\n)\s*(?:✅|✔|☑)/m

Cap 1 retry, requires hasTools, requires toolCallsThisIteration === 0,
requires finalText length >= 20. Logger.error severity surfaces matches
for triage. After cap reached, response passes through to avoid loops.

Wired in claude.provider.ts after the existing narration-guard block in the
zero-tool-calls branch. Shares fakeActionRetries counter scoped per session.

commits.title: fix(ai-orchestrator): SEND_MESSAGE AFTER agent é OBRIGATÓRIA, não proibida
commits.body:
fix(ai-orchestrator): SEND_MESSAGE AFTER agent é OBRIGATÓRIA, não proibida

User pegou regressão: meu fix anti-pattern #6 ("agente como única action")
deixou o agent gerando resposta SEM ninguém enviar pro user. Atendimento
WhatsApp tem dois pares de SEND_MESSAGE, com semântica oposta:

- ❌ STATIC SEND_MESSAGE *ANTES* de RUN_AGENT  (canned greeting tone-deaf)
- ✅ DYNAMIC SEND_MESSAGE *DEPOIS* de RUN_AGENT consumindo
  {{actions.AGENT.output.text}}  (envia resposta do agent ao user — sem
  ela atendimento não existe)

Padrão correto:

  trigger: MESSAGE_RECEIVED
    └─ action 1: RUN_AGENT  ("vetVirtual")
         └─ action 2: SEND_MESSAGE
              text={{actions.vetVirtual.output.text}}, dependsOn=[vetVirtual]
         └─ action 3 opcional: CREATE_LEAD se output do agent indica intenção

**Prompt anti-pattern #6 atualizado**:
- Seção "PADRÃO CORRETO" agora mostra 2 actions (agent + send), não 1
- Aviso CRÍTICO ⚠️ explicando que RUN_AGENT só GERA, SEND_MESSAGE ENVIA
- Exemplos concretos (igreja, petshop, vinharia) com SEND_MESSAGE após
- Auto-checklist 6.4 reescrito: pergunta "depois ou antes?" e tem
  duas perguntas separadas pra SEND_MESSAGE e pra RUN_AGENT

**Validator novo**: WORKFLOW_AGENT_RESPONSE_NOT_SENT
- Severity: error
- Só fire em workflows com trigger MESSAGE_RECEIVED (heurística "atendimento
  WhatsApp" — em workflows agendados/internos o agent pode legitimamente
  não enviar mensagem)
- Detecta RUN_AGENT/AI_HUB_AGENT cuja output não é consumido por NENHUM
  SEND_MESSAGE downstream
- Mensagem: "ADICIONE SEND_MESSAGE com text={{actions.X.output.text}}"

Inline validation hook em finalize_workflow_diagram já injeta esse erro
no tool_result com instrução, então o modelo auto-corrige antes de
responder ao user (mesma rota do anti-pattern #6).

commits.body:
fix(ai-orchestrator): use planningMode='off' for AI Assistant chat (no clarify/plan)

E2E smoke on stg revealed: when chat routed through clarify+plan phases (Builder
UX flow), the LLM hallucinated <tool_use>...</tool_use> markup as TEXT instead
of emitting real tool_use blocks. Verified via DB: workflow ID returned in chat
(clzqe8r9v...) didn't exist; real cuids start with 'cm...' and the IDs were
clearly sequential (...r9v → ...ra0 → ...ra2 → ...ra4) with createdAt 2024-08-14.

Root cause: clarify phase uses REPL_SYSTEM_PROMPT (Builder's spec-drafting
prompt). It teaches the model to draft workflows by example — including
examples of tool_use blocks. The model then mimics that style in its TEXT
response when no tools are made available (clarify uses provider.complete,
not completeWithTools).

Fix: AI Assistant chat now sets planningMode='off' which short-circuits the
clarify+plan branch in OrchestrationService.run and routes straight to the
executor's single-shot path. The model gets all 155 tools (TOOLS_REGISTRY +
preview) and the orchestrator-enriched system prompt with anti-patterns +
agent framework. It iterates real tool calls like Claude Code does.

Builder UX (BuilderExecutionService) keeps planningMode='always' because its
explicit DRAFTING → SPEC_READY → EXECUTING phases need the spec generation.

fix(ai-orchestrator): inline workflow validation on finalize + ABSOLUTE anti-pattern #6

User retested with "Atendimento Igreja" and got the same broken pattern
(SEND_MESSAGE → RUN_AGENT) DESPITE anti-pattern #6 being deployed. Root cause:
Claude has a strong training-data bias toward "greet first then process",
and the previous prompt was too soft (listed exceptions that the model
rationalized into "this case qualifies").

Three-layer reinforcement:

1. **Prompt: anti-pattern #6 made ABSOLUTE**
   - Header: "REGRA ABSOLUTA — leia 3×"
   - "NUNCA, JAMAIS, EM HIPÓTESE NENHUMA" + emoji ⛔
   - Concrete examples for igreja/petshop/vinharia showing the right pattern
     (RUN_AGENT as first action, single-action workflow)
   - Section "6.2 Exceções — NARROW e raras" reduces to 2 cases (LGPD
     disclaimer, off-hours filter), explicitly tells the model "if you don't
     have absolute clarity, OMIT"
   - Section "6.4 Auto-checklist" — explicit yes/no questions the model
     should ask itself BEFORE calling add_workflow_action

2. **Validator severity bumped warning → ERROR**
   - WORKFLOW_STATIC_GREETING_BEFORE_AGENT now blocks isValid=false
   - Error message tells the model exactly what to do (REMOVA, mover conteúdo
     pro systemPrompt do agente)

3. **Inline validation hook on finalize_workflow_diagram**
   - executor.dispatchTool now runs workflowValidator IMMEDIATELY when
     finalize_workflow_diagram returns successfully
   - If errors, injects them into the tool result via _validation field
     with explicit instruction "você DEVE corrigir antes de responder"
   - Model sees the errors INSIDE its iteration loop and can call
     update_workflow_action / delete_workflow_action to fix

commits.title: feat(ai-orchestrator): Phase 2.4 — token budget tracker
commits.body:
feat(ai-orchestrator): Phase 2.4 — token budget tracker

Replaces the hardcoded maxIterations cap as the primary execution control.
BudgetTracker accumulates input + output tokens across all provider iterations
and throws BudgetExceededError when total exceeds config.tokenBudget.perTurn.

Wired into executor.executeSingleShot via the onIterationComplete callback:
- After each iteration the LLM provider reports tokens used
- BudgetTracker.add() throws if consumed > limit
- Catch translates to ExecuteResult { stopReason: 'budget_exceeded' }
- isCancelled also returns true after budget exceeded so the loop exits cleanly

Why budget instead of iter cap:
- One iteration can be 10k tokens (large tool result) or 200 tokens (short text)
- Long-horizon plans may need 30+ iterations legitimately
- User-perceived cost is tokens, not iterations
- Provider-level maxIterations stays as a backstop (set to 25)

Default budgets (set by wrappers):
- AI Assistant: 50k tokens per turn
- AI Agent: 30k tokens per turn (configurable via Agent.executionBudgetMs)
- Builder UX (executeMultiTask): unlimited per turn (legacy behavior; tasks
  are themselves bounded). Phase 5 may add per-session budget.

   AI_HUB_AGENT.

commits.title: fix(ai-assistant): teach the model the right WorkflowActionType + recover from JSON-string config
commits.body:
fix(ai-assistant): teach the model the right WorkflowActionType + recover from JSON-string config

Two correlated bugs that broke `add_workflow_action` for RUN_AGENT
(reproduced live in stg today building "Atendimento Restaurante Demo"):

1. Knowledge Base referenced `AI_AGENT` as the workflow action type for
   internal agents. That value does not exist in the `WorkflowActionType`
   enum — only `RUN_AGENT` (internal) and `AI_HUB_AGENT` (legacy external).
   The model learned the wrong value and burned 4–7 iterations sending it
   before falling back to `get_action_schema`. Updated:
   - entries/workflow-building-blocks.md
   - entries/common-patterns.md
   - entries/anti-patterns.md  (also added an explicit "do not use AI_AGENT" callout)
   - core-knowledge.contributor.ts (two entries + the "common errors" list)
   - root CLAUDE.md (Action Types section)

2. The model occasionally serializes `config` as a JSON string instead of
   an object literal (Anthropic tool calling does not enforce JSON Schema
   on the model side). Inside `add_workflow_action` we ran
   `fieldName in input.config`, which throws TypeError on a string operand
   and surfaced as the opaque "Cannot use 'in' operator..." error. Added
   a defensive `coerceConfigObject` helper that auto-parses JSON-string
   configs at the tool entry point; non-strings and unparseable strings
   pass through so the SDK / validator still produces a real error if the
   shape is genuinely wrong.

Coverage: 9 unit tests in tools-executor.config-coercion.spec.ts pin the
parser behavior (object pass-through, JSON string parse, malformed input
unchanged, primitives pass-through) plus one regression assertion that
the KB does not contain positive guidance like `actionType="AI_AGENT"`.

   - entries/anti-patterns.md  (also added an explicit "do not use AI_AGENT" callout)
   - core-knowledge.contributor.ts (two entries + the "common errors" list)
   - root CLAUDE.md (Action Types section)

2. The model occasionally serializes `config` as a JSON string instead of
   an object literal (Anthropic tool calling does not enforce JSON Schema
   on the model side). Inside `add_workflow_action` we ran
   `fieldName in input.config`, which throws TypeError on a string operand
   and surfaced as the opaque "Cannot use 'in' operator..." error. Added
   a defensive `coerceConfigObject` helper that auto-parses JSON-string
   configs at the tool entry point; non-strings and unparseable strings
   pass through so the SDK / validator still produces a real error if the
   shape is genuinely wrong.

parser behavior (object pass-through, JSON string parse, malformed input
unchanged, primitives pass-through) plus one regression assertion that
the KB does not contain positive guidance like `actionType="AI_AGENT"`.

commits.body:
feat(wpp-business): encrypt WppBizAccount.accessToken at rest (Passagem 6)

Bug #1 (CRÍTICA): Meta WABA access token gravado em PLAINTEXT no DB
(prisma/schema.prisma:3834). appSecret já era encriptado, mas o token de
maior valor — full messaging permissions — ficava exposto.

Estratégia: encryption transparente no repo layer + backward-compat para
legacy plaintext rows + migration script idempotente. Services consumidores
(message, template, flow, media, webhook, analytics, campaign,
business-profile, account — 30+ pontos) não mudam: continuam vendo
plaintext porque a (de)cifragem acontece no boundary do repo.

Mudanças:

* utils/crypto.ts
  - Novo isEncryptedFormat(value): detecta o shape iv:authTag:ciphertext
    via 3 segmentos hex com tamanhos exatos (24/32/N). Não colide com
    Meta access tokens que começam com 'EAA' e não têm ':'.
  - Novo decryptSecretIfEncrypted(value): decripta se for o shape;
    senão devolve o valor inalterado. Usado pelas leituras do repo
    durante o rollout — legacy plaintext rows passam transparentes
    até a migration script rodar.

* repositories/account.repository.ts — wrap encrypt-on-write +
  decrypt-on-read em todos os métodos:
    - encryptCreateInput / encryptUpdateInput: encripta accessToken
      antes de mandar pro Prisma. Suporta tanto a forma primitive
      quanto { set: ... } do Prisma update input.
    - decryptAccount / decryptAccounts: aplica decryptSecretIfEncrypted
      em todo accessToken retornado.
    - Cobre create, findById, findByWabaId, findDeletedByWabaId,
      findByWabaIdGlobal, findMany, update, findByWebhookVerifyToken,
      softDelete.

* scripts/encrypt-wpp-biz-access-tokens.ts (novo) — migration one-shot
  idempotente:
    - Itera rows em batches (cursor por id, batchSize 100 default).
    - Para cada row, skip se isEncryptedFormat(accessToken)===true
      (já migrada) ou empty (segurança).
    - Re-encripta plaintext rows com encryptSecret(token).
    - --dry-run flag: conta o que mudaria sem escrever.
    - Erros por row são logados mas não abortam o batch (failed counter).
    - Exit code 1 se houver failures.
    - Operacional: rodar APÓS deploy do código de Passagem 6, ANTES de
      qualquer rotação de master key. Master key rotation é dance
      separado fora de escopo aqui.

Master key: WPP_BUSINESS_CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY em prod ainda é o
placeholder 5555… (memória credential_master_keys_placeholder). Esta
passagem coloca a infra; rotação no SOPS é follow-up separado.

Testes:
- crypto.test.ts: +12 testes para isEncryptedFormat (rounds-trip,
  Meta token rejeitado, separadores errados, lengths errados, non-hex)
  + decryptSecretIfEncrypted (decrypt happy path, plaintext passthrough,
  empty string).
- account.repository.test.ts: reescrito com seção 'at-rest encryption'
  cobrindo (1) encrypt on create, (2) encrypt on update primitive,
  (3) encrypt on update {set:...}, (4) update sem accessToken não toca,
  (5) decrypt on findById, (6) decrypt on findMany, (7) plaintext
  legacy passthrough, (8) null row passthrough. Plus regression suite
  CRUD inteira atualizada para shape encriptada.
- scripts/encrypt-wpp-biz-access-tokens.test.ts (novo): 5 testes
  cobrindo (1) encrypt plaintext + skip already-encrypted, (2) skip
  empty/null rows, (3) dry-run não escreve, (4) idempotência (rodar
  duas vezes não faz nada na 2a), (5) failures não abortam batch.

Total: 45 testes Passagem 6 todos passando + sem regressão nas demais
suítes (validação completa em commit seguinte).

Refs:
- docs/plans/2026-05-06-diagnostico-wpp-business-instabilidade.md (Passagem 6)

commits.title: feat(shared): differentiated auth errors with structured code/details
commits.body:
feat(shared): differentiated auth errors with structured code/details

Sintoma 1 (BB WPP upstream authentication failed) tinha como causa-raiz a
ausência de diferenciação entre tipos de falha de autenticação. Auth
middleware lançava HTTPException sem code, error filter descartava qualquer
info estruturada, e jwtVerify rodava sem clockTolerance — fazendo skew de
relógio rejeitar tokens válidos como expirados.

Mudanças:

* shared/errors/index.ts — novas factories TokenExpiredError,
  TokenInvalidSignatureError, TokenInvalidError, TokenClaimInvalidError,
  TokenTypeMismatchError, MissingAuthorizationError. Top-level code
  permanece UNAUTHORIZED (não inflar enum); sub-tipo vai em details.code
  para painel-cliente-api consumir via bb-wpp-exception.filter.ts.

* shared/errors/http.ts — novo helper httpExceptionFromAppError() anexa
  AppError em HTTPException.cause, preservando estrutura sem quebrar fluxo
  de throw/onError do Hono. Type guard isAppError() para extração defensiva.

* shared/middleware/auth.middleware.ts — verify() catch agora diferencia
  via instanceof joseErrors.JWTExpired / JWSSignatureVerificationFailed /
  JWTClaimValidationFailed / JWSInvalid / JOSEError. Type mismatch e
  missing-auth também passaram a usar AppError. API key error path agora
  preserva o AppError original em vez de descartá-lo.

* shared/middleware/error.middleware.ts — quando HTTPException carrega
  cause:AppError, emite { error, message, statusCode, details } match'ando
  o shape de handleResult. Caso contrário, fallback antigo { message,
  statusCode } preservado para compatibilidade.

* shared/lib/jwt.ts — adiciona clockTolerance:30s em jwtVerify. Absorve
  skew entre painel e BB; sem isso jose rejeita tokens válidos quando
  relógios divergem (intermitência reportada).

Testes:
- auth.middleware.test.ts: 19 testes cobrindo cada error type discriminado
  (TOKEN_EXPIRED, TOKEN_INVALID_SIGNATURE, TOKEN_CLAIM_INVALID, TOKEN_INVALID,
  TOKEN_TYPE_MISMATCH, MISSING_AUTHORIZATION) com asserts em error/message/details
- error.middleware.test.ts: 3 novos testes cobrindo extração de AppError
  via cause (positive, partial-shape, foreign-cause fallback)
- jwt.test.ts: 2 novos testes verificando clockTolerance — token expirado
  10s passa, token expirado 60s falha

Total: 59 testes (up from existentes), todos passando.

Refs:
- docs/plans/2026-05-06-diagnostico-wpp-business-instabilidade.md (Parte 3,
  Passagem 2)
- §A, §B do diagnóstico
