Bug pré-existente em main descoberto durante validação live em stg da
PR #130: cloud-api.client:getPhoneNumberInfo pedia o campo
'whatsapp_business_account' que Meta Graph API v25.0+ DEPRECOU para
tokens de system user. Resultado: POST /devices/standalone sempre
retornava 400 com '(#100) Tried accessing nonexisting field'.

Foi a Passagem 3 (typed Meta errors) que tornou esse bug visível —
antes virava INTERNAL 500 opaco.

Mudanças:

* types/index.ts createDeviceStandaloneSchema
  - Novo campo opcional 'wabaId' que o painel pode passar (já tem do
    Embedded Signup). Documentado o motivo no JSDoc.

* cloud-api.client.ts getPhoneNumberInfo
  - Removido 'whatsapp_business_account' do field selection — Meta v25.0+
    rejeita o field. Fields restantes (display_phone_number,
    verified_name, status) continuam funcionando.
  - Return wabaId='' sempre. Comentário explicando que callers de Mode B
    devem obter wabaId de outro lugar.

* services/account.service.ts createStandaloneDevice
  - const wabaId = input.wabaId || phoneInfo.wabaId
    Prefere input do painel; mantém fallback para compat com clientes
    legados (que vão receber erro tipado já que phoneInfo.wabaId é
    sempre vazio agora).
  - Se nenhum wabaId resolveu, retorna erro estruturado:
    { code:'BAD_REQUEST', details:{code:'META_WABA_ID_REQUIRED',phoneNumberId} }
  - Restante do flow usa wabaId resolvido (input ou fallback).

Testes:
- 2 novos testes em createStandaloneDevice describe:
  - 'uses input.wabaId when provided (overrides phoneInfo.wabaId)' —
    valida que getWabaInfo + accountRepo.create recebem o input
  - 'returns META_WABA_ID_REQUIRED when neither present' — reproduz
    Meta v25.0 case com phoneInfo.wabaId='' sem input

Migração painel-cliente-api:

commits.title: feat(wpp-business): typed Meta API errors + token validation
commits.body:
feat(wpp-business): typed Meta API errors + token validation

Sintomas 1 & 2 tinham raiz comum: 401/403 da Meta virava InternalError genérico
(cloud-api.client.ts:642-647) e debugToken().scopes era capturado mas nunca
validado (account.service.ts:217,261). Painel só recebia 500 'Cloud API
request failed: ...' onde o usuário precisava ver 'reautentique-se' ou
'permissões insuficientes'.

Mudanças:

* providers/cloud-api/cloud-api-errors.ts (novo)
  - CloudApiError class carrega envelope da Meta (httpStatus, metaCode,
    metaSubcode, metaType, metaMessage, fbtrace_id) parseado de doRequest.
  - parseCloudApiError(response) extrai o JSON de erro da Meta tolerante
    a payloads não-JSON (fallback para texto raw).
  - appErrorFromCloudApi(error) mapeia para AppError tipado por
    code/subcode da Meta:
      * code 190 + subcode 463 → META_TOKEN_EXPIRED (401, UNAUTHORIZED)
      * code 190 + subcode 460/467/458 → META_TOKEN_REVOKED (401)
      * code 190 (sem subcode) → META_TOKEN_INVALID (401)
      * HTTP 401 (sem code 190) → META_TOKEN_INVALID
      * HTTP 403 / code 200 / code 10 → META_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE (403, FORBIDDEN)
      * HTTP 429 / codes 4,17,32,80004 → META_RATE_LIMIT (429, INTERNAL)
      * resto → META_API_ERROR (status original, INTERNAL — mantém retry semantics)
  - InsufficientScopeError + InvalidTokenError factories standalone para uso
    em validações pré-Graph (ver account.service abaixo).

* providers/cloud-api/cloud-api.client.ts
  - doRequest agora joga CloudApiError (via parseCloudApiError) em vez de
    'throw new Error'.
  - requestWithRetry mapeia CloudApiError via appErrorFromCloudApi; non-HTTP
    errors caem no path legado InternalError para preservar shape.
  - isRetryable agora bloqueia retry de META_RATE_LIMIT (top-level INTERNAL
    cairia no retry mas hammerar mais não ajuda — Meta diz para back off).

* services/account.service.ts
  - Novo helper validateDebugTokenInfo() chamado em resolveWppBizAppId() e
    createStandaloneDevice() logo após client.debugToken().
  - Valida info.isValid → InvalidTokenError; info.scopes inclui
    'whatsapp_business_management' → InsufficientScopeError.
  - Sintoma 2 (import device falha tarde): agora token sem scope correto
    falha imediato com erro estruturado (FORBIDDEN + META_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE
    + presentScopes) antes de getPhoneNumberInfo retornar BAD_REQUEST opaco.

Testes:
- cloud-api.client.test.ts: 7 novos testes cobrindo cada branch do mapper
  (token expirado/revogado/inválido, scope insuficiente, rate limit HTTP
  429, rate limit por código 80004, fallback genérico INTERNAL, body
  não-JSON). 1 teste antigo atualizado (asserção INTERNAL → UNAUTHORIZED).
- account.service.test.ts: 4 novos testes (META_TOKEN_INVALID + scope
  insuficiente para create() e createStandaloneDevice()). Mocks existentes
  com scopes:[] atualizados para incluir whatsapp_business_management.

Total: 164 testes passando (1 falha pré-existente em 'appSecret encryption'
não relacionada a este change — confirmado via stash).

Refs:
- docs/plans/2026-05-06-diagnostico-wpp-business-instabilidade.md (Passagem 3)
- §C, §D do diagnóstico

commits.body:
feat(painel): AddDeviceWizard 3-step linear flow (Wave D)

Substitui a UX paralela de StandaloneDeviceModal + ImportDeviceModal por
um wizard linear unificado que vira o CTA primário em /whatsapp/devices.
Modais legados ficam como fallback 'avançado' (Importar conta existente +
Avançado).

Wizard 3 passos:
  1. Credenciais Meta — accessToken + phoneNumberId + wabaId (cada campo
     com helper text apontando pra Meta Business). Validação client-side
     numérica em phoneNumberId/wabaId.
  2. Detalhes do device — nome opcional + descrição opcional. Mostra
     summary das credenciais validadas.
  3. Resultado — auto-submete ao entrar; renderiza spinner/success/error.
     Erros são apresentados via presentBbError (Wave A) com retry → step 1.
     APP_NOT_REGISTERED dispara AppSecretInlinePrompt (Wave C); ao cadastrar
     o app, retentativa do submit ocorre transparentemente.

Race condition resolvida via useRef justRegisteredRef: AppSecretInlinePrompt
chama onClose após onRegistered, e o wizard precisa preservar o submission
success (vs reset pra step 1 em caso de cancel do user).

Mudanças:

* components/AddDeviceWizard.tsx (NOVO 380 linhas) — componente principal
  com Step1Form/Step2Details/Step3Result/Step3Footer subcomponents.
* components/AddDeviceWizard.test.tsx (NOVO 200 linhas) — 8 cenários
  cobrindo render, validação Step 1, transições, retry após erro,
  APP_NOT_REGISTERED → AppSecretInlinePrompt → retentativa transparente.
* pages/WhatsAppDevices.tsx — `wizardModal` disclosure novo, CTA primário
  'Adicionar Device WhatsApp' aponta pro wizard. 'Importar conta existente'
  + 'Avançado' viraram secondary buttons (variant ghost).

  * C3-delegate.sh — create NS records in DO for subzone delegation
  * D-monitor.sh — continuous multi-resolver health check
  * D1-smoke-test.sh — HTTPS smoke test for service FQDNs

- Rollback drill: zero downtime, 10min recovery

Move the NS-record management away from a hard-wired PowerDNS REST client
onto the new DnsBackend abstraction. The orchestrator and provisioner now
import from ./backends/ns-helpers, which routes through getDnsBackend()
— so PowerDNS, DigitalOcean, and the mock backend are all interchangeable

re-exports from ns-helpers; the obsolete resolvePdnsIp() now returns ""

Cluster lifecycle stays in the in-memory store (BeaconCluster) — the
backend is only consulted for the DNS write side. Herald events are

commits.title: feat(deploy): SSE stream endpoint for live job progress
commits.body:
feat(deploy): SSE stream endpoint for live job progress

GET /api/deploy/jobs/:id/stream
  - Returns text/event-stream; emits a `job.snapshot` up-front, then
    forwards every JobEvent for the job (phase.started/completed/failed,
    log.line, job.completed/failed/cancelled).
  - Heartbeat comment every 15s so proxies + curl don't drop the conn.
  - Auto-closes the stream once the job reaches a terminal status, and
    on `request.signal.abort()` (client disconnect).
  - Auth: session cookie OR `?token=…` query param (browser EventSource
    can't set custom headers; query token is verified the same way as
    the cookie payload via verifySessionToken).
  - Adds /api/deploy/ to the middleware PUBLIC_API_PATHS list so the
    bearer-token gate doesn't block the route — auth is enforced inside
    the handler.

commits.title: feat(db): generate initial migration
commits.body:
feat(db): generate initial migration

drizzle-kit generated 0000_initial.sql for the 21 tables across
aegis/audit/beacon/marketing/platform schemas (DDL + indexes + FKs +
enum types).

audit_events is hand-patched to add PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)
since drizzle-kit doesn't model partitioning. Postgres requires a
plain sequence (not bigserial) on the partitioned parent, so 'seq'
is rewritten as bigint DEFAULT nextval(…). Two seed partitions are
created (2026-05, 2026-06) plus a DEFAULT partition catch-all so
writes outside the seeded range can never silently fail before the
rotation job catches up.

Subsequent monthly partitions are created by a future cron/pg_cron
job — see follow-up issue.

The drizzle schema columns/PK match the SQL 1:1 so future
'drizzle-kit generate' diffs stay empty.

Includes meta/_journal.json + meta/0000_snapshot.json so other devs
can run db:migrate without regenerating.

commits.title: feat(builder-vm): add destroy.sh with strict confirmation gates
commits.body:
feat(builder-vm): add destroy.sh with strict confirmation gates

Last-resort emergency lever. STOPS and DESTROYS the configured VMID. The
script is gated by FIVE independent confirmations:

  1. --i-know-what-im-doing flag must be passed (no flag => die)
  2. .env BUILDER_VMID must exist on this node (qm status check)
  3. The VM's name (qm config | grep name:) must equal BUILDER_HOSTNAME
     (mismatch => refuse — protects against typos pointing at unrelated VMs)
  4. The VM must contain /etc/developy/builder-vm.marker with the string
     'managed-by: scripts/bootstrap/builder-vm/provision.sh'. This is
     written by the cloud-init template, so only VMs created by this repo
     can pass. Bypassable only via BUILDER_SKIP_MARKER_CHECK=1 (with a
     loud warning).
  5. Interactive prompt: must type 'DESTROY <vmid>' verbatim.

Even with all gates passed, dry-run is still the default; --apply must be
explicit. The first thing the script prints (after arg parsing) is a
multi-line ASCII banner reminding the operator this is irreversible
without a PBS / ZFS snapshot.

Before destruction:
  - Lists qm listsnapshot output for the VMID
  - Lists PBS backups (best-effort via proxmox-backup-client or pvesm)

After qm destroy (with --purge --destroy-unreferenced-disks 1), it also
removes the cloud-init snippet file in /var/lib/vz/snippets — but ONLY the
one tagged with this VMID (never a wildcard).

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly.

Adds the Aegis schema as the first concrete drizzle module:

- aegis_orgs        UUID PK, slug-unique, jsonb settings, tier enum

- aegis_teams       hierarchical via parent_team_id, slug unique per org

- aegis_ledger      bigserial high-cardinality auth-event log
                    (login attempts etc) — Herald is for everything else

Indexes target the hottest read paths: org+slug, org+user, token lookup.

Zod schemas (insert/select) generated via drizzle-zod for each table,
plus inferred types (Org, NewOrg, Team, ...) re-exported from the
module. Fits the existing zod 3.25 pin in apps/web.

  - runcmd: enable docker, add deploy-bot to docker group, install pnpm
    via corepack, install bun for deploy-bot user, install trivy via the
    official apt repo (non-fatal — install-tooling.sh retries)

feat(db/beacon): add PowerDNS-compatible schema (domains, records, supermasters, etc)

Mirrors the existing handwritten schema at
src/lib/server/beacon/schema.pgsql.sql in drizzle so the platform
can drive PowerDNS through the same client.

Tables follow the gpgsql backend spec exactly so pdns-auth can be
pointed at the same database with launch=gpgsql:

  domains          (id, name unique, master, last_check, type,
                    notified_serial, account, options, catalog)
  records          (id, domain_id, name, type, content, ttl, prio,
                    disabled, ordername, auth) + name + (name,type) +
                    domain_id indexes that PowerDNS expects
  supermasters     (ip INET, nameserver, account) — composite PK
                    via a custom inet type since drizzle-orm has no
                    first-class inet
  comments         (id, domain_id, name, type, modified_at, account,
                    comment)
  domainmetadata   (id, domain_id FK CASCADE, kind, content)
  cryptokeys       (id, domain_id FK CASCADE, flags, active,
                    published, content)
  tsigkeys         (id, name, algorithm, secret) UNIQUE(name, algorithm)

Naming and types are dictated by PowerDNS; do not refactor without
checking pdns-auth source. drizzle-zod schemas + inferred types
(Domain, NewDomain, Record, …) are exported for the rest of Beacon.

Ref: https://doc.powerdns.com/authoritative/backends/generic-postgresql.html

commits.title: feat(builder-vm): add provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)
commits.body:
feat(builder-vm): add provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)

The end-to-end orchestrator. Default mode is --dry-run: every qm/ssh/scp
invocation is prefixed with WOULD: and never executed. --apply requires
typing APPLY at an interactive prompt.

Steps:
  1. Run preflight.sh (read-only validation)
  2. Confirm: type APPLY (anything else aborts)
  3. Render cloud-init.yaml.tpl with awk substitution into a mktemp file
  4. cp the rendered snippet to /var/lib/vz/snippets/builder-cloudinit-<vmid>.yaml
  5. qm create — minimal VM stub with virtio-scsi, serial console, agent on
  6. qm importdisk — bring the cloud template into BUILDER_STORAGE
  7. qm set — wire scsi0 + boot order + cloudinit drive + cicustom + ipconfig
  8. qm resize scsi0 to BUILDER_DISK_GB
  9. qm start
 10. Wait up to BUILDER_SSH_TIMEOUT for qemu-guest-agent to expose an IP,
     then up to 60s for SSH (deploy-bot key-based)
 11. SCP + run zfs-datasets.sh inside the VM
 12. SCP + run install-tooling.sh inside the VM
 13. Run validate.sh from the operator host
 14. Print success summary + IP + concrete next steps

On failure: NEVER auto-destroys the VM. Prints the error, leaves the VM
running for inspection, and exits non-zero. Operator decides whether to
keep, fix, or destroy (via destroy.sh).

Logging: in --apply mode, all stdout/stderr is tee'd to
builder-vm-provision-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSZ.log in cwd via re-exec.

The script does NOT call the Proxmox HTTP API — it relies on local qm
(and so must run on the Proxmox node). This is the safest path for a
bootstrap that should never be executed by an automation it doesn't fully
trust.

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly. Dry-run output captured in PR description.

commits.body:
feat(db/audit): add Herald schema (events, partitioned by month)

Adds the Herald audit log as an append-only, monthly-partitioned table.

Drizzle definition (audit_events):
  seq          bigserial
  tenant_id    text (NULL = platform-wide)
  source       varchar(32) — module producing the event
  type         varchar(96) — 'iam.role.granted', 'forge.vm.start', …
  severity     enum info/notice/warn/error/critical
  actor        jsonb  — { id, kind, ip, user_agent, … }
  resource     jsonb  — { kind, id, name, parent, … }
  action       varchar(32)
  outcome      enum allow/deny/success/failure/conditional
  before       jsonb (nullable)
  after        jsonb (nullable)
  context      jsonb — request_id, trace_id, …
  created_at   timestamptz — partition key

Composite PK (seq, created_at) so the table can be declared
PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at) — Postgres requires the partition
key to be part of the PK on partitioned tables. The PARTITION BY
clause + first monthly partition are stitched into the generated
migration in the next commit (drizzle-kit doesn't model partitioning
natively).

Indexes target audit-explorer query shapes: by tenant+time, by type+time,
by source+time, by outcome+time. All include created_at as the second
column so they live happily inside per-partition btrees post-migration.

commits.body:
feat(web): multi-stage Dockerfile with Next.js standalone runtime

Replaces the previous single-stage Dockerfile with a proper deps/builder/
runner pipeline tuned for the developy.cloud monorepo build cadence
(plans/deploy-strategy.md §6.2).

deps stage:
  - corepack-pinned pnpm 9.15.9 (matches root package.json packageManager)
  - copies ALL workspace package.json files so the lockfile resolves
    cleanly under --frozen-lockfile
  - mounts a BuildKit cache at /root/.local/share/pnpm/store so the pnpm
    content-addressable store survives across rebuilds
  - alpine + libc6-compat for native deps (OTel, sharp, etc.)

builder stage:
  - reuses node_modules from deps via COPY --from
  - builds @proxmox-manager/core then @sidefuel/platform (dependency
    order — both must exist as dist/ before next build runs)
  - then `next build` (with output: standalone), telemetry off

runner stage:
  - node:22-alpine, no pnpm, no source code — only the standalone bundle
    + .next/static
  - non-root nextjs:1001 user
  - tini as PID 1 for proper SIGTERM forwarding (Next graceful shutdown)
  - HEALTHCHECK probes /api/health via 127.0.0.1 (alpine resolves
    "localhost" via IPv6 first, but Next binds to 0.0.0.0 IPv4 only;
    using the literal IP avoids a dual-stack mismatch)
  - HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 so the standalone server binds outside the loopback

Build is from the repo root: `docker build -f apps/web/Dockerfile .`.

Adds apps/web/Dockerfile.dockerignore (BuildKit picks up the
<dockerfile>.dockerignore convention automatically when -f targets this
Dockerfile). Excludes:
  - encrypted/per-host store files (.connections.json, .iam-store.json,
    .audit-store.json, all .*-store.json) — must NEVER ship in an image
  - node_modules / .next / .turbo / dist / coverage (rebuilt fresh)
  - tests, e2e, playwright artifacts (not needed at runtime)
  - .env / .env.local (secrets)
  - docs/, plans/, *.md (context bloat)

Local verification on this worktree:
  - cold build: ~85s wall (deps install + core/platform build + next
    build); pnpm install ~5s thanks to the cache mount
  - source-only rebuild (after touching apps/web/src/app/page.tsx):

  - final image: 261 MB (developy-web:test)

  - GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health returns

commits.body:
feat(beacon): add PowerDNS backend implementation (Postgres-backed)

Implements DnsBackend by writing directly to PowerDNS' gpgsql tables —
the same schema PowerDNS reads on every query (see schema.pgsql.sql).
Creates an SOA record automatically on createDomain so PowerDNS treats
the zone as authoritative; bumps notified_serial + the SOA record
serial on every mutation so secondaries notice the change.

Surfaces DNSSEC and TSIG capabilities (cryptokeys / tsigkeys tables
read+write) and supports a notifyReload hook for plugging in an
out-of-band 'pdns_control reload <zone>' once we have an SSH/HTTP
channel. Today notifyReload defaults to a no-op; PowerDNS will pick up
writes at the next query subject to its in-process record cache (60s
default).

The pg driver is injected via an SqlPool interface so tests can use a
hand-rolled mock without pulling pg-mem in as a dependency.

commits.title: feat(ship): orchestrator state machine, phases, target compositions
commits.body:
feat(ship): orchestrator state machine, phases, target compositions

Adds the deploy state machine and per-phase logic.

Phases (scripts/ship/phases/):
  - preflight    git clean/branch/pushed; Aegis policy stub
  - build        SSH builder VM: git checkout, pnpm install/build/test,
                 docker buildx + push, trivy scan; skipped if --image given
  - migrate      mgmt API dry-run + apply; renders schema diff to log;
                 self-skips for marketing/beacon
  - deploy       three flavors picked by strategy:
                   rolling   — single startDeploy via mgmt API
                   canary:N  — deploy cohort, verify, then promote to 100
                   blue-green— mgmt API does the swap atomically
                 every variant snapshots previousSha for rollback
  - verify       Pulse baseline check (error_rate < +2pp, p95 < 1.5x)
  - finalize     tag :env-current, Herald success event, Discord webhook
  - rollback     restores previousSha via mgmt API + Herald high event

Orchestrator (ship.ts):
  - composes phases per target + strategy
  - persists DeployJob to deploy log after each phase (atomic rename)
  - honors --skip and per-phase shouldRun()
  - auto-rollback when deploy/verify/finalize fail (unless --no-rollback)
                 — preflight/build failures don't trigger rollback (no
                 production impact yet)
  - explicit subcommand: 'bun ship rollback <env> <target> --to=<sha>|
    --previous' walks the deploy log for --previous

Target compositions (targets/):
  web, marketing, atlas, spark, tide, beacon — each defines its phase
  list. 'all' is a topo-ordered list fanned out by index.ts (one
  DeployJob per target, abort on first failure).

State (state/deploy-log.ts):
  Persists ~/.developy/deploys/<id>.json (or tmpdir in tests via
  createDeployLogStore(dir)). Atomic write via tmp + rename.

Entrypoint (index.ts):
  Bun shebang, import.meta.main guard, mock drivers by default.
  DEVELOPY_REAL_INFRA_ENABLED=1 currently throws — real impls are next PR.

commits.title: fix(painel-cliente): exclude /auth/login and /auth/register from 401 interceptor
commits.body:
fix(painel-cliente): exclude /auth/login and /auth/register from 401 interceptor

Login errors (invalid credentials, etc.) were swallowed by the global 401
interceptor in api.ts. When refreshToken was null (user not logged in yet),
the interceptor called clearAuth() + window.location.href='/login' BEFORE
the <Login> component could render its <Alert>. UX appeared as a silent
page reload — the component's setError() never reached the DOM.

The Login component already handles errors correctly (try/catch + setError +
<Alert role="alert">). Excluding /auth/login and /auth/register from the
interceptor's redirect logic lets components own their own error UX, mirroring
how /auth/refresh is already handled.

Wave A of docs/plans/2026-05-07-painel-auth-stale-perms-and-login-error-ux.md.
Bug 2 (stale permissions until logout+login) is addressed in Waves B+C.

## Tests

- Unit (vitest): 3 new cases in api.interceptor.test.ts under 'security:
  excluded endpoints bypass refresh' — covers /auth/login, /auth/register,
  and the regression case where refreshToken is null. 27/27 passing.
- E2E (Playwright): new tests/painel-cliente/login-error-ux.spec.ts with
  3 cases — Alert visible without reload, message text non-generic, no
  collateral clearAuth on existing localStorage.
- E2E (existing): strengthened iam-login.spec.ts:'should show error for
  invalid credentials' which previously counted alerts but never asserted

commits.title: fix(devices-bundle): hotfix CORS — Cache-Control no response, not request
commits.body:
fix(devices-bundle): hotfix CORS — Cache-Control no response, not request

Production smoke caught it: clicking "Exportar bundle" surfaces
"Network Error" with no HTTP status. Root cause: the frontend was
sending `Cache-Control: no-store` on the *request*, which is not in
CORS-safelisted request-headers (Accept, Accept-Language,
Content-Language, Content-Type) and so triggers a preflight OPTIONS.
The API's `enableCors({ allowedHeaders: [Content-Type, Authorization,
X-Requested-With, Accept, X-API-Key] })` doesn't list `Cache-Control`,
so the preflight is rejected and the browser blocks the POST entirely.
Axios sees no response and surfaces a generic "Network Error".

The intent of `no-store` was always to keep the plaintext payload
(carrying Meta accessToken + App Secret in the milliseconds between
server fetch and client-side encrypt) off intermediaries and disk
caches. That belongs on the *response*, not the request.

- painel-cliente: drop the `Cache-Control` header from
  exportBundleSingle + exportBundleMany requests.
- painel-cliente-api: add `@Header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')` and
  `@Header('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff')` to all three bundle
  endpoints (single export, many export, import).

Build verified: vite + tsc -p tsconfig.build.json both green.

commits.body:
docs(plans): painel auth — stale perms + login error UX 3-wave fix

Two correlated bugs share one architectural root: the painel treats tokens
and user identity as separate state, but IAM emits them atomically in the JWT.

- Bug 1: invalid login credentials trigger the global 401 interceptor before
  the Login component can render the error Alert (refreshToken is null,
  interceptor calls window.location.href='/login' synchronously).
- Bug 2: silent token refresh updates token strings only, leaving
  user.permissions stale in Zustand store. Endpoints like /whatsapp-devices
  return 403 'Insufficient permissions' until manual logout+login.

3 waves:
- A: exclude /auth/login + /auth/register from interceptor (tiny)
- B: /auth/refresh re-hydrates user with fresh perms via IAM getUser()
- C: App.tsx boot-time revalidation if JWT < 30min remaining

Plan is self-contained for fresh-context execution: snippets antes/depois,
12 unit tests + 4 E2E tests, copy-pasteable commands per wave, rollback tags.

fix(painel-cliente): explicit Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> for WebCrypto

the more general <ArrayBufferLike> which would allow SharedArrayBuffer).
The decrypt site choked on `iv` + `ciphertext` from fromBase64 because
their inferred generic was ArrayBufferLike.

Fix: declare fromBase64 return as Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> with a single
cast at the construction site (length-overload of Uint8Array creates an
ArrayBuffer-backed view); widen deriveKey's salt param to BufferSource
since that's what crypto.subtle.deriveKey actually wants.

Verified end-to-end via tsx roundtrip: encrypt → decrypt(correct) →
equal payload, decrypt(wrong) → BundleAuthTagError. Vite build green.

commits.title: docs(plans): painel auth — stale perms + login error UX 3-wave fix
commits.body:
docs(plans): painel auth — stale perms + login error UX 3-wave fix

Two correlated bugs share one architectural root: the painel treats tokens
and user identity as separate state, but IAM emits them atomically in the JWT.

- Bug 1: invalid login credentials trigger the global 401 interceptor before
  the Login component can render the error Alert (refreshToken is null,
  interceptor calls window.location.href='/login' synchronously).
- Bug 2: silent token refresh updates token strings only, leaving
  user.permissions stale in Zustand store. Endpoints like /whatsapp-devices
  return 403 'Insufficient permissions' until manual logout+login.

3 waves:
- A: exclude /auth/login + /auth/register from interceptor (tiny)
- B: /auth/refresh re-hydrates user with fresh perms via IAM getUser()
- C: App.tsx boot-time revalidation if JWT < 30min remaining

Plan is self-contained for fresh-context execution: snippets antes/depois,
12 unit tests + 4 E2E tests, copy-pasteable commands per wave, rollback tags.

feat(beacon): add beaconMetaAdapter (maps BeaconStoreData → drizzle ops)

Implements PostgresBackendAdapter<BeaconStoreData> for the StoreBackend
SPI. Only handles the collections beacon_meta owns:

  - clusters → beacon_meta_clusters  (full CRUD via drizzle)
  - nodes    → beacon_meta_nodes     (full CRUD via drizzle, FK CASCADE
                                       from cluster deletion)

Zones and records are intentionally no-ops here — they live in
PowerDNS's own tables and are read through the DnsBackend (see PR #15).
loadAll() returns empty arrays for them; replaceAll/upsertOne/deleteOne
skip the collection. The shape stays valid so BeaconStoreData consumers
don't have to special-case anything.

Mappers are explicit (clusterToRow/rowToCluster, nodeToRow/rowToNode)
so future schema drift surfaces as a type error at compile time. The
adapter is constructed lazily — getDb() is only called once
STORE_BACKEND=postgres routes here.

feat(atlas): adopt StoreBackend SPI + postgres adapter (Wave 2 Tier 3)

Migrates the Atlas meta store (.atlas-store.json) from encrypted JSON to
Postgres behind the StoreBackend SPI. Mirrors Beacon (PR #21), Aegis
(PR #24), Marketing (PR #23) shape — same lazy-singleton, env-flip
toggle, zero-regression JSON-mode default.

Schema (apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/atlas.ts):
- atlas_clusters            text PK, jsonb lxc_ids/tags, pgEnum
                            engine/size/status/ha_mode
- atlas_credentials         text PK, FK cluster_id ON DELETE CASCADE,
                            partial-index-friendly composite on
                            (cluster_id, revoked_at)
- atlas_idempotency_records request_id PK, 24h TTL (enforced at app),
                            indexes on expires_at + resource_id

Migration (0004_create_atlas_meta_tables.sql):
- All CREATE TABLE — no ALTER on incoming-FK columns, so the FK
  ordering bug from PR #27 doesn't apply.
- Hand-written via pnpm db:new (new workflow, not drizzle-kit generate).

Adapter (apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/postgres-adapter.ts):
- Lossless row↔domain mapping for all three collections.
- replaceAll uses a transaction; child-table deletes happen first to
  match the marketing/beacon pattern.
- upsertOne handles `idempotencyRecords` by routing the SPI id to
  request_id (the natural PK for that collection).

Store rewrite (apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/store.ts):
- Thin wrappers over backend.load/saveEntity/deleteEntity.
- Custom getItemId understands both `id` (clusters/credentials) and
  `requestId` (idempotency) for JSON-mode saveEntity.
- saveIdempotencyRecord preserves the expired-record sweep at the
  store layer so both backends behave identically.
- deleteCluster manually cascades credentials in JSON mode; Postgres
  mode also has FK CASCADE as defence-in-depth.
- revokeCredential reads → mutates → saveEntity (avoids partial
  upsert losing other columns).

Migrate-stores mapper (scripts/migrate-stores/modules/atlas.ts):
- Three collections mapped with conflictTargets for idempotent re-runs.
- `lxcIds`/`tags` jsonb columns serialized via JSON.stringify and
  parsed back through a tolerant helper that accepts both string and
  array shapes (drizzle returns objects, MemoryDriver compares strings).
- IdempotencyRecord aliases requestId as non-enumerable request_id so
  the runner's dedupe step sees a unique key without polluting the
  recovered JSON shape (same trick audit uses for external_id).

Tests added: 23 (8 mapper round-trip + 15 store regression).
- Mapper test covers row count parity, optional-field handling, jsonb
  array round-trip, idempotency, empty-store edge case.
- Store regression test covers JSON-mode CRUD + filter + cascade +
  revokeCredential + saveIdempotencyRecord sweep + env-flip routing.

Also updated tests/atlas/01-store.integration.test.ts to call
resetAtlasStoreBackendForTesting() around its ATLAS_STORE_PATH env
swaps — required because the lazy singleton caches the resolved path
on first call.

not touch any sibling _meta module (spark/tide/nexus/flux/mesh own

commits.body:
feat(migrate-stores): runner state machine + types + drivers

Adds the orchestrator that walks a ModuleMigrator's collections,
applies toRow/fromRow, and pushes rows through a PostgresDriver
interface. The runner is module-agnostic — all schema knowledge lives
in the mappers under modules/.

Drivers:
  - JsonSource: reads/writes the encrypted .{m}-store.json file
    (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2 salt matches @proxmox-manager/core byte-for-byte)
  - MemoryDriver: in-memory test fake with ON CONFLICT semantics
  - PostgresJsDriver: postgres-js-backed prod driver; lazy-imports
    the `postgres` package so the CLI loads cleanly in workspaces
    that don't depend on apps/web

Direction-aware behaviour:
  - json-to-postgres: read JSON, map, insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  - postgres-to-json: read tables, map back, merge into the existing
    JSON store (de-dup on conflict targets so it stays idempotent)

Dry-run path is fully exercised — reads source, runs every mapper,
logs counts + sample row — but skips destination mutation AND
checkpoint persistence so a dry-run never poisons a follow-up apply.

commits.title: fix(wave2): post-cutover fixes — root postgres dep + 0003 FK ordering
commits.body:
fix(wave2): post-cutover fixes — root postgres dep + 0003 FK ordering

Two issues discovered during 2026-05-11 prod cutover:

## 1. `postgres` package missing from root deps
`scripts/migrate-stores/drivers/postgres-driver.ts` lazy-imports `postgres`
but the package was only declared in `apps/web/package.json`. The CLI runs
from repo root via `bun scripts/migrate-stores/index.ts` and Bun's resolver
couldn't find the package there. Beacon cutover apparently worked because a
prior install left a stale copy. Fix: declare `postgres@^3.4.9` as a root
dependency so frozen-lockfile deploys keep it.

## 2. Migration 0003 ALTER COLUMN order incompatible with real Postgres
The aegis follow-up agent's drizzle-kit-generated 0003 alters columns in
declaration order. Postgres rejects `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE` on a
column that has an FK to a column whose type would mismatch — the alter
must drop the FK first. pg-mem in tests doesn't enforce this so the
agent's tests passed.

This caused 0003 to partially apply on prod (some text alters succeeded,
others failed mid-file, FK adds at end failed too). Prod was manually
repaired via explicit DDL (drop 7 FKs → alter all uuid→text → re-add FKs)
and 0003 was marked applied with hash `2b4a36ed1e043...`.

Fix: rewrite 0003_minor_saracen.sql to drop all referencing FKs first,
alter both sides of each relation, then re-ADD the FKs. Same end state,
order-of-operations correct for real Postgres.

* feat(ship): orchestrator state machine, phases, target compositions

Adds the deploy state machine and per-phase logic.

Phases (scripts/ship/phases/):
  - preflight    git clean/branch/pushed; Aegis policy stub
  - build        SSH builder VM: git checkout, pnpm install/build/test,
                 docker buildx + push, trivy scan; skipped if --image given
  - migrate      mgmt API dry-run + apply; renders schema diff to log;
                 self-skips for marketing/beacon
  - deploy       three flavors picked by strategy:
                   rolling   — single startDeploy via mgmt API
                   canary:N  — deploy cohort, verify, then promote to 100
                   blue-green— mgmt API does the swap atomically
                 every variant snapshots previousSha for rollback
  - verify       Pulse baseline check (error_rate < +2pp, p95 < 1.5x)
  - finalize     tag :env-current, Herald success event, Discord webhook
  - rollback     restores previousSha via mgmt API + Herald high event

Orchestrator (ship.ts):
  - composes phases per target + strategy
  - persists DeployJob to deploy log after each phase (atomic rename)
  - honors --skip and per-phase shouldRun()
  - auto-rollback when deploy/verify/finalize fail (unless --no-rollback)
                 — preflight/build failures don't trigger rollback (no
                 production impact yet)
  - explicit subcommand: 'bun ship rollback <env> <target> --to=<sha>|
    --previous' walks the deploy log for --previous

Target compositions (targets/):
  web, marketing, atlas, spark, tide, beacon — each defines its phase
  list. 'all' is a topo-ordered list fanned out by index.ts (one
  DeployJob per target, abort on first failure).

State (state/deploy-log.ts):
  Persists ~/.developy/deploys/<id>.json (or tmpdir in tests via
  createDeployLogStore(dir)). Atomic write via tmp + rename.

Entrypoint (index.ts):
  Bun shebang, import.meta.main guard, mock drivers by default.
  DEVELOPY_REAL_INFRA_ENABLED=1 currently throws — real impls are next PR.

  docker      — docker run --rm hello-world succeeds

* feat(builder-vm): add provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)

The end-to-end orchestrator. Default mode is --dry-run: every qm/ssh/scp
invocation is prefixed with WOULD: and never executed. --apply requires
typing APPLY at an interactive prompt.

Steps:
  1. Run preflight.sh (read-only validation)
  2. Confirm: type APPLY (anything else aborts)
  3. Render cloud-init.yaml.tpl with awk substitution into a mktemp file
  4. cp the rendered snippet to /var/lib/vz/snippets/builder-cloudinit-<vmid>.yaml
  5. qm create — minimal VM stub with virtio-scsi, serial console, agent on
  6. qm importdisk — bring the cloud template into BUILDER_STORAGE
  7. qm set — wire scsi0 + boot order + cloudinit drive + cicustom + ipconfig
  8. qm resize scsi0 to BUILDER_DISK_GB
  9. qm start
 10. Wait up to BUILDER_SSH_TIMEOUT for qemu-guest-agent to expose an IP,
     then up to 60s for SSH (deploy-bot key-based)
 11. SCP + run zfs-datasets.sh inside the VM
 12. SCP + run install-tooling.sh inside the VM
 13. Run validate.sh from the operator host
 14. Print success summary + IP + concrete next steps

On failure: NEVER auto-destroys the VM. Prints the error, leaves the VM
running for inspection, and exits non-zero. Operator decides whether to
keep, fix, or destroy (via destroy.sh).

Logging: in --apply mode, all stdout/stderr is tee'd to
builder-vm-provision-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSZ.log in cwd via re-exec.

The script does NOT call the Proxmox HTTP API — it relies on local qm
(and so must run on the Proxmox node). This is the safest path for a
bootstrap that should never be executed by an automation it doesn't fully
trust.

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly. Dry-run output captured in PR description.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(builder-vm): add destroy.sh with strict confirmation gates

Last-resort emergency lever. STOPS and DESTROYS the configured VMID. The
script is gated by FIVE independent confirmations:

  1. --i-know-what-im-doing flag must be passed (no flag => die)
  2. .env BUILDER_VMID must exist on this node (qm status check)
  3. The VM's name (qm config | grep name:) must equal BUILDER_HOSTNAME
     (mismatch => refuse — protects against typos pointing at unrelated VMs)
  4. The VM must contain /etc/developy/builder-vm.marker with the string
     'managed-by: scripts/bootstrap/builder-vm/provision.sh'. This is
     written by the cloud-init template, so only VMs created by this repo
     can pass. Bypassable only via BUILDER_SKIP_MARKER_CHECK=1 (with a
     loud warning).
  5. Interactive prompt: must type 'DESTROY <vmid>' verbatim.

Even with all gates passed, dry-run is still the default; --apply must be
explicit. The first thing the script prints (after arg parsing) is a
multi-line ASCII banner reminding the operator this is irreversible
without a PBS / ZFS snapshot.

Before destruction:
  - Lists qm listsnapshot output for the VMID
  - Lists PBS backups (best-effort via proxmox-backup-client or pvesm)

After qm destroy (with --purge --destroy-unreferenced-disks 1), it also
removes the cloud-init snippet file in /var/lib/vz/snippets — but ONLY the
one tagged with this VMID (never a wildcard).

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly.

beacon/store.ts and routes every cluster/node/zone/record call through
the StoreBackend SPI:

    beacon_meta_settings table is staged in the schema for a follow-up
    cutover.
  - All public function signatures (listClusters / getCluster /
    saveCluster / deleteCluster / saveNode / deleteNode / listZones /
    saveRecord / deleteRecord / getNextNsIndex / getBeaconSettings /
    saveBeaconSettings / resolveNsDomain / resolveNsIpVersion).

feat(migrate-stores): JSON↔Postgres migration CLI + Beacon mapper (Wave 2 Fase 3) (#20)

* feat(migrate-stores): CLI parser and entry point

Sets up scripts/migrate-stores/ with the Bun entrypoint, arg parser,
and tiny structured logger. Mirrors scripts/ship/ in shape — own
parseArgs (no yargs/commander), TTY-aware coloured output, silent
logger for tests.

CLI surface:
  bun migrate:stores --module=<m> --from=<json|postgres>
                     --to=<json|postgres> [flags]

Flags: --dry-run (default), --apply, --limit=N, --state-file,
--work-dir, --help. Validates that --from differs from --to and that
--apply isn't accidentally combined with --dry-run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(migrate-stores): runner state machine + types + drivers

Adds the orchestrator that walks a ModuleMigrator's collections,
applies toRow/fromRow, and pushes rows through a PostgresDriver
interface. The runner is module-agnostic — all schema knowledge lives
in the mappers under modules/.

Drivers:
  - JsonSource: reads/writes the encrypted .{m}-store.json file
    (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2 salt matches @proxmox-manager/core byte-for-byte)
  - MemoryDriver: in-memory test fake with ON CONFLICT semantics
  - PostgresJsDriver: postgres-js-backed prod driver; lazy-imports
    the `postgres` package so the CLI loads cleanly in workspaces
    that don't depend on apps/web

Direction-aware behaviour:
  - json-to-postgres: read JSON, map, insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  - postgres-to-json: read tables, map back, merge into the existing
    JSON store (de-dup on conflict targets so it stays idempotent)

Dry-run path is fully exercised — reads source, runs every mapper,
logs counts + sample row — but skips destination mutation AND
checkpoint persistence so a dry-run never poisons a follow-up apply.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(migrate-stores): checkpoint persistence

Per-module run state lives under ~/.developy/migrations/<m>.json so a
failed migration can resume from where it left off (the runner skips
collections marked `completed` on the second pass).

Schema is versioned (`version: 1`) so future changes don't trip
existing checkpoints. Writes are atomic — write to <path>.tmp, then
rename — surviving a crash mid-write. The runner gates checkpoint
saves through a `persistCheckpoint()` wrapper that's a no-op in
dry-run mode (a dry-run then an apply on the same --state-file works
as expected: apply still does the real work).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(migrate-stores): beacon module mapper (template)

First ModuleMigrator — maps BeaconStoreData (clusters, nodes, zones,
records) onto the planned beacon_meta_* tables, plus a kv-style
settings handler for BeaconSettings.

Table names are PROVISIONAL: the `beacon_meta` drizzle schema is
being built by a parallel agent (see plans/wave-2-execution.md §1).
TODO comments mark every spot that should switch from a magic
string to `getTableName(beaconMetaClusters)` once the schema lands.

This file doubles as the **template artifact** for every subsequent
module — the README documents the six steps to copy it. Each
collection has:
  - tableName (matches drizzle's pgTable(...))
  - conflictTargets (PK columns; used for ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
  - toRow (json → row) + fromRow (row → json), inverse of each other
  - optional label for log output

The settings handler is a separate optional surface for kv blobs
(BeaconSettings has 6 keys); serialise/deserialise stringify nested
values to keep the wire format dialect-agnostic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Central registry mapping `--module=<key>` strings to their

Started with `beacon` only; commented placeholders for the rest of

commits.title: fix(hooks): inject Bearer auth header in 20 client hooks (#14)
commits.body:
fix(hooks): inject Bearer auth header in 20 client hooks (#14)

* fix(beacon): inject Bearer auth header in apiFetch

The Beacon GET routes call requireSession() (unlike Nexus/Atlas which
don't), so the client must send the Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

The apiFetch helper was only sending Content-Type, causing all Beacon
client queries to fail silently with 401 — manifesting as empty cluster
and zone lists in the dashboard even though the underlying store had
data.

Other modules (use-ignite, use-iam, use-aegis, etc) likely have the
same bug — separate audit PR forthcoming.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(hooks): inject Bearer auth header across all API helpers

Same root cause as previous Beacon fix: client hooks were not sending
the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Endpoints that call
requireSession() on the server (beacon, ignite, iam, mesh, etc) were
returning 401 silently, manifesting as empty dashboards.

Patched 19 hooks: aegis-settings, atlas, audit, blaze, connections,
flux, herald, ignite, memberships, mesh, nexus, organizations,
projects, pulse, radar, reconciliation, spark, teams, tide.

(use-beacon already patched in previous commit.)

This is the cause of the 'Beacon shows 0 clusters', 'Mesh shows nothing',
'Ignite not working' user reports.

A more permanent fix is to introduce a shared lib/api-fetch.ts helper
that all hooks consume. Deferred to a refactor PR — this patch is
mechanical and minimal.

Records the root cause, symptom matrix, fix approach, validation, and

commits.body:
feat(beacon): PowerDNS backend + zones/records read through backend (#15)

* feat(beacon): define DnsBackend interface and shared types

Add the abstraction Beacon will use to talk to DNS providers (DigitalOcean,
PowerDNS, or in-memory mocks). Establishes Zod schemas for record/domain
shapes, a typed DnsBackendError, and the capability matrix surfaced by
backends. Documents the idempotency contract that callers can rely on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): add mock backend for tests

In-memory DnsBackend implementation that honours the full contract: SOA
serial bumping, idempotent createRecord, TSIG storage, capability flags.
Used as the default backend when nothing else is configured in dev/test
(see factory.ts) and as the contract baseline that the SQL- and CLI-
backed implementations are validated against.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(beacon): migrate DigitalOcean logic to backend implementation

Move the doctl-based DNS code out of doctl-client.ts and into a proper
DnsBackend implementation. Adds idempotent createDomain/createRecord,
healthCheck via 'doctl account get', and an injectable executor so tests
can replay canned doctl JSON without spawning the binary.

Capability flags reflect what doctl actually exposes — DigitalOcean does
not surface DNSSEC or TSIG via the CLI, so those are false here.

doctl-client.ts is intentionally left in place for now; subsequent commits
will turn it into a deprecation shim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): add PowerDNS backend implementation (Postgres-backed)

Implements DnsBackend by writing directly to PowerDNS' gpgsql tables —
the same schema PowerDNS reads on every query (see schema.pgsql.sql).
Creates an SOA record automatically on createDomain so PowerDNS treats
the zone as authoritative; bumps notified_serial + the SOA record
serial on every mutation so secondaries notice the change.

Surfaces DNSSEC and TSIG capabilities (cryptokeys / tsigkeys tables
read+write) and supports a notifyReload hook for plugging in an
out-of-band 'pdns_control reload <zone>' once we have an SSH/HTTP
channel. Today notifyReload defaults to a no-op; PowerDNS will pick up
writes at the next query subject to its in-process record cache (60s
default).

The pg driver is injected via an SqlPool interface so tests can use a
hand-rolled mock without pulling pg-mem in as a dependency.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): backend factory with env-based selection

Add getDnsBackend() / selectBackendId() / resetDnsBackend(). Selection
priority documented at the top of factory.ts: explicit BEACON_BACKEND
beats inferred-from-env, which prefers PowerDNS when DATABASE_URL is set
and falls back to DigitalOcean when only the doctl token is present.
Production must configure something explicitly — no silent mock fallback.

The factory caches per-process; tests can call resetDnsBackend() or
setDnsBackend(stub) to swap implementations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(beacon): contract tests for all backends + smoke

Three test layers:
- interface.test.ts: contract suite that runs the same scenarios against
  Mock, PowerDNS (with fake pg pool), and DigitalOcean (with fake doctl).
  Covers idempotent create, update keeps id, delete is no-op on missing,
  list filters, capability-flag presence, TSIG roundtrip where supported.
- powerdns-backend.test.ts: SQL-shape regression tests — auto SOA insertion,
  NS seeding, serial bumping, disabled flag, notifyReload hook firing.
- digitalocean-backend.test.ts: doctl arg shape, idempotency on
  (name, type, content), token-leak guard.
- factory.test.ts: env-based selection rules + cache behavior.

Adjusts two backend behaviours so contract tests pass uniformly across
all three implementations:
- DigitalOceanDnsBackend.listRecords swallows not_found and returns [],
  matching Mock and PowerDNS contracts.
- PowerDNS buildPgPool wraps pg.Pool.query with a properly typed adapter.

Helpers (helpers/sql-fake.ts, helpers/doctl-fake.ts) are intentionally
narrow — they recognise only the SQL/CLI shapes the backends emit. Adding
a new query in the backend requires extending the fake.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(beacon): orchestrator uses DnsBackend interface

Move the NS-record management away from a hard-wired PowerDNS REST client
onto the new DnsBackend abstraction. The orchestrator and provisioner now
import from ./backends/ns-helpers, which routes through getDnsBackend()
— so PowerDNS, DigitalOcean, and the mock backend are all interchangeable
without code changes elsewhere.

The legacy pdns-client.ts is reduced to a deprecation shim that
re-exports from ns-helpers; the obsolete resolvePdnsIp() now returns ""
since the configured backend handles transport.

Cluster lifecycle stays in the in-memory store (BeaconCluster) — the
backend is only consulted for the DNS write side. Herald events are
preserved verbatim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(beacon): deprecate doctl-client.ts (re-export shim)

Reduce doctl-client.ts to a thin shim that delegates to the new
DigitalOceanDnsBackend. The exported surface (listDomainRecords,
createDomainRecord, updateDomainRecord, deleteDomainRecord, setNsRecord,
removeNsRecord) is preserved 1:1 so any out-of-tree consumer keeps
compiling. Each export carries a @deprecated tag pointing at the
DnsBackend abstraction or ./backends/ns-helpers.

The file will be removed after the next release cycle once external
imports are migrated.

Document the DnsBackend abstraction:
- Capability matrix per backend (DNSSEC / TSIG support).
- Env-var selection rules with priority order.

commits.body:
feat(db): StoreBackend SPI + Beacon as reference implementation (#21)

* feat(db/schema): add beacon_meta tables (clusters, nodes, settings)

Append three tables to schema/beacon.ts for Beacon's platform metadata:

- beacon_meta_clusters — BeaconCluster (cluster topology, HA mode, size,
  Proxmox node placement, audit fields). Indexed on (org_id, status) and
  (proxmox_node) for the most common dashboard queries.
- beacon_meta_nodes — BeaconNode (NS LXC tracking, IP, status). FK to
  beacon_meta_clusters with ON DELETE CASCADE so the cluster lifecycle
  drives node lifecycle.
- beacon_meta_settings — key/value singleton (nsDomain, nsCount,
  nsIpv6Pool, …). jsonb value so new settings don't need DDL changes.

Enums (beacon_cluster_status, beacon_ha_mode, beacon_size,
beacon_node_status) mirror the corresponding unions in
@sidefuel/platform/beacon and data-products/types — kept in sync by
convention.

The existing PowerDNS tables (domains, records, supermasters, …) are
left untouched; pdns_auth still reads them directly, and the read-side
delegation from PR #15 still routes zone/record traffic through the
DnsBackend interface.

Part of Wave 2 Fase 2 (StoreBackend SPI). See plans/wave-2-execution.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db): generate migration 0001 for beacon_meta + load-all in test-helpers

- 0001_cold_sandman.sql: emitted by `drizzle-kit generate` from the new
  schema/beacon.ts beacon_meta tables. Pure DDL: 4 enums + 3 tables + 1
  FK + 4 indexes. No data migration.
- meta/0001_snapshot.json + journal update: drizzle-kit's view of the
  schema state after applying 0001. Committed as-is so future
  `drizzle-kit generate` diffs are stable.
- test-helpers: `loadAllMigrations()` walks the migrations dir in order
  and concatenates the sanitized SQL. `bootTestDb()` defaults to
  applying every migration, so any future migration is exercised by the
  smoke suite without code changes. Set `allMigrations: false` to
  pin to 0000 for tests that explicitly want the legacy schema.

All 19 existing pg-mem smoke tests still pass — backward compatible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db): add StoreBackend<T> interface and types

Introduces the SPI every module's persistence layer will plug into:

  - StoreBackend<TStore>.load()      → full snapshot read
  - StoreBackend<TStore>.save(data)  → full snapshot write
  - StoreBackend<TStore>.saveEntity? → targeted upsert (Postgres-preferred)
  - StoreBackend<TStore>.deleteEntity? → targeted delete

Generic TStore matches the module's shape (e.g. BeaconStoreData with
clusters/nodes/zones/records arrays). `ItemOf<TStore, K>` resolves the
array element type so saveEntity's signature is fully typed at the call
site.

No implementations land here — JsonFileBackend and PostgresBackend follow
in subsequent commits. Module code can already type its backend handle
against this interface today.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db): add JsonFileBackend<T> implementation

Wraps the legacy readStore/writeStore pattern behind the StoreBackend
interface. Behaviour is bit-equivalent to what each module had inline:

  - load() reads the encrypted file, decrypts AES-256-GCM, JSON.parse
  - load() returns a deep clone of emptyStore on any failure (missing
    file, key mismatch, parse error) — matches legacy contract
  - save() encrypts + writes the whole snapshot
  - saveEntity()/deleteEntity() are read-modify-write convenience built
    on top of save(), with a per-backend write lock so concurrent
    callers don't lose writes
  - getItemId defaults to `item.id` and throws a clear error if the
    item shape doesn't match — modules with non-standard ids pass a
    custom getter

Tests (9) cover: empty store, encrypt/decrypt round-trip, key mismatch
fallback, saveEntity insert + update, deleteEntity, concurrent
saveEntity serialization, untouched collections, non-array rejection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db): add PostgresBackend<T> with adapter pattern

PostgresBackend is intentionally thin: it forwards every SPI call to a
PostgresBackendAdapter that the module ships. The adapter is where SQL
lives, and where drizzle is wired in production.

  - load()         → adapter.loadAll()
  - save()         → adapter.replaceAll(data)
  - saveEntity()   → adapter.upsertOne(collection, item)
  - deleteEntity() → adapter.deleteOne(collection, id)

The adapter seam matters for two reasons:

  1. Modules pick how to map TStore to SQL (drizzle queries today, raw
     SQL for tests, possibly other engines later).
  2. pg-mem doesn't support drizzle's postgres-js driver. Tests can
     write a raw-SQL adapter against pg-mem (see postgres-backend.test.ts)
     while production uses a drizzle adapter — both flow through the
     same PostgresBackend instance.

Tests (6) prove the backend is a faithful pass-through: snapshot
round-trip, replace semantics, upsert insert+update, delete with
hit/miss return.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db): add store-factory selecting backend by env + contract tests

getStoreBackend(moduleId, options) is the single entry point every
module uses to get its persistence handle. Resolution order:

  1. <MODULE>_STORE_BACKEND   (per-module override)
  2. STORE_BACKEND            (global default)
  3. fallback: "json"

  module-id dashes are normalized to underscores in the env-var name,
  so BEACON_META_STORE_BACKEND matches getStoreBackend("beacon-meta").

Laziness: in json mode buildPostgresAdapter is never invoked, so the
factory stays decoupled from drizzle / DATABASE_URL. That keeps dev,
CI, and the partial-cutover plan working: a module can be on json
while its neighbor flips to postgres.

Tests:
  - store-factory.test.ts (11): every documented precedence rule +
    failure modes + laziness check
  - store-backend.test.ts (10): contract suite that runs the same
    assertions against both backends — round-trip, upsert, delete,
    backend type — so symmetry is guaranteed by CI

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): add beaconMetaAdapter (maps BeaconStoreData → drizzle ops)

Implements PostgresBackendAdapter<BeaconStoreData> for the StoreBackend
SPI. Only handles the collections beacon_meta owns:

  - clusters → beacon_meta_clusters  (full CRUD via drizzle)
  - nodes    → beacon_meta_nodes     (full CRUD via drizzle, FK CASCADE
                                       from cluster deletion)

Zones and records are intentionally no-ops here — they live in
PowerDNS's own tables and are read through the DnsBackend (see PR #15).
loadAll() returns empty arrays for them; replaceAll/upsertOne/deleteOne
skip the collection. The shape stays valid so BeaconStoreData consumers
don't have to special-case anything.

Mappers are explicit (clusterToRow/rowToCluster, nodeToRow/rowToNode)
so future schema drift surfaces as a type error at compile time. The
adapter is constructed lazily — getDb() is only called once
STORE_BACKEND=postgres routes here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(beacon): store.ts consumes StoreBackend via factory (default = json)

Lifts the inline readStore/writeStore + withWriteLock pattern out of
beacon/store.ts and routes every cluster/node/zone/record call through
the StoreBackend SPI:

  - backend() returns a lazy singleton from getStoreBackend("beacon-meta")
  - Default env (BEACON_META_STORE_BACKEND unset) → JsonFileBackend with
    the exact same encrypted .beacon-store.json file the legacy code
    wrote. Bit-equivalent on disk, zero regression for current deploys.
  - BEACON_META_STORE_BACKEND=postgres → PostgresBackend +
    beaconMetaAdapter. Cluster/node CRUD against the mgmt-db.

What's preserved untouched:

  - PowerDNS DnsBackend delegation for zone/record reads (PR #15) —
    that block is still in place; the SPI is only the authority for
    cluster/node metadata.
  - Settings (BEACON_NS_*) still use .beacon-settings.json; the
    beacon_meta_settings table is staged in the schema for a follow-up
    cutover.
  - All public function signatures (listClusters / getCluster /
    saveCluster / deleteCluster / saveNode / deleteNode / listZones /
    saveRecord / deleteRecord / getNextNsIndex / getBeaconSettings /
    saveBeaconSettings / resolveNsDomain / resolveNsIpVersion).

Tests:
  - store.test.ts (11): JSON-mode regression suite covering the full
    cluster/node CRUD surface + cascade behaviour + filter semantics +
    getNextNsIndex. Plus two env-flip checks.
  - All 71 existing beacon/* tests still pass.

resetBeaconStoreBackendForTesting() is a test hook for swapping the
backend after env-var changes — modules using the SPI singleton pattern
need this and it costs nothing in production.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(db): document StoreBackend SPI usage + 'add a new module' runbook

Updates the db README so the next module-author has a complete recipe:

  - SPI interface signature + the StoreBackend<T> generics it accepts
  - env-var resolution table (default/global/per-module) with the

Points the reader at apps/web/src/lib/server/beacon/ as the canonical

commits.title: feat(atlas-mgmt): preflight.sh — twelve read-only checks
commits.body:
feat(atlas-mgmt): preflight.sh — twelve read-only checks

Runs on the Proxmox node. Validates everything before provision.sh
touches a single resource. NEVER mutates. Pure read-only.

Checks:
   1. pct/pvesm/ip tools present  (we are on a Proxmox node)
   2. Proxmox version is 8.x
   3. $ATLAS_MGMT_STORAGE exists and is active
   4. $ATLAS_MGMT_SNIPPETS_STORAGE supports 'snippets' content
   5. $ATLAS_MGMT_BRIDGE is up
   6. $ATLAS_MGMT_TEMPLATE is present in the storage
   7. $ATLAS_MGMT_VMID is free  (also checks qm — VMID/CTID share namespace)
   8. $ATLAS_MGMT_IP does NOT respond to ping  (no IP conflict)
   9. SSH public key file exists and looks like an OpenSSH public key
  10. Storage has $ATLAS_MGMT_DISK_GB + 20 GiB free  (headroom for snapshots/WAL)
  11. PG_OWNER_PASSWORD and PG_APP_PASSWORD set, >=16 chars, distinct
  12. ATLAS_MGMT_IP is inside PG_ALLOWED_CIDR  (prefix-match; warns for non-/24)

Exits 0 on full pass, 1 on any failure, 2 on bad invocation. Provision.sh
gates on this — preflight failure aborts before any state change.

Mirrors Beacon template (PR #21). Adapter maps IamStore <-> drizzle rows

  - end-to-end json -> memory-postgres -> recovered json round-trip
  - idempotency (second --apply run writes 0 rows)

The Beacon GET routes call requireSession() (unlike Nexus/Atlas which

commits.body:
feat(atlas-mgmt): destroy.sh with 5-gate confirmation

Last-resort emergency lever. Mirrors builder-vm/destroy.sh's posture
and extends it to LXC (pct instead of qm).

Five gates — ALL must pass:
  Gate 1  --i-know-what-im-doing flag is passed
  Gate 2  pct status $ATLAS_MGMT_VMID exists on this node
  Gate 3  pct config $ATLAS_MGMT_VMID hostname == .env ATLAS_MGMT_HOSTNAME
  Gate 4  /etc/developy/lxc.marker inside the LXC references
          scripts/bootstrap/atlas-mgmt/provision.sh
  Gate 5  Operator types  "DESTROY <vmid>"  verbatim at prompt

If the LXC is stopped at Gate 4, the script briefly starts it to read
the marker, then stops it again before destroy. This prevents the
"VM was stopped, marker check skipped" footgun while still being
non-destructive.

Escape hatches:
  ATLAS_MGMT_SKIP_MARKER_CHECK=1   bypasses Gate 4 only
                                   (logged as WARN; never silent)
  ATLAS_MGMT_NONINTERACTIVE=1      skips Gate 5 typed-confirm
                                   (intended for controlled CI-like reruns,
                                   never for casual destroys)

Lists current snapshots + PBS backups before destroying. Removes the
cloud-init snippet from /var/lib/vz/snippets after pct destroy succeeds.
Does NOT delete pg_dumps in mgmt-tide or weekly B2 archives — restore
remains possible.

Running with no flags: prints banner, fails Gate 1, exits 1.

commits.title: feat(db): add PostgresBackend<T> with adapter pattern
commits.body:
feat(db): add PostgresBackend<T> with adapter pattern

PostgresBackend is intentionally thin: it forwards every SPI call to a
PostgresBackendAdapter that the module ships. The adapter is where SQL
lives, and where drizzle is wired in production.

  - load()         → adapter.loadAll()
  - save()         → adapter.replaceAll(data)
  - saveEntity()   → adapter.upsertOne(collection, item)
  - deleteEntity() → adapter.deleteOne(collection, id)

The adapter seam matters for two reasons:

  1. Modules pick how to map TStore to SQL (drizzle queries today, raw
     SQL for tests, possibly other engines later).
  2. pg-mem doesn't support drizzle's postgres-js driver. Tests can
     write a raw-SQL adapter against pg-mem (see postgres-backend.test.ts)
     while production uses a drizzle adapter — both flow through the
     same PostgresBackend instance.

Tests (6) prove the backend is a faithful pass-through: snapshot
round-trip, replace semantics, upsert insert+update, delete with
hit/miss return.

commits.body:
feat(migrate-stores): checkpoint persistence

Per-module run state lives under ~/.developy/migrations/<m>.json so a
failed migration can resume from where it left off (the runner skips
collections marked `completed` on the second pass).

Schema is versioned (`version: 1`) so future changes don't trip
existing checkpoints. Writes are atomic — write to <path>.tmp, then
rename — surviving a crash mid-write. The runner gates checkpoint
saves through a `persistCheckpoint()` wrapper that's a no-op in
dry-run mode (a dry-run then an apply on the same --state-file works
as expected: apply still does the real work).

Adds Postgres ORM stack to apps/web:

* feat(db): add drizzle config and client singleton

Adds the foundation for Postgres-backed module stores:

- drizzle.config.ts: schema glob, migrations dir, postgresql dialect.
  Uses DATABASE_URL or falls back to a stub URL so drizzle-kit can run
  even without a real DB (the runtime client refuses the stub).

- src/lib/server/db/index.ts: lazy singleton that wires postgres-js +
  drizzle. Exposes:
    - getDb(): Database  — opens pool on first call
    - getStoreBackend(): 'json'|'postgres' — drives StoreBackend SPI
    - setDbForTesting / closeDbForTesting — pg-mem hooks
    - re-exports per-schema namespaces (aegis, audit, beacon, marketing, platform)

* feat(db/aegis): add IAM schema (orgs, teams, members, policies, sessions, service_tokens)

Adds the Aegis schema as the first concrete drizzle module:

Tables (all prefixed aegis_ in the public schema for now):
- aegis_orgs        UUID PK, slug-unique, jsonb settings, tier enum
                    (starter/growth/enterprise/cooperative)
- aegis_teams       hierarchical via parent_team_id, slug unique per org
- aegis_members     M:N (org, userId) with role/status enums and
                    teamIds jsonb array; userId is the principal id
                    (Aegis-issued or external IdP sub)
- aegis_policies    ABAC statements jsonb + version, name unique per org
- aegis_sessions    SHA-256 token_hash (never plaintext), expires/revoke
                    columns, indexed by user and expiresAt
- aegis_service_tokens  bearer tokens for bots (deploy bot, ship CLI):
                    SHA-256 hash + scopes jsonb + expiresAt
- aegis_ledger      bigserial high-cardinality auth-event log
                    (login attempts etc) — Herald is for everything else

Indexes target the hottest read paths: org+slug, org+user, token lookup.

Zod schemas (insert/select) generated via drizzle-zod for each table,
plus inferred types (Org, NewOrg, Team, ...) re-exported from the
module. Fits the existing zod 3.25 pin in apps/web.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db/audit): add Herald schema (events, partitioned by month)

Adds the Herald audit log as an append-only, monthly-partitioned table.

Drizzle definition (audit_events):
  seq          bigserial
  tenant_id    text (NULL = platform-wide)
  source       varchar(32) — module producing the event
  type         varchar(96) — 'iam.role.granted', 'forge.vm.start', …
  severity     enum info/notice/warn/error/critical
  actor        jsonb  — { id, kind, ip, user_agent, … }
  resource     jsonb  — { kind, id, name, parent, … }
  action       varchar(32)
  outcome      enum allow/deny/success/failure/conditional
  before       jsonb (nullable)
  after        jsonb (nullable)
  context      jsonb — request_id, trace_id, …
  created_at   timestamptz — partition key

Composite PK (seq, created_at) so the table can be declared
PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at) — Postgres requires the partition
key to be part of the PK on partitioned tables. The PARTITION BY
clause + first monthly partition are stitched into the generated
migration in the next commit (drizzle-kit doesn't model partitioning
natively).

Indexes target audit-explorer query shapes: by tenant+time, by type+time,
by source+time, by outcome+time. All include created_at as the second
column so they live happily inside per-partition btrees post-migration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db/beacon): add PowerDNS-compatible schema (domains, records, supermasters, etc)

Mirrors the existing handwritten schema at
src/lib/server/beacon/schema.pgsql.sql in drizzle so the platform
can drive PowerDNS through the same client.

Tables follow the gpgsql backend spec exactly so pdns-auth can be
pointed at the same database with launch=gpgsql:

  domains          (id, name unique, master, last_check, type,
                    notified_serial, account, options, catalog)
  records          (id, domain_id, name, type, content, ttl, prio,
                    disabled, ordername, auth) + name + (name,type) +
                    domain_id indexes that PowerDNS expects
  supermasters     (ip INET, nameserver, account) — composite PK
                    via a custom inet type since drizzle-orm has no
                    first-class inet
  comments         (id, domain_id, name, type, modified_at, account,
                    comment)
  domainmetadata   (id, domain_id FK CASCADE, kind, content)
  cryptokeys       (id, domain_id FK CASCADE, flags, active,
                    published, content)
  tsigkeys         (id, name, algorithm, secret) UNIQUE(name, algorithm)

Naming and types are dictated by PowerDNS; do not refactor without
checking pdns-auth source. drizzle-zod schemas + inferred types
(Domain, NewDomain, Record, …) are exported for the rest of Beacon.

Ref: https://doc.powerdns.com/authoritative/backends/generic-postgresql.html

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(db/platform): add platform schema (connection_profiles, feature_flags, migrations_state)

Adds the platform-level tables — the bits that aren't owned by a single
product module:

- platform_connection_profiles
    UUID PK + nullable org_id (NULL = platform-wide).
    encrypted_payload bytea holds AES-256-GCM ciphertext of the full
    ConnectionProfile JSON (iv ‖ ciphertext ‖ auth-tag layout, same key
    as today: CONNECTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY). DB never sees plaintext.
    Unique (org_id, name).

- platform_feature_flags
    UUID PK, nullable org_id (platform-wide flags allowed).
    enabled boolean (cheap hot-path), value jsonb (richer config).
    Unique (org_id, key).

- platform_migrations_state
    Free-form key/value store consumed by the future StoreBackend SPI.
    Tracks per-module JSON→Postgres migration progress separately from
    drizzle's migration journal so we can resume mid-flight.

- platform_ops_log
    Bigserial ledger for ad-hoc ops kicks (JSON→Postgres migration
    breadcrumbs etc.).

bytea handled via drizzle's customType — drizzle-orm doesn't expose
a first-class bytea constructor.

* feat(db): generate initial migration

drizzle-kit generated 0000_initial.sql for the 21 tables across
aegis/audit/beacon/marketing/platform schemas (DDL + indexes + FKs +
enum types).

audit_events is hand-patched to add PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)
since drizzle-kit doesn't model partitioning. Postgres requires a
plain sequence (not bigserial) on the partitioned parent, so 'seq'
is rewritten as bigint DEFAULT nextval(…). Two seed partitions are
created (2026-05, 2026-06) plus a DEFAULT partition catch-all so
writes outside the seeded range can never silently fail before the
rotation job catches up.

Subsequent monthly partitions are created by a future cron/pg_cron
job — see follow-up issue.

The drizzle schema columns/PK match the SQL 1:1 so future
'drizzle-kit generate' diffs stay empty.

Includes meta/_journal.json + meta/0000_snapshot.json so other devs
can run db:migrate without regenerating.

* test(db): pg-mem smoke tests for all schemas

Adds an in-memory smoke test suite that exercises the generated
migration end-to-end on pg-mem:

- bootTestDb() applies the (sanitized) initial migration. pg-mem
  doesn't speak PARTITION BY, so audit_events is loaded as a regular
  table for tests; the bigserial->sequence rewrite the partitioned
  parent needs is undone before pg-mem sees it. partitioning is the
  one thing the test bed cannot validate; everything else is real.

- gen_random_uuid() registered against pg-mem with impure:true so
  multi-row inserts get distinct UUIDs (default uuid is consumed
  once per statement otherwise → duplicate-key failures).

19 cases across 6 describe blocks:

  migration applies on pg-mem
    ✓ creates all 21 tables
    ✓ enums reject out-of-range values

  aegis schema
    ✓ unique slug
    ✓ default tier + timestamps + jsonb '{}' default
    ✓ enum reject for member.role
    ✓ drizzle-zod (org/member/policy)

  audit schema
    ✓ NOT NULL action+outcome, default severity 'info'
    ✓ enum reject for outcome
    ✓ drizzle-zod minimum shape

  beacon (PowerDNS) schema
    ✓ insert domain+records, CASCADE on domainmetadata
    ✓ drizzle-zod required fields

  platform schema
    ✓ encrypted_payload bytea round-trips as Buffer
    ✓ composite (org_id, key) unique fires for explicit org_id, allows
      multiple NULL-org rows (Postgres NULL-unique semantics)
    ✓ drizzle-zod for connection_profile + feature_flag

  marketing schema
    ✓ unique email
    ✓ enum reject for intent + accept 'operator'
    ✓ CASCADE pledges on signup delete
    ✓ drizzle-zod (waitlist + pledge)

  counters query
    ✓ confirmed builders + total nodes pledged

Note: drizzle-orm/node-postgres can't run against pg-mem (it relies
on getTypeParser + rowMode='array' which pg-mem rejects), so tests
use raw SQL via mem.public.exec/many. drizzle-zod schemas are still
covered directly. For a real Postgres integration test we'll wire
testcontainers in a follow-up.

commits.title: fix(provisioner): centralize vmidToIp + reserved-IP guard (prevents collisions like 2026-05-11 outage)
commits.body:
fix(provisioner): centralize vmidToIp + reserved-IP guard (prevents collisions like 2026-05-11 outage)

## Why

On 2026-05-11 around 21:15, the dashboard hung on 'Loading organizations...'.
Root cause: a Herald lifecycle test instance had been provisioned as Proxmox
VMID 151 and assigned IP 172.10.0.151 — the same IP as atlas-mgmt-01 (LXC
9101, the management postgres). ARP races silently routed half of the app's
postgres queries to the Herald container, which obviously had nothing on
5432. Connections timed out, app couldn't read aegis_orgs, UI stuck.

The local fix was `pct stop 151` + bridge fdb flush. The structural fix is
this PR.

## What was wrong

Every data-product provisioner (atlas, beacon, blaze, flux, herald, ignite,
nexus, spark, tide — nine files) had its own copy of:

    function vmidToIp(vmid: number): string {
      ...
      parts[3] = String(vmid % 256);
      ...
    }

Two structural failures:

1. **Manual management LXCs were given IPs from inside the provisioner range.**
   atlas-mgmt-01 was provisioned with IP 172.10.0.151 by hand; developy-quickstart
   with 172.10.0.150. Both .150 and .151 are valid outputs of `vmid % 256` for
   common VMIDs (150, 151, 406, 407, …). Collision was inevitable.

2. **No reservation mechanism.** Even if we wanted to keep the management IPs
   out of the provisioner range, there was no single place to declare them.

## Fix

- Move `vmidToIp` to a single canonical implementation in
  `data-products/provisioner-base.ts`. Re-implementations in all nine
  provisioner files deleted; each imports the shared one.
- Add a configurable reserved-octet set. Defaults reflect prod state on
  2026-05-11:
    10, 11  — PVE host vmbr1 interfaces
    103     — pg-beacon-default
    127     — pdns-ns1
    150     — developy-quickstart (manual mgmt LXC)
    151     — atlas-mgmt-01 (manual mgmt LXC)
  Overridable via `DATA_PRODUCTS_RESERVED_IPS` env (comma-separated).
- When `vmid % 256` lands on a reserved octet, walk forward to the next free
  one. Loop bound 256 — never hangs.
- Env is re-read on each call so operators can rotate the reserved list at
  runtime.

## What this still does NOT fix (follow-up)

VMIDs that differ by 256 still collide (VMID 200 and VMID 456 both → .200).
The real fix is an explicit IPAM allocation table; the mesh module already
has `ipam-engine.ts` we can reuse. Tracked as a follow-up.

## Tests

- 11 new vitest cases in `provisioner-base.test.ts` covering: dhcp fallback,
  non-reserved mapping, mask preservation, the exact VMID-151 regression that
  caused the outage, env override, default reserved set, and wrap-around
  bound.
- Typecheck clean (pre-existing `tests/ignite/03,04-*` errors are on
  origin/main, unrelated).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.title: feat(db): plain SQL migration runner + new pnpm scripts (drizzle-kit becomes optional)
commits.body:
feat(db): plain SQL migration runner + new pnpm scripts (drizzle-kit becomes optional)

Replaces `drizzle-kit migrate` with a tiny custom runner at
`scripts/db-migrate/`. drizzle-orm itself stays — it's the query builder
used by all the postgres adapters. Only the migration tooling changes.

## Why

Two pain points hit us during 2026-05-11 Wave 2 cutover:

1. drizzle-kit auto-generated migrations with FK ordering bugs (pg-mem
   in tests accepted them; real Postgres rejected). PR #27 fixed the
   immediate breakage and documented the rule. Going forward, all
   migrations are hand-written and reviewed; the runner has no
   auto-generation step that could repeat the bug.

2. drizzle-kit's snapshot + hash + journal made post-deploy fixes
   complex. Modifying an applied migration meant updating
   `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations.hash` on every deployed DB. This
   runner uses filename tracking only — no snapshot, no hash drama.

## What

- `scripts/db-migrate/runner.ts` — < 150 LOC, lex-orders SQL files,
  tracks in `__migrations(filename PK, applied_at)`, each migration
  in its own transaction
- `scripts/db-migrate/index.ts` — CLI: `status`, `apply`, `new <desc>`
- `scripts/db-migrate/runner.test.ts` — 9 vitest cases covering
  file discovery, ordering, idempotency, scaffolding, bootstrap
- Bootstrap path: on first run against a DB with the legacy
  `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` table, drizzle's id-ordered rows map
  to migration files sorted by filename — already-applied skip cleanly

## pnpm scripts

New (use these):
- `db:status` — list applied/pending
- `db:apply` — run pending in order
- `db:new "<desc>"` — scaffold next-numbered .sql with header
- `test:db-migrate` — vitest

Kept for fallback during transition:
- `db:generate`, `db:migrate`, `db:studio`, `db:check` (drizzle-kit)

A follow-up PR will remove drizzle-kit entirely once `db:apply` has
been exercised against prod cutover cycles a few times.

## Updates

- `plans/deploy-runbook.md` §3.1 — points to `pnpm db:apply`
- `scripts/db-migrate/README.md` — full usage + history
- CLAUDE.md — "Database migrations" section + "Adding a schema change"
  workflow with FK-ordering reminder

Introduces the SPI every module's persistence layer will plug into:

  - StoreBackend<TStore>.deleteEntity? → targeted delete

Generic TStore matches the module's shape (e.g. BeaconStoreData with
clusters/nodes/zones/records arrays). `ItemOf<TStore, K>` resolves the
array element type so saveEntity's signature is fully typed at the call
site.

against this interface today.
