* fix(mesh): counter math, IPv6 enumerator, anti-exhaustion guard

Bugs the user surfaced testing carves on a /56 parent:

1. enumerateIPv6Addresses produced INVALID IPv6 for carved children.
   Old code: `${base}::1` where base="2804:1740:f:2000::100" yields
   "2804:1740:f:2000::100::1" — two `::` per RFC 4291 §2.2 is illegal,
   and Proxmox rejected the LXC create with
   'net0.ip6: invalid format - value does not look like a valid ipv6
   network configuration'. New code does the arithmetic in bigint
   (base + i) and compresses back via bigIntToIpv6(). Also bounds the
   enumeration by the pool's actual /N size — a /124 has 16 addresses,
   not 256.

2. calculateTotalAddresses was wrong twice:
   • /128 returned -1 (Math.pow(2, 0) - 2). Now: 1.
   • Any IPv6 /N < 120 capped at 65534. That made a /112 carve from a
     /56 parent show 65534/65534 on the parent — 'looks like 100% used'
     when the parent actually has 4.7e21 addresses. Now:
     /128 → 1, /N with bits<31 → exact, otherwise INT_MAX (display
     cap, the gap-finder uses bigint anyway).

3. Anti-exhaustion guard in carveSubPool: childPrefix - parentPrefix
   must be >= 8. Otherwise a single rent can take half of a /56 with
   one click and starve every other tenant. 8-bit delta caps the
   biggest rent at 1/256 of parent — for a /56 that's /64 (still
   2^64 addresses, plenty for any customer), for a /24 IPv4 it's /32
   (single host). UI dropdown now filters its predefined sizes by the
   same rule via sizesForParent().

End-to-end validation
=====================

LXC actually came up with valid IPv6 this time:
  Cluster on-teste2-v2 (rented from teste2 = ::100/120 child)
    requested → provisioning IP ::101/120 → configuring → active
    endpoint = [2804:1740:f:2000::101]:5432  (~3m53s total)
    Postgres protocol probe from real-IPv6 host: 'S' (alive, SSL).

Pool counters after fix (recomputed via SQL on prod):
  default /56  →   9 / 2,147,483,647   (was 5 / 65534)
  teste   /120 →   0 / 256             (was 0 / 254)
  teste4  /128 →   0 / 1               (was 0 / -1)
  teste5  /112 →   0 / 65,536          (was 0 / 65534, looked = parent)

Known follow-ups
================

- Storing IPv6 totalAddresses in an integer column truncates at
  INT_MAX (2.1B). Real /56 has ~4.7e21 addresses; for display purposes
  the cap is fine but operators querying the column shouldn't expect
  exactness for IPv6 prefixes shorter than /97. Move to bigint or a
  string representation if accurate operator dashboards become a thing.
- UI dropdown is still hardcoded — a more dynamic version would derive
  options from parent prefix delta steps (parent+8, +16, +24, +32, +64)
  rather than the predefined list, removing the need to keep them in
  sync as we add new parent sizes.

* test(mesh): pin carving / counter / guard / conflict behavior

The 2026-05-15 testing session uncovered four classes of bugs that
were silent until carving was exercised at scale. Each has a test now
so a future refactor that breaks any of them fails loud.

ipam-engine.carving.test.ts — 25 unit cases
============================================

  enumerateIPv6Addresses
    - base ending in :: → consecutive valid IPv6 strings
    - carved-child base (offset away from ::) → no double-:: in output
      (the bug Proxmox rejected with 400 'invalid format')
    - bounded by pool size, not a flat 256

  calculateTotalAddresses
    - IPv4 /32 → 1   (was 2 pre-fix)
    - IPv4 /31 → 2   RFC 3021 point-to-point
    - IPv4 /30 → 2   (network + broadcast deducted)
    - IPv4 /24 → 254
    - IPv6 /128 → 1   (was -1 pre-fix)
    - IPv6 /120 → 256 (no IPv6 'broadcast' deduction)
    - IPv6 /112 → 65536
    - IPv6 /56  → INT_MAX cap (was 65534, made carves look like 100%)
    - IPv6 /96  → INT_MAX cap (column is integer)

  carveSubPool gap-finder
    - first /120 lands AFTER parent infra reservations (::1/::2/::3)
    - subsequent /120 carves skip past earlier children (deterministic)
    - /128 single-IP rents start at the unblocked ::0 then skip
      ::1/::2/::3 to land at ::4 for the next one
    - parent counter +1 per carve

  carveSubPool anti-exhaustion guard
    - IPv6 /56 → /64 REFUSED (delta 8 < required 16, the 'eats 1/256
      of parent in one click' case)
    - IPv6 /56 → /71 REFUSED (just under min delta)
    - IPv6 /56 → /72 ALLOWED (exactly min delta)
    - IPv4 /29 → /32 ALLOWED (delta 1 — small parents need a relaxed rule)
    - IPv4 /29 → /29 REFUSED (must be strictly smaller)

  detectPoolConflict
    - clean carved child → empty conflicts + null proposal
    - bad pool with parent allocations inside → reports the addresses
      and proposes the next aligned safe CIDR (the auto-fix proposal)

  autoFixPoolConflict
    - rebuilds the same-named child in the safe slot
    - refuses to fix when the pool has active allocations (no data loss)

Engine bug fix unblocked by the tests
=====================================

createPool's overlap check now skips the parent in the new pool's
parentPoolId — a carved child is *expected* to overlap its parent, so
the old greedy CIDR_OVERLAP check refused every carve under a small
IPv4 parent. Sibling carves still fail-fast on overlap (which the
gap-finder prevents by construction).

networks-api.smoke.test.ts — 5 API cases (skipped without app)
===============================================================

Hits real Next.js route handlers with an HMAC-signed bearer (same
shape the prod auth flow produces). Each test asserts a documented
response envelope:

  POST /api/mesh/ipam/pools                    → 200 + new pool
  POST /api/mesh/ipam/pools/:id/carve  (/72)   → 200 + parent-rented child
  POST /api/mesh/ipam/pools/:id/carve  (/64)   → 4xx + CARVE_TOO_LARGE
  GET  /api/mesh/ipam/pools/:id/conflicts      → empty for clean child
  DELETE → recarve → same CIDR  (slot recycling end-to-end)

Tests skip when localhost:3000 isn't responding, so they don't fail
in clean CI but DO run in dev (and against staging/prod via APP_URL).

End-to-end is still operator-driven (a live Proxmox is required —
no harness in the repo). The provisioning chain ran green in this
session against the prod /56 pool: clusters on the IPv4 default,
/120 rented child, and IPv6 public endpoint.

fix(tests): clean up stale Bearer-only auth + pg-mem migration parsing (#40)

After commit 2f6e6ef switched auth from cookies to Bearer tokens, three
route tests still asserted the old Set-Cookie shape and started failing.
Separately, migration 0010 wraps a one-shot data cleanup in PL/pgSQL
which pg-mem can't parse, blocking every db.test.ts case, and 0003
drops FKs that 0000 never created on a fresh DB.

Changes:
- 0003: DROP CONSTRAINT → DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS (safe no-op on
  real PG, unblocks pg-mem on fresh boot). FK-ordering bug that
  motivated this migration is independent and stays fixed.
- test-helpers: strip DO $$ ... $$ blocks during sanitization for
  pg-mem (cleanup is a no-op on fresh test DB anyway).
- auth-routes.test: drop cookie assertions, assert Bearer token in
  response body; rewrite session/logout tests for Bearer flow.
- reconciliation-api.test: pass session via Authorization header
  instead of mock cookies.
- proxmox route.test: same — Authorization header replaces
  SESSION_COOKIE_NAME mock cookie.

Net: 37 previously-failing tests now pass (pg-mem 20, auth 3,
reconciliation 3, proxmox 2, plus all derived tests that depend on
pg-mem migrations loading). Remaining 79 failures are integration
suites that need a running localhost:3000 dev server — environment-
dependent, pre-existing, not addressed here.

commits.title: fix(atlas+mesh): unblock /128 pools, surface silent provisioner crashes, DNS-safe names (#43)
commits.body:
fix(atlas+mesh): unblock /128 pools, surface silent provisioner crashes, DNS-safe names (#43)

End-to-end validated in prod 2026-05-16: user created a cluster pinning
network=teste6 (2804:1740:f:2000::301/128) via the new <NetworkSelect>
and watched the row sit in `status=requested` forever with zero logs.

Three orthogonal bugs combined to make the failure invisible:

1. mesh ipam-engine: `enumerateIPv6Addresses` skipped offset 0 for every
   prefix length, so /128 (one address) returned []. `reserveAddress`
   then threw POOL_EXHAUSTED on a pool with 0/1 allocated. Fix: when
   poolSize <= 1 (i.e. /127 and /128), start from offset 0. IPv6 has no
   broadcast and the network address of a small prefix is routable.

2. atlas service.ts: provisionAtlasCluster was dispatched as
   `.catch(() => {})`. Any throw before the first `[Atlas] Cluster X:
   provisioning` log (in getIPPool / detectPoolConflict / reserveAddress)
   was invisible — operators had to dig into pg_stat or guess. Fix: log
   the err with stack so the next failure is actionable.

3. atlas validation.ts + provisioner.ts: cluster names allowed any
   character via `z.string().min(2).max(64)`, but the name is embedded
   in the LXC hostname (`atlas-${name}-primary`) which Proxmox validates
   as RFC-1123. Names with `_` (eg. `teste-select_network`) accepted,
   then Proxmox 400'd "invalid format - value does not look like a valid
   DNS name". Fix: tighten the schema to DNS-safe regex AND sanitize
   defensively at hostname construction so legacy rows still create.

4. atlas service.ts (related): added `requested` + `provisioning` to
   `deletableStatuses` so stuck rows can be cleaned via the API/UI
   path instead of needing direct DB DELETE. Safe — those statuses
   imply no LXC nor allocation (the failure paths set rows to `failed`).

End-to-end check after fixes: created teste-select-network → status
transitioned requested → provisioning → configuring → active in 125s,
LXC 147 came up with IP 2804:1740:f:2000::301, pool teste6 now reads
1/1 allocated, and `nc 2804:1740:f:2000::301:5432` returns OK from
the hypervisor. NetworkSelect feature confirmed end-to-end.

commits.title: fix(ui+atlas): dialog overflow + surface real error message from Atlas API (#42)
commits.body:
fix(ui+atlas): dialog overflow + surface real error message from Atlas API (#42)

Two unrelated-looking issues with the same symptom: "I clicked the
button and nothing useful happened."

1. DialogContent had no max-h / overflow handling. Once a dialog grew
   past viewport height (eg. Atlas cluster-create after we added the
   Network field), the bottom content — including the footer with the
   submit button — was silently clipped. Many users reported "I don't
   see the field" when really the field rendered offscreen. Adds
   max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto so any dialog scrolls. Global-by-design
   so future field additions don't reintroduce the bug elsewhere.

2. Atlas API handleError swallowed every server-side error and returned
   "Internal server error" with no context. Cred creation goes through
   `pct exec` over SSH — if the chain fails (cluster unreachable, ssh
   key mismatch, postgres not started, etc.) the actual stderr from
   provisioner-base was logged to console but the operator only saw
   the generic message in the toast. Now surfaces err.message so the
   first line of failure reaches the UI. Stack traces / sensitive
   details still aren't returned (only the Error.message string, which
   is already non-sensitive in our provisioner paths).

commits.title: docs(atlas): resolve all 6 open decisions in v2 plan (#45)
commits.body:
docs(atlas): resolve all 6 open decisions in v2 plan (#45)

User confirmed all 6 v2 design decisions on 2026-05-16:

1. Backup storage: THREE modes — Proxmox local + rsync (configurable
   target with ed25519 keypair flow) + download-only (one-shot link).
   Adds atlas_backup_targets table + Wave G now has 3 PRs.

2. DNS naming: `<safe-name>-<id-rand6>.db.developy.cloud` instead of
   the 4-level hierarchical scheme. Stable across cluster renames
   (suffix = cluster ID tail), no org/project leakage in public DNS,
   global uniqueness automatic.

3. Extension whitelist: 5 safe-and-easy defaults (pg_stat_statements,
   pg_trgm, pgcrypto, citext, hstore) instead of the 7-conservative
   proposal. postgis/pgvector/timescaledb move to admin-flagged tier.

4. Tier limits: full matrix added in §6.1.1 — databases/roles/firewall
   rules per cluster, backup retention/frequency, PITR availability,
   replicas, alert rules, extensions, rsync target count.

5. Sync vs async: always async + .catch error logging (the pattern
   shipped in PR #43). No special-case for destructive ops — the
   catch logger gives visibility.

6. MariaDB: postgres-first confirmed. MariaDB gets lifecycle only.

Also updates Wave E (DNS) provisioner snippet, Wave G (backups) to
3 PRs with full atlas_backup_targets schema + UI mockup, and Wave J
extension whitelist to match the new safe/admin split.

The §6.1 "Open decisions" table is now §6.1 "Resolved decisions"
with the rationale baked in. Next Claude session has no questions
to ask the user before starting Wave A.

commits.title: fix(atlas): inherit LC_COLLATE from template1 on database create (#49)
commits.body:
fix(atlas): inherit LC_COLLATE from template1 on database create (#49)

Smoke on prod surfaced `ERROR: invalid LC_COLLATE locale name:
"en_US.utf8"` — Postgres 16+ rejects the legacy lowercased form some
defaults resolve to. The request shouldn't fail just because the
fallback locale doesn't match the cluster's available set.

- validation: `collation` is now optional (no default); callers that
  need a specific locale pass the canonical form ("en_US.UTF-8" etc.)
  explicitly.
- service: omits the `LC_COLLATE` clause when caller didn't set one, so
  the new database inherits from template1.
- store row records "(inherited)" when caller didn't override — the
  observer wave will replace this with the actual `pg_database.datcollate`.
- validation test asserts the default is now undefined.

Tested locally; awaiting prod smoke.

commits.body:
fix(atlas): default CREATE DATABASE template to template0 (#50)

Smoke on prod hit `new encoding (UTF8) is incompatible with the encoding
of the template database (SQL_ASCII)` — the cluster's template1 is
SQL_ASCII, so it can't seed a UTF8 database. template0 is the canonical
"clean slate, custom encoding" target (Postgres docs §22.3) and works
even when template1 is custom-tuned.

Callers that explicitly want template1 (e.g. to inherit installed
extensions) pass it as `template: "template1"` in the request body.

Test plan: redeploy; create wave_b_smoke via curl; verify with \\l in
the LXC; drop.

commits.title: fix(atlas): rename atlas_databases.collation column → lc_collate (#48)
commits.body:
fix(atlas): rename atlas_databases.collation column → lc_collate (#48)

`collation` is a SQL-reserved word — unquoted, real Postgres rejects
the CREATE TABLE with a syntax error. pg-mem accepts it, so this only
surfaced when applying 0015 to the prod developy_mgmt cluster.

- Migration: column renamed to `lc_collate` (mirrors Postgres'
  `CREATE DATABASE ... LC_COLLATE` option name).
- Drizzle schema: column SQL name is `lc_collate`, JS property stays
  `collation` so the AtlasDatabase domain type, the postgres-adapter
  mappers, the validation schemas, the API JSON, and the UI all keep
  using the friendlier name unchanged.

Atlas tests still green (55 unit pass). Wave B migration was rolled
back on the failure (CREATE TABLE never committed), so re-applying
this fixed file is the only step needed in prod.

Adds per-cluster firewall rules backing pg_hba.conf. Schema, store SPI,
postgres adapter, validation, and service ops all wired. Provisioner gains
regeneratePgHba — single source-of-truth function rebuilding the whole
pg_hba.conf from the rule table + a hard-coded lockout-safety block, then
SELECT pg_reload_conf() (no restart).

Lockout safety: 172.10.0.150/32 (developy-web LXC) is ALWAYS appended,
never user-controllable. Removing every user rule still leaves the app
able to manage the cluster.

Mesh integration: rules can carry sourcePoolId. At apply time the live
pool CIDR is resolved from mesh/store.getIPPool — so editing the pool's
CIDR propagates to all clusters using it without UI edits. Snapshot
CIDR persists as audit + fallback.

  - starter: 10 rules
  - growth: 50
  - enterprise: unlimited

needed at apps/web/src/app/api/atlas/[...path]/route.ts. Smoke test
deferred until UI lands.

commits.title: feat(atlas): Wave E retro-sync DNS + Wave G.1 backups (Proxmox local snapshots)
commits.body:
feat(atlas): Wave E retro-sync DNS + Wave G.1 backups (Proxmox local snapshots)

Two follow-ups from the previous PR:

Wave E retro-sync (legacy clusters get DNS)
  - POST /api/atlas/clusters/:id/dns/sync — re-extracts primary IP from
    cluster.endpoint, calls Beacon to upsert AAAA/A, persists dns_name
  - syncClusterDnsRecord exported from provisioner so service can dispatch
    it for rows that pre-date Wave E (or where the initial sync failed)
  - UI: when cluster.dnsName is null, Overview shows "Sync DNS now" button
    instead of the FQDN. Single click → toast with the assigned name.
  - Atlas API gains GET (via cluster detail) — no new GET route needed,
    dnsName flows through the existing cluster row.

Wave G.1 backups (on-demand snapshots → Proxmox local)
  - Schema 0019: atlas_backups table (cluster_id FK CASCADE, type,
    status running|completed|failed, storage_kind proxmox_local|rsync|
    download_only, storage_location, size_bytes, started_at, finished_at,
    error_message, initiated_by) + index on (cluster_id, started_at)
  - Adapter: full row↔domain mapper, upsertOne/deleteOne wired
  - Provisioner:
      * runProxmoxLocalBackup — pg_dumpall|gzip inside LXC → pct pull
        to /var/lib/vz/dump/atlas-<id>-<ts>.sql.gz on the host node
        (uses remote.node() for correct cluster-routing of pct commands)
      * deleteProxmoxLocalBackup — rm the file, guards against
        directory escape
  - Service:
      * listAtlasBackups — replaces the v1 stub (no more fake fixtures)
      * createAtlasBackup — inserts row in "running", dispatches the
        actual snapshot async with status update on completion / failure
      * deleteAtlasBackup — drops bytes first (best-effort), then row
  - Validation: CreateBackupSchema + DeleteBackupSchema
  - Routes: POST + DELETE under /clusters/:id/backups
  - Hook: useCreateAtlasBackup, useDeleteAtlasBackup
  - UI: new <BackupsTab> with polling while a backup is running, size/
    duration formatters, delete confirmation showing original error
  - AtlasBackup domain type unified: hook + service + store all reference
    the canonical store shape (was 3 different versions of the interface)

commits.title: fix(beacon): route record CRUD through DnsBackend so UI writes are visible (#55)
commits.body:
fix(beacon): route record CRUD through DnsBackend so UI writes are visible (#55)

POST/PUT/DELETE on /api/beacon/zones/:id/records used to write to the local
meta store and then attempt a best-effort sync to PowerDNS via the cluster
node's HTTP API. The GET path reads through the configured DnsBackend
(PowerDNS via BEACON_DATABASE_URL in prod), so any write that bypassed the
backend appeared to succeed (201) but vanished on the next refresh — the UI
showed no error and the new record never appeared in the list.

Route record CRUD through getDnsBackend() when one is configured. The
legacy local-store path stays as fallback for the json-only dev mode.

Adds route-level regression tests covering POST/PUT/DELETE round-trip
through a MockDnsBackend.

commits.title: fix(wpp): normalize media mimetype before file-storage upload
commits.body:
fix(wpp): normalize media mimetype before file-storage upload

WhatsApp media mimetypes carry codec parameters (e.g. "audio/ogg; codecs=opus")
that fail file-storage's exact-match mime allowlist, so createFile was rejected
with a ZodError and wpp_messages.mediaFileId stayed null for every audio.

Strip parameters to the base type ("audio/ogg") before calling createFile, and
reuse the same normalized value for the presigned PUT Content-Type — the upload
URL is signed with that ContentType, so the two must match or S3 rejects the PUT.

Verified end-to-end (audio/ogg, image/jpeg, video/mp4 all stored). Does not
change the lazy on-demand download behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(email): expose native inbox category (Outlook Focused/Other + Gmail tabs) (#151)

* fix(email/calendar): point OAuth callback at standalone (:7621/:7620), not monolith :3099

The bootstrap provider-configs baked redirect_uri = http://localhost:3099/... (old
monolith). Standalone runs email on :7621 and calendar on :7620, so that callback
404s and OAuth can't complete.

- scripts/fix-oauth-callback-standalone.ts: idempotent, REVERSIBLE rewrite of the
  redirect_uri inside the encrypted email/calendar provider-config credentials.
  Backs up the exact prior ciphertext (byte-exact restore, no master key needed) and
  is parameterized by callback host (EMAIL/CALENDAR_CALLBACK_BASE) so prod can target
  a public https callback instead of the dev localhost one. Supports --dry-run / --restore.
- email-oauth-bootstrap.ts: HOST is env-driven (EMAIL_BB_HOST) defaulting to the
  standalone :7621 so a re-bootstrap can't reintroduce :3099.

Applied to dev org b0000000-…001 (2 email configs → :7621). Prod uses its own configs
(public https), so this is dev-scoped. Backup json gitignored (holds ciphertext).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(calendar): create dev CalendarProviderConfig reusing email OAuth creds

The standalone calendar module had no provider-config (GET …/provider-configs → []),
so /calendar/connect 503'd. This adds an idempotent script that creates Google +
Outlook calendar configs by reusing the client_id/client_secret already stored in the
email configs (one OAuth app to configure, not two), with the :7620 callback + calendar
scopes. Parameterized by CALENDAR_CALLBACK_BASE for prod (public https). Additive +
reversible (soft-delete the config to revert).

Verified via the operacao-digital app proxy: /calendar/connect GOOGLE+OUTLOOK now return real
authorizationUrls (redirect_uri=…:7620, calendar scopes).

commits.body:
fix(dev:standalone): garante o MinIO up+saudável antes de subir file-storage

Toda vez que a máquina reinicia, o container building-blocks-minio-alt (criado à
mão fora do compose p/ usar :9002, já que :9000 é do Whisper) ficava com
restart=no e não subia. O file-storage então bootava sem S3, nunca reconectava,
e quebrava mídia de chat + áudio do "Resumo do dia" da operacao-digital — sempre o mesmo
erro, fix manual (docker start) toda vez.

Agora dev:standalone tem um preflight ensureMinio() (idempotente) que, quando o
conjunto inclui file-storage ou wpp-session-worker:
- start do container existente (ou docker run recriando em vol nomeado se sumiu);
- espera o health (:<porta>/minio/health/live, ~15s) — porta vem do S3_ENDPOINT;
- seta --restart unless-stopped (sobrevive a reboots futuros);
- garante o bucket (best-effort via mc; file-storage também cria no boot).
Degrada com aviso se docker faltar; não toca no fluxo monolith.

Testado: docker stop minio → dev:standalone file-storage → MinIO sobe sozinho,
saudável em :9002, restart=unless-stopped.

commits.title: fix(ipam): collision-free LXC IPv4 allocation (scan in-use IPs)
commits.body:
fix(ipam): collision-free LXC IPv4 allocation (scan in-use IPs)

Root cause of the 2026-06-08 mgmt-db outage: two independent allocators wrote
the same /24. `vmidToIp(vmid)=172.10.0.(vmid%256)` handed data-product LXCs IPs
already held by platform-static services — herald(151)→.151 collided with
atlas-mgmt-01, blaze(150)→.150 with developy-quickstart — intermittently
killing the control-plane store (ECONNREFUSED → atlas_clusters INTERNAL_ERROR).

- add `allocateLxcIp(node,vmid)`: scans cluster /cluster/resources + per-guest
  net configs for in-use last-octets, picks the first free one (pure
  `pickFreeOctet`, starts at vmid%256 for stable allocations, skips
  used+reserved+.0/.255). Falls back to vmidToIp on scan error.
- swap all data-product provisioners (spark/blaze/nexus/flux/ignite/herald/
  tide/beacon) from `vmidToIp` to `await allocateLxcIp`. Atlas untouched
  (uses the mesh pool).
- tests for pickFreeOctet (incl. the .151 regression).

This is the FAST fix. The durable design (data-products on IPv6 + single IPv4
ingress) is specced in docs/ipam-ipv6-migration.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.title: fix(spark): pin reliable DNS so valkey/memcached install can resolve repos
commits.body:
fix(spark): pin reliable DNS so valkey/memcached install can resolve repos

Spark cluster provisioning failed with "Could not resolve host:
packages.valkey.io". Root cause: createLxcContainer only sets the LXC
nameserver when config.nameserver is truthy, and Spark passes
process.env.DATA_PRODUCTS_NAMESERVER, which is unset on the deployed
control-plane — so the container inherited the node's ISP resolvers, which
fail for external package repos. (Atlas is unaffected: it sources nameservers
from the Mesh network pool, and Postgres needs no external repo.)

Two belt-and-suspenders fixes:
- Default the LXC nameserver to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 when DATA_PRODUCTS_NAMESERVER
  is empty.
- Pin /etc/resolv.conf inside the container before any apt/curl (valkey and
  memcached paths), so install is deterministic regardless of host config.

Repro: created operacao-digital-cache-stg (valkey-sentinel, xs) on sp1-sd-catalisatec-1
→ status=failed; Herald showed the curl resolve error on LXC 156.

commits.title: feat(create): mandatory network + IP selection on VM/CT create, via Mesh IPAM (#66)
commits.body:
feat(create): mandatory network + IP selection on VM/CT create, via Mesh IPAM (#66)

Creating a VM/CT now requires picking a client network and gets a real IP,
reusing Mesh as the single source of truth — no parallel allocator.

UX (shared NetworkStep, used by both VM and Container wizards):
- <NetworkSelect> (existing) to pick a bridge-backed Mesh network — required
- IP auto-filled from the next free address (useSuggestIP), editable, with a
  live availability indicator (useCheckIPAvailability)
- "+ New" opens <CreateNetworkDialog> to generate a network inline (BYO CIDR or
  rent/carve), reusing useCreateMeshIPPool / useCarveSubPool — no leaving the flow

Allocation goes through Mesh IPAM exactly like the data products: on submit the
wizard reserves the IP (serviceId = `vm:<id>` / `ct:<id>`) and rolls the
reservation back if the Proxmox create fails. IP is applied as cloud-init
ipconfig0 (VM) or net0 ip=/gw= (LXC), with bridge/gateway/prefix derived from
the pool.

Mesh change (minimal, no new endpoint): createIPAllocation accepts infra
resource refs (`vm:`/`ct:`) — skipping the traffic-service existence check while
keeping all IPAM business rules — and an optional specific `address`
(reserveSpecificAddress) for the "pick your own IP" path. Traffic-service
allocations are unchanged. Covered by 2 new mesh-api tests; full mesh suite green.

Co-authored-by: Klederson Bueno <klederson@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.title: fix(tags): sanitize Proxmox tags — colons/accents/spaces broke VM/CT create (#65)
commits.body:
fix(tags): sanitize Proxmox tags — colons/accents/spaces broke VM/CT create (#65)

Auto-tags were built as `env:prod`, `role:web`, `depends-on:123`. The colon
is not a valid Proxmox tag character (default pve-tag style allows only
[A-Za-z0-9_+.-]), so every create/update with an env or role set was rejected
with "invalid format - invalid characters in tag" — failing by default, before
the user typed anything. Accents (produção) and spaces in custom tags hit the
same wall.

New lib/tags.ts sanitizeTag/sanitizeTags slugifies tags (strip accents, invalid
runs -> "-", trim edges). Applied at every tag write path: VM create, CT create,
VM/CT config edit, dependency tagging, and the TagEditor add handler (so the
badge shown matches what the API accepts). Unit-tested.

Completes the clone-from-template + auto-start work:

  useContainerAction, so a newly created container comes up running like the
  VM path already does.

commits.body:
fix(mesh): family-aware child prefixes in inline network create dialog (#70)

The "Rent from platform" mode hardcoded IPv4 child prefixes (/24../29) and
IPv4 address math, so renting from an IPv6 parent (e.g. the default
2804:1740:f:2000::/56 pool) offered invalid sizes — picking /25 failed with
"Child prefix /25 must be longer than parent /56".

Now the subnet-size options are derived from the selected parent: IPv6 parents
get IPv6 prefixes (/60../124), IPv4 parents get /24../30, and only prefixes
strictly more specific than the parent are shown. The selected size resets to a
valid one when the parent changes, and the address-count label is family-aware.

availability check still used a hextet-string compare (ceil(prefixLen/16)
groups) that wrongly rejected valid hosts in non-16-aligned pools (e.g. /120)
and was fragile vs ::-compressed forms — so the wizard's IP-availability
indicator still failed for carved IPv6 pools. Replace with a bigint prefix

commits.title: fix(create): drop per-NIC firewall (default off, remove toggle) — it breaks NAT egress (#68)
commits.body:
fix(create): drop per-NIC firewall (default off, remove toggle) — it breaks NAT egress (#68)

The VM/Container create wizards defaulted firewall=1 on net0, which makes
Proxmox build a firewall bridge (fwbr) in front of the NIC. On this cluster
that fwbr breaks the NAT/conntrack path for the guest: the masquerade rule
matches but nf_nat never translates the source, so the packet egresses the WAN
bridge with its private IP and gets no reply — every wizard-created VM/CT lost
internet access (and the cicustom guest-agent install in PR #67 failed for the
same reason).

Confirmed empirically: a guest with firewall=1 has no egress; flipping it to
firewall=0 restores egress immediately (ping + https + apt). NAT itself is fine
(other internal guests without the firewall translate and reach the internet).

Cluster/node firewall is disabled here and traffic policy lives in Mesh, so the
per-NIC firewall provided no real filtering — only the broken NAT path. Remove
the firewall toggle from both wizards and never add firewall=1 to net0.

Co-authored-by: Klederson Bueno <klederson@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.title: fix(mesh): respect carve min-delta in network create child sizes (#71)
commits.body:
fix(mesh): respect carve min-delta in network create child sizes (#71)

The inline network dialog offered child prefixes (e.g. IPv6 /60, /64) that the
carve engine rejects: it requires the child to be more specific than the parent
by at least MIN_DELTA bits — 1 for IPv4, 16 for IPv6 — within the family max.
So an IPv6 /56 parent needs at least /72, but /60 failed with
"Child /60 is too large for parent /56 (ipv6, min delta 16)".

childOptions now filters candidates by `child - parent >= minDelta` (and `<= max`),
matching the engine, so only carve-able sizes are shown (/56 → /72,/80,/96,…).

commits.title: fix(mesh): suggestRandomAddress respects IPv6 prefix length (#72)
commits.body:
fix(mesh): suggestRandomAddress respects IPv6 prefix length (#72)

The IPv6 branch hardcoded a /56 layout (randomizing the 4th hextet + host),
so suggesting an address for a carved sub-pool produced an out-of-range IP —
e.g. a /72 pool 2804:1740:f:2000:100::/72 suggested 2804:1740:f:201f::… (in
the parent /56, not the child). The wizard's availability check then rejected
every suggestion ("already allocated"), blocking IPv6 network creation.

Now it picks a random offset via bigint within the pool's real host range
(128 − prefixLen), reusing ipv6ToBigInt/bigIntToIpv6 like enumerateIPv6Addresses,
capped to JS-safe precision. Always in-CIDR for any prefix. IPv4 unchanged.

commits.title: fix(test): unwrap idempotent-migration guards for pg-mem (#79)
commits.body:
fix(test): unwrap idempotent-migration guards for pg-mem (#79)

PR #75 made migrations 0013–0017 idempotent by wrapping CREATE TYPE / ADD
CONSTRAINT in `DO $$ BEGIN <ddl>; EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN null;
END $$;` and using IF NOT EXISTS. The pg-mem test harness strips ALL `DO $$ ...
$$` blocks (originally for migration 0010's data-cleanup PL/pgSQL), so the
wrapped CREATE TYPE was being removed — the enum type never got created and the
following `ADD COLUMN ... "mesh_ip_pool_source"` failed. This broke the
pg-mem-backed db tests (db.test, postgres-backend, store-backend).

Fix the sanitizer: before the blanket DO-block strip, unwrap the
duplicate_object guard blocks to their inner DDL (so CREATE TYPE / ADD
CONSTRAINT still apply) and drop the IF NOT EXISTS clauses (no-ops on a fresh
DB). Migrations are unchanged — they stay idempotent for prod.

commits.title: fix(create): push pool DNS servers to static-IP guests (VM + CT)
commits.body:
fix(create): push pool DNS servers to static-IP guests (VM + CT)

E2e on real Proxmox surfaced a DNS gap once guests actually boot an OS: a
static-IP guest has no DHCP to learn DNS from, so it comes up with internet
reachable *by IP* but unable to resolve hostnames — apt, the guest-agent
install, everything by name fails. An IPv6-only guest is worse: it inherits
the host's IPv4 nameservers, which it can't even reach.

- VM create: set cloud-init `nameserver` from the selected Mesh pool's
  nameservers (both template-clone and ISO paths).
- CT create: when the DNS field is left blank, default `nameserver` to the
  pool's servers instead of the host's (unreachable) resolv.conf.

Verified end-to-end: fresh clone of template 9000 boots, resolves
cloudflare.com over IPv6, `curl https://one.one.one.one` → HTTP/2 200, and the
qemu-guest-agent auto-installs on first boot (Ubuntu 24.04). CT with pool
nameservers resolves DNS after the IPv6 servers land in resolv.conf.

fix(mesh,test): triage spark/02 (stale) + ipam /120 suggest (real bug) (#80)

1. spark/02 (stale test): asserted the credential passwordHash equals
   SHA-256(password), but the service intentionally switched to bcrypt
   ("never store ... a fast unsalted digest", service.ts). Update the test to
   verify the hash is bcrypt ($2*) and bcrypt.compare()s against the plaintext.

2. ipam-engine suggestRandomAddress (real bug): the IPv6 offset was
   `random(0..span-1) + 1` = [1, span] — the max (span) overshoots into the

   suggest base+256 = ::100, outside the ::00–::ff range, which
   isAddressAvailable then rejected. Pick the offset in [1, span-1] instead.
   Fixes the "suggests in-range addresses for a narrow /120 pool" regression.

   (typecheck error) — corrected to `Mesh.TrafficService`.

commits.title: fix(spark): deprovisioner must not swallow LXC delete failures (#78)
commits.body:
fix(spark): deprovisioner must not swallow LXC delete failures (#78)

A failed `pct destroy` (e.g. the stale-dm `lvremove ... in use` case) was only
console.error'd; the cluster was then marked `deleted` and a `success` Herald
event emitted unconditionally — so the container survived as an untracked
orphan while the system reported the cluster gone. This is how the 2026-06-09
smoke left CTs 160/164/165/166 behind (docs/storage-and-node-placement.md §5).

Now: track which LXCs failed to delete; IP/DNS cleanup still runs best-effort;
but if any container survived, mark the cluster `failed` (a DELETABLE state, so
the delete can be retried — the stale-dm case needs a node reboot first), emit a
`failure` event with the orphaned vmids, and throw. Only a fully-removed cluster
becomes `deleted`/`success`. Mirrors the existing provision-failure path.

Adds a regression test (real JSON store + mocked Proxmox boundary).

commits.body:
fix(deploy): add basePath prefix to MODULE_*_URL in prod stack

The standalone basePath migration mounts every service under /{service}
(e.g. /webhooks-engine), but the prod stack's inter-module MODULE_*_URL
env vars still pointed at bare http://<service>:3000. Module-to-module
HTTP calls (notably wpp-business -> webhooks-engine createSubscription)
404'd with a text/plain body -> "Failed to parse JSON" -> dispatcher never
registered -> inbound WhatsApp webhooks never delivered to the panel ->
MESSAGE_RECEIVED workflows stopped firing in prod.

Add the basePath to each MODULE_*_URL so URLs match the served routes:
  MODULE_IAM_URL -> /iam, MODULE_WEBHOOKS_ENGINE_URL -> /webhooks-engine,
  MODULE_DECISION_ENGINE_URL -> /decision-engine, MODULE_WPP_URL -> /wpp

Makes the live hotfix permanent so the next `docker stack deploy
bb-production` doesn't revert it.

  POST /api/harbor/repositories/<name…>/tags/<tag>/scan (registry:pull, tenant-scoped).

  C/H/M/L vuln badges + a per-tag Scan button.

feat(harbor): Phase 3 — tag retention policies (multi-tenant) (#93)

Auto-prune old tags per policy. Multi-tenant: a policy belongs to a namespace
(=org); CRUD + apply gated by registry:delete for that namespace (it deletes, so
admin-level like manual delete). The operator baseline spans all namespaces.

- retention.ts: pure computeTagsToDelete (keepLast protects N newest; maxAgeDays
  prunes the rest; undatable tags never pruned by age — fail safe) + applyPolicy
  (lists repos in the namespace, prunes via the delete path) + applyRetentionForRepo.
- Auto-runs on push (events route triggers retention for the pushed repo,
  non-blocking); manual "Apply now" endpoint too.
- Stores share one encrypted file via harbor-json-store.ts (webhooks + retention);
  webhook-store refactored onto it.
- Registry datasource resolveTag now reads the image config blob for the real
  `created` (pushedAt) + os/arch — needed for recency ordering, also fills the
  "Pushed" column in registry mode.
- API: GET/POST /api/harbor/retention, DELETE [id], POST [id]/apply; hooks + a
  /harbor/retention page (+ nav). 5 new tests (keep-last, age, combined, fail-safe).
  23 Harbor tests green.

GC to reclaim blob disk after pruning is a follow-up (registry garbage-collect).

commits.title: feat(harbor): Phase 2a — Registry v2 token service (Aegis-backed) (#89)
commits.body:
feat(harbor): Phase 2a — Registry v2 token service (Aegis-backed) (#89)

Implements the Docker Registry v2 token auth service so `docker login`/pull/push
authenticate against Aegis. No JWT dependency — RS256 + x5c signed with node:crypto.

- `registry-token.ts`: RS256 JWT signer (x5c header) + payload decode.
- `registry-scopes.ts`: parse Docker scope strings, namespace (=org) extraction,
  entitlement→granted-actions mapping (registry:pull/push/delete).
- `GET /api/harbor/token` (the registry `realm`): Basic-auth password = a platform
  bearer; resolves the subject's registry entitlements per namespace (baseline ∪
  IAM role) and issues a scoped JWT. Returns 503 until HARBOR_TOKEN_KEY/CERT set,
  so deploying this is inert until the registry is switched to token auth.
- `POST /api/harbor/registry-token`: mints a 24h `docker login` credential for the
  logged-in user (reuses issueSession, like the bun ship CLI token).
- IAM roles gain registry:pull/push/delete (viewer=pull, member=pull+push,
  admin/owner=+delete).
- Registry datasource: when the app holds the signing key it self-signs a short
  read token for server-side catalog reads, so switching the registry to
  `auth: token` won't break the Harbor UI.

Tests: 7 new (scope parsing, entitlement mapping, real RS256 signature verify).
Phase 2b wires the keys + flips the live registry (skopeo-verified) + ingress.

  detail (tags/digests/sizes, catch-all `[...name]` since repo names have slashes).

security plane — console login + entitlements for the UI, Registry v2 token service

commits.body:
feat(harbor): Phase 3 — push/delete webhooks (multi-tenant) (#92)

Registry push/delete events fan out to user-configured webhooks, fully
tenant-scoped: a webhook belongs to a namespace (=org), and an event for
`org/repo` only ever reaches that tenant's webhooks. A caller sees/manages only
webhooks for namespaces they can push to (operator baseline spans all).

- `POST /api/harbor/events`: Distribution `notifications` sink (shared-secret via
  HARBOR_EVENTS_SECRET); keeps tagged manifest push/delete events and dispatches.
- `webhook-store.ts`: encrypted JSON store (.harbor-store.json), CRUD + delivery
  status. `webhook-delivery.ts`: namespace/repo matching + HMAC-SHA256 signed
  POST (X-Harbor-Signature).
- `GET/POST /api/harbor/webhooks` + `DELETE /api/harbor/webhooks/[id]`: session +
  registry:push for the namespace (tenant isolation); secret returned only on create.
- Shared `authz.ts` (hasRegistryEntitlement) — also now used by the delete route.
- Hooks + a /harbor/webhooks management page (+ nav entry).
- Tests: tenant-isolated matching (cross-tenant excluded), repoPattern, enabled/
  event filters, HMAC signing. 18 Harbor tests green.

Registry-side `notifications` config + HARBOR_EVENTS_SECRET wiring done at deploy.

commits.title: fix(spark): IPv6 cluster support — bind, DNS-probe timeout, no duplicate IPs (#97)
commits.body:
fix(spark): IPv6 cluster support — bind, DNS-probe timeout, no duplicate IPs (#97)

* fix(spark): bind valkey/sentinel/memcached on IPv6 too (not 0.0.0.0-only)

A valkey-sentinel cluster created on an IPv6 Mesh pool failed at provisioning:
'Sentinel verification failed: connected_slaves:0'. The primary listened only on
0.0.0.0 (`bind 0.0.0.0`/`-l 0.0.0.0` = IPv4-only), so replicas — reaching it by
its IPv6 address — could never attach. Confirmed via ss -ltn inside the primary
(LISTEN 0.0.0.0:6379 only).

- valkey + sentinel: `bind * -::*` (all IPv4 AND IPv6; `-` makes the v6 bind
  non-fatal on IPv4-only hosts).
- memcached: `-l 0.0.0.0,::`.
Adds an IPv6 sentinelConf regression test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(spark): timeout DNS probe + delete LXCs on provision failure (no duplicate IPs)

Two issues surfaced validating IPv6 provisioning:

- aptSetup's wait-for-DNS used a bare `getent`, which hangs indefinitely when
  the (IPv6) resolver is unreachable — wedging the whole provision in
  'configuring' forever. Wrap each probe in `timeout 5` so the loop always
  completes and apt fails cleanly (caught) instead of hanging.

- On provision failure we released the Mesh IP allocations but left the created
  LXCs running. The next cluster then reserved the same 'freed' address while the
  orphan container still held it → DUPLICATE IP (two CTs on 2804:...::401), which
  broke IPv6 egress on the newcomer. Now: delete each LXC first, and release its
  allocation ONLY if the delete succeeded (a survivor keeps its IP reserved).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(spark): deprovision keeps IP reserved when LXC delete fails (stale-dm)

Same duplicate-IP guard as the provision-failure path, now on the delete path:
#78 released every Mesh allocation unconditionally, even for containers that
survived a stale-dm 'lvremove ... in use'. The surviving LXC still holds its IP,
so the next cluster could reserve the same address. Release only allocations
whose LXC was actually removed; keep the rest reserved until a node reboot frees
the container.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ignite): OCI image flow — build source → push to Harbor → pull to run (#98)

Wires Ignite to the Harbor registry: a function's source is built into an OCI
image, pushed to registry.developy.cloud/ignite/<org>/<fn> (auto-scanned by
Trivy), and the function pulls that image to run. Multi-tenant via orgId.

- store: IgniteFunction gains imageRef/imageDigest/buildStatus/buildError/
  buildNumber/lastBuiltAt.
- build.ts: buildFunctionImage() calls a build agent (IGNITE_BUILD_URL +
  IGNITE_BUILD_SECRET) with the source + a short-lived "ignite" push bearer
  (colon-free username); image repo = ignite/<org>/<fn>, tag = build number.
- API: POST /api/ignite/functions/:id/build (write + tenant-gated; always 200,
  buildStatus conveys outcome).
- provisioner: when imageRef is set, install Docker + login + pull + run the
  image (port 8080) instead of apt-installing a bare runtime.
- hook useBuildIgniteFunction + a Source & image card on the function detail
  page (editor, Build & push, status badge, image ref, "view scan in Harbor").

The build agent (buildah + runtime base images) is provisioned on the registry
CT at deploy.

without creating a second connection; advisory-lock.ts now uses
sql.reserve() / reserved.unsafe(...) / reserved.release().

commits.title: fix(beacon): SOA serial overflow from BIGINT-as-string concat (#107)
commits.body:
fix(beacon): SOA serial overflow from BIGINT-as-string concat (#107)

* docs: Beacon DNS outage 2026-06-12 incident + runbook

Two root causes (not the VM): (1) systemd-resolved stole :53 from PowerDNS on
ns1 CT 123 → intermittent SERVFAIL; (2) SOA serial overflowed uint32 on
developy.cloud/io (record content + domains.notified_serial) → REFUSED.
Live fixes, preventive scan, and follow-ups (serial-gen code fix, dup ::10
decom, IPv4 glue, mask resolved in template).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(beacon): SOA serial overflow from BIGINT-as-string concat

node-postgres returns BIGINT (domains.notified_serial) as a string, so
bumpSerial's `oldSerial + 1` concatenated ("2026061201" + 1 → "20260612011")
instead of incrementing — appending a digit per zone mutation until the serial
blew past the 32-bit ceiling. PowerDNS then REFUSED the zone (developy.cloud,
developy.io), taking the platform domain + a tenant zone NXDOMAIN on 2026-06-12.

- add pure nextSerial() helper: coerce to number, cap at MAX_DNS_SERIAL,
  fall back to today's serial for corrupt/overflowed inputs
- coerce notified_serial reads in getDomain/listDomains
- sql-fake now returns notified_serial as a string (mirrors pg) so the
  regression is actually exercised
- unit tests for nextSerial + an end-to-end overflow regression test

Verified: reintroducing the bug fails the new e2e test; fix → 19/19 pass.
Incident write-up in docs/incidents/2026-06-12-beacon-dns-outage.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(file-storage): internal-endpoint presigned upload URLs for server-side callers

In-cluster server-side consumers (e.g. wpp-session-worker materializing WhatsApp
media) PUT the bytes themselves, but presigned upload URLs were always signed
against S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT — unreachable from inside the swarm (ConnectionRefused/
timeout) → media never materialized → GET /messages/media 202-eternal → transcribe
failed. Exposed once the WPP session-affinity fix routed DOWNLOAD_MEDIA to the
owning replica.

Deterministic, automatic selection: upload URLs for the internal file-storage
facade user (INTERNAL_FILE_STORAGE_USER_ID, the server-to-server sentinel) are
signed against the internal S3 endpoint; external clients and all download URLs
keep the public endpoint. No per-call flag, no per-env hack. Docs in
docs/file-storage-internal-presigned-urls.md.

commits.title: fix(workflows): make CONDITIONAL multi-branch routing corruption-proof
commits.body:
fix(workflows): make CONDITIONAL multi-branch routing corruption-proof

Root cause: when the visual builder loaded a workflow, apiToCanvas reconstructed
CONDITIONAL branch edges from dependsOn ["<cond>:N"] but only handled the boolean
true/false case — every NUMERIC branch index collapsed to branch-1 (branchName
"False"). The next save persisted that collapse into both dependsOn and layout.edges,
so all multi-branch (>2) routing silently broke (every branch routed to index 1).

Fixes (generic, single source of truth = sourceHandle):
- apiToCanvas: reconstruct numeric branch indices and the "default"/else branch
  correctly, pulling the real branch name from config; dedup with the
  branch.actions edge pass. (the actual defect)
- edge-graph.service (graph executor, the live path): derive the canonical
  index-based edgeType from sourceHandle FIRST, so a stale/denormalized
  data.edgeType can never override the real branch; drop the name-based form
  that could never match ConditionalRouter.determineEdgeType (branch:<index>).
- dag-executor: when a target declares an explicit branch dependency, defer the
  eager layout-edge skip to the reliable matchedIndex + dependsOn gating, so
  execution is independent of stale layout edges.
- scripts/repair-conditional-routing.ts: conservative audit/repair for already
  corrupted workflows — recovers the mapping from the authoritative sourceHandle
  (or declarative branch.actions) and normalizes all three representations; flags
  anything ambiguous for manual review instead of guessing. Dry-run by default.

Tests:
- apiToCanvas.test.ts: 5-branch reconstruction + apiToCanvas↔canvasToApi round-trip
  proves a builder save preserves rota:0..4 (regression lock).
- edge-graph.service.spec: index-based edgeType + corruption-proof derivation
  (stale data.edgeType ignored in favor of sourceHandle).

commits.title: fix(workflows): make CONDITIONAL multi-branch routing corruption-proof (#322)
commits.body:
fix(workflows): make CONDITIONAL multi-branch routing corruption-proof (#322)

Root cause: when the visual builder loaded a workflow, apiToCanvas reconstructed
CONDITIONAL branch edges from dependsOn ["<cond>:N"] but only handled the boolean
true/false case — every NUMERIC branch index collapsed to branch-1 (branchName
"False"). The next save persisted that collapse into both dependsOn and layout.edges,
so all multi-branch (>2) routing silently broke (every branch routed to index 1).

Fixes (generic, single source of truth = sourceHandle):
- apiToCanvas: reconstruct numeric branch indices and the "default"/else branch
  correctly, pulling the real branch name from config; dedup with the
  branch.actions edge pass. (the actual defect)
- edge-graph.service (graph executor, the live path): derive the canonical
  index-based edgeType from sourceHandle FIRST, so a stale/denormalized
  data.edgeType can never override the real branch; drop the name-based form
  that could never match ConditionalRouter.determineEdgeType (branch:<index>).
- dag-executor: when a target declares an explicit branch dependency, defer the
  eager layout-edge skip to the reliable matchedIndex + dependsOn gating, so
  execution is independent of stale layout edges.
- scripts/repair-conditional-routing.ts: conservative audit/repair for already
  corrupted workflows — recovers the mapping from the authoritative sourceHandle
  (or declarative branch.actions) and normalizes all three representations; flags
  anything ambiguous for manual review instead of guessing. Dry-run by default.

Tests:
- apiToCanvas.test.ts: 5-branch reconstruction + apiToCanvas↔canvasToApi round-trip
  proves a builder save preserves rota:0..4 (regression lock).
- edge-graph.service.spec: index-based edgeType + corruption-proof derivation
  (stale data.edgeType ignored in favor of sourceHandle).

commits.title: fix(calendar): expand date-only single-day window for getSchedule
commits.body:
fix(calendar): expand date-only single-day window for getSchedule

A single-day slot query arrives as startDate === endDate; both are
date-only and resolve to midnight, so getSchedule received
startTime === endTime (a zero-length window) and returned an error
("Failed to get Outlook busy periods"). Expand date-only bounds to cover
the full day — start at 00:00:00, end at 23:59:59 — matching the legacy
calendar-outlook-api. Range queries are unaffected.

commits.title: fix(calendar): convert Outlook getSchedule busy times to UTC instants
commits.body:
fix(calendar): convert Outlook getSchedule busy times to UTC instants

getBusyPeriods read scheduleItem times (bare local-clock strings) straight
into CanonicalBusyPeriod, so downstream `new Date(...)` interpreted them as
UTC — shifting every busy block by the local↔UTC delta and blocking the
wrong slots (e.g. a 17:00 meeting blocked the 14:00 slot while the real
15:00 lunch stayed bookable).

Pin the getSchedule response timezone with `Prefer: outlook.timezone` and
convert each busy boundary to a UTC instant via parseInTimezone in the
mapper. Mirrors the legacy calendar-outlook-api behaviour.

commits.title: fix(calendar): use connected account email for Outlook free/busy
commits.body:
fix(calendar): use connected account email for Outlook free/busy

OutlookProvider.getBusyPeriods called MS Graph getSchedule with
schedules: ['me']. 'me' is not a resolvable SMTP address, so Graph
returned an empty (all-free) schedule and every slot looked available —
causing the scheduler agent to offer times that conflict with real
meetings (double-booking).

Thread the connection's externalEmail through CalendarProviderOptions and
use it in getSchedule. Fail loudly when the email is absent instead of
silently returning no busy periods. Google provider already uses /freeBusy
correctly and is unaffected.

request failed 100% of the time. The downstream calendar service treats the
range as inclusive, so start === end correctly yields that single day —
only a strictly-earlier endDate is invalid.

fix(bulk): archive/activate must patch `active`, not `isActive`

The shared bulk-actions hook (`runToggleActive`) sent
`{ patch: { isActive } }` to `/:resource/bulk-update`. The backend forwards
the patch as-is to `prisma.<model>.update({ data })`, but every model that
exposes archive/activate (Workflow, Agent, CustomAction, CaptureLink) names
the boolean column `active` — there is no `isActive`. Prisma rejected the
unknown argument, so bulk archive/activate failed (500) on all four pages in
every environment.

Fix the patch field to `active`. No backend or schema change needed.

commits.title: fix(wpp): normalize pairing-code phone to digits (strip '+' → fixes 401 bind)
commits.body:
fix(wpp): normalize pairing-code phone to digits (strip '+' → fixes 401 bind)

Baileys' requestPairingCode bakes the number straight into the device JID via
jidEncode(phoneNumber, 's.whatsapp.net') WITHOUT stripping non-digits. When the
caller (e.g. the panel) sends a number with a '+' (or spaces/dashes), the device
registers as an invalid JID like '+5511...@s.whatsapp.net', so WhatsApp rejects
the link-code-companion bind with a 401 — the code is generated but pairing never
completes. Verified live on staging: codes from the panel (pairingPhoneNumber
stored as '+5511930802555') all 401'd, while a digits-only number paired fine.

Normalize to digits in two places:
- BaileysDriver.requestPairingCode: strip non-digits before sock.requestPairingCode
  (last line before Baileys; guards against any caller), reject < 10 digits.
- pairingCodeSchema: transform phoneNumber to digits so the persisted
  pairingPhoneNumber and job payload are clean too.

commits.body:
fix(wpp): normalize @lid send target to PN (avoid undecryptable "delivered" sends)

Sending to a raw @lid jid makes WhatsApp ack "delivered" while the recipient
can't decrypt it (the session was established under the PN form) → the message
is silently lost (a widely-reported Baileys LID bug). dispatchSend now resolves
an @lid target to <phone>@s.whatsapp.net via the lid→PN mapping before sending,
so Baileys sets up the correct session and actually delivers; if the lid can't
be resolved it throws (clear failure) instead of a false "delivered".

Also fixes resolveLidToPhone: getPNForLID requires a full '@lid' jid (callers
passed the bare lid user → always null) and returns '<pn>:<device>@...'; now we
normalize the input and return digits. This also makes senderPhone + the
on-connect sweep actually resolve lids.

Covers all send types (text/media/reaction/location/contact via dispatchSend).
Unit tests: @lid→PN send, unresolvable @lid throws, resolveLidToPhone digits.

already normalize date-only bounds; Google getBusyPeriods now does the

commits.title: fix(baileys-patch): capture socket ref at close time (v1 killed the NEW socket on fast reconnect)
commits.body:
fix(baileys-patch): capture socket ref at close time (v1 killed the NEW socket on fast reconnect)

v1 called `this.socket?.terminate?.()` inside the 250ms setTimeout — a LATE
binding. When Baileys reconnects in <250ms, `this.socket` already points at
the NEW socket when the timeout fires, so v1 terminated the fresh connection
instead of the stale one → 'stream errored' loop in prod (deploy reverted).

v2 captures `const sockRef = this.socket;` at close() entry and uses only
sockRef in the timeout path (and for the 'close' listener, so resolve comes
from the socket actually being closed). Terminating the stale socket is still
unconditional on timeout — waiting for a close frame is exactly what hangs
under bun (the rc10+ regression this patch exists for).

Context: stale socket left alive → 'conflict: replaced' on next connection,
in-flight messages dropped silently (WhiskeySockets/Baileys #2132, #1963).

Validation:
- patch reverse+forward-applies cleanly against pristine rc13 (git apply --check both ways)
- docker build -t building-blocks:terminate-test-v2 . OK; sockRef/terminate
  confirmed inside the image (node_modules/baileys/lib/Socket/Client/websocket.js)
- wpp unit tests green (98 files / 1580 tests)

commits.title: fix(wpp): send to canonical JID via onWhatsApp; fail explicit on not_on_whatsapp
commits.body:
fix(wpp): send to canonical JID via onWhatsApp; fail explicit on not_on_whatsapp

WhatsApp never migrates a JID: accounts registered pre-9th-digit keep the
short-form JID (553484017015@s.whatsapp.net) even though the phone is saved
with the 9 (5534984017015). Sending to the literal with-9 JID is accepted,
echoed and acked by the server — and never delivered (silent void). Same for
numbers with no account at all (landlines). Proven live in prod 2026-07-02.

Baileys driver (send path):
- Before sending to a PN (@s.whatsapp.net) target, resolve the canonical JID
  via sock.onWhatsApp() (USync) and send to THAT jid.
- exists=false / empty result => throw TargetNotOnWhatsAppError
  (code `not_on_whatsapp`, carries the queried number) — never "succeed"
  into the void.
- USync query transport errors fail OPEN (send as requested) so infra flakes
  don't block sends; only a definitive "no account" answer blocks.
- Per-device in-memory cache (digits -> canonical jid), 24h positive TTL /
  1h negative TTL, bounded at 5k entries — one USync per number, not per
  message.
- @lid targets keep the existing lid->PN mapping path and NEVER go through
  onWhatsApp; groups/broadcasts pass through untouched.
- SendMessageResult now carries `remoteJid` = the JID actually used.

Consumer (async 202+correlationId flow):
- New events `wpp.message.failed` (internal) + `wpp.v1.message.failed`
  (public, webhooks/dispatchers) published on any send failure with a
  structured payload: { organizationId, deviceId, jid, requestedJid, type,
  code: 'not_on_whatsapp'|'send_failed', error, number?, correlationId }.
- Operation fails with the structured message (starts with the code).
- MESSAGE_SENT event + operation result now report the canonical jid
  actually used (`jid`/`remoteJid`) alongside `requestedJid`.

Tests: with-9 -> canonical no-9; not-on-whatsapp blocks send (structured
error, no sendMessage call); @lid/group bypass; positive+negative cache;
fail-open on USync flake; consumer failure events + canonical-jid sent event.

commits.title: fix(wpp): terminate() stale socket on baileys close() timeout (conflict: replaced)
commits.body:
fix(wpp): terminate() stale socket on baileys close() timeout (conflict: replaced)

The bun patch for baileys@7.0.0-rc13 (b226d44) races close() against a
250ms timeout so teardown never hangs under bun (whose ws shim doesn't
reliably emit 'close'). But the timeout path only resolve()d — it never
killed the underlying socket. The stale socket stayed connected to
WhatsApp, so the NEXT connection for the same device triggered
'conflict: replaced' (440) and in-flight messages were dropped silently.

Fix: on the timeout path, call socket.terminate() (forced destruction,
no close handshake) before resolving. It must be unconditional — waiting
for a close frame is exactly what hangs under bun, which is why the
timeout race exists in the first place. On Node, the real 'close' event
usually wins the race and terminate() on an already-nulled/closed socket
is a harmless no-op (optional chaining + try/catch).

Upstream context: WhiskeySockets/Baileys#2132 (conflict/replaced on
reconnect) and WhiskeySockets/Baileys#1963 (ws close hang). rc.9 is not
an option (no pairing-by-code), so the patch stays.

Validation:
- patch reverse/forward-applies cleanly against pristine rc13 (git apply)
- docker build of the repo image OK; patched terminate() confirmed
  inside the image at node_modules/baileys/lib/Socket/Client/websocket.js
- wpp unit tests green (98 files / 1580 tests)

Incidente 2026-07-03: device deslogado (401 LoggedOut) ficava com status
'closed' — indistinguível de queda transitória — e o reconciler de saúde do
consumidor (operacao-digital) re-kickava devices.connect a cada ~3min com credencial
morta, 26h+ de 401-loop contra o WhatsApp → bans temporários do número do
usuário.

- Novo status TERMINAL 'logged_out' (enum Prisma + migração):
  LoggedOut/BadSession → 'logged_out' (antes 'closed'); Banned → 'banned'.
- Guard no choke point getOrCreateSession (cobre rota, consumer e reconnect
  interno): device terminal sem repair explícito → CONFLICT requires_repair
  + connection_log reconnect_skipped. Fast-path 409 também na rota /connect.
- Repair path: connect com force=true (ou reconnect force) wipa o auth state
  persistido (creds+signal keys via BaileysAuthStateProvider.clear) e reseta
  o device p/ registro limpo (QR/pairing code novos).
- Orçamento de connect por device (Redis, janela 1h, default 30, env
  WPP_CONNECT_BUDGET_PER_HOUR): nenhum consumidor consegue martelar o número
  além do teto; excedente → CONFLICT connect_budget_exceeded + log. Fail-open
  em erro de Redis.
- Evento DEVICE_DISCONNECTED não-recuperável agora carrega requiresRepair +
  deviceStatus p/ consumidores pararem de auto-reconectar na hora.
- Fix handleReset: limpava só chaves Redis legadas; agora wipa as creds

commits.body:
fix(wpp): mata a causa-raiz do socket duplicado — owner pre-flight + destroy sem ressurreição

Investigação do churn 428 (docs 109 do app): os milhares de 428/401 eram
consequência; a ORIGEM das mortes de sessão eram dois bugs que criavam um
segundo socket da mesma sessão → WhatsApp responde 440 conflict em ping-pong
(~5s) até INVALIDAR a credencial (401) — foi exatamente assim que a sessão da
beta tester morreu (session_restore às 06:53 duplicou; conflict+401 às 09:41).

1) Owner pre-flight no getOrCreateSession: claim ATÔMICO no OwnerRegistry
   (SET NX + refresh se já nosso) antes de criar socket. Job de
   restore/connect que cai em réplica não-dona é recusado com CONFLICT
   owner_held + connection_log reconnect_skipped. Dono morto expira com o
   TTL de 45s → takeover rápido. Fail-open em erro de Redis.
2) Disconnect manual não reconecta: DisconnectReason.ManualDisconnect (-1,
   sentinela local) emitido pelos drivers baileys/mock; o handler de close
   pula o caminho recuperável (antes reason=0 agendava reconnect segundos
   após o destroy — ressurreição + duplicata). destroySession também cancela
   timer de reconnect pendente (inclusive quando a sessão já saiu do mapa).

Testes: session-manager 53/53 (5 novos: owner_held, claim ok, fail-open,
manual sem reconnect, destroy cancela timer). Suíte unit wpp 1623 verdes.
(Integração wpp-business já quebrava antes: migração 20260410 meta_account
com erro de sintaxe no setup do DB de teste — pré-existente.)

O tool-use da Anthropic não rejeita chaves fora do input_schema. No e2e da
fase 2 RecruitCRM o agente consultor chamou run_custom_action com
{ slug: 'recruitcrm-search-jobs', input: { search: 'Paper' } } — a chave

rodou com query vazia, a API devolveu [] e o modelo concluiu, errado, "não
localizei". Execução direta com { name: 'Paper' } retorna a vaga.

Fix genérico (cobre as 20 actions RecruitCRM + futuras): o executor do
run_custom_action resolve a action (getBySlug, raw→norm), valida as chaves
do input contra o inputSchema e devolve um erro INSTRUTIVO listando os
params esperados para o modelo se auto-corrigir na iteração seguinte. A
resolução também dá o slug canônico, dispensando o fallback raw→norm no
execute. Se a action não resolver, a validação é pulada (nunca regride).

Spec: 5 casos (chave desconhecida, chave válida, slug hífen→underscore,
additionalProperties:true, action não resolvível). 97/97 no tools-executor.

commits.body:
fix(personal-trainer): persona guard (no double-fire) + personal lead type + notification/summary delivery

Gaps found comparing with the recrutamento vertical:

1. DOUBLE-FIRE (critical): atendimento-aluno and atendimento-personal both
   trigger on messages.upsert on the same device — every message ran BOTH flows
   (double response). Recrutamento avoids this by shipping persona workflows
   inactive (operator must activate only one). Here we do better: a rotaPersona
   CONDITIONAL guard by {{$lead.type}} is the first action of each workflow —
   both stay ACTIVE on the same device; the other persona's message dies at the
   guard (no agent run, no response). Aluno flow: ALUNO + unknown senders
   proceed (new student → onboarding), PERSONAL_TRAINER blocked. Personal flow:
   only PERSONAL_TRAINER proceeds.

2. PERSONAL_TRAINER lead type (setupAction, autoExecute) on the personal
   agents: identifies the personal by their WhatsApp phone for routing and as
   the notification target.

3. Notification/summary delivery: onboarding notified via execute_workflow
   which pointed to no workflow; resumo diário had no delivery tool. Both now
   use list_leads {type: PERSONAL_TRAINER} → send_whatsapp_message to the
   personal's phone. execute_workflow tool removed (unused).

Verified: docker build green; dist contains rotaPersona guard + PERSONAL_TRAINER.

budget de 30k tokens do orchestrator em 12 iterações — "[Budget excedido —

cache do prompt funcionou (creation 6.2k na 1ª chamada, read nas demais), mas
o input_tokens NÃO-cacheado cresce a cada iteração (685→1292→…→7364) porque o
histórico re-conta — e cada tool result de REST action carregava o envelope
HTTP completo com headers (~300+ tokens de date/vary/cache-control por
chamada), inflando o crescimento.

Dois fixes:
1. stripActionResultHttpNoise: run_custom_action (tools-executor, caminho

   (era o loop de 12 iterações: search/list/get atrás de um candidato que
   acabou de chegar pelo webhook); busca vira enriquecimento opcional.

Spec novo no run-custom-action (headers removidos, statusCode/body intactos).

commits.title: feat(data-store): Phase 3 — field-level PII encryption + KV fast-path
commits.body:
feat(data-store): Phase 3 — field-level PII encryption + KV fast-path

- PII encryption: fields marked `encrypted: true` in a collection's JSON
  schema are stored as AES-256-GCM envelopes (enc:v1:iv:tag:ct) and
  transparently decrypted on read. Filtering/sorting on encrypted fields is
  rejected (ciphertext at rest). Keyed by DATASTORE_CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY.
- KV fast-path: PUT/GET/DELETE /kv/:namespace/:key over a reserved
  kv_<namespace> collection, upsert by natural key, auto-created on first PUT.
  New driver ops upsertByKey/getByKey/deleteByKey on the SPI.

Validated: 14/14 Phase-3 HTTP smoke (incl. DB proof that ssn is stored as
`enc:v1:…` while name stays plaintext) + 27/27 unit; typecheck/lint clean.

Lightweight, schemaless document store exposed as a client capability
(orchestration state, lookup tables, user records) — not a client's primary
app DB. Tenant isolation is row-level (tenant_id, always from the JWT).

  (single JSONB table in `datastore` schema, GIN index, zero DDL per tenant).
- Collections + documents CRUD, portable Query DSL (validated paths, bound
  params), schema-lite validation, per-tenant quota, optimistic concurrency.
- Facade (monolith/standalone), events, permissions DATASTORE_READ/WRITE/ADMIN.
- Validated: 16/16 HTTP smoke (tenant isolation, SQL-injection barred,
  permissions) + 12/12 unit tests; typecheck/lint clean.

commits.body:
feat(data-store): Phase 2 — Postgres RLS + per-collection ACL

Defense in depth on top of the always-present tenant_id filter:

- RLS: every driver op now runs inside a transaction that sets
  `app.tenant_id` via set_config(); idempotent tenant_isolation policies
  (ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY) are installed once on all datastore
  tables. Gated by DATASTORE_RLS_ENABLED (default true); DDL failures are
  non-fatal (managed DBs). Verified with a non-superuser role: unscoped
  reads return 0 (default-deny), scoped reads see only their tenant, and a
  cross-tenant tenant_id filter still returns 0.
- ACL: optional per-collection { read[], write[] } allowlist of caller
  userIds ("*" = open), enforced in the service ON TOP of RBAC for
  insert/update/delete (write) and get/query (read).

Validated: 16/16 HTTP smoke (unchanged) + 7/7 ACL smoke (owner allowed,
non-owner 403 on write/read/query) + 16/16 unit; typecheck/lint clean.

commits.body:
feat(datastore): idempotent per-user CATALISA_BB key rotation script

Phase 2 of docs/plans/2026-07-12-catalisa-bb-auth-per-user-and-rotation.md.

scripts/rotate-catalisa-bb-credentials.ts logs in as each target (master)
user, mints a fresh BB api-key via /credentials/generate-bb-key, then PUTs
their existing wpp-bb credential(s) in place (ids preserved) or POSTs a new
one, and validates each with /credentials/:id/test against the data-store
(expect 200). Dry-run is the default (read-only); --live enables writes,
--probe reports current validity. Targets (incl. passwords) come from an
external JSON file so no secret is committed.

Notes baked into the design (validated on staging):
- /credentials/:id/test reads the test URL from ?url= (query), not a body.
- generate-bb-key rejects duplicate key NAMES and does not revoke old keys,
  so every generation uses a unique [base36ts.seq] name suffix.

Validated live on staging for admin@catalisa.app (rotated 2 creds) and
staging@operacao-digital.ai (created 1 cred, different org) — both pass /test 200 and
a real data_store_* agent E2E, proving per-user/per-org isolation.

fix(pt): throttle-aware paced inserts in provisioner (panel rate limits)

Real staging --live run hit the panel's NestJS Throttler (30/s, 200/min,
2000/h — app.module.ts): concurrency-5 inserts with short backoff blew
through the 200/min window (200 inserted, 673 failed with
ThrottlerException). The run must converge in one pass:

- insertDocumentsPaced (lib): sequential insert loop paced to an rpm
  budget via a minimum inter-request gap (default 150/min = 400ms; first
  request unpaced), with injectable sleep/now so tests use a fake clock.
- 429-specific retry in insertDocumentWithRetry: long exponential
  backoff (20s doubling, capped 60s, up to 5 retries) on a SEPARATE
  budget from the 3x transient-error retries — rate-limit hits virtually
  never end as failed. Sleep injectable.
- Progress logging every 50 docs (n/total + inserted/skipped/failed) —
  a full 873-doc seed now takes ~6-7 min.
- --rpm=N / PT_PROVISION_RPM override (validated 1..200; >200 would
  always hit the 200/min window); throttle tiers documented in the
  script header; pacing shown in the run banner.
- 7 new mocked tests (RED-first): 429 waits-then-succeeds, 60s cap +
  5-retry exhaustion, separate budgets, pace-gate gaps (60rpm/150rpm),
  outcome tally, progress cadence. No test really sleeps.

leaks a raw 401 to the caller.

feat(datastore): idempotent per-user CATALISA_BB key rotation script

Phase 2 of docs/plans/2026-07-12-catalisa-bb-auth-per-user-and-rotation.md.

scripts/rotate-catalisa-bb-credentials.ts logs in as each target (master)
user, mints a fresh BB api-key via /credentials/generate-bb-key, then PUTs
their existing wpp-bb credential(s) in place (ids preserved) or POSTs a new
one, and validates each with /credentials/:id/test against the data-store
(expect 200). Dry-run is the default (read-only); --live enables writes,
--probe reports current validity. Targets (incl. passwords) come from an
external JSON file so no secret is committed.

Notes baked into the design (validated on staging):
- /credentials/:id/test reads the test URL from ?url= (query), not a body.
- generate-bb-key rejects duplicate key NAMES and does not revoke old keys,
  so every generation uses a unique [base36ts.seq] name suffix.

Validated live on staging for admin@catalisa.app (rotated 2 creds) and
staging@operacao-digital.ai (created 1 cred, different org) — both pass /test 200 and
a real data_store_* agent E2E, proving per-user/per-org isolation.

commits.body:
fix(pt): retag query must go through POST fn (PUT->query 404'd as silent no-op) + 0-items guard (F5)

Staging dry-run caught runRetag(put) feeding the PUT-bound fn into
listExistingDocItems: PUT /collections/pt_exercises/query has no route,
the 404 read as "empty collection", and --retag reported checked=0 /
would-retag=0 silently. The DsPutFn = DsPostFn structural alias makes
tsc blind to the HTTP verb, so the fix moves the retag orchestration
into the lib (runRetagFlow({post, put})) where unit tests pin the
wiring by fn IDENTITY (query -> post, updates -> put), and adds a
runtime guard: 0 items fetched while the seed step counted
existed+inserted > 0 docs now ABORTS loudly instead of no-oping.

docs(spec): template genérico de Agendamento de Serviços (marketplace)

Design aprovado para um único workflow template `agendamento-servicos` que
qualquer negócio de serviço instala e configura sem código: identidade,
catálogo, expediente, políticas e prazo de lembrete vivem em configuração no
Data Store (coleções `agenda_*`), não em prompt.

Promove a demo descartável de petshop (2026-06-02, escopada como "só-stg, não
vira template versionado") a produto genérico.

Escopo: 3 workflows (Atendimento / Lembretes+No-show / Escalação), 3 agentes,
3 coleções, mais 2 primitivas de plataforma:
- BB (main): expor `ensureByKey` no documents router — a composição no painel
  (QUERY→CONDITIONAL→INSERT) tem corrida e um trap de 409 permanente por causa
  do soft-delete ocupar o slot do docKey unique.
- painel (master): action DATASTORE_ENSURE_DOCUMENT + `confirmed`/`no_show`
  em LEAD_DISPOSITIONS.

Reusa (não recria) `customData.funnel`, o motor de timers FOLLOW_UP_DUE e
`credentialRequirements` — os namespaces são fixos nas tools de plataforma.

Diferença conceitual vs operacao-investimentos: agenda é inbound-first, então o gate é
deny-list (atende todos exceto opted_out) e o lead nasce tarde, via tool
`create_lead` (que dedupa, emite evento e adota o chat órfão) — nunca via
action CREATE_LEAD (que duplica silenciosamente).

- Fase 4: deploy stg, install self-service (API + picker visual), matriz de 14

constraints globais (dep única por branch, deviceId:null em triggers não-WhatsApp,

evento de plataforma FOLLOW_UP_DUE (trigger type 'system', config.eventType

device-agnostic - um deviceId não-nulo faria o trigger nunca casar. Device
do SEND_MESSAGE continua injetado por action pelo instalador.

Estende WorkflowTemplateData.workflowData.workflow com deviceId?: string |
null (opcional, aditivo) para permitir declarar essa intenção - documentado
no comentário do export que o instalador genérico ainda precisa de ajuste

fix(code-portal): provision email pre-check→409 + reorder (no orphans) + sync calendar on getConfig

- provision() now pre-checks email uniqueness (ConflictException/409)
  before generating a codigo or seeding anything, and creates the
  CodeAccount row BEFORE seeding Data Store docs / minting the calendar
  invite, so a later failure never orphans docs/invites without a DB
  row (config self-heals via ensureConfigDoc's createIfNotExists; the
  invite can be re-minted via /portal/calendar/reconnect). P2002 on
  create is still caught as belt-and-suspenders, mapped to the same 409.
- GET /portal/config now also runs syncCalendar first, matching
  /portal/me, so a personal who connects their calendar and never
  reopens /portal/me still gets calendarIntegrationId reconciled.

feat(sites): portal estático Personal Lite (signup/login/config)

Duas páginas estáticas autossuficientes (sem framework/build), reaproveitando
a casca visual (tokens/tema/tipografia/botões) de sites/personal-lite/index.html:

- signup.html: form e-mail+senha -> POST /personal-lite/auth/signup -> tela
  de sucesso com código, botão "Conectar calendário" e link wa.me copiável.
  captchaToken vai vazio (TODO(sp2-deploy) documentado inline: hCaptcha exige
  <script src> externo, proibido pelo molde zero-requisição-externa).
- portal.html: login (guarda JWT em localStorage['personal-lite-token']) ->
  GET /portal/me (código, wa.me, status do calendário), editor de
  agenda_config via GET/PUT /portal/config (negocio/expediente/politicas/
  lembrete/escalacao/tom/leadTypeName), botão reconectar calendário via
  POST /portal/calendar/reconnect. Logout limpa o token e volta ao login;
  401 da API também força logout com mensagem de sessão expirada.

API_BASE é uma const única por arquivo, default produção, com comentário
apontando a troca pra staging. Zero dependência externa (verificado por grep:
nenhum <script src> externo, nenhum <link> remoto, nenhum @import, nenhuma
URL http(s) fora do xmlns do SVG inline e da própria API_BASE). Dois temas
(claro/escuro) via prefers-color-scheme + toggle [data-theme], mesmo padrão
de index.html.

commits.title: fix(code-portal): 503 clear error when unconfigured + frontend guards waNumber null
commits.body:
fix(code-portal): 503 clear error when unconfigured + frontend guards waNumber null

Review findings on the dynamic-config rework: CodePortalConfigService threw
a plain Error when SystemSettings.codePortalDeviceId was unset/broken, which
fell through the controller uncaught into Nest's generic, message-less 500
(staging is in exactly this state right now) — violating "no unexpected
4xx/5xx". Introduces CodePortalNotConfiguredError (typed, instanceof-
checkable) thrown by the service; the controller now wraps every handler
that can reach it (signup, getMe, getConfig, updateConfig,
reconnectCalendar — all of them transitively call into the config service)
and maps that one typed error to ServiceUnavailableException (503) carrying
the original PT-BR message, while any other error passes through untouched.

Also: whatsappShareUrl can be null (BB best-effort). signup.html and
portal.html were setting the input value/href directly, coercing null into
the literal string "null" (broken href="null"). Both now guard on
whatsappShareUrl and hide the copy/open row in favor of a short
"aparece aqui assim que a configuração terminar" message when it's absent.

commits.title: fix(code-portal): opt-out persists for lead-less senders (drop obsolete optoutGuard)
commits.body:
fix(code-portal): opt-out persists for lead-less senders (drop obsolete optoutGuard)

optoutGuard (CONDITIONAL on {{$lead?.id}} is_not_empty) existed only to
protect the OLD UPDATE_LEAD do_optout, which needed a leadId. Now that
do_optout is SET_CODE_OPTOUT (needs only phone+codigo, both always present),
the guard was actively harmful: a brand-new client opting out on their very
first message (no Lead yet) hit the SemLead branch, do_optout was skipped,
and CodeClientLink.optedOut never got set — the opt-out silently didn't
persist, reintroducing a variant of the isolation bug for lead-less senders.

Removed optoutGuard entirely; do_optout now depends directly on
rotaIntent:1 (same as sendOptout), so it always runs when opt-out intent is
routed, lead or no lead. Renumbered action orders (0..16) and updated
workflows.spec.ts accordingly.
