feat(baas): quórum de assinatura e alçada por representante (D-PJ2)

Modo QUORUM na política de autorização: representantes com teto por operação,
teto diário, vigência e minSigners ("conjunta, n"), e quórum por faixa de valor
(n de m, ou "ALL" = todos em vigor). signingRules entra no policyHash só quando
existe — as políticas já ancoradas não mudam de hash.

Numa conta QUORUM nenhuma assinatura sozinha move dinheiro: Pix, TED e chaves
Pix (e a própria mudança de política) viram um pedido de assinatura que coleta
assinaturas de representantes DIFERENTES sobre o mesmo payload (tipo, conta,
id e nonce do pedido, params). Aprovação decidida no banco sob trava do
representante e do pedido; execução pelos mesmos serviços das rotas diretas,
com o portão reconstruindo o payload, reconferindo as assinaturas e
reivindicando a execução (APPROVED → EXECUTING condicionado): uma execução só.
Expira (varredura + na assinatura), recusa assinada, cancelamento, retomada
idempotente (a chave da transferência é o id do pedido). Trilha
baas.signing.request.* com catraca de recusa.

Fachada: requireSigningQuorum e enforcesQuorum (quorumGate) para o #547 trocar
a pausa de pix.send/pix.keys pelo quórum.

Testes de corrida contra Postgres real (8 casos; sem as travas e a
reivindicação condicionada, 4 falham).

commits.title: fix(baas): o status só avança — webhook, consulta e KYC não rebaixam nem republicam
commits.body:
fix(baas): o status só avança — webhook, consulta e KYC não rebaixam nem republicam

O handler de webhook gravava o status que o provedor dizia com `update`
incondicional e publicava a cada aviso. O README §14 dizia que a
reivindicação condicionada segurava o aviso repetido sem id de evento; no
webhook ela não existia. Consequências medidas em teste:

- dois avisos do mesmo Pix sem id de evento (Celcoin, QI Tech e FitBank não
  mandam) publicavam `baas.pix.transfer.completed` duas vezes;
- `created`/`failed` atrasado rebaixava um Pix já concluído (FAILED com o
  dinheiro fora);
- `kyc.approved` atrasado reativava conta BLOCKED e ressuscitava conta CLOSED;
  reenviar KYC pela rota fazia o mesmo;
- `GET /pix/transfers/:id` (BAAS_READ) devolvia a COMPLETED um Pix recebido já
  estornado, porque no banco a ENTRADA continua concluída.

Agora as escritas de status usam `advanceStatus` (updateMany condicionado à
tabela de `utils/status-transitions.ts`) e só quem vira publica. A busca da
transação pelo aviso aceita o id do provedor além do `endToEndId` (a Celcoin
manda `transactionId` primeiro; a busca só por `endToEndId` nunca casava) e
fica restrita à configuração que recebeu o aviso. A consulta de uma reserva
(`reserva:`/`sem-chave:`) responde a linha local em vez de perguntar ao banco
por um id que ele não conhece.

Achado da auditoria de completude e segurança do BaaS (01/10/2026).

fix(biometrics): a purga de retenção apaga o arquivo de verdade, e o cadastro facial vence

O smoke de staging (01/10) achou a purga zerando só o ponteiro: o arquivo ficava no
file-storage, a foto do documento tirada pela página ficava, e o cadastro facial não tinha
validade. Agora (BiometricsRetentionPurgeService):

- Mídia vencida (retainedUntil, ou o snapshot da sessão) sai DO FILE-STORAGE: melhor frame e
  vídeo de TODAS as tentativas, retrato extraído e foto do documento; a cópia do vetor facial
  (state.templateCipher) sai do estado. Ficam linha, checks, decisão e hashes.
- Sessões vencidas sem avaliação (documento tirado, selfie nunca feita) entram.
- Varredura por cursor: o take:200 sem ordem relia as mesmas sessões no prazo a cada passada.
- Sessões purgadas pela versão antiga: os ponteiros que sobraram nas colunas e nas capturas
  são apagados na passada seguinte (leftover: true).
- Cadastro facial vencido (templateDays): revogado, vetor zerado no cadastro E na sessão de
  origem. Cadastro sem validade recebe createdAt + templateDays da política vigente.
- Trilha: biometrics.media.purged / media.purge_failed / enrollment.expired /
  enrollment.expiry_set — só ids, hashes e resultado por arquivo.
- Idempotente e segura com 2 réplicas: trava no Redis + fechamento condicional por linha
  (só quem fecha publica); arquivo que não saiu deixa a sessão para a próxima passada.
- file-storage: objeto no S3 ANTES da linha. Na ordem antiga, S3 falhando deixava os bytes e
  a nova tentativa respondia 404 ("já não existe").
- BIOMETRICS_RETENTION_PURGE_ENABLED com envFlag: z.coerce.boolean fazia "false" LIGAR a purga.

commits.title: fix(iam): MFA lock holds under parallel guesses; reset confined to single-org users; challenge consumed once
commits.body:
fix(iam): MFA lock holds under parallel guesses; reset confined to single-org users; challenge consumed once

Adversarial review of #525:

- Lock bypass by parallelism: the lock was read before evaluating and the failure counted
  after, so a burst of N concurrent guesses (one challenge each; the IP rate limit trusts
  X-Forwarded-For) had all N evaluated. Each answer now reserves an attempt with a
  conditional UPDATE before matching; the (max+1)-th request of a burst is refused unread.
- Reset across organizations: the factor belongs to the person and protects every org, but
  any admin whose org the user is linked to could reset it — and an admin can link any user
  into their own org. Non-root admins now reset only users who belong to no other org, never
  a root account, and never by API key.
- Challenge single use: consume() now reports whether it deleted the challenge; the loser of
  two concurrent second steps gets no session.

commits.body:
feat(banking): operações pedidas pelo computador, aprovadas e executadas no celular (fatia 2 do desktop) (#544)

* feat(banking): desktop operations requested on the computer, approved and executed on the phone

The desktop session still never moves money: it only creates a request
(createDesktopOperation, write, no signature). The phone lists it with amount,
recipient and key, opens the Pix intent FROM THE ROW through the same
createPixIntent, signs the canonical BaaS payload and sends with the same
sendPix (step-up, limits, spendable balance, idempotency and trail unchanged).

- table banking.desktop_operation_requests (raw additive migration) and
  DesktopOperationRequestRepository: conditional transitions, intent swap
  bound to the previous intent_id, unique intent_id, unique idempotency key
  per desktop session
- PixIntentRepository.abandon (PENDING -> FAILED, conditional): refuse,
  cancel and intent swap race sendPix and exactly one wins
- 6 routes (create/get/cancel from the desktop, intent/refuse from the
  phone, desktop sessions list); getPixContacts, lookupPixKey, getDevices
  and signOutDesktop now reachable by the desktop session (read or
  privilege-reducing only); getPendingApprovals merges access and operations
- signOutDesktop cancels pending operation requests
- banking.desktop.operation.* events; every refusal is published
- unit tests (memory DB) and real-Postgres race tests; README section 7.4

POST /policy/reapply-retention, deixando a purga apagar antes do contado:

commits.title: feat(template-builder): remote build host tooling and a single fleet-wide template GC
commits.body:
feat(template-builder): remote build host tooling and a single fleet-wide template GC

Templates were built on the developer's machine, where the build died at
"exporting to image" with the disk full, and each build script carried its
own retention. The date-based one deleted in-use templates twice: bb-runtime
on 28/09 (#491) and the panel's production api template on 01/10.

- host/template-build: single build entry point for any repo/family — host
  lock (one build at a time), free-space floor before starting, size check on
  both nodes after publishing, cleanup of image and tarball on exit. Exports
  LXC_TEMPLATE_KEEP=1000 to neutralise retention embedded in older commits.
- host/docker-gc + timer: Docker state is cache, pruned by age and size;
  skipped while a build runs.
- template-gc.sh: the one place that removes templates from the nodes, for
  every family. In use = templateRef or runningTemplateRef across all Launch
  projects; fail closed globally and per family; keeps the 5 newest unused and
  anything younger than 72h; removing is moving to a 7-day trash; an in-use
  template absent from a node fails the run.
- workflows: build-template (dispatch + reusable) and template-gc (daily,
  report-only until TEMPLATE_GC_APPLY=true), both on the template-builder runner.
- docs/RUNBOOK-TEMPLATE-BUILDER.md, including what is still pending.

O smoke de staging (01/10) achou a purga zerando só o ponteiro: o arquivo ficava no
file-storage, a foto do documento tirada pela página ficava, e o cadastro facial não tinha
validade. Agora (BiometricsRetentionPurgeService):

- Mídia vencida (retainedUntil, ou o snapshot da sessão) sai DO FILE-STORAGE: melhor frame e
  vídeo de TODAS as tentativas, retrato extraído e foto do documento; a cópia do vetor facial
  (state.templateCipher) sai do estado. Ficam linha, checks, decisão e hashes.
- Sessões vencidas sem avaliação (documento tirado, selfie nunca feita) entram.
- Varredura por cursor: o take:200 sem ordem relia as mesmas sessões no prazo a cada passada.
- Sessões purgadas pela versão antiga: os ponteiros que sobraram nas colunas e nas capturas
  são apagados na passada seguinte (leftover: true).
- Cadastro facial vencido (templateDays): revogado, vetor zerado no cadastro E na sessão de
  origem. Cadastro sem validade recebe createdAt + templateDays da política vigente.
- Trilha: biometrics.media.purged / media.purge_failed / enrollment.expired /
  enrollment.expiry_set — só ids, hashes e resultado por arquivo.
- Idempotente e segura com 2 réplicas: trava no Redis + fechamento condicional por linha
  (só quem fecha publica); arquivo que não saiu deixa a sessão para a próxima passada.
- file-storage: objeto no S3 ANTES da linha. Na ordem antiga, S3 falhando deixava os bytes e
  a nova tentativa respondia 404 ("já não existe").
- BIOMETRICS_RETENTION_PURGE_ENABLED com envFlag: z.coerce.boolean fazia "false" LIGAR a purga.

commits.title: feat(analytics): bloco novo — catálogo, evento cru e guarda de dado pessoal (M1) (#512)
commits.body:
feat(analytics): bloco novo — catálogo, evento cru e guarda de dado pessoal (M1) (#512)

* feat(analytics): bloco novo — catálogo, evento cru e guarda de dado pessoal (M1)

Primeira fatia do bloco `analytics` (PRs 1 e 2 da spec
analytics-funis-metricas-e-alertas): contagem de jornada, não prova.

- Schema `analytics` com três tabelas, migration SQL crua, aditiva e
  idempotente: `analytics_event_catalog` (espelho do catálogo em código),
  `analytics_events` (cru, único por organização + clientEventId) e
  `analytics_quality_daily` (recusa e perda de atributo por motivo).
  Nenhuma coluna de IP, agente de usuário, valor exato ou texto livre.
- Catálogo em código, só eventos de bloco (DM1): banking.session.*,
  banking.pix.intent.created, banking.pix.transfer.*, baas.pix.transfer.*.
  Classificação escrita com motivo; quatro tipos de atributo (enumeração,
  número, booleano, faixa); valor vira faixa.
- Gravador: recusa um evento por vez (o lote não morre), com motivo, e
  conta a recusa; dedupe por ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
- Guarda de dado pessoal: nome do campo por palavra (fonte-escalas phoneNumber,
  pixKey, documentNumber, que o cms deixa passar) e formato do valor (CPF,
  CNPJ, telefone, e-mail, JWT, segredo), até profundidade 6. Recusa, não
  mascara.
- Registro: container sem @Service() (PR #488), registry, porta 3041,
  package.json, build, deploy-swarm, stacks, compose, tsconfig, vitest,
  INDEX e README de 16 seções. O serviço sobe só com /analytics/health e

commits.body:
fix(iam): refresh grant re-resolves organization and roles instead of dropping them

The refresh token carried only sub/email, so every renewed access token came
back without organizationId and without permissions: the banking console
dropped the session at the first renewal (~1h) and other clients silently lost
their permissions.

- Refresh token now carries the login's organizationId (and amr, if any).
- New TokenRenewalService re-reads the user and the CURRENT roles: deactivated,
  deleted, or removed from the organization -> invalid_grant, with a
  security.token.refused event (USER_INACTIVE | ORGANIZATION_ACCESS_REVOKED).
- isRoot comes from the user now; amr is copied verbatim, never upgraded.
- Legacy refresh tokens without organization renew unscoped, as before.

The desktop session still never moves money: it only creates a request
(createDesktopOperation, write, no signature). The phone lists it with amount,
recipient and key, opens the Pix intent FROM THE ROW through the same

  DesktopOperationRequestRepository: conditional transitions, intent swap
  bound to the previous intent_id, unique intent_id, unique idempotency key
  per desktop session
- PixIntentRepository.abandon (PENDING -> FAILED, conditional): refuse,
  cancel and intent swap race sendPix and exactly one wins
- 6 routes (create/get/cancel from the desktop, intent/refuse from the
  phone, desktop sessions list); getPixContacts, lookupPixKey, getDevices
  and signOutDesktop now reachable by the desktop session (read or
  privilege-reducing only); getPendingApprovals merges access and operations
- signOutDesktop cancels pending operation requests
- banking.desktop.operation.* events; every refusal is published

commits.body:
feat(iam): TOTP second factor with recovery codes, two-step login and amr claim

- Two-step login: right password + factor owed returns an opaque short-lived
  challenge (hash in Redis), never a token; the TOTP or recovery code exchanges
  it for the token pair.
- amr claim (RFC 8176) in access and refresh tokens: pwd | pwd+otp+mfa |
  pwd+mfa (recovery); the refresh grant preserves it.
- Enrollment (self-service or owed at login when the organization has
  mfaRequired): secret encrypted with IAM_MFA_MASTER_KEY via credential-crypto,
  otpauth URI for the QR, first code confirms, 10 recovery codes shown once and
  stored only as SHA-256.
- Replay guard: each TOTP step claimed once with a conditional UPDATE (race
  tested against Postgres); 5 wrong codes lock the factor for 15 min.
- Admin reset of another user's factor with mandatory reason, refresh tokens
  revoked; self reset refused; mfaEnabled removed from PATCH /users/:id.
- iam.mfa.* events mapped in the audit trail (resource user_mfa); no secret,
  code or recovery code in events or logs.
- Organization policy mfaRequired (default false). Additive, idempotent migration.

commits.body:
fix(baas): o status só avança — webhook, consulta e KYC não rebaixam nem republicam (#542)

* fix(baas): o status só avança — webhook, consulta e KYC não rebaixam nem republicam

O handler de webhook gravava o status que o provedor dizia com `update`
incondicional e publicava a cada aviso. O README §14 dizia que a
reivindicação condicionada segurava o aviso repetido sem id de evento; no
webhook ela não existia. Consequências medidas em teste:

- dois avisos do mesmo Pix sem id de evento (Celcoin, QI Tech e FitBank não
  mandam) publicavam `baas.pix.transfer.completed` duas vezes;
- `created`/`failed` atrasado rebaixava um Pix já concluído (FAILED com o
  dinheiro fora);
- `kyc.approved` atrasado reativava conta BLOCKED e ressuscitava conta CLOSED;
  reenviar KYC pela rota fazia o mesmo;
- `GET /pix/transfers/:id` (BAAS_READ) devolvia a COMPLETED um Pix recebido já
  estornado, porque no banco a ENTRADA continua concluída.

Agora as escritas de status usam `advanceStatus` (updateMany condicionado à
tabela de `utils/status-transitions.ts`) e só quem vira publica. A busca da
transação pelo aviso aceita o id do provedor além do `endToEndId` (a Celcoin
manda `transactionId` primeiro; a busca só por `endToEndId` nunca casava) e
fica restrita à configuração que recebeu o aviso. A consulta de uma reserva
(`reserva:`/`sem-chave:`) responde a linha local em vez de perguntar ao banco
por um id que ele não conhece.

Achado da auditoria de completude e segurança do BaaS (01/10/2026).

fix(baas): G1 — trava por conta e saídas em voo no saldo gastável (#548)

* fix(baas): G1 — trava por conta e saídas em voo no saldo gastável

A conferência do gastável lia o disponível e a soma dos bloqueios sem trava
e sem contar saídas em voo; a reserva só vinha depois. Dois Pix simultâneos
(ou um logo após outro ainda PROCESSING) gastavam o saldo bloqueado LEDGER.

- SpendableBalanceService.reserveOutflow: conferência + INSERT da reserva sob
  SELECT … FOR UPDATE na baas_accounts (lock_timeout 5 s → 503 ACCOUNT_BUSY).
  Leitura do disponível e chamada ao provedor ficam FORA da trava.
- gastável = disponível − bloqueios LEDGER − saídas em voo (PENDING/PROCESSING
  e COMPLETED depois da leitura do saldo, com folga de 5 s).
- Consumo de bloqueio: reivindicação + reserva na mesma transação, sob a
  trava; a reserva leva metadata.holdCustody e protege o valor enquanto em
  voo (o consumo que esgota o bloqueio o fechava antes de o banco pagar).
- Criação de bloqueio desconta saídas em voo (HOLD_EXCEEDS_BALANCE com
  inFlightAmount).
- Desfecho do provedor: 4xx ou falha antes do banco → reserva FAILED (o
  valor volta); timeout/5xx → fica PENDING e segue contando (#516).
- Trilha: envio de Pix e TED passam por auditHoldRoute
  (baas.pix.transfer.* / baas.ted.transfer.*), com os números da decisão.
- Índice (account_id, status) em baas_transactions, migration idempotente.
- Teste de corrida contra Postgres real (testcontainers), 14 casos; sem a
  correção, 11 falham.

Com a compensação falhando, a reserva ia a FAILED e o valor ficava fora do
bloqueio e fora das saídas em voo: gastável inflado pela porta do erro.
Agora a reserva fica PENDING com o motivo. O espião do teste repassa o tx.

mediaDays do snapshot) e o expiresAt do cadastro. Subir a retenção na política (decisão de
01/10: 360 dias) não alcançava as sessões antigas, gravadas com 30 — a purga as apagaria
antes do prazo decidido.

- sessão com evidência: retainedUntil = (evaluatedAt ?? createdAt) + mediaDays (fora do
  bundleHash e da assinatura; o snapshot, que entra no hash, não muda)
- sessão sem evidência: sobe o mediaDays do snapshot
- cadastro ativo com validade: expiresAt = createdAt + templateDays

feat(iti-verifier): cofre do .war no registry, deploy automatizado e portão de token

- 0-guardar-war: o dono baixa o .war UMA vez; ele vai para a imagem-cofre
  iti-verifier-war (FROM scratch, registry privado do Launch, por digest, nos
  tenants de staging e produção). war.lock fixa sha256 + referência.
- 1-construir-e-publicar: build lê o .war do cofre (--build-context war=...),
  confere o sha, prova local COM o portão (403 sem token / token errado) e
  publica a MESMA imagem (mesmo digest) em staging e produção; image.lock.
- 2-implantar --env staging|prod: converge bb-iti-verifier (docker, sem rota
  pública) para o image.lock, gera VERIFIER_TOKEN e liga o e-signature (URL +
  token, PATCH do env inteiro com backup 0600). Produção só cria com --criar.
- 3-provar: smoke de contrato em bash (DOU válido, 1 byte trocado, sem
  assinatura, autoassinado + portão), sem pular.
- Portão: RewriteValve do Tomcat exige X-Verifier-Token (a malha do Launch é
  IPv6 global); falha fechada sem token. e-signature envia
  ESIGNATURE_ITI_VERIFIER_TOKEN; 401/403 → INDETERMINATE/PROVIDER_ERROR.
- deploy-native: serviços runtime docker saem da frota de template; passo 4
  "motores" converge o iti-verifier e roda o smoke.

feat(iam): membros trazem a pessoa (e-mail, segundo fator, último acesso) e a mudança de vínculo nomeia o autor (#540)

* feat(iam): members carry the person (e-mail, second factor, last login) and access changes name their author

The backoffice console's access-control area reads "who has access to this
organization" from GET /organizations/:id/members. That listing returned only
the link (userId, roleId), so the console would need one GET /users/:id per
person, and there was no last-login anywhere in the IAM.

- users.last_login_at (additive, idempotent migration), stamped when a session
  is issued (password, password + second factor, enrollment at login). Renewal
  does not count. Raw SQL so signing in does not bump updatedAt; a failed stamp
  is a warning, never a refused login.
- The members listing returns email, status, mfaEnabled and lastLoginAt per
  member. No secret.
- iam.association.created/deleted now carry the AUTHOR in metadata.userId
  (plus actorType, IP and user agent) and the person whose access changed in
  payload.userId. Before, metadata.userId was the target, so the audit trail
  recorded that every person had granted themselves their own role.

commits.title: fix(iam): quem concede papel, recusa com rastro e quatro olhos para acesso sensível (#549)
commits.body:
fix(iam): quem concede papel, recusa com rastro e quatro olhos para acesso sensível (#549)

* fix(iam): quem concede papel, recusa com rastro e quatro olhos para acesso sensível

Três furos de controle de acesso no iam, achados no console do backoffice do CBP
(painel #1750) e na auditoria do BaaS (G3).

1. Escalada de privilégio. Quem tinha gestão de acesso (IAM_MANAGER) dava ADMIN a si
   ou a outra pessoa. Agora (src/iam/authorization/access-guard.ts):
   - só concede ou tira um papel quem tem TODAS as permissões dele, comparado com o
     mesmo mapa que monta o token (teste roda a guarda ao lado de resolvePermissions
     para todo par de papéis);
   - ninguém altera os próprios papéis, nem root;
   - máquina (chave, M2M) não concede papel de pessoa, salvo a organização `dono`
     (como o painel provisiona o dono de um tenant novo);
   - não há rota de papel customizado/editar permissão; catraca falha se nascer.

2. Recusa sem rastro. Middleware auditAccessRefusals entre authMiddleware e
   requirePermission publica `*.refused` (association, mfa, access-request,
   access-policy, api-keys.key) com a organização do autor e o autor — nunca
   actorType sem userId, nunca o alvo em payload.userId.

3. Quatro olhos. Política por organização (organizations.access_approval_required,
   NULL = padrão da casa desligado, declarado como padrão; recomendação: ligado no
   CBP). Papel administrativo/financeiro, reset de segundo fator, chave com escrita e
   afrouxar a própria política viram pedido (iam.access_requests) que outra pessoa da
   organização aprova, com prazo de 24 h, reivindicação condicionada e trilha. Chave
   aprovada é resgatada só pelo autor; PATCH não amplia chave para escrita.

Migration 20261002100000_iam_access_requests, aditiva e idempotente (provada contra
o schema da main, aplicada duas vezes, diff vazio).

* fix(iam): revisão adversarial do quatro olhos — conta-irmã, tomar a conta, virar dono, rotação e varredura

Escaladas medidas na revisão do #549 e fechadas, cada uma com teste (unitário e integração):

- Conta-irmã aprova: `users.email` é único com caixa (Ana@ ≠ ana@) e aceita +sufixo; a segunda
  conta da mesma caixa postal aprovava o pedido da primeira. Decidir compara o e-mail canônico do
  decisor com o de quem pediu e o do alvo.
- Tomar a conta em vez de receber o papel: IAM_MANAGER trocava senha/e-mail e resetava o segundo
  fator do ADMIN (e o ADMIN de um tenant, de alguém que é admin em outra organização). Nova régua
  `checkCredentialChange` (regra 1 sobre os papéis sensíveis do alvo; multi-organização e root só
  o operador), no PATCH /users, no reset e na aprovação do reset. Recusa com rastro.
- Virar operador: PATCH/POST /organizations com type 'dono' por admin de tenant dava à chave dele
  o alcance do operador (conceder papel, editar usuário de qualquer tenant). Só root ou a `dono`.
- Rotação: com a política ligada, rotacionar a chave de ESCRITA de outra pessoa devolvia o segredo
  sem segunda aprovação. Agora 403 WRITE_SCOPE_NEEDS_APPROVAL, com rastro.
- Cancelar pedido de papel APROVADO (execução em curso) deixava CANCELLED com o papel concedido.
- Varredura: listar grava EXPIRED (com evento sem autor) o pendente vencido.
- Migration renomeada para 20261002110000: colidia com o carimbo do #548 (baas).

fix(iam): refresh grant re-resolves organization and roles instead of dropping them (#526)

The refresh token carried only sub/email, so every renewed access token came
back without organizationId and without permissions: the banking console
dropped the session at the first renewal (~1h) and other clients silently lost
their permissions.

- Refresh token now carries the login's organizationId (and amr, if any).
- New TokenRenewalService re-reads the user and the CURRENT roles: deactivated,
  deleted, or removed from the organization -> invalid_grant, with a
  security.token.refused event (USER_INACTIVE | ORGANIZATION_ACCESS_REVOKED).
- isRoot comes from the user now; amr is copied verbatim, never upgraded.
- Legacy refresh tokens without organization renew unscoped, as before.

commits.body:
fix(analytics): consumer health no longer fails /health/ready; bounded dead-letter without loss; subject-based suppression in the event list

- /analytics/health/ready keeps the consumer check in the body (degraded) but never fails on it:
  Launch probes ready and pulls failing replicas from the route, so a stalled consumer would take
  the read API (including the instrumentation health that shows the problem) off the air. The 503
  moves to /analytics/health/consumer, for monitoring only.
- analytics:dead-letter is capped (ANALYTICS_DEAD_LETTER_MAX, default 10000). When full, the
  message is neither copied nor acked: it stays pending and is retried (stats.deadLetterFull) and
  the consumer health reports the full list.
- /events by dimension at day granularity also suppresses cells with fewer than 5 subjects.
- Integration: another organization's token sees nothing from /events, /overview and /alerts.

commits.title: feat(iam): segundo fator TOTP com códigos de recuperação, login em duas etapas e claim amr (#525)
commits.body:
feat(iam): segundo fator TOTP com códigos de recuperação, login em duas etapas e claim amr (#525)

* feat(iam): TOTP second factor with recovery codes, two-step login and amr claim

- Two-step login: right password + factor owed returns an opaque short-lived
  challenge (hash in Redis), never a token; the TOTP or recovery code exchanges
  it for the token pair.
- amr claim (RFC 8176) in access and refresh tokens: pwd | pwd+otp+mfa |
  pwd+mfa (recovery); the refresh grant preserves it.
- Enrollment (self-service or owed at login when the organization has
  mfaRequired): secret encrypted with IAM_MFA_MASTER_KEY via credential-crypto,
  otpauth URI for the QR, first code confirms, 10 recovery codes shown once and
  stored only as SHA-256.
- Replay guard: each TOTP step claimed once with a conditional UPDATE (race
  tested against Postgres); 5 wrong codes lock the factor for 15 min.
- Admin reset of another user's factor with mandatory reason, refresh tokens
  revoked; self reset refused; mfaEnabled removed from PATCH /users/:id.
- iam.mfa.* events mapped in the audit trail (resource user_mfa); no secret,
  code or recovery code in events or logs.
- Organization policy mfaRequired (default false). Additive, idempotent migration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(iam): MFA lock holds under parallel guesses; reset confined to single-org users; challenge consumed once

Adversarial review of #525:

- Lock bypass by parallelism: the lock was read before evaluating and the failure counted
  after, so a burst of N concurrent guesses (one challenge each; the IP rate limit trusts
  X-Forwarded-For) had all N evaluated. Each answer now reserves an attempt with a
  conditional UPDATE before matching; the (max+1)-th request of a burst is refused unread.
- Reset across organizations: the factor belongs to the person and protects every org, but
  any admin whose org the user is linked to could reset it — and an admin can link any user
  into their own org. Non-root admins now reset only users who belong to no other org, never
  a root account, and never by API key.
- Challenge single use: consume() now reports whether it deleted the challenge; the loser of
  two concurrent second steps gets no session.

commits.body:
fix(e-signature): plain call no longer waits out the timeout behind a signer check; masks compared by position

A plain conference that hit the lock held by a signer check polled for a reusable row that
never comes (signer-checked rows are never handed over) and answered 409 only after
providerTimeoutMs + 5s. The waiter now takes the lock once it frees (re-checking for a row
first) and runs its own conference.

signerMatches against a masked document compared the visible run anywhere in the expected
number; it now compares slot by slot when the mask keeps the document's shape, so a CPF with
the same digits at another offset is false, not null.

commits.body:
feat(analytics): agregado diário e funil do Pix por coorte, com passos cegos e a invariante (M4) (#536)

* feat(analytics): agregado diário e funil do Pix por coorte, com passos cegos e a invariante (M4)

PRs 6 e 7 da spec analytics-funis-metricas-e-alertas. As telas passam a ter de onde ler, e nunca
do evento cru.

- `analytics_event_daily`: por organização, dono, dia (UTC do occurred_at) e evento, o total e uma
  linha por atributo declarado (enumeração, booleano, faixa): eventos, sujeitos e jornadas
  distintos no dia.
- `analytics_funnel_daily`: o funil POR COORTE — jornadas que começaram no dia e o desfecho delas
  dentro da janela. É o que faz a janela de conversão valer (quem conclui depois não converte) e a
  leitura sobreviver à retenção do cru.
- Funil declarado em código (`src/analytics/funnels/`). Pix por intenção, janela de 24 h:
  - passos cegos declarados (`key_lookup`, `amount`, `step_up_passed`): `null` e "sem
    instrumento", nunca 0 nem 100%; a conversão ponta a ponta vem `null` enquanto o denominador
    (do app) for cego;
  - exigência de selfie é passo próprio (opcional);
  - saídas separadas: recusa por política (por motivo), falha técnica, desconhecido e abandono;
  - invariante: passo com volume menor que o seguinte e desfecho sem início (órfão) marcam
    instrumentação quebrada, e a queda não é desenhada;
  - sessões abertas como contexto (outra unidade), nunca divididas.
- Agregação agendada (15 min, molde LockedPass): refaz do cru os dias que receberam evento desde o
  cursor (`received_at`), apagando e reinserindo numa transação com a trava da organização. Dia
  cujo cru já começou a vencer NUNCA é refeito: apagaria o agregado.
- `GET /analytics/api/v1/funnels[/:key]`: JWT ou chave, permissão nova `ANALYTICS_READ` (ADMIN e
  VIEWER), dono exato pelo crachá (analytics em SUBACCOUNT_AWARE), período em UTC até 92 dias.
- `banking.pix.transfer.failed` entra no catálogo (o banking já publica).
- Os eventos do `baas` ficam fora do funil: a transação dele não carrega a intenção. A menor
  mudança (o `baas` publicar o `businessId` = `banking:intent:<id>` que já grava) está proposta no
  README §12, não feita aqui.

Testes: unidade (precedência dos desfechos, passos cegos, saídas separadas, invariante, órfão,
coorte parcial, período, funil x catálogo, container); integração com Postgres e Redis reais, do
barramento à rota HTTP (sete intenções com desfechos diferentes, janela, órfão, subconta, outra
organização com parâmetro forjado, idempotência e duas passadas simultâneas, agregado intacto
depois do expurgo do cru e evento atrasado para dia vencido, 401/403/404/400).

commits.body:
feat(e-signature): conferir assinatura de arquivo — Verificador de Conformidade ICP-Brasil (ITI) como primeiro provedor

- Porta própria SignatureVerificationProvider (separada da de assinatura) e o driver ITI_VERIFIER:
  POST {ESIGNATURE_ITI_VERIFIER_URL}/report, multipart signature_files[]/detached_files[],
  relatório normalizado e mascarado (VALID/INVALID/INDETERMINATE, signatário, CPF/CNPJ mascarado,
  data, política, cadeia, motivos). Sem URL padrão: os termos do ITI proíbem apontar para o domínio dele.
- Rotas /verifications (POST multipart ou fileId, GET, GET :id, GET /proof?fileHash=) e
  /verification-settings (GET, PUT admin). Organização só do token.
- Envio a terceiro desligado por padrão, declarado como padrão (source: DEFAULT); ligar é do admin e
  vai para a trilha com antes/depois.
- Retenção: cópia temporária no file-storage (padrão 30 dias, 1–365) com limpeza automática; hash e
  relatório permanentes no audit-trail (esignature.verification.completed, fixado na poda); prova
  por hash lida da trilha.
- Robustez: teto de tamanho, tipo pelo conteúdo, destacada exige o conteúdo, idempotência por hash
  em janela, trava por arquivo; tempo/fora do ar/5xx viram INDETERMINATE com PROVIDER_TIMEOUT /
  PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE / PROVIDER_ERROR, nunca VALID.
- Toda conferência (concluída, reaproveitada ou recusada) publica evento e loga; sem CPF/CNPJ em log.
- Fachada ESignatureVerificationFacade local/remota, DI, dependências file-storage e audit-trail.
- Testes: unitários com o verificador simulado e contrato contra o verificador real (5/5 em 01/10/2026).

feat(iam): members carry the person (e-mail, second factor, last login) and access changes name their author

The backoffice console's access-control area reads "who has access to this
organization" from GET /organizations/:id/members. That listing returned only
the link (userId, roleId), so the console would need one GET /users/:id per
person, and there was no last-login anywhere in the IAM.

  is issued (password, password + second factor, enrollment at login). Renewal
  does not count. Raw SQL so signing in does not bump updatedAt; a failed stamp
  is a warning, never a refused login.
- The members listing returns email, status, mfaEnabled and lastLoginAt per
  member. No secret.
- iam.association.created/deleted now carry the AUTHOR in metadata.userId
  (plus actorType, IP and user agent) and the person whose access changed in
  payload.userId. Before, metadata.userId was the target, so the audit trail
  recorded that every person had granted themselves their own role.

The owner's test: wrong number burned the first request, the desktop retried, and the
new request stayed PENDING on the server while the app showed nothing. The app only
asked on open, on resume, on sign-in and with the approval screen open.

- src/security/desktop-access-watch.ts (pure TS): with a session and the app in the
  foreground it polls GET /v1/approvals every 4 s on any screen; in background it does
  not call the server and only ticks every 30 s to notice a return whose `active` event
  Android dropped; `active` asks right away; sign-out stops it and discards in-flight
  answers. A new request opens DesktopAccess once per requestId; whatever leaves the
  server list (refused, wrong number, approved, expired) never reopens; PixPending and
  Biometric are not interrupted.
- App.tsx owns the single watch; DesktopAccessScreen reads its list through
  useDesktopPending() instead of running a second poller (createPendingPoller removed).
- Tests: other screen, background pause/resume, frozen-Android return, no duplicate,
  refused/expired never reopen, sign-out, plus the owner's scenario end to end against

commits.title: fix(banking-app): one central watch for desktop access requests, on every screen
commits.body:
fix(banking-app): one central watch for desktop access requests, on every screen

The owner's test: wrong number burned the first request, the desktop retried, and the
new request stayed PENDING on the server while the app showed nothing. The app only
asked on open, on resume, on sign-in and with the approval screen open.

- src/security/desktop-access-watch.ts (pure TS): with a session and the app in the
  foreground it polls GET /v1/approvals every 4 s on any screen; in background it does
  not call the server and only ticks every 30 s to notice a return whose `active` event
  Android dropped; `active` asks right away; sign-out stops it and discards in-flight
  answers. A new request opens DesktopAccess once per requestId; whatever leaves the
  server list (refused, wrong number, approved, expired) never reopens; PixPending and
  Biometric are not interrupted.
- App.tsx owns the single watch; DesktopAccessScreen reads its list through
  useDesktopPending() instead of running a second poller (createPendingPoller removed).
- Tests: other screen, background pause/resume, frozen-Android return, no duplicate,
  refused/expired never reopen, sign-out, plus the owner's scenario end to end against
  the reference server.

fix(agents): the agent's model is the one that answers

The agent has a "model" field (fast / smart / powerful). The orchestrator was
called with a fixed 'smart' on both the chat and the test path, so the field
was decoration: every agent ran, and was billed, as smart.

The orchestrator now receives the agent's model, normalised under the provider
that actually answers — an alias resolves there, and a model name from a
provider we fell back from degrades to fast instead of a 404. The test endpoint
uses the same model as the conversation, so a test tells the truth.

Owner's rule (2026-09-29): every AI call uses what is configured.

commits.body:
fix(credit-channel): late retry of the same acceptance no longer re-dispatches W8 nor overwrites the stored outcome

- re-read the stored result under the run lock: a call with the same acceptanceId that finished
  between the first read and the claim used to let the late call dispatch W8 again, get REPETIDA,
  overwrite the stored success with a refusal and release the proposal;
- stored result and run lock keyed by tenant + proposal + acceptanceId (an id replayed on another
  proposal never reads the first one's outcome), and read BEFORE the hash check, so a retry after
  the acceptance touched the proposal is not PROPOSAL_CHANGED;
- the Pix key goes to the lead alone: the stale customData snapshot deep-merged back over what the
  desk changed meanwhile.

Achado 4 da revisão do BB #532. O ObTermsScreen buscava `getLegalDocument` no momento do "Aceitar"
e mandava esse hash: um release do cms entre a leitura e o aceite fazia a pessoa aceitar um texto
que nunca abriu.

- `LEGAL_DOCUMENT_OUTDATED`: zera o aceite e o visto, recarrega os textos e mostra "Os termos
  foram atualizados" (o desfecho que já existia).
- A linha de cada documento mostra a versão que veio do servidor.

commits.title: feat(banking-console): access control area — people, roles × permissions, machine credentials, four-eyes, organization and trail (#1750)
commits.body:
feat(banking-console): access control area — people, roles × permissions, machine credentials, four-eyes, organization and trail (#1750)

The owner's 24/09 decision: the backoffice exposes access control as its
own area. Every rule stays in the blocks (iam, api-keys, audit-trail); the
console reads, asks and shows the refusal.

Bridge
- The closed table reaches four blocks (baas, iam, api-keys, audit-trail),
  each at its own URL and prefix. api-keys and audit-trail URLs are
  optional: without them those tabs answer 503 AREA_UNAVAILABLE.
- Operations that need the organization declare sessionOrg ('path' or
  'body'); the bridge puts the BADGE's organization in after reading the
  session (withSessionScope). The browser still cannot send one: scope keys
  are refused anywhere in the request, path params only take UUIDs.
- 13 new ops: accessOrganization, listMembers, listRoles, createPerson,
  grantRole, activatePerson (status 'ativo' only), revokeRole (DELETE with
  body), resetSecondFactor (reason >= 5), listApiKeys, apiKey, createApiKey
  (allowedResources REQUIRED — without it api-keys mints an unrestricted
  key), revokeApiKey, listAccessTrail (resourceType required).
- Per-op refusal phrases for the iam's code-less 409/403; 204 becomes 200 {}.

Screens (/access/*)
- People: role, second factor, last login, status; invite = create ->
  grant -> activate, resumable from the failed step with the same person;
  temporary password generated in the browser and shown once.
- Person: change role (grant new before removing old), reset another
  person's second factor with reason (not offered to oneself; iam refuses
  it anyway), revoke access (all roles here).
- Roles x permissions with search and holders count; machine credentials
  with scope, create (always scoped) and revoke, key shown once; four-eyes
  page (block guarantees, who holds which power today, what still has no
  second approval); organization of the badge; access trail.
- Every write confirms and repeats the environment (access wording).

Tests: closed-table invariants and the scope ratchet for every op, the real
bridge against fake iam/api-keys/audit (organization from the token, never
from the browser), 20 screen tests. 103 vitest + 97 node tests green.

Depends on building-blocks-v2 #540 for e-mail/second factor/last login in
the members listing and for the trail to name who changed a role; on an
older iam the screen says the iam does not inform it yet.

commits.body:
feat(banking-console): access control area — people, roles × permissions, machine credentials, four-eyes, organization and trail

The owner's 24/09 decision: the backoffice exposes access control as its
own area. Every rule stays in the blocks (iam, api-keys, audit-trail); the
console reads, asks and shows the refusal.

Bridge
- The closed table reaches four blocks (baas, iam, api-keys, audit-trail),
  each at its own URL and prefix. api-keys and audit-trail URLs are
  optional: without them those tabs answer 503 AREA_UNAVAILABLE.
- Operations that need the organization declare sessionOrg ('path' or
  'body'); the bridge puts the BADGE's organization in after reading the
  session (withSessionScope). The browser still cannot send one: scope keys
  are refused anywhere in the request, path params only take UUIDs.
- 13 new ops: accessOrganization, listMembers, listRoles, createPerson,
  grantRole, activatePerson (status 'ativo' only), revokeRole (DELETE with
  body), resetSecondFactor (reason >= 5), listApiKeys, apiKey, createApiKey
  (allowedResources REQUIRED — without it api-keys mints an unrestricted
  key), revokeApiKey, listAccessTrail (resourceType required).
- Per-op refusal phrases for the iam's code-less 409/403; 204 becomes 200 {}.

Screens (/access/*)
- People: role, second factor, last login, status; invite = create ->
  grant -> activate, resumable from the failed step with the same person;
  temporary password generated in the browser and shown once.
- Person: change role (grant new before removing old), reset another
  person's second factor with reason (not offered to oneself; iam refuses
  it anyway), revoke access (all roles here).
- Roles x permissions with search and holders count; machine credentials
  with scope, create (always scoped) and revoke, key shown once; four-eyes
  page (block guarantees, who holds which power today, what still has no
  second approval); organization of the badge; access trail.
- Every write confirms and repeats the environment (access wording).

Tests: closed-table invariants and the scope ratchet for every op, the real
bridge against fake iam/api-keys/audit (organization from the token, never
from the browser), 20 screen tests. 103 vitest + 97 node tests green.

Depends on building-blocks-v2 #540 for e-mail/second factor/last login in
the members listing and for the trail to name who changed a role; on an
older iam the screen says the iam does not inform it yet.

commits.body:
feat(banking,biometrics): review dossier — applicant data and 5-min media for the human review desk

The human reviewer of an INCONCLUSIVE opening selfie needs to see who applied and what the
machine saw. Two person-only, audited reads, both POST with a mandatory reason:

- banking: POST /admin/opening-reviews/:biometricSessionId/applicant — the data declared in the
  opening draft (pii_cipher): full name, birth date, e-mail, masked phone, masked CPF, step, state
  and deadline. Never the CPF in clear.
- biometrics: POST /sessions/:id/review-media — 5-minute read-only presigned URLs for the document
  photo, the portrait extracted from it, the best selfie frame and the challenge video. DISCARD
  retention, purged media and missing evidence answer 200 with the reason and no URL.

Rules in both: BIOMETRICS_ADMIN and a PERSON (API key, client_credentials and the internal
block token are refused with 403); organization/subaccount only from the token (other org = 404);
every access publishes banking.onboarding.pii.viewed / biometrics.review.media.viewed (who, why,
which fields/pieces, never values or URLs) BEFORE responding — trail down = 503 and nothing leaves;
every refusal publishes *.refused. Cache-Control: no-store.

Supporting changes:
- file-storage download-url accepts expiresIn (30..3600 s) that only shortens PRESIGNED_URL_EXPIRY;
  the facade passes expiresInSeconds.
- credentialKindOf moved to @shared/utils/credential-kind (biometrics review reuses it).
- audit mapper: biometrics.review.* points at the biometrics_session.
- DI: BiometricsReviewService (#554) was resolved via @Service() with constructor deps and no
  Container.set — the DI ratchet flagged it BROKEN (the build emits no decorator metadata). It and
  the new media service are now registered explicitly.

A person with BIOMETRICS_ADMIN approves or rejects an INCONCLUSIVE session the policy sent to
review (onInconclusive: REVIEW), always with a reason. Machine credentials (API key,
client_credentials) are refused; REJECTED never becomes APPROVED; the declared subject
(customerId) cannot review their own session. Approving an ONBOARDING with enrollOnApprove forms
the face enrollment (anchor) like the automatic approval does; enrollment preconditions are
checked first and a failed enrollment rolls the session back to INCONCLUSIVE. The reason goes
into decision.review and out on biometrics.session.reviewed (audit trail). banking needs no
change: its next read of the opening draft sees APPROVED with an anchor and opens the account.

perf(lxc): templates build in a fraction of the time — COPY --chown and rootfs straight from the build

Where the minutes went in a bb-runtime build (measured 02/10/2026): 4m12s in
'exporting to image' and 2m04s in 'chown -R /app' out of 7m18s — and the chown
grew to 6m54s by the end of the day, as cache and disk filled.

- Dockerfile, docker/Dockerfile.rooms-agent-worker: the user is created before
  /app and the COPY carries --chown. Same ownership, one copy instead of two,
  and the hard links bun creates survive (9048 instead of 2).
- scripts/build-lxc-template.sh: the rootfs comes straight out of the build
  (--output type=tar) instead of image → docker create → docker export.
- template-build / docker-gc: clean the intermediate tar.
- build-template.sh fila: shows fleet deploys that build on the same host.

Checked file by file against the old rootfs: 59405 entries, zero differences
in name, owner or mode. The tar exporter differs from docker export only in
what docker create injects (/.dockerenv, dev/console, dev/pts, dev/shm, empty
etc/hostname, etc/hosts, etc/resolv.conf).

commits.title: feat(banking,biometrics): dossiê da revisão — dados do solicitante e mídia de 5 min para a mesa (#557)
commits.body:
feat(banking,biometrics): dossiê da revisão — dados do solicitante e mídia de 5 min para a mesa (#557)

* feat(banking,biometrics): review dossier — applicant data and 5-min media for the human review desk

The human reviewer of an INCONCLUSIVE opening selfie needs to see who applied and what the
machine saw. Two person-only, audited reads, both POST with a mandatory reason:

- banking: POST /admin/opening-reviews/:biometricSessionId/applicant — the data declared in the
  opening draft (pii_cipher): full name, birth date, e-mail, masked phone, masked CPF, step, state
  and deadline. Never the CPF in clear.
- biometrics: POST /sessions/:id/review-media — 5-minute read-only presigned URLs for the document
  photo, the portrait extracted from it, the best selfie frame and the challenge video. DISCARD
  retention, purged media and missing evidence answer 200 with the reason and no URL.

Rules in both: BIOMETRICS_ADMIN and a PERSON (API key, client_credentials and the internal
block token are refused with 403); organization/subaccount only from the token (other org = 404);
every access publishes banking.onboarding.pii.viewed / biometrics.review.media.viewed (who, why,
which fields/pieces, never values or URLs) BEFORE responding — trail down = 503 and nothing leaves;
every refusal publishes *.refused. Cache-Control: no-store.

Supporting changes:
- file-storage download-url accepts expiresIn (30..3600 s) that only shortens PRESIGNED_URL_EXPIRY;
  the facade passes expiresInSeconds.
- credentialKindOf moved to @shared/utils/credential-kind (biometrics review reuses it).
- audit mapper: biometrics.review.* points at the biometrics_session.
- DI: BiometricsReviewService (#554) was resolved via @Service() with constructor deps and no
  Container.set — the DI ratchet flagged it BROKEN (the build emits no decorator metadata). It and
  the new media service are now registered explicitly.

commits.title: feat(template-builder): deterministic, queue-aware and failure-proof builds
commits.body:
feat(template-builder): deterministic, queue-aware and failure-proof builds

The host builds many times a day for several sessions at once. This makes the
outcome the same whoever else is building, and gives visibility and control
over what piles up.

template-build (host):
- skips a commit already published and whole on every node (ledger + size
  check on the nodes); force to rebuild
- cleans before and after EVERY build (cache stays), not only when short
- refuses before starting: free disk and memory here, free disk on each node,
  Docker and nodes answering
- runs the build in its own process group and waits: a cancelled or timed-out
  run kills the whole build, removes what it left half-written on the nodes,
  cleans, reports and frees the lock in seconds
- tells whoever waits who holds the host and for how long
- reports disk before/after and peak memory next to the time per phase

build-template.sh (client): fila, cancelar; joins an existing run for the same
commit and family; shows what is ahead with an estimate; refuses to queue on
top of 3 or more unless told to; --force.

build-template.yml: run-name says what is being built; per-commit concurrency
group; force input.

build-lxc-template.sh: atomic publish (temporary name + size check + mv), as
the panel's script already did.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.title: feat(biometrics): human review of INCONCLUSIVE sessions — POST /sessions/:id/review
commits.body:
feat(biometrics): human review of INCONCLUSIVE sessions — POST /sessions/:id/review

A person with BIOMETRICS_ADMIN approves or rejects an INCONCLUSIVE session the policy sent to
review (onInconclusive: REVIEW), always with a reason. Machine credentials (API key,
client_credentials) are refused; REJECTED never becomes APPROVED; the declared subject
(customerId) cannot review their own session. Approving an ONBOARDING with enrollOnApprove forms
the face enrollment (anchor) like the automatic approval does; enrollment preconditions are
checked first and a failed enrollment rolls the session back to INCONCLUSIVE. The reason goes
into decision.review and out on biometrics.session.reviewed (audit trail). banking needs no
change: its next read of the opening draft sees APPROVED with an anchor and opens the account.

feat(decision-engine): executar a decisão-FOLHA do DRG, não decisions.first()

A execução direta de política (decision.service) chamava o runner sem
decisionKey. O runner então usa `decisions.first()` — e o Camunda reordena as
decisões no parse, então "first" não é a primeira do XML e, num DRG, costuma ser
uma dependência, não a decisão que o chamador quer. Resultado: um DMN
multi-decisão rodava/simulava a decisão errada (uma não-folha) e nunca mostrava
o desfecho final.

findLeafDecisionId(dmnXml) acha a folha (decisão que nenhum requiredDecision
aponta) e a passamos como decisionKey; o runner então encadeia as dependências
(DmnExecutionService.kt:89-94). Modelo de 1 decisão: a única é a folha. Folha
ambígua (nenhuma ou várias) → undefined, mantém o comportamento do runner.

Parse por regex de propósito (conteúdo DMN confiável, sem puxar parser XML pro
hot path). 6 testes unitários.

feat(face-engine): enquadrar o documento antes do rosto e do CPF — 2026.10.2

Print do celular (CNH digital deitada na tela) ou foto do cartão torto sobre a mesa:
o /v1/portrait agora enquadra (quadrilátero ID-1/passaporte com warp de perspectiva,
retângulo do cartão no print, ou margem em volta do rosto), depois orienta (2026.10.1)
e só então recorta o retrato e lê o CPF.

- Proporção real pela focal estimada (Zhang & He), não pela média dos lados.
- Candidato só vale com exatamente um rosto ocupando <= 30% dele; senão, caminho de hoje.
- CPF = união da imagem inteira com o documento enquadrado (em paralelo): nenhum limiar
  mudou e outro CPF fora do cartão continua dando mismatch.
- document.frame / quality.details.documentFrame para diagnóstico.

Medido em cenas sintéticas (rosto GAN): mesa 55° 0,676 -> 0,907; mesa 35° 0,866 -> 0,925;
print 0,971 -> 0,979; cartão pequeno 0,910 -> 0,944; CPF unread -> match nas fotos.

Templates are built from any pushed commit and PRs are squash-merged. Once

refs/deploy-guard/ so it does not flood `git branch -r`. Test: a commit
reachable only by refs/pull/7/head on a bare origin (red before, green after).

commits.title: fix: the bot survives a real-disk volume, login refuses an empty body, and the AI path gets a real smoke
commits.body:
fix: the bot survives a real-disk volume, login refuses an empty body, and the AI path gets a real smoke

Three leftovers of the 'copilot stopped' front.

The meeting bot's entrypoint copied the profile seed with one `cp -a`. A
volume that is a real filesystem (Launch's is) comes with `lost+found`, which
not even the root of an unprivileged LXC can read: the copy failed, `set -e`
killed the container, and it restarted forever. The seed is now copied item by
item, without `lost+found`, and an unreadable cache file no longer costs the
session. It says so when the seed brings no session.
`entrypoint.selftest.sh` proves it without Chrome or audio, and fails on the
old entrypoint.

`POST /auth/login` took an inline type the ValidationPipe cannot see, so a body
without `email` reached Prisma as `undefined` and came back as a 500. It now
has a DTO: a missing field is a 400.

`scripts/smoke-painel-prod.sh` is the real smoke of the AI path in production —
assistant, agents, video copilot, knowledge index, link bot — 31 checks against
the live API on a demo account, credentials read from outside the repo.

commits.title: feat(ai-insights): motor de análise por IA genérico + Insights/Agentes do Decision
commits.body:
feat(ai-insights): motor de análise por IA genérico + Insights/Agentes do Decision

Um subsistema de análise por IA desacoplado, reutilizável por qualquer
vertical, e o primeiro consumidor dele: as telas Insights e Agentes de
análise do console do Decision.

## Motor genérico (`ai-insights`)
Módulo novo, cego ao domínio. `AnalysisRunnerService` roda um agente sobre
dados que o chamador montou, mede contra um saldo de créditos por ciclo e
guarda o histórico — tudo por uma chave opaca `(context, ownerKey, cycleKey)`
que o motor nunca interpreta. Usa o `ai-core` (LLMProviderFactory) para a
chamada ao LLM (CatalisaAI/Claude por padrão), pede uma saída JSON estruturada
e tolera resposta fora do formato (guarda o texto cru). Uma corrida que falha
entra no histórico como FAILED e NÃO é cobrada. Tabela/ledger `AiAnalysis`
(migração aditiva e idempotente).

## Decision: Insights + Agentes de análise (adaptador fino)
- Catálogo `DECISION_AGENTS` (4 agentes: desfechos, carteira, política, resumo
  executivo) com custo e gate por plano — catálogo interno, agentes sob medida
  são roadmap.
- Franquia mensal de créditos por plano (`aiCredits`: 20/100/500/2000/10000),
  no mesmo ciclo civil da cota e da fatura.
- `DecisionInsightsService`: resolve conta→franquia→ciclo, monta só o dado que
  o agente escolhido lê (via métodos públicos do portal) e chama o motor. As
  análises do Decision rodam na chave do fornecedor, pagas por créditos.
- 5 rotas no controller + 5 ops fechadas no BFF + telas `Insights.tsx` e
  `Agentes.tsx` no console (grupo "Inteligência" na sidebar).

## Mesmo motor como action de workflow (`AI_ANALYZE`)
Prova do desacoplamento: o handler `AI_ANALYZE` reusa o MESMO runner, mas paga
com a credencial do próprio tenant (como os demais handlers de IA), sem gate de
crédito. Registrado como os outros (barrel, registry, módulo, schema de
validação).

49 testes: motor (8), adaptador (8), catálogo (6), handler (4), planos (18), +
console (21) e BFF (6) inalterados e verdes.

feat(banking): console and desktop templates are built on the remote build host

No template is built on the machine of whoever runs a deploy (owner's rule).
deploy-banking-console.sh and deploy-banking-desktop.sh still built theirs
locally (npm build, package, docker build, export, scp).

- The scripts ask the build host for the template (scripts/lib/remote-template.sh
  → workflow build-template, family banking-<app>-<env>) and go on through the
  path that already existed for --template: guards, bridge env and the Launch
  stay on the operator's machine.
- --publish-template (build host only) runs what the scripts always did up to
  the copy to the nodes — front build, package, local rehearsal, secret scan,
  template, atomic publish — and stops before the Launch. On the host the
  'HEAD is origin/master' guard becomes 'the commit is in master'.
- Publishing deletes nothing: the date-based retention in the publish step is
  gone; template-gc is the only cleaner.
- build-template.yml: routes banking-* to the app's script through
  template-build (lock, checks, cleanup, node verification, skip-if-published,
  report), with Node and npm ci for the package build.
- --dry-run stays local and uses no Docker.

commits.title: perf(lxc): templates build in a fraction of the time — COPY --chown and rootfs straight from the build
commits.body:
perf(lxc): templates build in a fraction of the time — COPY --chown and rootfs straight from the build

Where the minutes went in a panel-runtime build (measured 02/10/2026): 2m19s
in 'exporting to image' and 2m05s in 'chown -R /app' out of 5m15s.

- api and worker Dockerfiles: the user is created before /app and each COPY
  carries --chown. The worker assembles its /app in a stage of its own
  (lxc-deps) so it can be copied with ownership instead of chowned afterwards.
- scripts/build-lxc-template.sh: the rootfs comes straight out of the build
  (--output type=tar) instead of image → docker create → docker export.

Checked file by file against the old rootfs (name, owner, mode):
- api: 65949 entries, zero differences.
- worker: /app identical (23909 entries); the only difference is that
  /root/.cache/prisma — the CLI's download cache, 51 MB left behind by running
  'prisma generate' inside the rootfs stage — is no longer shipped.
The tar exporter differs from docker export only in what docker create
injects (/.dockerenv, dev/console, dev/pts, dev/shm, empty etc/hostname,
etc/hosts, etc/resolv.conf).

commits.body:
fix(decision): ícones do DMN renderizam — CSP bloqueava a fonte (causa raiz)

A causa raiz de "os ícones do modeler somem" NÃO era cache nem o bundler: o CSP
do hotsite-kit tinha `font-src https://fonts.gstatic.com` — só fonte do Google.
A fonte de ícones do dmn-js (self-hosted + base64) era barrada em silêncio, então
NENHUM ícone (paleta, lápis, arrastar, glifo do nó) renderizava.

- http.mjs: `font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com` (permite a fonte
  de ícone local e a embutida). Vale para o painel em prod também.
- DmnModeler: imports do dmn-js passam a ESTÁTICOS (seguem no chunk lazy, mas o
  Vite empacota a fonte e reescreve a url, o que o import dinâmico não fazia);
  a dmn-embedded.css entra como ?raw (o minificador do esbuild apagava o escape
  do glifo e dropava a @font-face base64); e a fonte é carregada pela FontFace
  API a partir do .woff2 com hash do Vite — caminho mais confiável.
- Marcação por tipo de elemento (decisão/input/nota/knowledge) via elementRegistry
  para o CSS dar identidade a cada um.

Também: notas viram POST-ITS estilizados (fundo âmbar + lombada âmbar à esquerda,
a "dobra"), em vez do colchete cinza que destoava do tema.

commits.body:
fix(ai-insights): resolver a credencial de IA pelos settings do usuário (nada hardcoded)

A LLMProviderFactory RECUSA a chave crua do ambiente de propósito: um call roda
numa credencial do sistema de credenciais. O runner chamava getProvider() sem
credencial quando o chamador não passava uma (o caminho medido/pago pelo
fornecedor, ex.: Decision) — e a factory recusava com "este usuário ainda não
tem credencial de IA", derrubando toda análise.

Agora o runner, quando não recebe `userCredential`, resolve pelo
`UserLlmCredentialResolver` a partir de um `resolveForUserId` que o chamador
passa: a credencial que o usuário escolheu nos settings → a do dono → a de
plataforma `catalisa-ai-<provider>`, com o PROVIDER vindo dos settings do
próprio usuário. NADA hardcoded (sem "anthropic" fixo, sem chave de env).

O adaptador do Decision passa como `resolveForUserId` o DONO da vertical
DECISION, que é CONFIGURÁVEL em `SystemSettings.codePortalOwnerUserIdByVertical`
— não um id fixo. A análise roda nos settings de IA desse dono; o cliente nunca
paga o modelo (o saldo de créditos paga).

Dependência de INSTALADOR: o dono da vertical precisa ter uma credencial de IA
utilizável (própria, ou a de plataforma `catalisa-ai-<provider>`). Sem ela a
análise falha graciosa (FAILED, sem cobrar). Injeções @Optional; testes que dão
`new` seguem passando (+ testes de resolveForUserId).

Incident 03/10/2026 (bb-staging): `--to-template bb-runtime-afee7669` (short
name) was passed to the Launch as is. The Launch stored it on
bb-calculations-engine and answered 200; `pct create` failed and the service
ended `active`, no message, still running the old template.

  any other shape is refused before any call (scripts/lib/template-ref.sh);

  touched (also on --dry-run and --rollback);

  runningTemplateRef must be the target; otherwise the gate fails right away
  showing requested × running, instead of burning the whole window.

commits.title: fix(deploy-guard): find the running commit through refs/pull/*/head (#567)
commits.body:
fix(deploy-guard): find the running commit through refs/pull/*/head (#567)

Templates are built from any pushed commit and PRs are squash-merged. Once
the PR branch is deleted, the commit a block runs is reachable only through
refs/pull/<n>/head, which `git fetch origin` does not bring even with
fetch-depth: 0. Guard 0b then refused every following deploy with "commit
desconhecido", and the only way out (--ignorar-migrations) turned off the
migration check for the whole fleet.

dg_commit's one-time fetch now also brings refs/pull/*/head, into
refs/deploy-guard/ so it does not flood `git branch -r`. Test: a commit
reachable only by refs/pull/7/head on a bare origin (red before, green after).

commits.body:
fix(iam): close two four-eyes bypasses found in review

- With the rule on, changing the password or e-mail of ANOTHER person holding a
  sensitive role is refused (403 CREDENTIAL_CHANGE_FOUR_EYES), except root and the
  `dono` operator key. An ADMIN could set the other approver's password, log in as
  them and approve their own POLICY_RELAX; the weaker MFA reset already became a
  request (MFA_RESET), the password did not.
- PUT access-policy goes back to assertOrgAccess (person of the org, or root). Through
  the `dono` key the POLICY_RELAX request was authored by the platform key's user, so
  SELF_APPROVAL never matched the person who asked from the panel and the trail showed
  the platform. GET still accepts the operator key (count only).

commits.title: feat(iam): four-eyes rule configurable by the account admin without trapping a single-admin org
commits.body:
feat(iam): four-eyes rule configurable by the account admin without trapping a single-admin org

- Turning the access-approval policy ON requires at least 2 eligible approvers (distinct people
  who could decide POLICY_RELAX: active, already signed in, not root, same canonical e-mail counts
  once). Fewer -> 409 APPROVERS_INSUFFICIENT, refused on the trail.
- Turning it OFF with 2+ approvers still becomes a POLICY_RELAX request. With fewer it applies
  immediately, with reason 'single_approver' on iam.access-policy.changed — only by a person who
  holds the permission NOW in the database, root or the platform (dono) key.
- Turning it off (immediately or by approved request) CANCELS the org's PENDING requests, with
  iam.access-request.cancelled (cancelReason 'policy_disabled'). Approved key requests stay.
- Closes the "remove the other approver, then disable alone" shortcut: with the rule on, revoking
  or swapping a role, deactivating, deleting or re-e-mailing a user cannot take the org from 2+ to
  fewer than 2 approvers (409 APPROVER_QUORUM_PROTECTED); only root bypasses.
- Deciding a request re-checks the approver in the database (token permissions intersected with
  current roles): an admin removed while the request waited cannot approve with the old token.
- GET access-policy returns eligibleApprovers (count only), minApprovers, canEnable and
  canDisableImmediately; GET/PUT also accept the platform (dono) key for any org, so the panel can
  offer the toggle to the tenant's account admin.

commits.title: fix(iam): serialize approver-quorum check and write per organization
commits.body:
fix(iam): serialize approver-quorum check and write per organization

Two concurrent removals each saw 3 approvers and both passed, leaving 1 who
could then turn the rule off alone (10/10 in review). Removing/swapping a role,
deactivating, changing e-mail, deleting a user and turning the rule on/off now
check and write under pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(org)), held by a transaction
that stays open until the write lands. The lock is tried (not awaited) so a waiter
never holds a pool connection while the holder needs another to write; busy for
10 s -> 409 APPROVER_QUORUM_BUSY.

The new integration race test fails without the lock (all four removals pass)
and passes with it.

fix(demo-antecipacao): CPF lookup in the reset filtered by the script path instead of the org

`'"'$0'"'` sat outside the single quotes of the `bash -c`, so the OUTER shell expanded it to the
script path. Postgres rejected the uuid, `2>/dev/null` hid it, the lookup always came back empty
and, without a terminal, the script died on `/dev/tty: No such device or address`.

terminal the script stops asking for PROVA_CPF. Regression test without network or database:
`bash scripts/demo-antecipacao/cbp-resetar-demo.test.sh` (fails on master, passes here).

production Atlas (401 "Invalid API key" on step 4).

feat(banking-console): access requests — list, decide and redeem iam four-eyes requests

answer 202 with a request that ANOTHER person of the organization must decide, and
the console had no screen for it (and called the 202 "done").

  (pending by default), detail, Approve / Reject with a mandatory reason, Withdraw
  (requester only) and Redeem the key (requester only, approved key; shown once).

  'query'), accessRequest, approve/reject/cancelAccessRequest, redeemApiKey.
  Projection drops organizationId, requestedByKey and the redeem link, and returns
  null for another organization's request.
- iam refusals translated (SELF_APPROVAL, BENEFICIARY_APPROVAL, APPROVER_NOT_A_PERSON,
  MISSING_PERMISSIONS, ACCESS_REQUEST_EXPIRED, NOT_THE_REQUESTER...).
- 202 is no longer "done": new key, role change, MFA reset and invite say it became a
  request. Role change uses replacesRoleId (one call) so the old role is never removed
  while the new one waits; invite stops before activating.

commits.body:
fix(account-security): change the four-eyes rule with the person's IAM token, not the platform key

Through the platform (`dono`) key the IAM recorded the platform key's user as the
author of the POLICY_RELAX request: the master who asked from the panel could
approve it himself in the IAM (SELF_APPROVAL never matched him), the IAM trail
showed the platform, and any panel master could turn the rule off immediately even
without being an approver in the IAM. PUT now forwards the user's own bearer, so
the IAM checks IAM_ORGANIZATIONS_UPDATE on the person and records them. GET keeps
the platform key (read-only count; PANEL_MASTER has no IAM_* by design).

Pairs with building-blocks-v2#579, which now refuses the `dono` key on that PUT.

commits.title: fix(credentials): BB key under four-eyes returns PENDING_APPROVAL and can be redeemed
commits.body:
fix(credentials): BB key under four-eyes returns PENDING_APPROVAL and can be redeemed

With the iam four-eyes policy on (building-blocks-v2 #549), POST /api-keys with a
write scope answers 202 with an access request and no key. generateBbApiKey read
`data.key` from it and returned `key: undefined`, and the credential modal toasted
"API Key gerada" over an empty field (staging, 06/10, org b0000000-...-0001).

API
- generateBbApiKey returns {status:'ISSUED', key, keyId, prefix} or
  {status:'PENDING_APPROVAL', requestId, expiresAt}; a 2xx without key (or a 202
  without request) is now a 502, never a success.
- POST /credentials/redeem-bb-key/:requestId calls from-request with the caller's
  own token (BB enforces author-only, once, 24h); BB refusal codes become pt-BR.
- Every outcome goes to the log and to AccessLog (BB_API_KEY_ISSUED / _PENDING_APPROVAL
  / _GENERATE_FAILED / _REDEEMED / _REDEEM_REFUSED), with id and prefix only — the
  key never reaches log or trail.
- merchant-bb and credit-blocks-bb no longer store a credential with an undefined
  key when the request is pending; they refuse with an explanation.

Front
- CredentialModal shows the approval notice and a "Resgatar a chave" button that
  fills the field; the success toast only fires with a real key. The pending request
  id (never the key) survives closing the modal.

commits.title: feat(billing): planos da vertical de recrutamento — franquia por unidade
commits.body:
feat(billing): planos da vertical de recrutamento — franquia por unidade

Decisão do dono (06/10): cada vitrine tem planos próprios; recrutamento primeiro,
só franquias das unidades da vertical por enquanto.

- Planos Recrutamento Essencial / Consultoria / Operação / Rede no billing da
  plataforma (o mesmo dos planos Starter/Growth), com franquia e excedente para
  conversa, consultor ativo, entrevista com copiloto e teste de perfil, mais um teto
  de mensagens de WhatsApp sem excedente que segura o pior caso enquanto o agente
  não limita a conversa a 15 mensagens. Dados em
  src/modules/billing/verticals/recrutamento.plans.ts; o spec falha se qualquer
  plano ou excedente deixar menos de 50 % no pior caso (regra do dono).
- seed-billing ganha `--vertical=<chave>`: só produtos, medidores e planos da
  vertical, sem tocar em organizações nem assinaturas; planos levam `metadata`
  (slug, kind, vertical) e itens levam `priceOverride`.
- Ação genérica RECORD_USAGE (allowlist VERTICAL_METERS, migration aditiva): o
  pacote registra as próprias unidades. O BB só agrega por SOMA, então a contagem
  distinta vem da chave de idempotência (contato+dia, consultor+mês, pessoa+teste+mês,
  reunião). Nunca derruba o workflow.
- Pacote recrutamento-v2: nós medirConversa, medirTesteDisc, medirTesteMbti (WF-A,
  TS e export em sincronia) e medirEntrevista (pós-entrevista). Provados pelo
  InterpolationService real.
- Guia de operação: como publicar os planos e como cada unidade é contada.
- Plano 100 %: item das catracas corrigido (o mecanismo já existia no BB).

commits.title: feat(wpp-business): "digitando…" na conversa — POST /messages/typing
commits.body:
feat(wpp-business): "digitando…" na conversa — POST /messages/typing

Mostra o indicador de digitação ao contato a partir da mensagem RECEBIDA que vai
ser respondida, e a marca como lida: é a chamada de "lida" da Cloud API com
`typing_indicator: {type: 'text'}`. Recebe o wamid (`waMessageId`), que é o que o
consumidor do webhook tem; a cópia local da mensagem, quando é da organização,
ganha `readAt`.

A Meta tira o indicador quando a resposta sai ou após 25 s, e não há chamada para
desligar: manter vivo (e parar) é de quem chama — o painel ganha SEND_TYPING e
CANCEL_TYPING.

A fleet rollout (07/10/2026) wrote templateRef on OCI-image services
(bb-dmn-engine in bb-prod). Docker with a template is refused at provisioning
and no route could clear the field: redeploy and PATCH only accept a
non-empty string, so the service stayed failed with delete-and-recreate as
the only way out. Redeploy now accepts templateRef: null (docker only; the
route refuses it for native, which needs a template).

feat(recrutamento): de→para de campos por tenant (mapping-on-passthrough) (#1792)

* feat(recrutamento): de→para de campos por tenant (mapping-on-passthrough)

Permite que cada tenant decida como os campos de uma fonte externa (RecruitCRM)
alimentam a vertical de recrutamento, sem código específico de cliente e sem
perder dados — base para a tela em painel-cliente (Configurações › Integrações).

- Schema: enum FieldMappingMode + model IntegrationFieldMapping (escopo por
  owner, @@unique[owner,source,entityType,sourceKey]) + migration aditiva.
- FieldMappingResolver (núcleo puro): roteia cada campo de origem para canônico
  (MAP), balde namespaced customData.__integration.<source>.<entityType>
  (PASSTHROUGH, default) ou descarte (IGNORE). Ausência de config = passthrough.
- IntegrationFieldMappingService + controller (/integration/field-mappings):
  CRUD escopado pelo JWT; MAP valida targetField ∈ LeadType.fields (guarda: não
  renomeia/apaga chave canônica — contrato das automações DISC/MBTI/hiring_stage).
- RecruitcrmLeadMapper: converte a entidade crua do webhook em Lead (candidato
  no Fase 1), upsert por recruitcrm_candidate_id. No-op se o dono não tem a
  vertical; nunca lança (webhook segue ACK 200).
- Testes unitários do resolver (roteamento, transforms, composição do balde).
- Plano: docs/plans/2026-10-07-recrutamento-field-mapping-de-para.md.

commits.title: feat(workflows): SEND_TYPING e CANCEL_TYPING — "digitando…" até a resposta sair
commits.body:
feat(workflows): SEND_TYPING e CANCEL_TYPING — "digitando…" até a resposta sair

SEND_TYPING liga o indicador na conversa da mensagem recebida e o mantém vivo
(re-envio a cada 20 s; a Meta apaga em 25 s). Desliga no primeiro destes:
CANCEL_TYPING, uma mensagem SAIR para a conversa (conferido no banco a cada volta —
vale para agente, SEND_MESSAGE, template e envio pela tela, em qualquer réplica) ou
o teto de 300 s. O fluxo não lida com segundos: `timeoutSeconds` só reduz o teto.

Conversa, mensagem e device saem do gatilho de mensagem recebida: no atendimento o
nó não tem configuração. Nunca derruba o workflow. Só Cloud API por enquanto
(Baileys registrado como não suportado, sem erro). Depende do BB
POST /wpp-business/api/v1/messages/typing (building-blocks-v2, feat/wpp-biz-typing-indicator).

Pacote recrutamento-v2: nó ligarDigitando no WF-A (TS e export em sincronia).

commits.body:
feat(mesa): liga o bb-mesa no build, no start e no monolito + teste de escopo do consumer (#581)

O PR #562 trouxe o bloco Mesa (src/mesa, dev:mesa, aliases nos 7 vitest
configs) mas deixou de fora o que faz o BB virar deployável:

- scripts/build.mjs: src/mesa/main.ts não estava nos entryPoints, então
  dist/mesa/main.mjs nunca era gerado.
- package.json: faltava start:mesa. Sem ele o gerar-entrypoints.cjs (que lê
  os scripts start:) não cria o entrypoint do mesa, e o launch-env.sh não
  resolve porta/healthPath (lê start:<mod> pra achar o main).
- src/app.ts: o app do mesa não era montado no monolito (todos os outros BBs
  são). Agora /mesa responde em `bun run dev`.

Teste novo do MesaExecutionConsumer cobre a decisão #4 do desenho (o caso abre
no MESMO escopo org/subconta/environment que rodou a decisão): escopo vindo do
registro da execução, fallback pro metadata.subaccountId do evento, caso
org-level sem subconta, outcome resolvido não chega à mesa, e sem fila roteada
não abre caso.

commits.body:
fix(network): scope port forwards to the host's own addresses

DNAT rules were written without a destination match, so a forward for
public port N also rewrote container-to-container traffic to port N on the
bridge. On 09/10/2026 the Scylla forward --dport 8112 -> 172.10.0.112:9042
was hijacking Traefik's connections to a hotsite listening on
172.10.0.231:8112, which answered 500 for weeks; about twenty other forwards
on the node had the same reach.

- dnatSpec adds -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL (every address the host owns,
  nothing else; no per-node config).
- parseDnatRules flags rules without a destination match as unscoped.
- The reconciler rescopes a wanted legacy rule (scoped rule added first,
  legacy copy removed after, so the port never goes dark); on by default,
  rescopeLegacy:false turns it off.
- Deletes remove both shapes, so a deprovision cannot leave the legacy
  rule behind.

commits.title: feat(launch): path-prefix routing per custom domain
commits.body:
feat(launch): path-prefix routing per custom domain

A Launch service's customDomains entry can now be a bare host (as before)
or {host, paths}: only those path prefixes of the host reach the service,
so two services can share one hostname (e.g. api.operacao-digital.ai /waitlist /kb on
the hotsite API, everything else on the app API).

- ingress/traefik: optional explicit router priority; prunePublicRoutes
  removes a service's stale route files by prefix.
- provisioner: bare hosts stay on launch-<id>; each path-scoped domain gets
  launch-<id>-p<n> with PathPrefix and priority 10000, written before the
  main router; stale path routers are pruned on every finalize and removed
  on stop / delete / no healthy replicas / no HTTP. All routers share the
  same cert subjects, so no extra ACME order per host.
- launch-domains: pure helper (split / normalize / parse / text form).
- validation: both shapes accepted on create and POST /services/:id/domains;
  paths match traefik's safePath guard, 1-10 per host.
- postgres adapter + migrate-stores read both shapes back from the jsonb.
- UI: domains card and create dialog take `host /path /path`; detail page
  renders path entries instead of [object Object].
