commits.title: fix(launch): native redeploy keeps the volume's data
commits.body:
fix(launch): native redeploy keeps the volume's data

A native rolling redeploy deleted each replica's LXC before creating the
new one, and the Launch volume (mp0) is a disk owned by that LXC, so every
redeploy brought the service back with an empty volume (operacao-digital-site,
/srv/operacao-digital, on 2026-10-09).

With a volume, the rebuild now stops the old guest, creates the new one
without a disk of its own, reassigns the old mp0 to it before the first
boot (POST /nodes/{node}/lxc/{vmid}/move_volume with target-vmid and
target-volume=mp0), and only then deletes the old guest. If the move or
anything after it fails, the disk is moved back and the old replica is
restarted with its row; if moving it back fails, the new guest is kept
stopped. Nothing that holds the volume is deleted on a failure path, and
the rollout stops with a statusMessage saying where the data is.

The escorted single-replica flow uses the same rebuild for replica 0; the
temporary replica's fresh volume is destroyed with it. Services without a
volume rebuild exactly as before. A pinned vmid (baseVmid) plus a volume
is refused before anything is touched, since the new guest cannot take
back the id while the old one still holds the disk.

Also fixes the comment that claimed the mount point survives a redeploy.

commits.title: feat(hotsites): one Launch template for every public hotsite (hotsite-runtime)
commits.body:
feat(hotsites): one Launch template for every public hotsite (hotsite-runtime)

The hotsites run on hand-made LXC guests (CT 140/141/142/143/154/306). This
adds the template family that lets them run as Launch native services instead:

- deploy/lxc/hotsite/Dockerfile: builds all six sites (`node build.mjs`) from
  the commit, scans dist/ for secrets, boots every site from the built tree
  (rehearse.mjs: healthz, pt home, en home, real 404 per language) and only
  then lays the tree on Debian + systemd as `lxc-rootfs`.
- hotsite@.service + hotsite-start: the instance picks the site
  (`hotsite@agora` -> /srv/apps/agora, env in /etc/bb/agora.env); the
  launcher drops the guests' *_DIST paths and points COUNTER_FILE at the
  unit's StateDirectory. Same sandbox the guests run with.
- apps/med/server/index.mjs: med has no BFF; this reproduces the Caddyfile
  contract (try_files, real 404 per language, the three 301s with the query
  kept, nosniff/referrer headers, gzip, etag) so med runs from the same
  template. Covered by server.test.mjs; the Caddy guest is unchanged.
- build-lxc-template.sh: `--only hotsite-runtime` (opt-in; a panel build
  does not build hotsites). Built only on the build host, like every family.

The assignment term is born in a workflow sandbox without crypto, so termo.hash is a

waiting for the analysis, opening the proposal showed 'serviço indisponível'. The
channel now hashes the exact text it shows; the acceptance compares against the same
value, and the internal termo.hash (portal signature, disbursement check) is untouched.

commits.body:
fix(web): allow microphone and camera on our own origin

The security headers from #740 set `Permissions-Policy: microphone=(), camera=()`,
which disables both features for every origin, including ours. Chrome then rejects
getUserMedia with NotAllowedError without prompting, and enumerateDevices returns
unlabeled entries, so the video room (/video-meetings/:id and the guest link /v/:code)
lists no microphone or camera. Measured in production on 2026-10-09.

`(self)` keeps them off for any embedded third party while letting the room work.

fix(workflows): scope manual-execution trigger lookup to the checked workflow (#1819)

POST /workflows/:id/execute and /execute/start checked access to :id but
resolved body.triggerId with an unscoped findUnique and then ran
trigger.workflow, so a trigger of another workflow (another tenant's) could
decide which workflow ran.

{ id, workflowId } and refuses anything else with the same 404 as a missing
trigger. dispatchManualEvent resolves it before emitting the audit event, and
the streaming endpoint validates it before creating the execution record.
Without a triggerId the oldest trigger of the workflow is used, as before.

commits.title: fix(billing): cartão salvo agnóstico de vertical — o Decision salvava no gateway do Biometrics
commits.body:
fix(billing): cartão salvo agnóstico de vertical — o Decision salvava no gateway do Biometrics

O adaptador de cartão salvo (`BbSavedCardPaymentMethod`) nomeava a vertical
e a tabela: lia e gravava o cliente do provedor em `biometricsAccount`, abria
o cadastro com o dono da vertical BIOMETRICS e marcava as cobranças com
`origin: 'code-portal-biometrics'`. O Decision reusava o mesmo adaptador, então
o cartão de um cliente do Decision iria para o gateway do vendedor do
Biometrics. Em staging aparece como "Code Portal não configurado para a
vertical BIOMETRICS"; em produção, onde o Biometrics tem dono, salvaria e
cobraria pelo vendedor errado. Achado no smoke da tela de cartões.

Agora o adaptador não conhece vertical nenhuma:
- a porta ganha `bindTo(owner)`; o núcleo (`SubscriptionBillingService`)
  amarra o adaptador à vertical que ele cobra, a partir das portas que já
  tem: `product.verticalKey` e `store.accounts`;
- a conta genérica (`BillingAccount`) declara `company` e
  `paymentsCustomerId`, que as duas tabelas já têm, e o store ganha
  `claimPaymentsCustomer` (grava só se ainda não houver);
- a origem da cobrança vem da vertical; sem `bindTo`, o adaptador recusa
  em vez de adivinhar;
- o adaptador sai de `code-portal-billing/` para `subscription-billing/`.

Testes: o do adaptador roda com verticais inventadas e um prisma sem tabela
de produto; um guarda (`vertical-agnostic.spec.ts`) reprova código do núcleo
que nomeie produto, tabela ou descritor de vertical; o do Decision trava que
o cartão fica na vertical DECISION e na DecisionAccount. 342 passam no
núcleo, Biometrics e Decision.

fix(demo-antecipacao): CPF lookup in the reset filtered by the script path instead of the org (#1784)

`'"'$0'"'` sat outside the single quotes of the `bash -c`, so the OUTER shell expanded it to the
script path. Postgres rejected the uuid, `2>/dev/null` hid it, the lookup always came back empty
and, without a terminal, the script died on `/dev/tty: No such device or address`.

Now the org is expanded on purpose (`$ORG`), a 0/2+ result is reported, and with no CPF and no
terminal the script stops asking for PROVA_CPF. Regression test without network or database:
`bash scripts/demo-antecipacao/cbp-resetar-demo.test.sh` (fails on master, passes here).

Roteiro: two new troubleshooting rows, including the staging bb-decision-engine pointing at the
production Atlas (401 "Invalid API key" on step 4).

commits.title: fix(credit-desk): resolve the flow to execute by ownership, never by visibility (#1818)
commits.body:
fix(credit-desk): resolve the flow to execute by ownership, never by visibility (#1818)

The credit desk resolved the workflow to dispatch through
`findTriggerIndex` -> `getVisibleUserIds`, which is `null` (no filter) for
a PANEL_ADMIN. When a banking channel's tenant owner was a PANEL_ADMIN, the
newest active workflow listening to the event from ANY tenant won: measured
in staging on 2026-10-09, the channel dispatched another tenant's analysis
flow, which ran as that other user with its credentials and failed with
"Lead not found". A cross-tenant execution.

- WorkflowsService: `findTriggerIndex` and `findOne` take `ownedOnly`; it is
  the visibility rule with the admin escape removed (user + descendants,
  never null). Non-admin paths and the acting context are unchanged.
- CreditDeskService: `creditWorkflows` (feeds the server `workflowFor` for
  apply/decide/banking channel, the kit's `workflowFor` and the assistant's
  `creditWorkflowFor`) and `execute` use `ownedOnly: true`.
- Regression spec wiring the real WorkflowsService into the real desk.

fix(decision): o editor salva política de tamanho real — teto de corpo por operação

Todo o console passa por uma rota só (`/api/portal`), e ela tinha o teto do
cadastro: 16 KB. Uma versão de política carrega a DMN inteira com o
diagrama, e uma política PJ de 8 entradas e 6 nós (18 KB) voltou 413
"pedido grande demais" — o editor não salvava uma política real. Achado
populando staging com políticas de verdade em 09/10/2026. O painel aceita 10 MB.

Agora cada operação da tabela pode declarar o seu teto (`maxBodyBytes`), e
quem não declara fica nos 16 KB de sempre. A rota lê até o maior teto
declarado — calculado da tabela (`routeBodyCap`), sem número repetido — e a
ponte segura cada operação no dela: login e cadastro continuam pequenos.
No Decision, só `createPolicyVersion` declara 1 MiB. Os outros sites do kit
não mudam.

Testes: kit (op sem teto recusa acima do padrão; op com teto aceita até ele;
teto da rota derivado da tabela) e Decision (DMN de ~420 KB passa; login e
cadastro com 20 KB não). Sem a checagem por operação, o teste do login falha.

commits.title: fix(credit-desk): resolve the flow to execute by ownership, never by visibility
commits.body:
fix(credit-desk): resolve the flow to execute by ownership, never by visibility

The credit desk resolved the workflow to dispatch through
`findTriggerIndex` -> `getVisibleUserIds`, which is `null` (no filter) for
a PANEL_ADMIN. When a banking channel's tenant owner was a PANEL_ADMIN, the
newest active workflow listening to the event from ANY tenant won: measured
in staging on 2026-10-09, the channel dispatched another tenant's analysis
flow, which ran as that other user with its credentials and failed with
"Lead not found". A cross-tenant execution.

- WorkflowsService: `findTriggerIndex` and `findOne` take `ownedOnly`; it is
  the visibility rule with the admin escape removed (user + descendants,
  never null). Non-admin paths and the acting context are unchanged.
- CreditDeskService: `creditWorkflows` (feeds the server `workflowFor` for
  apply/decide/banking channel, the kit's `workflowFor` and the assistant's
  `creditWorkflowFor`) and `execute` use `ownedOnly: true`.
- Regression spec wiring the real WorkflowsService into the real desk.

commits.title: fix(tide): credential path takes mc from the mirror, verified
commits.body:
fix(tide): credential path takes mc from the mirror, verified

Creating a Tide credential ran
`which mc || curl -sSL https://dl.min.io/... -o /usr/local/bin/mc`.
dl.min.io answers 410 since 09/2026, so on an instance without mc that
line saved the error page as the binary, and `which mc` then found it
forever. Production has such an instance today (ct 301).

ensureMcCommand() tests `mc --version` instead, downloads from
TIDE_MC_URL with -f, checks sha256, runs --version, and only then moves
the file into place. With no mirror configured it fails naming the
variables, and no credential is issued.

Also adds scripts/ops/tide-minio-mirror.sh --conferir, a read-only check
of whether production can provision a new Tide instance.

fix(hotsites): point-panel survives the restart it causes; tenant password always fits the IAM policy

Two defects found on the first production run (10/10):

- hotsite-point-panel.sh died silently 10 s after the PATCH: under set -e the
  unguarded GOT="$(ssh ...)" failed while the replica was restarting, so the
  script exited with no message, no revert line and no smoke. The read is now
  guarded and the vmid is resolved again on every round.
- provision-tenant.mjs generated base64url passwords, which often carry no
  special character: the production IAM refused two of four. Passwords are now
  generated to fit the policy, and a stored password with no confirmed user id
  is replaced instead of blocking the rerun.

commits.body:
feat(code-portal): mais de uma pessoa por conta; a Mesa do Decision assina com a pessoa

Com um login por conta, um veredito acima do limite de alçada nunca podia
ser aprovado pela tela: o quatro-olhos pede uma segunda pessoa, e ela não
tinha como existir (decisão 4 do dono, 10/10).

Painel (camada do code portal, agnóstica de vertical):
- `CodeAccountMember` (migration aditiva): e-mail próprio, papel
  ADMIN/ANALYST, convite por link de escolher senha (7 dias, uso único).
- Login tenta o membro quando o e-mail não é de titular; mesma resposta
  genérica e mesmo custo de bcrypt. O token do membro leva `member`.
- `CodePortalGuard`: token de membro só passa em rota marcada com
  `@PortalMembers`, e o membro é conferido no banco a cada pedido. As
  outras verticais continuam fechadas para membros.
- Um e-mail entra em um lugar só; ninguém é apagado (REMOVED mantém o nome
  atrás do que a pessoa assinou).

Decision:
- O console inteiro abre para membros; plano, cartão, chaves, lista de
  pessoas e as regras das filas da Mesa ficam com titular e administradores.
- A Mesa assina com a pessoa: titular = código da conta (como antes),
  membro = `<código>/<id>`. O painel devolve os nomes (`people`) e a tela
  mostra nome, não código.
- Rotas e tela "Pessoas" (convidar, papel, novo link, remover) e o aceite
  do convite na tela de senha.

commits.title: fix(baas): simulated provider grant publishes before it writes; nothing is ever undone
commits.body:
fix(baas): simulated provider grant publishes before it writes; nothing is ever undone

Final review round for #600: the "undo" made revocation fail open and let a
grant be visible before it was confirmed.

One rule: the trail may have one record too many, never one too few, and
state never goes back.

- Grant: the id is generated first, the event is published with it, and the
  row is inserted only after the publication is confirmed. No confirmation
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_TRAIL_UNAVAILABLE with the table untouched, so
  isAllowed never sees an unconfirmed grant. Insert failing after the event
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_NOT_RECORDED. Idempotent PUT publishes nothing.
- Revocation: active grant ids are read, the event is published with them,
  and only then revokedAt/revokedBy are written (loop and 409 STILL_GRANTED
  kept). No confirmation -> 503 with no row touched; the organization stays
  granted and the caller is told so.
- undoGrant, undoRevoke and the deleteMany are gone: the grant table never
  loses a row and no row is reactivated. "My rows" are no longer recognised
  by revokedAt + revokedBy.
- Emergency path: DELETE ...?force=true (platform operator only) writes the
  revocation without a confirmed publication, logs at error level with
  operator, organization and grant ids, and answers trail: 'unconfirmed'.
- Tests cover the reviewer's sequences (slow-trail revoke vs a second DELETE,
  revoke/grant/revoke interleaving, grant with the trail down never allowed,
  concurrent PUT during the wait) and both force outcomes. README updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

commits.title: fix(baas): simulated provider grant — revoke every active grant, no act without a trail event, operator events never reach client webhooks
commits.body:
fix(baas): simulated provider grant — revoke every active grant, no act without a trail event, operator events never reach client webhooks

Review follow-up for #600.

- Revocation revokes ALL active grants of the organization and only answers
  204 when none is left (409 if one was granted again meanwhile). The code no

commits.body:
fix(webhooks): platform operator events never reach a client webhook

Measured on staging (2026-10-11): `baas.simulated-provider.grant.*` reached a
client webhook (`baas.*` subscription) with `actorId`, `grantedBy` and
`operatorOrganizationId` in the payload. An orphan webhooks-engine replica on
a 25/09 build shared the `webhook-delivery-consumers` group and had no filter.
Filtering only in the consumer cannot protect: an old consumer never has it.

Source filter (what actually fixes it)
- `EventPublisher` routes by event type: platform operator events (prefix list
  in `@shared/lib/operator-events`, today `baas.simulated-provider.`) go to
  their own stream, `platform-operator-events`. No webhook consumer of any
  build reads it. Callers do not choose the stream.
- `AuditConsumer` reads both streams with the same group (created at `0`, so
  events published before it is deployed are consumed when it starts). A group
  failure on the operator stream does not stop the bus trail.

Defense in depth at the single delivery point
- `DeliveryService.deliverEvent` refuses non-deliverable events before any row
  is created. `retryDelivery` (retry job, manual retry, facade) answers
  `409 EVENT_NOT_DELIVERABLE` and marks the row (`FAILED`, no next retry,
  reason in `errorMessage`) without deleting it.
- `delivery-logs` list/detail/retry responses omit the payload of operator
  event rows written before this fix (`payloadOmitted: true`).

Delivery notification loop (old defect, present in production)
- `webhooks.delivery.*` is no longer published for the delivery of a
  `webhooks.delivery.*`, and one whose source `eventType` is already
  `webhooks.delivery.*` is not delivered. A `*` subscription with a broken
  endpoint now gets one business delivery plus one failure notice, and stops.

Consumer identity
- Consumer name is `webhook-consumer@<build>@<host>@<pid>` (pid alone collided
  across guests). `/health` reports `checks.consumerGroup` (XINFO CONSUMERS:
  version, idle, `staleVersionActive`). Informational only: never degrades.

baas platform routes
- 404 message no longer presents the organization id as a grant id.
- 404 and validation 400 are audited as `…not_found` / `…invalid` (ACCESS),
  not `…refused` (ACCESS_DENIED). Hold, Pix and TED routes are unchanged.
- PUT validation 400 uses the repo error shape (`error`, `message`, `details`).

* feat(baas): simulated provider is granted per organization by the platform operator; the env variable becomes the fallback

The G5 gate (#599) decided who may create a provider config that accepts test
evidence in production (MOCKBANK, or settings.sandbox: true) from
BAAS_SIMULATED_PROVIDER_ORGANIZATION_IDS alone, so every new demo organization
required editing the service env and restarting the block.

- New table baas.baas_simulated_provider_grants (BaaSSimulatedProviderGrant):
  one ACTIVE grant per organization (partial unique index, SQL only), with
  reason, grantedBy/grantedAt and revokedBy/revokedAt. Additive, idempotent
  migration.
- The decision is now async: outside production it allows; in production it
  allows when the env variable lists the organization or `*` (fallback,
  unchanged) OR when the organization has an active grant. Creation and the
  PATCH that marks sandbox keep the same 403, message and refusal log; an
  unreadable grant fails closed (503).
- Platform operator routes in baas: GET/PUT/DELETE
  /baas/api/v1/admin/platform/organizations/:organizationId/simulated-provider.
  PUT is idempotent and requires `reason`; DELETE revokes and never touches
  existing provider configs.
- The platform operator check (IAM_ORGANIZATIONS_UPDATE + caller organization
  in BANKING_PLATFORM_ORGANIZATION_IDS) moves to
  @shared/middleware/platform-operator.middleware and is used by both banking
  and baas. Banking behaviour and tests are unchanged.
- Every grant, revocation and refusal is logged and published to the audit
  trail (baas.simulated-provider.*); the audit-trail mapper learns the new
  resource type.
- The stack env catalog gives the baas service BANKING_PLATFORM_ORGANIZATION_IDS
  (existing variable, no new env); READMEs updated.

* fix(baas): simulated provider grant publishes before it writes; nothing is ever undone

Final review round for #600: the "undo" made revocation fail open and let a
grant be visible before it was confirmed.

One rule: the trail may have one record too many, never one too few, and
state never goes back.

- Grant: the id is generated first, the event is published with it, and the
  row is inserted only after the publication is confirmed. No confirmation
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_TRAIL_UNAVAILABLE with the table untouched, so
  isAllowed never sees an unconfirmed grant. Insert failing after the event
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_NOT_RECORDED. Idempotent PUT publishes nothing.
- Revocation: active grant ids are read, the event is published with them,
  and only then revokedAt/revokedBy are written (loop and 409 STILL_GRANTED
  kept). No confirmation -> 503 with no row touched; the organization stays
  granted and the caller is told so.
- undoGrant, undoRevoke and the deleteMany are gone: the grant table never
  loses a row and no row is reactivated. "My rows" are no longer recognised
  by revokedAt + revokedBy.
- Emergency path: DELETE ...?force=true (platform operator only) writes the
  revocation without a confirmed publication, logs at error level with
  operator, organization and grant ids, and answers trail: 'unconfirmed'.
- Tests cover the reviewer's sequences (slow-trail revoke vs a second DELETE,
  revoke/grant/revoke interleaving, grant with the trail down never allowed,
  concurrent PUT during the wait) and both force outcomes. README updated.

commits.title: fix(packages): the banking channel extends the table the tenant runs instead of shipping one
commits.body:
fix(packages): the banking channel extends the table the tenant runs instead of shipping one

Review of #1863. The package declared a factory "1.3.0" derived from the 1.2.1
in the code, so installing it replaced a table the desk had edited with the
default one, in silence.

- `creditBlocks.decisao` takes a declared table or `{ projectKey, key, extends }`:
  a generic, data-only DecisionTableExtension the seed applies, at install
  time, over the content of the version in effect in the tenant's engine. The
  package declares the extension; nothing is derived (or thrown) at module load;
- idempotent; published one minor above the highest readable version (1.3.0 on
  a factory tenant, 2.1.0 over a desk 2.0.0); the table goes BEFORE the product,
  and a table that cannot be extended fails the seed with the reason, so no
  channel product is left offering what the table refuses (`blocos.ok: false`);
- the engine runs the version PUBLISHED LAST (read in the block's code, cited in
  decision-version.ts and in the plan). The generic seed therefore does not
  publish a declared version under a newer published one, stops on a published
  version whose name is not a number, and answers the snapshot of the version
  the engine runs — read from the engine, or null with the reason — never one
  of a table it does not execute. This changes every package with creditBlocks;
- the install result reports preserved tables (`blocos.preservedTables`), and a
  declared version that never reached the tenant becomes a pendência;
- new identifiers in English; the CONDITIONAL of the package's workflow is now
  executed by the real handler in the spec;
- docs: plan (design change, engine behaviour, limits until slice 8), channel
  README, demo guide.

What only the house knows is informed once, in the installation, and the
tenant gets a default BaaS provider and the fund's account without a manual
step.

  validated in the preflight (CNPJ check digits, city/state, e-mail) — an
  invalid value is a 400 with one message per field, before any effect.
  Absent means keep. A value present and different from what the policy
  holds is refused (409 PACKAGE_INPUT_CONFLICT) unless confirmed per field
  in `confirmInputChanges`; `force` does not stand for it. Written the way
  the policy screen publishes (previous version kept, expectedVersion).
- `baasProvision` (generic), with the tenant key: keeps the default
  provider; creates the simulated one only when asked and the organization
  has none (the block's 403 without the operator's grant is `needs-input`);
  reads the account the policy points at; opens the fund's account only in
  the simulated provider, in the creditor's name, with the block's
  idempotency key, and writes the returned id into the policy.
- The `house-policy` prerequisite now requires an account that EXISTS and
  is active in the BaaS, read by the installation — a made-up id used to
  turn contracting on (measured in staging on 11/10).
- FEATURE_FLAG_WAITING_PREREQUISITE says exactly what is missing; the
  result lists met/unmet prerequisites per flag; no doubled full stop in
  the 409 message.

commits.title: feat(packages): feature flags of a package — registered with the tenant key, turned on with the installer's token (slice 3)
commits.body:
feat(packages): feature flags of a package — registered with the tenant key, turned on with the installer's token (slice 3)

A package now declares the feature flags it needs (`featureFlags`: key, state, name, description and
the house prerequisites it waits for), one declaration per key over the closure, and the installer
registers and turns them on in the tenant's organization as its LAST step.

Read in the blocks repo: `banking` evaluates `products.receivables` and `credit.contract` as
capabilities and treats "not registered" as off; a flag is born off; turning it on is publishing, which
the tenant's key is refused on purpose (403) and the account's main user carries in the token. So:
- register, list and read back: the tenant's machine key (a sub-user and a script register too);
- turn on: the token of who installs, and only that.

Rules:
- order: after the credit blocks and the policy pointers; when an earlier step failed or the pointers
  are not in the policy yet the step is `skipped` (new status) and no flag is touched;
- prerequisite: the showcase flag is turned on at installation; the CONTRACTING flag declares
  `requires: ['house-policy']` and is turned on only when the policy was read and has creditor, market
  place and the disbursement account — the reinstall after the house fills them turns it on;
- what the house decided is not undone: the block keeps no readable history, so a flag the installer
  created and has not turned on carries a sentence in its description, removed when it is turned on;
  off WITHOUT it is the house's and is never turned on;
- who cannot turn on (script without a token, sub-user, 403): `needs-input` with its own code and who
  can — never a failure; block down: `failed` in a strict package (409), `degraded` in a default one;
- what should be on is read back as a consumer reads it.

Also: the `feature-flags` block joins the tenant-key probe, and the dead routes are fixed — the
workflow actions and the assistant's tools called `/api/v1/feature-flags/...`, which matches no route
of the block (`/feature-flags/api/v1/flags/...`, `/feature-flags/api/v1/evaluate/:key`). One contract
(routes, module prefix recomposed when the base lacks it, answer parsing) is now shared by the
installer's client, the three actions and the three tools, with a ratchet against the old path.

`receivables-banking-channel` declares both flags. Nothing here ran against the real block.

  (older installation still on, or an imported workflow without a record)
  reinstalls, which switches the others off — the path that converges a
  tenant to one copy was lost when the root started being reused
  (WorkflowTemplatesService.otherActiveCopies); `force: true` in the package
  install request reinstalls everything, as before

Important
- absent in the request means keep: only a device, credential or agent that
  is present and is not what the installed workflow has reinstalls, read
  from the workflow itself (not from an earlier request); the screen's
  `{ acceptedDisclaimer: true }` no longer strips a device, and a script
  repeating the same device/credential no longer hands back switched-off

* feat(packages): the operator grants the bank app's host and the simulated provider; the installation checks them in the blocks (slice 7a/7b)

Two things a tenant cannot do for itself, by the blocks' design, were manual scripts: binding the bank
app's HOST to its organization (`banking`) and releasing the SIMULATED provider (`baas`). Measured in
staging on 11/10: without a host bound, the route the app reads its terms through answered the MAIN
organization's document.

7a — the operator grants
- `PlatformProvisioningGrant` (`platform_provisioning_grants`) + migration (additive, re-appliable).
- `PUT | GET | DELETE /admin/clients/:userId/provisioning-grants/:packageSlug` (`PANEL_ADMIN`): the act
  is performed with the operator's OWN IAM token; who is a platform operator is the block's decision.
  Host shape and allowed suffix (`BANKING_HOST_ALLOWED_SUFFIXES`, no default in code), typed
  confirmation, one outcome per block (APPLIED | ALREADY | CONFLICT | REFUSED | UNAVAILABLE |
  NOT_REQUESTED) written on the row; a refusal never leaves as a success. Revoking only records it.
- `GET /workflow-templates/packages/:slug/operator-grant` for the tenant: the host and what is missing,
  never the reason nor who granted.
- A minimal form on the client's admin page.

7b — the installation checks
- `operatorSteps` on the package type; steps `operator-grant` and `banking-host`: the host is bound to
  THIS organization, answers, and serves THIS tenant (each with its own code and who acts). The fact in
  the block decides, not the panel's row: an organization whose host already works passes without one.
- The probes go only to a valid host under an allowed suffix: https, no redirect, short timeout, no
  credential.
- `banking-onboarding` gains the host gaps: contracting only turns on with a working host. Nothing that
  is on is ever turned off.
- Without the grant the installation does NOT refuse: it installs and contracting waits.

Corrections from the smoke of slice 6 (staging, 11/10): a discarded code channel is always said; a
refused sender carries its real code in the prerequisite gap; a flag that is ON with an unmet
prerequisite gets a step of its own; the keys-mismatch message tells surplus from missing;
demonstration notices are never written into a content space the installer did not create.

Docs: plan (slice 7 rewritten, slice 6 smoke recorded, the owner's four questions) and handoff.

* fix(packages): an attempt that did not work never rewrites a grant that stands; only a tenant's host is granted (review of #1871)

Adversarial review of PR #1871: one blocker, two important, four minor.

1. (blocker) The grant row was written with reason, authorship and `revokedAt: null` BEFORE the block
   answered, and the attempt's outcome went over the previous one. A `PANEL_ADMIN` who is not an
   operator, repeating a grant that stood, became "who granted" with a 403; a refused attempt undid a
   recorded revocation; and a repetition with the block down turned APPLIED into UNAVAILABLE, which let a
   SECOND host be bound. Now the row keeps three different things apart:
   - what STANDS (host/outcomes): only what a block confirmed, never lowered by 401/403/5xx/timeout —
     only by a fact of the block (the host is another organization's; the simulated grant is gone);
   - who GRANTED (nullable): written only when the attempt actually granted something;
   - the LAST ATTEMPT (`lastAttempt*`, new columns; the migration was not applied anywhere yet).
   The second-host lock looks at what stands, and an attempt for another host that got NO ANSWER locks
   too, until the same host is repeated (idempotent) and the block says what happened to it.
2. The grant accepted the hosts of the other services and the canonical `banking` one. It now requires
   `banking-<something>` and refuses the host of any service the environment uses (computed from the
   env). The installer's probe keeps the suffix rule: it only reads.
3. The deploy brings the API up BEFORE the migrations: docs corrected to the real order and effect;
   the tenant's read no longer breaks without the table (it answers from the block, like the installer).
4. The tenant's read answers by the FACT in the block when it can read it and says "not checked" when it
   cannot; a revocation recorded on the panel changes nothing there.
5. The target organization is the oldest membership, explicitly ordered, and is shown on the screen
   before confirming.
6. Probes: a ceiling on the answer's size and one time budget for all the probes of an installation.
7. Tests: the reviewer's cases A, B, D, E, F and the host matrix; edge answering 404/502 and a wildcard
   route; the four new routes denied when acting as another tenant; a copyable env example.

* fix(packages): the unsettled-host lock is only armed and lifted by what the block says about the host; reserved platform labels (review of #1871, round 2)

1. The lock that keeps a second host out while a first attempt got no answer was armed by anybody
   (the attempt was written before the block answered) and lifted by a 401/403, which says nothing about
   the host. It now lives in its own column (`unsettledHost`): only no-answer (5xx, timeout) arms it,
   only an answer of the block ABOUT the host settles it (200, 409, 400/404), and a 401/403 puts it back
   as it was. Since, with the block down, anybody through the panel's door can leave a host pending,
   the operator has an explicit way out that does not bind it: `discardUnsettledHost`, typed, recorded
   (`discarded*`) and said for what it is — the discarded host may have stayed bound in the block. The
   409 no longer tells anybody to bind the pending host: it offers both ways out.
2. In the Launch the panel's `*_URL` variables are mesh addresses, so the computed list held no public
   host: `banking-product-portfolio`, `banking-console` and `banking-desktop` went through, and the
   screen SUGGESTED `banking-console…` for an organization whose slug is `console`. An explicit list of
   reserved labels is added to the computed one, the service name is derived from mesh hosts
   (`bb-<name>` → `<name>`), and the suggestion is never a reserved host (`-app` is appended).
Also: the screen no longer shows "granted by" when nothing stands any more; the plan records the
follow-ups (history table, the migration changed after its first version — check the table does not
exist before applying).

* feat(banking-channel): first request of a not-enabled assignor goes to the desk; approving enables (slice 8, channel part)

The account holder created by the bank app is born without the fund manager's
enablement, and the channel refused NOT_HABILITATED before the analysis, so the
decision table's "not enabled -> desk" rule was unreachable from the app.

- A product may declare `enablement: 'desk-on-first-request'` (read from the
  catalog, never by slug). With it, and only on the product declared for the
  bank channel, the request is analysed as "not enabled" and lands on the desk.
  Without it the refusal stays exactly as it was.
- The desk's decision route (`decideQueueItem`) enables the assignor when it
  APPROVES a proposal the engine held (ANALISE_MANUAL) with the recorded input
  `decisaoInput.habilitado === false`, in a product that declares the
  parameter. Refusing does not enable; a proposal the engine refused never
  does (A20 untouched); A17 still runs first. No installed workflow changes.
- While not enabled, one request under review at a time: a second one is
  refused with APPLICATION_UNDER_REVIEW and no analysis is enqueued (atomic
  slot in the ledger + the proposal waiting for the desk).
- Trail events and logs for the forwarded request, the refusal and the
  enablement.
- Package `receivables-banking-channel`: the product declares the parameter
  and version 1.1.0 for new tenants. An existing tenant keeps 1.0.0 (the seed
  only publishes when there is no version) and gets the key on the product's
  live parameters when the package is reinstalled; the channel reads it there.

  writes a document that does not exist; anything different is kept and reported. A release is only

commits.body:
fix(packages): review of #1864 — one live copy, absent means keep, pending key request, eventual steps

Blocking
- a template is kept only when it is THE active copy: another active copy
  (older installation still on, or an imported workflow without a record)
  reinstalls, which switches the others off — the path that converges a
  tenant to one copy was lost when the root started being reused
  (WorkflowTemplatesService.otherActiveCopies); `force: true` in the package
  install request reinstalls everything, as before

Important
- absent in the request means keep: only a device, credential or agent that
  is present and is not what the installed workflow has reinstalls, read
  from the workflow itself (not from an earlier request); the screen's
  `{ acceptedDisclaimer: true }` no longer strips a device, and a script
  repeating the same device/credential no longer hands back switched-off
  flows the house had turned on
- pendências and steps of a kept template answer by the real workflow
  (device bound, on or off)
- four eyes: the key request is remembered (inactive, keyless credential
  `<service>:pending-request`) and the next install redeems it instead of
  opening another; still pending, somebody else's and gone-for-good each
  have their own code and message, for both keys
- strict does not answer 409 for an eventual step: pointers waiting for the
  policy are `pending` (new status); a post-install step that already
  completed on a kept workflow is not dispatched again
- the key probe reads the variable each block's real client reads
  (decision-engine has one for the credit client and one for the decision
  console); a block without an address is `degraded` in a default package

Minor
- syncCatalog keeps `active` as the database has it and the installer
  refuses a package with a disabled template before any effect
- the key service re-reads before saving (no second credential in a race)
- 403 message no longer asserts the cause; DATA_STORE_UNAVAILABLE is 503
- new identifiers in English; agentsReused doc; reinstall-lastros header

commits.title: fix(packages): only what is provably the same flow is switched off as a copy — review of #1865
commits.body:
fix(packages): only what is provably the same flow is switched off as a copy — review of #1865

The first version of the new copy rule (same triggers + same action names) switched off things that
were not copies. Two blockers found by the adversarial review, both fixed here:

1. Reinstalling a template switched off the INSTALLED workflow of another template of the catalogue
   with the same triggers and action names (vehicle × property release deadline, the three
   appointment reminders): only the last one installed kept working.
2. A duplicate the house reconfigured (a second WhatsApp number, another text) was switched off by an
   ordinary reinstall, and the new copy could be born without the number.

The rule now:
(a) a workflow with an installation record of ANY template is never a stray copy;
(b) switched off: (i) the installer's name ("X" / "X (importado)") on the same triggers, exactly as
    before this PR — it is what cleans a tenant restored with an earlier version of the template —
    and (ii) an EXACT duplicate of the installed copy (same triggers and actions with the same
    configuration, device, credentials, agents; a webhook with its own slug is not one);
(c) same structure with another configuration is never switched off: reported on named `event`
    triggers as `OTHER_ACTIVE_COPY_ON_SAME_EVENT` — `needs-input` in a default package, `failed`
    (409) in a strict one;
(d) a structure shared by more than one template of the catalogue is not attributed to any;
(e) a reinstall nobody asked for (another active copy, no `force`) inherits device, credentials,
    agents and the on/off state of the installed workflow;
(f) catalogue ratchet: the three groups of look-alike templates are a declared list.

Also: the same-event warning only for triggers of type `event` that name their event; the request's
references are checked on the single-template route too, only for what will be used, with a message
for platform staff that says how to install on behalf of a customer; copy candidates are read once
per installation; the credit policy field of a house pendência goes in the step (`field`, one code
per pendência) instead of vanishing.

Copy rules are specified on the real catalogue and the real service over an in-memory tenant
(`workflow-templates.copies.spec.ts`). Plan updated: the rule, the pre-existing sub-user defect, the
feature-flag routes the panel calls and the block does not serve, and the slice 3 decision (turn
flags on with the installer's JWT).

Until now the tenant's machine key was minted only when the closure had
`credito-base`. A tenant installing just `decision` got no key: its native
handlers fell back to the PLATFORM key (policies would live in Catalisa's
organization) and the review desk was out of reach of any tenant key.

- `tenantBlocks` on the package template; the installer mints the key when
  any package of the closure declares it
- `mesa` joins the tenant key scope
- the six decision-platform handlers speak as the tenant (same chain as the
  credit blocks: chosen credential, tenant key, platform key out loud)
- `decision` declares decision-engine, decision-platform and mesa

* fix(packages): the banking channel extends the table the tenant runs instead of shipping one

Review of #1863. The package declared a factory "1.3.0" derived from the 1.2.1
in the code, so installing it replaced a table the desk had edited with the
default one, in silence.

- `creditBlocks.decisao` takes a declared table or `{ projectKey, key, extends }`:
  a generic, data-only DecisionTableExtension the seed applies, at install
  time, over the content of the version in effect in the tenant's engine. The
  package declares the extension; nothing is derived (or thrown) at module load;
- idempotent; published one minor above the highest readable version (1.3.0 on
  a factory tenant, 2.1.0 over a desk 2.0.0); the table goes BEFORE the product,
  and a table that cannot be extended fails the seed with the reason, so no
  channel product is left offering what the table refuses (`blocos.ok: false`);
- the engine runs the version PUBLISHED LAST (read in the block's code, cited in
  decision-version.ts and in the plan). The generic seed therefore does not
  publish a declared version under a newer published one, stops on a published
  version whose name is not a number, and answers the snapshot of the version
  the engine runs — read from the engine, or null with the reason — never one
  of a table it does not execute. This changes every package with creditBlocks;
- the install result reports preserved tables (`blocos.preservedTables`), and a
  declared version that never reached the tenant becomes a pendência;
- new identifiers in English; the CONDITIONAL of the package's workflow is now
  executed by the real handler in the spec;

  README, demo guide.

commits.title: feat(packages): o pacote registra e liga as flags do app; corrige rotas mortas de feature flag (fatia 3) (#1866)
commits.body:
feat(packages): o pacote registra e liga as flags do app; corrige rotas mortas de feature flag (fatia 3) (#1866)

* feat(packages): feature flags of a package — registered with the tenant key, turned on with the installer's token (slice 3)

A package now declares the feature flags it needs (`featureFlags`: key, state, name, description and
the house prerequisites it waits for), one declaration per key over the closure, and the installer
registers and turns them on in the tenant's organization as its LAST step.

Read in the blocks repo: `banking` evaluates `products.receivables` and `credit.contract` as
capabilities and treats "not registered" as off; a flag is born off; turning it on is publishing, which
the tenant's key is refused on purpose (403) and the account's main user carries in the token. So:
- register, list and read back: the tenant's machine key (a sub-user and a script register too);
- turn on: the token of who installs, and only that.

Rules:
- order: after the credit blocks and the policy pointers; when an earlier step failed or the pointers
  are not in the policy yet the step is `skipped` (new status) and no flag is touched;
- prerequisite: the showcase flag is turned on at installation; the CONTRACTING flag declares
  `requires: ['house-policy']` and is turned on only when the policy was read and has creditor, market
  place and the disbursement account — the reinstall after the house fills them turns it on;
- what the house decided is not undone: the block keeps no readable history, so a flag the installer
  created and has not turned on carries a sentence in its description, removed when it is turned on;
  off WITHOUT it is the house's and is never turned on;
- who cannot turn on (script without a token, sub-user, 403): `needs-input` with its own code and who
  can — never a failure; block down: `failed` in a strict package (409), `degraded` in a default one;
- what should be on is read back as a consumer reads it.

Also: the `feature-flags` block joins the tenant-key probe, and the dead routes are fixed — the
workflow actions and the assistant's tools called `/api/v1/feature-flags/...`, which matches no route
of the block (`/feature-flags/api/v1/flags/...`, `/feature-flags/api/v1/evaluate/:key`). One contract
(routes, module prefix recomposed when the base lacks it, answer parsing) is now shared by the
installer's client, the three actions and the three tools, with a ratchet against the old path.

`receivables-banking-channel` declares both flags. Nothing here ran against the real block.

* fix(packages): a flag somebody touched is never turned back on; the panel's API token stays in the panel — review of #1866

Blocker: the marker in the flag's description did not hold the real case. The bank's console turns a
flag on and off without touching the description, so "registered -> turned on by hand -> turned off by
hand (an incident) -> reinstall" turned it back on, contracting included. The marker is gone. Every
write of anybody (state or description) moves the flag's `updatedAt`; the installer keeps, on the
panel's side (the installation record of the declaring template, per account), the id and the
`updatedAt` of the flag it created, read right after creating. "The installer's and untouched" = off,
same id, same `updatedAt`. Anything else that is off is somebody's decision and is never turned on.

Also:
- only a PERSON's IAM token is passed on to a block (`shared/auth/iam-bearer-token.ts`): an installation
  by script authenticates with an API token of the panel, which was being sent to the flags block and,
  before this slice, to the key service. Applied to package install, key minting/redeem and merchant
  payments enable;
- 404 when turning on (who installs is logged into another organization) is `needs-input` with its own
  code, not "the service did not answer"; a flag the house deleted is not recreated and is said so; a
  key the block breaks on when registering (its unique index counts deleted flags) is said too;
- the three workflow actions and the three assistant tools now speak in the name of the ACCOUNT (the
  tenant key), never the platform token; without it they fail out loud. Turning on with the account's
  key is refused by the block by design: they say a person is needed and where. Evaluation answers by
  `enabled` (a flag that is off with a default of true reads `value: true, reason: DISABLED`), the
  context from the form is parsed as JSON with flat keys moved to `attributes`, and a 4xx fails the
  action instead of reading as "off";
- `decision-table` is a prerequisite too: contracting waits while the package's table is not the one in
  effect; the module prefix is decided by the PATH of the base address; a step that stops says what it
  had already turned on.

Plan rewritten for the slice: the rule, the block defect on deleted flags, the behaviour change of the
actions and tools, where the token helper was and was not applied, and the mutation record.

commits.title: feat(packages): termos e perfil do banco pela instalação; a contratação exige que o app consiga abrir conta (fatia 6) (#1869)
commits.body:
feat(packages): termos e perfil do banco pela instalação; a contratação exige que o app consiga abrir conta (fatia 6) (#1869)

* feat(packages): the installer publishes the app's terms and configures the app's profile; contracting waits for the app being able to open an account (slice 6)

`cmsContent` and `bankingProfile`, generic fields of a package, with the session of the person installing
(the tenant key does not reach `cms` or `banking`, on purpose):

- `cms-content`: the space and the legal documents the app asks the customer to accept. The channel package
  brings ONLY the three demonstration notices the staging script publishes, word for word, marked in the
  version (`demo-2026.10`), and they are written and published only while the organization's bank is the
  simulated one, as the BaaS step resolved it. With a real bank nothing is published in the house's name:
  the step waits for the house's terms, or only checks the ones it already published. The installer only
  writes a document that does not exist; anything different is kept and reported. A release is only
  published over a space nobody else published (publishing a release publishes the whole draft).
- `banking-profile`: the app is pointed at the content space when it points at none, and the channel of the
  verification code comes from the house as inputs (`otpSenderId`, `otpTemplateName`, `otpLanguageCode`).
  The `banking` block has no platform default for it; without a channel the step is `needs-input`. A channel
  the profile already has is only replaced with a confirmation per field.
- `banking-onboarding`, a new generic prerequisite: required terms published in the space the profile points
  at, and a channel for the code. `credit.contract` waits for it; the showcase does not.
- `tenant-block:cms` / `tenant-block:banking`: the preflight checks the address only (public health route).
- `banking` and `cms` in `bb-endpoints.ts` (`BANKING_BB_BASE_URL`, `CMS_BB_BASE_URL`), added to the versioned
  env files.

Four corrections from the staging smoke of slice 5:

- an account informed in the request is only written with a confirmation by field (the BaaS does not say who
  the holder is), and any sign of a customer's account refuses it;
- the "account kept after the creditor changed" warning persists across installations: the panel keeps the
  creditor the account was opened or confirmed for;
- `packageInputs.applied` lists `fundAccountId` when the informed account is written;
- `BAAS_FUND_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` says the two ways out.

Nothing changes for packages that declare neither field (catalogue ratchet).

Not proven against the real blocks: local tests over a `cms` and a `banking` in memory that follow the rules
read in building-blocks-v2 a88aeca7. Two decisions are left for the owner and recorded in the plan: the model
texts of the terms, and a shared sender for the verification code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(packages): review of slice 6 — demo notices never count as the house's terms, the app's keys, the code channel checked where it sends, and the installer's organization

Adversarial review of PR #1869 (one blocking, five important):

1. A demonstration notice is never read as "the house's terms". With a bank that is not the simulated one,
   a required document the installer published (in the record, or with the package's key and version, or the
   package's very text) makes the step `needs-input` (`CMS_DEMO_TERMS_ON_REAL_BANK`) and does not count for
   `banking-onboarding`. Nothing is unpublished.
2. A release is only published over a space the installer created (this call, or an earlier one by the
   record) or over the release it published. A space that was already there, published or not, gets the
   documents as a draft (`CMS_RELEASE_NEEDS_THE_HOUSE`).
3. "Terms published" means the keys the app asks for: every document of the package required in the current
   release and no other required one (`CMS_APP_TERMS_KEYS_MISMATCH` says what is missing and what is extra).
4. The verification code's channel is checked in `wpp-business` with the installer's token before it is
   written, and the one already in the profile too: the number is the organization's and active; the
   template exists in that number's account, is an authentication one, approved, in that language. One code
   per reason; not checked is not met. New client `shared/wpp-business/wpp-business-channel.client.ts`.
5. The organization of the token is compared with the organization of the tenant's key before any call with
   the token: the provider configuration the key resolved is read with the token in the BaaS (404 = another
   organization). Different: `BANKING_ONBOARDING_INSTALLER_NOT_OF_THIS_ACCOUNT`, no block called, nothing
   written. Without a resolved bank the app steps wait; a closure that declares `cmsContent` or
   `bankingProfile` without `baasProvision` is a catalogue defect.
6. Plan and handoff: the two new variables are a mandatory step before the deploy, staging first, and
   `BB_WPP_BUSINESS_BASE_URL` has to be present.

Minor: the profile is read again right before the write (the block has no conditional write); a fund-account
record without creditor says "not known" instead of nothing; the two app steps say the same thing about
where the house acts; limits recorded in the plan.

Also, from the slice-5 smoke: a reinstall with nothing to change no longer writes the policy document (the
pointers were rewritten every time because of the "seeded at" stamps: 4 -> 16 versions in six reinstalls).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(packages): review round 2 of slice 6 — publish only a space created by this call, altered demo notices, an approved template row among drafts, and the informed channel that was not kept

- A release is published ONLY over a space created by this very call whose legal-document draft was empty
  before the package's documents. A space the installer created earlier and could not publish, or one that
  already has the installer's own release, may hold somebody's draft by now, and the installer cannot see a
  space's whole draft: the documents stay as a draft (`CMS_RELEASE_NEEDS_THE_HOUSE`). An unavailable block is
  retried once in the same call.
- A demonstration notice somebody altered (another version, a line more) is still recognised by the
  sentence it carries (`demonstrationMark`, generic) and never counts over a bank that is not the simulated one.
- Code channel: "some row of this template is an approved authentication one in that language" (a newer
  draft does not hide the approved row); a WhatsApp block that does not answer only FAILS a strict package
  when the channel was informed in this installation — with nothing to change the step is `degraded`.
- No bank resolved and the channel informed in the request: the steps are still skipped, and a pendência now
  says the channel was NOT kept and has to be informed again.
- Plan: the principle (a prerequisite checks that the thing exists and works in the owning block, never that
  a field is filled) and the limits of this round.

commits.body:
feat(packages): a casa informa credor e praça na instalação; o instalador provisiona a conta do fundo e só abre a contratação com conta real (fatia 5) (#1868)

* feat(packages): inputs and baasProvision in the package installer (slice 5)

What only the house knows is informed once, in the installation, and the
tenant gets a default BaaS provider and the fund's account without a manual
step.

- `inputs` (generic): declared per package, returned by `packages/list`,
  validated in the preflight (CNPJ check digits, city/state, e-mail) — an
  invalid value is a 400 with one message per field, before any effect.
  Absent means keep. A value present and different from what the policy
  holds is refused (409 PACKAGE_INPUT_CONFLICT) unless confirmed per field
  in `confirmInputChanges`; `force` does not stand for it. Written the way
  the policy screen publishes (previous version kept, expectedVersion).
- `baasProvision` (generic), with the tenant key: keeps the default
  provider; creates the simulated one only when asked and the organization
  has none (the block's 403 without the operator's grant is `needs-input`);
  reads the account the policy points at; opens the fund's account only in
  the simulated provider, in the creditor's name, with the block's
  idempotency key, and writes the returned id into the policy.
- The `house-policy` prerequisite now requires an account that EXISTS and
  is active in the BaaS, read by the installation — a made-up id used to
  turn contracting on (measured in staging on 11/10).
- FEATURE_FLAG_WAITING_PREREQUISITE says exactly what is missing; the
  result lists met/unmet prerequisites per flag; no doubled full stop in
  the 409 message.
- `receivables-banking-channel` declares both. No other package changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(packages): one creditor resolution, the readers'; review of #1868

Blocking: writing `credor.email` (or only `credor.nome`) over a policy that
only has `fundo` took the creditor off the note, the instrument and the
master agreement (they resolve by object), and the installer, checking field
by field, turned contracting on.

- The creditor's name and document are compared and written in the entity
  that ANSWERS today (the `credor` object, otherwise the fund); the contact
  e-mail lives outside `credor` (`contatoCredorEmail`); a creditor is born
  whole or not at all. The policy's pendências, the account holder and the
  `house-policy` prerequisite use `resolveCreditor`.
- The assignment term resolves its assignee (naoperacao-saude, otherwise the
  creditor) and is refused with a reason when there is none — never
  generated with a placeholder. Terms of houses with a fund are unchanged.
- Holder CNPJ normalized; an invalid recorded one is `needs-input`.
- The account is opened in the configuration checked as simulated
  (`configId`); idempotency key per holder CNPJ; `created` only when born in
  this call; a warning when the creditor changes and the account stays.

fix(packages): the unsettled-host lock is only armed and lifted by what the block says about the host; reserved platform labels (review of #1871, round 2)

1. The lock that keeps a second host out while a first attempt got no answer was armed by anybody
   (the attempt was written before the block answered) and lifted by a 401/403, which says nothing about
   the host. It now lives in its own column (`unsettledHost`): only no-answer (5xx, timeout) arms it,
   only an answer of the block ABOUT the host settles it (200, 409, 400/404), and a 401/403 puts it back
   as it was. Since, with the block down, anybody through the panel's door can leave a host pending,
   the operator has an explicit way out that does not bind it: `discardUnsettledHost`, typed, recorded
   (`discarded*`) and said for what it is — the discarded host may have stayed bound in the block. The
   409 no longer tells anybody to bind the pending host: it offers both ways out.
2. In the Launch the panel's `*_URL` variables are mesh addresses, so the computed list held no public
   host: `banking-product-portfolio`, `banking-console` and `banking-desktop` went through, and the
   screen SUGGESTED `banking-console…` for an organization whose slug is `console`. An explicit list of
   reserved labels is added to the computed one, the service name is derived from mesh hosts

* fix(bureaus): mask the subject in the MOCK raw payload; grant reason goes to the operator event (bureaus and baas)

Two findings, same area.

1. The simulated bureau provider (`MOCK`) returned `raw.subject` with the whole
   document. `raw` is persisted as-is in `bureau_queries.raw` and
   `bureau_cache.raw` and is returned by default (`includeRaw: true`), so the
   block that "never stores the document in clear" stored it, and so did
   whoever kept the envelope. `raw.subject` is now the mask (same as
   `subject.masked`), on FOUND and NOT_FOUND. `profile`/`forced`/`kind`/
   `generatedFrom` are unchanged. The `includeRaw` default does NOT change:
   the panel reads the raw BigDataCorp envelope.

2. The reason of a simulated-provider grant never reached the audit trail:
   `<block>.simulated-provider.grant.created` carried `grantId`, `grantedBy`,
   `grantedAt` but not `reason`, and after a revoke the `GET` no longer shows
   it. The event now carries `reason` in `bureaus` and in `baas`. This reverses
   the earlier "reason stays in the row only" choice, with the guards that
   make it safe: the event is a platform-operator event (own stream, only the
   audit trail reads it, never a customer webhook), the text is capped at 500
   and the SAME trimmed/capped text goes to the event and the row, it is not
   logged, and a reason carrying something CPF/CNPJ-shaped is refused with
   400 `SIMULATED_PROVIDER_REASON_HAS_DOCUMENT` (route and service) before
   anything is published or written.

`@shared/utils/free-text-document` holds the document-shape check.

Not changed: rows already written keep the old `raw.subject` until retention
or cache expiry; the canonical `person.basic`/`company.basic` still carry
`taxId` (type contract); the revoke event does not repeat the reason.

  number is still refused — verifying check digits would let mistyped

commits.title: fix(bureaus): baseUrl de fornecedor real só em host oficial em produção (lista de hosts, falha fechada) (#607)
commits.body:
fix(bureaus): baseUrl de fornecedor real só em host oficial em produção (lista de hosts, falha fechada) (#607)

* fix(bureaus): provider baseUrl must be an official host in production (allowlist, fail closed)

`settings.baseUrl` of a BIGDATACORP config accepted any public URL from the
tenant. An organization in production could point the "real provider" at its
own server and get invented credit data stamped as BIGDATACORP, with no MOCK
config and no operator grant (bypassing the simulated-provider gate of #602),
and it made the service an outbound request vector to a tenant-chosen host.

With NODE_ENV=production the effective provider URL must now be https, carry
no userinfo, query or fragment, and have a host (and non-default port) that
matches EXACTLY one of the provider's hosts: the official ones, fixed in
`providers/base-url-policy.ts` (BIGDATACORP -> plataforma.bigdatacorp.com.br),
plus the ones added through the new optional `BUREAUS_PROVIDER_EXTRA_HOSTS`
(`PROVIDER=host[:port]` pairs; no wildcard; malformed entries are ignored and
never release anything). Outside production the rule does not apply, same cut
as the simulated-provider gate. MOCK makes no network call and is unaffected.

Where it applies:
- create: 400 before the connection test, so the credential is never sent to
  the informed host; nothing is stored
- update: 400 when the settings sent are off the list (even on an inactive
  config), or when the config stays active with stored settings off the list;
  deactivating and fixing the URL pass
- test-connection: 403, no network call
- query (and batch): 403, fail closed and BEFORE the cache — an existing config
  off the list answers nothing, not even what it cached; the attempt is
  recorded in bureau_queries as ERROR with errorCode
  PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NOT_ALLOWED and `bureaus.query.failed` is published
- the driver repeats the check before each request (last barrier)

Every refusal has the stable `details.code` PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NOT_ALLOWED and
a `details.reason`, a `warn` log and the new `bureaus.provider_config.refused`
event carrying organization, config, action, reason and only the host (never
path, query or credential). The shared SSRF guard (`secureFetch`) stays in
place behind it; the repo has no shared host allowlist to reuse.

Deploy stacks gain the variable (catalog). Staging runs with
NODE_ENV=production: a BIGDATACORP config there pointing at an external mock
stops answering unless its host is written to `BUREAUS_PROVIDER_EXTRA_HOSTS`
on bb-bureaus before this version goes up. The README has the SQL to find
such configs.

* fix(bureaus): provider call refuses redirects; refusal notice deduplicated per config; document what the allowlist does not undo

Review follow-ups on the provider baseUrl allowlist.

- driver: the BigDataCorp call passes `redirect: 'error'`. The allowlist checks
  the host of the request; `fetch` would follow a 30x to a destination nobody
  checked, and on 307/308 the credential headers go along. Proven against two
  local servers: without the option the credential reaches the redirect target,
  with it the query fails and nothing reaches the target.
- refusal notice: a batch over one irregular config still refuses every query
  and records each one as ERROR, but the `warn` log and the
  `bureaus.provider_config.refused` event are emitted once per config, action,
  reason and host every 5 minutes; the next notice carries
  `repeatsSinceLastNotice`. In-process on purpose (up to one notice per replica
  per window, no Redis dependency). Create/update refusals are not deduplicated.
- README: FOUND queries already recorded by an irregular config stay readable
  (SQL to list them by `config_id`), the rule depends on `NODE_ENV=production`
  being set on the service, and the two behaviours above.

`secureFetch` itself is unchanged: making redirects an error for every caller
would break customer webhook endpoints that redirect. Callers that send
credentials or secrets and still follow redirects are listed in the PR.

commits.title: fix(audit-trail): bound the wait for the chain lock; a locked organization no longer stops the trail of all
commits.body:
fix(audit-trail): bound the wait for the chain lock; a locked organization no longer stops the trail of all

A lock held on ONE organization's chain (a transaction left open, a long
prune) made AuditChainRepository.append wait for as long as the lock lasted:
Prisma's 20 s transaction timeout does not cancel a statement that is waiting.
The consumer writes one message at a time, so the trail of every organization
on that stream stopped, with no error and no dead letter.

- The first statement of the append and of the prune transaction is
  set_config('lock_timeout', <ms>, true): transaction-local, it covers the
  advisory lock and the FOR UPDATE on the head row. Configurable through
  AUDIT_CHAIN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS (100..9000, default 5000).
- Running out is a classified failure (CHAIN_LOCK_TIMEOUT / 55P03), not
  retried inside the write: it counts as an attempt, the 4th delivery goes to
  the dead letter, the other organizations go on, the replay recovers it.
- Replay: the lookup of the already-written row is bounded by
  created_at >= deadLetteredAt - 10 min, an index range scan on
  (organization_id, created_at).
- scripts/audit-trail/append-contention.ts: the measurement behind the default.
- README: the `_audit` metadata prefix is reserved in POST /events;
  idle_in_transaction_session_timeout recommended; who waits for the lock.

commits.body:
fix(analytics): receivables funnel and catalog read the credit events banking really publishes

The credit catalog was written as a contract before `banking` published
anything, and three fields plus one event name drifted from the code. Nothing
failed (a missing attribute is not an error), the values were just never
recorded:

- `operation.credited`: the amount band read `amountCents`; banking publishes
  `netCents` (entry version 2)
- `receivable.added`: the amount band read `amountCents`; banking publishes
  `faceCents` (entry version 2)
- `proposal.accepted`: channel enum was `mobile|desktop`; banking publishes
  `app|desktop`, so every app acceptance became `OTHER` (entry version 2)
- funnel outcome `acceptance_refused` read `banking.credit.acceptance.refused`,
  which no block publishes; the refusal is the error response of
  `acceptProposal`, `banking.credit.proposal.accept.refused` (funnel version 3).
  The dead catalog entry is removed (the sync retires it).

The catalog side moves, not banking: the published bodies also feed the audit
trail and webhooks, and `faceCents`/`netCents` are the vocabulary of the block.

New ratchet `credit-published-bodies.test.ts` runs the real credit service
through note, request, acceptance and credit, and feeds every published body to
the bus mapper and the catalog normalizer; it also pins that every event the
funnel reads is a name banking can publish.

Not done here, on purpose: the credit events stay PENDING. Only
`application.requested` carries `applicationId` (the `journeyRef`). banking does
not know which application a proposal or an operation came from (the credit
service does not return it and `credit_acceptances` has no such column), so
acceptance and credit cannot join the cohort yet. README section 15 states what
is missing; the new test pins `journeyRef` null on both so the day banking
starts publishing it the test asks for the README and the status to be revisited.

commits.title: feat(banking): idempotent credit application by Idempotency-Key
commits.body:
feat(banking): idempotent credit application by Idempotency-Key

`POST /v1/credit/applications` generated `applicationId = randomUUID()` on
every call. When the response was lost and the customer tapped again, the
credit service saw a NEW request: a holder not yet enabled got
`APPLICATION_UNDER_REVIEW` without the id to follow, and an enabled holder
had the paid analysis run twice.

The route now accepts an idempotency key, in the `Idempotency-Key` header or
in the body (same mold as Pix and desktop operations; both present must be
equal):

- the key is bound to an `applicationId` BEFORE the credit service is called,
  in the new `banking.credit_application_requests` (the row id IS the
  `applicationId`); unique per (organization, account, key), so two taps or
  two replicas share one row and the loser reads the winner
- same key -> same `applicationId` sent to the channel, which deduplicates by
  it and returns the usual answer
- same key with other notes -> 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH (the block's
  existing code and status), nothing reaches the service; the comparison is a
  SHA-256 of the sorted note ids, the notes themselves are not stored
- the gate comes before the key; a malformed key is 400 BAD_REQUEST
- `banking.credit.application.requested` carries `repeated`: false only for
  whoever flipped `answered_at` (conditional updateMany), true on replays;
  refusals carry the key to the refusal trail
- no key -> legacy behaviour, unchanged and documented as legacy

analytics: `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH` joins the credit refusal code list (the
hand-versioned entries to version 3.

Migration `20261012150000_banking_credit_application_requests` is additive
and idempotent (one table, two indexes). It does not reach an environment by
itself: run scripts/launch phases 0 -> 1 -> 2 before deploying `banking`.

Review follow-up on #606.

- MOCK `raw` no longer carries `generatedFrom`: it is a 32-bit seed derived
  from the document, and next to the masked subject it gives the document
  back by brute force in seconds. Profiles and data are unchanged.

  audit trail has no read-time redaction (masking happens on write, and the

  document grouping and recognises the alphanumeric CNPJ (uppercase, letters
  and digits mixed). Phone numbers in a phone shape pass; a bare 11-digit
  number is still refused — verifying check digits would let mistyped
  documents through.

commits.title: fix(calculations-engine): rate solvers always terminate and never return an unconverged rate (#609)
commits.body:
fix(calculations-engine): rate solvers always terminate and never return an unconverged rate (#609)

* fix(calculations-engine): rate solvers always terminate and never return an unconverged rate

`calculateReceivablesDiscount` with `dayCount: 'ACTUAL_365'` never returned for
short titles with face values in the millions and a deep discount (e.g.
`advanceRate` 0.531 over 3- and 7-day titles). formulajs' XIRR is Newton with
no iteration cap and ABSOLUTE 1e-10 tolerances on both the step and the
residual: with sums in the millions the residual cannot go below one ulp
(~1e-9) and, once the root is large, neither can the step, so it cycles between
neighbouring doubles forever. It is a public route: one request pinned the
process.

All rate searches now go through `calculators/rate-solver.ts`: bounded work
(iteration caps, plus a repeated-iterate exit), a bracketed bisection fallback,
and an explicit "no rate" (`null`) instead of the last iterate. A value is only
returned after its residual is checked against the equation.

- receivables discount, ACTUAL_365: Newton with XIRR's own arithmetic, guess
  and stopping rule (same double for every input that converged), then
  bisection on ln(1 + rate) in [0, 709]; no representable root -> `cet.*` null
  with the existing `EFFECTIVE_RATE_NOT_SOLVABLE` warning
- receivables discount, COMMERCIAL_30: the [0, 1] bisection is kept step for
  step; above 100% a month it used to answer exactly `1` with no warning and
  now keeps searching; a yearly rate that overflows is reported as not solvable
- loan-cet-rate / loan-interest-rate (and portability, which composes them):
  formulajs' RATE gives up after 100 steps by returning the last iterate; its
  answer is kept only when it solves the equation, otherwise the positive root
  is found by bisection, otherwise the existing domain error is raised
- service logs a warning (numbers only) when no effective rate exists
- README: the solver contract, what changed and what did not

Measured against main on generated inputs: 38,915 of 40,000 receivables
portfolios byte-identical; the other 1,085 are the 503 that hang on main and the
582 COMMERCIAL_30 answers that were pinned at 1. Same split under TZ=UTC and
TZ=Asia/Tokyo (8,000 each). Annuities: 17,845 of 30,000 identical; 17 were a
silently wrong rate on main (e.g. 16.1% where the rate is 12.1%); 12,138 raised
an error on main although a rate exists.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(calculations-engine): close review findings on the rate solvers (boundary, size limit, day count, pins)

Follow-up to the review of #609.

- R3: COMMERCIAL_30 at exactly 100% a month answered null where it had always
  answered 1 — `npv(1)` (Math.pow) and the log bisection (Math.exp) can disagree
  by one ulp about ln 2. The bracket now starts at zero.
- R1: the receivables-discount route accepts at most 2,000 titles
  (`RECEIVABLES_DISCOUNT_MAX_TITLES`); the calculation is synchronous and an
  unbounded list blocked the event loop for seconds. Newton cap 1000 -> 400
  (slowest converging input measured: 309 steps).
- R2/R5: the annuity answer is accepted only within 1e-12 of the amount (was
  1e-6, which let RATE's unconverged iterate through next to a zero rate), and
  the bisection now covers negative rates. Interest-free instalments whose sum
  is exact answer 0.
- R8: ACTUAL_365 solves the effective rate over `line.days` (UTC calendar
  days, the same the discount uses) instead of formulajs' DAYS in the server's
  local time. Same double on a UTC server; outside UTC the CET no longer
  depends on the timezone.
- R4: exact-double pins (26 portfolios, 24 annuities, taken from the pre-solver
  code under the test runtime) plus one rate above e^50.
- R9: the child-process regression is skipped with a clear name when `bun` is
  not in PATH; time bound loosened.
- R10: README no longer says the CET search does not signal non-convergence.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(calculations-engine): near-zero rate on large amounts answers again; pin the Newton cap from below

Review follow-up on #609.

`solveAnnuityRate(406531.52, 476, 193509003.56)` answered null (the calculators
raised an error) where main answered. `annuityFactor` jumped to its zero-rate
limit for |rate| < 1e-12; on amounts of hundreds of millions the root of an
almost interest-free plan (a cent of rounding) sits inside that band, so
neither RATE's iterate nor the bisection could meet the 1e-12 acceptance. Only
an exact zero takes the limit now: expm1/log1p are accurate all the way down.

feat(bureaus): gate the simulated provider per organization and answer credit signals in MOCK (#602)

* feat(bureaus): simulated provider gate (operator grant + fallback env) and credit signals in the MOCK provider

The MOCK bureau provider had no gate: any organization with BUREAUS_ADMIN could
create it in any environment. It also did not answer the signals a credit
analysis needs, so every analysis in staging came out with a neutral score.

Gate (same rule as the baas G5 gate):
- Outside production it allows. In production it allows when
  BUREAUS_SIMULATED_PROVIDER_ORGANIZATION_IDS lists the organization (or `*`)
  OR when the organization has an active grant from the platform operator.
- Applies to creating a MOCK config and to the PATCH that activates it or makes
  it the default (transition only). It does NOT apply to query resolution:
  like baas, revoking a grant never takes down an existing config.
- Refusal is 403 with a stable details.code (SIMULATED_PROVIDER_NOT_GRANTED),
  a structured log and a best-effort trail event that never holds the answer.
  An unreadable grant fails closed (503).
- New table bureaus.bureau_simulated_provider_grants (additive, idempotent
  migration 20261012090000, partial unique index in SQL only) and operator
  routes GET|PUT|DELETE
  /bureaus/api/v1/admin/platform/organizations/:organizationId/simulated-provider,
  mirroring baas: publish before recording, nothing is rolled back, `force`
  only on revocation.
- `bureaus.simulated-provider.` joins the platform operator event prefixes
  (own stream, never delivered to client webhooks); the audit-trail mapper
  learns the bureaus_simulated_provider_grant resource.
- The grant is owned by bureaus instead of shared with baas: the baas grant is
  only readable through its operator routes, IBaasFacade does not expose it,
  and bureaus has no dependency on another block.

MOCK provider:
- Answers person|company.credit_score (value + scale 0-1000),
  person|company.restrictions (per-kind summaries incl. PROTEST, plus
  totalCount/totalAmount), person.collections and company.lawsuits,
  deterministic by document and consistent across the six kinds.
- Distribution 70% good / 15% low score / 15% restricted, and a test rule by
  document ending: 00 NOT_FOUND (unchanged), 11 good, 22 low score,
  33 restricted, with fixed numbers. Cost stays 0.
- The catalog reports the six kinds as supported by MOCK; real providers are
  unchanged.

baas: the simulated provider refusal now carries the same details.code; status
and message are unchanged.

Deploy stacks gain BUREAUS_SIMULATED_PROVIDER_ORGANIZATION_IDS and
BANKING_PLATFORM_ORGANIZATION_IDS for the bureaus service. Staging runs with
NODE_ENV=production: the variable must be set to `*` on bb-bureaus before this
version is deployed, or creating a MOCK config there is refused.
