commits.title: fix(credit): an unanswered bureau is not a clean record in the five loan dossiers; read the bureaus contract by structure
commits.body:
fix(credit): an unanswered bureau is not a clean record in the five loan dossiers; read the bureaus contract by structure

personal-loan, payroll-loan, rural-loan, vehicle-collateral and property-collateral shared a
copied bureau block with two defects, both generous with credit:

1. An error scored as a clean record. `results: []` is truthy, so a refused batch (4xx/5xx), an
   empty batch, a batch with every item in error and a document NOT_FOUND all read as "consulted,
   nothing against the borrower": full points (200/200). A bureau that was down approved better
   than one that answered.
2. Only the sanction was seen. The signals were searched as substrings under names the bureaus
   block never emits (hasCollections, hasProtests, negativado, hasLawsuits, pep). An active
   collection, lawsuits and a politically exposed person went unread.

Now one shared reader (`_shared/bureau-reading.ts`, same mold as note-reading.ts: one source text,
interpolated into each sandboxed action and evaluated for the API/specs):

- "Clean" only when the answer is whole: batch not in error, every item of the borrower's document
  FOUND, and the three signals the scorecards weigh each covered by a readable answer
  (collections or restrictions; lawsuits; compliance). Anything else — batch ERROR, no results,
  item ERROR/DENIED/NOT_SUPPORTED, NOT_FOUND, partial, FOUND with a null field, a score outside
  0–1000, a company (no kind answers compliance for a CNPJ) — scores half the block (the weight
  "unavailable" already had) and sets `bureauDisponivel: false`.
- The decision tables of personal, payroll, rural and property (1.0.0 → 1.1.0) gain the rule the
  vehicle table already had: `bureauDisponivel = false → MESA`. The catalog simulator sends the
  new input.
- Findings are read by structure and keep the weight each scorecard already gave them:
  isCurrentlyOnCollection / restrictions → the old hasCollections|hasProtests|negativado (blocker);
  lawsuits totalCount/asDefendantCount → the old hasLawsuits (reduced block);
  politicallyExposed / sanctioned → the old sanctioned|pep (blocker).
  The legacy flags and the raw BigDataCorp envelope still count AGAINST the borrower, never for.
- The bureau's own credit score is validated and reported; no scorecard weighs it, so no points.

This CHANGES CREDIT DECISIONS in the five verticals, always to the conservative side, and only
reaches a tenant when the package is reinstalled (custom actions are text installed per tenant;
the five dossiers go to version 2). A tenant that kept its own newer table is not republished by
the installer: there the block stops scoring as clean, but no rule sends the proposal to the desk.

commits.body:
fix(credit): newly read bureau findings go to the desk, never refuse on their own; desk rule before the score cut

Follow-up on the same PR, after review of its first cut. That cut turned the signals nobody had
ever read (active collection, restriction/protest, politically exposed person) into blockers,
because that was the weight the scorecards declared — switching on, at once, an automatic refusal
policy that never ran in production. The owner's rule is "in doubt, the desk".

- What was ALREADY read decides exactly as it did: the legacy flags, searched as the same
  substrings in the same shapes (`results|subjects|data`) — which is also how a sanction in the
  block's answer was and is caught. Blockers are byte-for-byte the master's.
- What NOBODY read before is a finding (`achados`) that only sends the proposal to the desk, with
  one reason each: "cobrança ativa no bureau", "restrição ou protesto no bureau", "ações judiciais
  no bureau", "pessoa exposta politicamente", and the findings of the raw BigDataCorp envelope.
- One table input, `bureauRequerMesa` = the answer is not whole OR there is a finding. The rule
  `true → MESA|bureau: conferencia manual (motivos no dossie)` sits BEFORE the score cut and after
  every refusal that does not hang on the score, so an unanswered bureau never becomes a refusal
  by score and nobody refused for another reason is rescued. personal/payroll/rural/property
  1.0.0 → 1.1.0; vehicle 2.0.3 → 2.0.4 (its rule guarded by `gravameOrdem <= 2`: the third
  creditor is still refused by its own rule).
- Points: a blocker → 0 (as before); `bureauRequerMesa` → half the block; otherwise full.
- A company borrower goes to the desk and the reason says the bureau does not answer for a company.
- Installer: when the account's own table is the one in effect and does not read
  `bureauRequerMesa`, the step `decision-table-bureau-desk-rule:<key>` is `needs-input` with code
  DECISION_TABLE_WITHOUT_BUREAU_DESK_RULE (`blocos.preservedTables[].missingInputs`). No lock
  outside the table.

Differential master × PR, 14,000 generated answers, final decision: the only change is
approved → desk (6,385); 0 new refusals; 3,103 whole clean answers identical.

commits.body:
fix(garantia-viva): rastreio vira resumo por lote; o painel nunca mais baixa a frota

Incidente de 15/10 em staging: os fluxos de lastro e monitoramento pediam ao Traccar
GET /api/devices?groupId= (a 6.15.3 ignora o filtro e devolve a frota, ~10 MB) e
GET /api/positions (~9 MB) por lote e por operação, em paralelo; a resposta inteira ia para a
memória e para o log de execução, e o painel (2 GB) caiu.

Serviço de rastreio (docker/traccar):
- rota GET /gv/api/lots/:lotCode/summary (ou /gv/api/lots/summary?groupId=) → {lotCode, groupId,
  heads, seen, noSignal48h, noSignalHours, outsideFence, geofenceIds, firstSeenAt, historyDays,
  measuredAt}, calculada por SQL no Postgres embutido (cerca WKT → polygon nativo, @>), só leitura
- autenticação delegada ao próprio Traccar (o basic auth é repassado a /api/groups): mesma regra de
  senha e, de quebra, a autorização — lote que o usuário não vê é 404
- nginx na porta única 8082: Traccar em "/", resumo em "/gv/"; Traccar e resumo só em 127.0.0.1.
  O nginx só sobe depois da prova de cadastro fechado (boot frio: porta fechada → 502 → 400, nunca
  200); se o nginx ou o resumo cair, o container sai com erro
- smoke.py confere o resumo de cada lote contra o manifesto, 401 sem credencial/senha errada, 404
  de lote inexistente (--summary-only pula a leitura bruta)
- medido local (lote de 5000): ~95 ms por HTTP, 35 ms de SQL, 246 bytes

Pacote livestock-collateral:
- fetchDevices + fetchPositions viram UMA chamada, fetchTrackingSummary
- livestock_build_backing lê trackingStatus + summaryJson; erro, outro lote, campo faltando ou
  janela diferente da política → LASTRO_INCOMPLETO (MESA), nunca aprovação; cabeça declarada sem
  aparelho segue contando como sem sinal
- pacote.spec falha se algum fluxo chamar /api/devices, /api/positions ou /api/reports/

feat(security): user invites with acceptance; e-mail login never joins an account

Creating a user (POST /users, /users/me/sub-users, /users/:id/sub-users) now
issues a UserInvite: single-use token (only its SHA-256 stored), 7-day expiry,
e-mail with the acceptance link. Nobody joins an account until the owner of
the e-mail accepts, authenticated with that e-mail (logged in, or on login via
inviteToken).

- iam-identity-link: one resolution for the strategy (every API call) and
  AuthService (login/me). Never adopts a pre-registration with a parent (R1),
  refuses a row bound to another IAM identity (R2), service tokens resolve by
  id and never link.
- Invitees without an accepted invite get an account of their own; a notice
  points them to the link. Role resync never lifts a joined sub-user to master.
- Legacy pre-registrations (12 in prod) migrate to PENDING, expired invites
  tied to the existing row; the parent account resends from the Users screen.
- Users screen: invites with status, resend (old link dies), cancel; PANEL_MASTER
  only offered to staff. Public /convite-usuario/:token page, throttled preview.
- R4: managing users is self + descendants (no siblings), also in bulk.

commits.body:
feat(credit): owner's decisions on #1889 — a house table without the bureau rule still sends to the desk; approving without a bureau answer only by a recorded, revocable acceptance

Owner, 14/10/2026:

(a) A house that kept its OWN decision table (no `bureauRequerMesa` rule): the proposal goes to the
    desk anyway. `vehicle_compose_proposal` (version 2) overrides an approval while the dossier says
    `bureauRequerMesa: true`; the engine's verdict stays recorded as the engine's (`decisaoMotor`),
    the proposal carries `salvaguarda` and a pt-BR reason, and the installer's step
    DECISION_TABLE_WITHOUT_BUREAU_DESK_RULE (now classified as the house's) says so.
(b) A house WITHOUT a bureau: the desk by default. It may let the automatic decision go on without
    any bureau answer only by a person reading `BUREAU_WAIVER` (versioned text, sha256) and accepting
    it: `GET/POST/DELETE /credit-desk/bureau-waiver` (BureauWaiverService). Who is the authenticated
    user (never the body); the trail event (`auditoria_eventos`: bureau.waiver.accepted / revoked) is
    written BEFORE the policy (`bureau.aprovacaoSemBureau` + append-only history, claimed by
    expectedVersion); revocable; an acceptance of an older text does not count.
    The dossiers honour it only when the bureau said NOTHING about a CPF borrower (no answer, failed
    batch, every item in error) — never an incomplete answer, a document not found, a finding, a
    legacy/raw shape, a company or a proposal without a CPF — and the block still scores half.
    Vehicle table 2.0.5: the old `bureauDisponivel = false → MESA` rule goes (bureauRequerMesa covers
    it and honours the acceptance).
    Screen: Política › Regras da casa › "Bureau na análise" (BureauWaiverCard): the default, the text
    in full, a box to tick, accept / revoke, who and when, history.

Differential master × PR (14,120 cases, final decision through the real compose): package table and
house's own table — only approved → desk, 0 new refusals, 0 more generous; with the acceptance —
0 new refusals, more generous than master only where the bureau said nothing (52, vehicle, where
master already sent "no answer" to the desk), 0 outside that.

commits.title: fix(workflows): execução manual ancora no gatilho que escuta o evento pedido (#1921)
commits.body:
fix(workflows): execução manual ancora no gatilho que escuta o evento pedido (#1921)

* fix(workflows): anchor a manual run on the trigger that listens to the requested event

The desk authorizes a disbursement through POST /credit-desk/workflows/:id/execute
with the authorization event and no triggerId. resolveManualTrigger then took
"the oldest" trigger, but the disbursement flow's two triggers (authorize and
check) are created in one transaction with the same createdAt, so the order was
the database's: in the staging smoke of #1892, 9 of 9 authorizations were
anchored on the CHECK trigger, payloadForTrigger injected somenteConferir and
the flow answered NADA_A_CONFERIR. The desk never paid.

- resolveManualTrigger(workflowId, triggerId?, eventType?): without a triggerId,
  a check-only event goes to resolveCheckOnlyTrigger; any other event anchors on
  the trigger that listens to it (eventName/fullEventName/event, plain or
  workflow.<id>.<name>) and NEVER on a check-only trigger; with no listener the
  oldest non-check trigger anchors; a flow with only check triggers is refused
  (409 MANUAL_RUN_ONLY_CHECK_TRIGGERS) before anything runs.
- Deterministic order everywhere a trigger is anchored by creation:
  [{ createdAt: 'asc' }, { id: 'asc' }], also re-sorted in memory.
- dispatchManualEvent and POST /workflows/:id/execute/start pass the eventType.
- Tests: the inverse door "an authorization never becomes a check" with the real
  executor (graph and DAG) in both trigger orders — red without the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(workflows): refuse a manual run whose named event no trigger hears on a flow with a check

Review of #1921:
- Without a triggerId, a NAMED event that no trigger listens to, sent to a flow
  that has a check-only trigger (e.g. `antecipacao.desembolso.Conferir`,
  `antecipacao.qualquer` on the disbursement flow), used to fall back to the
  oldest trigger — the authorization — and run as a payment. It is now refused
  (409 MANUAL_RUN_EVENT_NOT_HEARD) before anything is emitted or run. Generic
  runs (`manual` / no event) keep the fallback, minus check triggers.
- `requireListener`: the credit desk's generic execute route requires a trigger
  that listens to the event it names — no fallback at all.
- Removed the unreachable check-event branch of resolveManualTrigger
  (dispatchManualEvent already routes checks to resolveCheckOnlyTrigger; a check
  event reaching it now ends in the same refusal) and the no-op eventType at
  POST /workflows/:id/execute/start (that call only runs with a triggerId).
- Tests: two ordinary triggers of real templates (credit-commission-payout, the
  vehicle lien flow) — the second event anchors on the second trigger and, in
  graph mode, reaches only its branch; unheard named events refused through the
  desk and the manual run with the real executor (graph and DAG).

commits.body:
fix(credit): seed — an unreadable version is not "the package table", and two DMNs are compared by what they decide

Second review of #1889, two reservations on `CreditBlocksSeedService`:

R1. `catch { existing = null }` read "could not read the version in the engine" as "it is the
    package's table": an account with its own table under the declared label, a listing without
    content and a failing read came back `preserved: null`, no warning, the package snapshot in the
    policy. Now a read that fails, or comes back without content, is `preserved { published: false }`
    with the snapshot (and its reason) taken from the engine: "I do not know" never claims the table.
R2. "Same label, another DMN" was a byte comparison: an engine handing the same document back with
    other whitespace made a reinstall warn about an "own version" in an account running the package
    table. `sameDecisionTable` compares what decides — hit policy, inputs, each rule's cells and
    output, as the DMN reader interprets them — and, outside what the reader represents, the XML
    without the whitespace between tags.

The installer's message for a same-label table no longer asserts "another content" when the cause
may be an unreadable version.

commits.body:
feat(security): convite com aceite — o login por e-mail nunca coloca ninguém numa conta (#1938)

* fix(security): only masters create users; e-mail link never adopts a member-squatted row

POST /users, /users/me/sub-users and /users/:id/sub-users had no role check.
Any PANEL_MEMBER could create a PANEL_MASTER under itself and pre-register
someone else's e-mail; the first IAM login links by e-mail (IamJwtAuthStrategy
and AuthService.findOrCreateLocalUser), dropping the victim under the
attacker's hierarchy.

- assertCanCreateUser: only PANEL_MASTER (incl. legacy PANEL_COMERCIAL) and
  staff create users; masters create only PANEL_MEMBER inside their own
  hierarchy (parent defaults to the caller); staff may create masters.
- isAdoptableByEmail: a pre-registered row (no iamUserId) is adopted only if
  it has no parent or its parent is a master/staff; otherwise 403 and no link.
  Adoptions are logged with parent and IAM org.
- USER_MANAGER_ROLES includes PANEL_COMERCIAL (legacy master) for role/parent
  changes too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* feat(security): user invites with acceptance; e-mail login never joins an account

Creating a user (POST /users, /users/me/sub-users, /users/:id/sub-users) now
issues a UserInvite: single-use token (only its SHA-256 stored), 7-day expiry,
e-mail with the acceptance link. Nobody joins an account until the owner of
the e-mail accepts, authenticated with that e-mail (logged in, or on login via
inviteToken).

- iam-identity-link: one resolution for the strategy (every API call) and
  AuthService (login/me). Never adopts a pre-registration with a parent (R1),
  refuses a row bound to another IAM identity (R2), service tokens resolve by
  id and never link.
- Invitees without an accepted invite get an account of their own; a notice
  points them to the link. Role resync never lifts a joined sub-user to master.
- Legacy pre-registrations (12 in prod) migrate to PENDING, expired invites
  tied to the existing row; the parent account resends from the Users screen.
- Users screen: invites with status, resend (old link dies), cancel; PANEL_MASTER
  only offered to staff. Public /convite-usuario/:token page, throttled preview.
- R4: managing users is self + descendants (no siblings), also in bulk.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(security): invite acceptance is always explicit; no token to the inviter

Review of #1938: a self-signup master could invite a victim, forward the
acceptUrl returned to it, and the victim's login with inviteToken accepted
silently — victim moved under the attacker, demoted, data exposed.

- Login never accepts a new invite (token ignored, notice on bad tokens);
  a legacy pre-registration is accepted on login only with acceptInvite:true,
  sent by the invite screen after the explicit click.
- create/resend return only the invite state; if the e-mail fails -> 503
  with a clear message, never the link. AI tools return state only.
- Accepting with an existing account: refused for staff, accounts with
  users, and masters with data / billing document / other members; an empty
  master needs confirmOwnAccount (409 OWN_ACCOUNT_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED),
  and the screen lists the effects. Texts mention existing data.
- Users import creates invites, not dead-end rows.
- Limits: 20 sends/day per inviter, 3/day per recipient, 60 s resend
  cooldown; neutral message, no cross-tenant oracle on create.
- Accept race: claim on id+PENDING+read hash -> 409; P2002 -> 409.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(security): invite limits count real sends on every path

Review of #1938: limits counted UserInvite rows by lastSentAt, but re-invite
and resend update the same row, so it counted as one send forever and the
re-invite path skipped the 60 s wait (50 creates -> 50 e-mails).

- New UserInviteSend table (inviterId, normalized recipientEmail, sentAt),
  migration 20261015233000. A send is recorded before delivery (failed
  deliveries count too).
- 60 s per recipient, 20/day per inviter, 3/day per recipient, applied to
  new invite, re-invite and resend alike.
- "Has data" also counts agents, credentials, chats and agent conversations;
  a parentless PANEL_MEMBER account needs the same explicit confirmation.

commits.title: fix(credit): action pins never come back to life, and the template switch fails clean (#1905)
commits.body:
fix(credit): action pins never come back to life, and the template switch fails clean (#1905)

* fix(credit): action pins never come back to life, and the template switch fails clean

Follow-up of #1897.
- Pointing a step at another action, editing the original and pointing the step back used to
  revive the old pin (pin=A, live=C, ran A in silence). The editor save (ActionsService.update)
  drops the pin whenever the step is pointed elsewhere, also when the stored pin was already
  "suspended"; editing an action drops suspended pins of its slug in the account's active flows.
- The installation record is written inside the switch transaction: a failed switch leaves no
  record pointing at the removed copy (proven against a real database).
- The switch transaction gets explicit maxWait/timeout and a bounded lock wait (lock_timeout);
  waiting too long for another switch of the same template answers 409
  TEMPLATE_INSTALL_IN_PROGRESS with a sentence instead of a bare P2028.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(credit): a request never introduces nor swaps an action pin

Review of #1905. An editor tab opened before the action was edited (active flows moved to the new
version) saved the step back with its stale pin and an input change: the step ran the old version
again, in silence (measured: newer before, old after).

- ActionsService.update: the pin of a saved step comes from the DATABASE; whatever the request
  carries is dropped, and the stored pin is kept only while the step still calls the action it was
  written for (pinFromStore, replacing dropStalePin).
- ActionsService.create and WorkflowsService.create drop any pin the client sends: only the
  template installer writes pins. Duplicate already copies the original's config from the
  database (same account).

commits.title: fix(credit): no dead end on the desk, and no door through which a check pays
commits.body:
fix(credit): no dead end on the desk, and no door through which a check pays

Review of #1892.

B1 — in processing with no id of the bank the desk always offers "Autorizar de novo"
beside "Conferir pagamento", whatever is installed. With W6 1.8 + validator v1 the check
never records "nothing found", and with the old flow + validator v2 the check is refused:
both left only a button that could never move the operation. Authorizing again restarts
the walk at the first key, so a Pix that was paid or is still at the bank is not sent twice.

B2 — a manual run labelled with the check event is anchored on the trigger that LISTENS
to it; a flow with no such trigger is refused (409 CHECK_ONLY_NOT_SUPPORTED, logged,
nothing emitted or run). POST /workflows/:id/execute with the check event against the old
W6 used to pay: the flag was added, the old flow ignored it, and the oldest trigger (the
authorization) anchored the run.

(a) The single point of execution (`WorkflowExecutionService.execute` →
`payloadForTrigger`) forces the restriction from the configuration of the trigger that
fired: the Pub/Sub listener, the queue, RUN_WORKFLOW and future doors hand the payload raw.
(b) ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED no longer blocks the reversal of the boleta (all keys seen FAILED,
nothing paid; the desk has no button for it).
(c) "Nothing found" can be false for a transaction older than the marks: the sentence now
says what is true in both cases.
(d) The provider's text in the operator's hover is masked (e-mail, CPF/CNPJ, phone, random
key, long digit runs).
(e) Guide: an operation paid outside the flow stays `falhou/PIX_LIMIT`; the future safe
split must check the support ticket first.
(f) The flow specs got a 60 s per-test limit: under a parallel suite the default 5 s cut
cases with no assertion failing. No assertion changed.

commits.body:
fix(decision-console): show the rule's name, not its DMN id, on Funnel and Decisions

The block records the rule that fired by its DMN id (DecisionRule_xxx). The
human name is the rule's annotation (<description>) in the XML of the policy
version that decided. The panel now resolves it server side and attaches
`ruleLabel` to funnel rule hits and execution summaries/detail (plus
`ruleLabels` for the rules in a detail's trace):

- decision-rule-labels.ts: ruleId -> label from the DMN (fast-xml-parser);
  fallback "Regra N · <table>" when a rule has no annotation; malformed XML
  yields no labels. RuleLabelResolver walks pipeline -> policy -> version ->
  XML, caches parsed non-draft versions per subaccount+version (bounded LRU)
  and never fails the request.
- Funnel: resolved only when pinned to a pipeline (rule ids are only unique
  inside a policy), against the latest published version, falling back to
  older ones for rules it no longer has.
- Console: Funil, Decisions and Decision show `ruleLabel ?? ruleId` with the
  id in the tooltip.

commits.body:
refactor(decision): bridge and service take a DecisionAccountContext

The Decision bridge (`DecisionTenantClient`) and service
(`DecisionPortalService`) stop receiving the account `code` and receive a
context: which key, which scope, who signs. The SaaS console resolves it
through `DecisionAccountResolver.fromPortal`, doing what every service
method did before (`ready(code)`): the account's subaccount, the vendor's
`decision-tenant-bb`, the owner or the member signing.

No behaviour change: same key, same X-Subaccount-Id, same signatures,
same 503 "being prepared". The key cache becomes one slot per credential
owner, so a second owner (the installed mode, P1-b) can never be served
the vendor's key.

Subaccount administration and the customer's per-subaccount keys keep
taking the subaccount id: they only exist in SaaS. Insights keep their
`code` and resolve the context only where they read decisions.

fix(credit): a disbursement check never pays, and the desk never shows the bank's raw text

Follow-up of #1881, from its adversarial review and its staging smoke of 12/10/2026.

Desk (reaches every tenant on deploy, whatever flow wrote the record):
- A record of the flow of before 12/10 carries the provider's words in `desembolso.erro`
  and no `codigo`. The desk showed them ("Amount exceeds PIX limit of 100000"). It now
  shows the sentence the action wrote for it (only with a code) or one of its own; the
  raw text stays on hover in the operation sheet. Same rule for the toast, the sheet and
  the timeline.
- A refusal no new authorization can pay (PIX_LIMIT, ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED — one list,
  compared with the action's by a contract spec) has no "Tentar de novo".
- "Conferir pagamento" goes to POST /credit-desk/operations/:id/disbursement/check.
  The server writes the request (`somenteConferir: true`), picks the tenant's own flow
  and refuses (409, nothing runs) an installation that cannot be trusted to only
  check. It used to send the AUTHORIZATION event: on an operation in processing with no
  id of the bank it would have sent the first Pix under the label of a check.

Server (deploy):
- The event `antecipacao.desembolso.conferir` carries the restriction from its NAME, in
  `EventDispatchService.dispatch` and `dispatchManualEvent`, with or without the field
  (a `false` included), plain or namespaced by DISPATCH_EVENT.
- The desk's generic execute route diverts any request that asks to only check.
- One gate for the sweep and the desk (`installationHonoursCheckOnly`).
- The installer writes a description the edit route accepts (the template's when it
  fits, the short one otherwise): 39 of 177 templates installed an action that
  `PUT /custom-actions/:id` then refused. The limit is one constant, read by the spec
  from the DTOs.

Template (reaches a tenant on REINSTALL): `antecipacao-validar-desembolso` version 2
- a check has its own number on `tentativas[]` (`conferencia`, `tentativa`), no `n`;
- `repetivel: false` on a refusal of the list;
- a check the bank ANSWERED with no transaction records `nada_encontrado`, changes
  nothing else, and the desk then offers "Autorizar de novo";
- description cut from 1,356 to 400 characters (the detail moved to the guide).
W6 is untouched.

commits.title: fix(workflows): anchor a manual run on the trigger that listens to the requested event
commits.body:
fix(workflows): anchor a manual run on the trigger that listens to the requested event

The desk authorizes a disbursement through POST /credit-desk/workflows/:id/execute
with the authorization event and no triggerId. resolveManualTrigger then took
"the oldest" trigger, but the disbursement flow's two triggers (authorize and
check) are created in one transaction with the same createdAt, so the order was
the database's: in the staging smoke of #1892, 9 of 9 authorizations were
anchored on the CHECK trigger, payloadForTrigger injected somenteConferir and
the flow answered NADA_A_CONFERIR. The desk never paid.

- resolveManualTrigger(workflowId, triggerId?, eventType?): without a triggerId,
  a check-only event goes to resolveCheckOnlyTrigger; any other event anchors on
  the trigger that listens to it (eventName/fullEventName/event, plain or
  workflow.<id>.<name>) and NEVER on a check-only trigger; with no listener the
  oldest non-check trigger anchors; a flow with only check triggers is refused
  (409 MANUAL_RUN_ONLY_CHECK_TRIGGERS) before anything runs.
- Deterministic order everywhere a trigger is anchored by creation:
  [{ createdAt: 'asc' }, { id: 'asc' }], also re-sorted in memory.
- dispatchManualEvent and POST /workflows/:id/execute/start pass the eventType.
- Tests: the inverse door "an authorization never becomes a check" with the real
  executor (graph and DAG) in both trigger orders — red without the fix.

commits.body:
fix(credit): 2nd review of #1889 — a revoked bureau waiver cannot come back; one write rule for every path; accepting is a person's act

- R1: the server keeps the waiver state in Postgres (credit_bureau_waiver_state:
  monotonic epoch, active, policy document, trail event; additive migration). The
  seal now covers the epoch; a record decides only while the state names it, so a
  sealed record pasted back after a revocation is without effect. Revocation is
  durable first (state inactive before the policy is touched). The workflow policy
  readers drop any record not in force (no state = none). One write rule
  (guardPolicyWrite) for the data-store proxy, the assistant's data-store tools,
  the DATASTORE_UPDATE/INSERT/ENSURE handlers and the installer: server-owned keys
  stay as stored, snapshots and ensure never carry a copy, a failed read refuses.
  The waiver routes never return the seal.
- R2: the text says it counts from the next analysis, and only after a reinstall
  when the account's package does not read it yet; the API says which
  (pacoteLeAceite) and the screen shows the right sentence (text version bumped).
- R4: accepting requires an interactive IAM access token; API tokens are refused
  (revoking stays open to them). A policy recreated as a new document, a key change
  or a stale record shows "o aceite anterior não vale mais; aceite de novo".

* feat(workflows): retain workflow execution history for 36 months, configurable

Hourly sweep (WorkflowExecutionRetentionService) deletes only terminal
executions (completed/failed) started and finished before the cutoff and
with no wait state still waiting, in batches of 200 ids (max 25 per sweep).
Action logs and wait states go with them via onDelete: Cascade.

WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_RETENTION_MONTHS (default 36); 0, negative or
non-integer turns it off and logs a warning. One replica per tick via a
Redis lock; Redis down = run anyway (delete by id is idempotent).

feat(workflows): limite de tamanho da resposta HTTP nas ações

Em 15/10 um fluxo WEB_REQUEST baixou ~10 MB por chamada, várias em paralelo,
e derrubou o panel-api de staging por falta de memória. O BaseHttpHandler
chamava o axios sem limite de resposta.

Decisão do dono (15/10):
- 1 MB por padrão; a ação pode pedir mais com `maxResponseBytes`, preso ao
  teto WORKFLOW_HTTP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (padrão 5 MB);
- passou do limite, a ação FALHA com mensagem em português; nada é truncado;
- o corte é do próprio axios (`maxContentLength`), que aborta a conexão sem
  bufferizar o resto.

Vale para todos os herdeiros de BaseHttpHandler: WEB_REQUEST, a família
BaseCatalisaHandler (blocos BB) e o REST de custom action.
`makeCatalisaRequest` deixa o erro de tamanho passar intacto, em vez de
reescrevê-lo como "não foi possível conectar".

DATASTORE_QUERY_DOCUMENTS declara o teto (5 MB) como padrão próprio: os
templates de crédito pedem pageSize 200 de coleções com arrays aninhados.

`maxBodyLength` (corpo ENVIADO) fica de fora de propósito: já está em
memória e limitá-lo quebraria uploads legítimos (EXTRACT_DATA, biometria).

commits.body:
fix(credit): a disbursement check never pays, and the desk never shows the bank's raw text (#1892)

* fix(credit): a disbursement check never pays, and the desk never shows the bank's raw text

Follow-up of #1881, from its adversarial review and its staging smoke of 12/10/2026.

Desk (reaches every tenant on deploy, whatever flow wrote the record):
- A record of the flow of before 12/10 carries the provider's words in `desembolso.erro`
  and no `codigo`. The desk showed them ("Amount exceeds PIX limit of 100000"). It now
  shows the sentence the action wrote for it (only with a code) or one of its own; the
  raw text stays on hover in the operation sheet. Same rule for the toast, the sheet and
  the timeline.
- A refusal no new authorization can pay (PIX_LIMIT, ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED — one list,
  compared with the action's by a contract spec) has no "Tentar de novo".
- "Conferir pagamento" goes to POST /credit-desk/operations/:id/disbursement/check.
  The server writes the request (`somenteConferir: true`), picks the tenant's own flow
  and refuses (409, nothing runs) an installation that cannot be trusted to only
  check. It used to send the AUTHORIZATION event: on an operation in processing with no
  id of the bank it would have sent the first Pix under the label of a check.

Server (deploy):
- The event `antecipacao.desembolso.conferir` carries the restriction from its NAME, in
  `EventDispatchService.dispatch` and `dispatchManualEvent`, with or without the field
  (a `false` included), plain or namespaced by DISPATCH_EVENT.
- The desk's generic execute route diverts any request that asks to only check.
- One gate for the sweep and the desk (`installationHonoursCheckOnly`).
- The installer writes a description the edit route accepts (the template's when it
  fits, the short one otherwise): 39 of 177 templates installed an action that
  `PUT /custom-actions/:id` then refused. The limit is one constant, read by the spec
  from the DTOs.

Template (reaches a tenant on REINSTALL): `antecipacao-validar-desembolso` version 2
- a check has its own number on `tentativas[]` (`conferencia`, `tentativa`), no `n`;
- `repetivel: false` on a refusal of the list;
- a check the bank ANSWERED with no transaction records `nada_encontrado`, changes
  nothing else, and the desk then offers "Autorizar de novo";
- description cut from 1,356 to 400 characters (the detail moved to the guide).
W6 is untouched.

* fix(credit): no dead end on the desk, and no door through which a check pays

Review of #1892.

B1 — in processing with no id of the bank the desk always offers "Autorizar de novo"
beside "Conferir pagamento", whatever is installed. With W6 1.8 + validator v1 the check
never records "nothing found", and with the old flow + validator v2 the check is refused:
both left only a button that could never move the operation. Authorizing again restarts
the walk at the first key, so a Pix that was paid or is still at the bank is not sent twice.

B2 — a manual run labelled with the check event is anchored on the trigger that LISTENS
to it; a flow with no such trigger is refused (409 CHECK_ONLY_NOT_SUPPORTED, logged,
nothing emitted or run). POST /workflows/:id/execute with the check event against the old
W6 used to pay: the flag was added, the old flow ignored it, and the oldest trigger (the
authorization) anchored the run.

(a) The single point of execution (`WorkflowExecutionService.execute` →
`payloadForTrigger`) forces the restriction from the configuration of the trigger that
fired: the Pub/Sub listener, the queue, RUN_WORKFLOW and future doors hand the payload raw.
(b) ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED no longer blocks the reversal of the boleta (all keys seen FAILED,
nothing paid; the desk has no button for it).
(c) "Nothing found" can be false for a transaction older than the marks: the sentence now
says what is true in both cases.
(d) The provider's text in the operator's hover is masked (e-mail, CPF/CNPJ, phone, random
key, long digit runs).
(e) Guide: an operation paid outside the flow stays `falhou/PIX_LIMIT`; the future safe
split must check the support ticket first.
(f) The flow specs got a 60 s per-test limit: under a parallel suite the default 5 s cut
cases with no assertion failing. No assertion changed.

commits.title: fix(workflows): refuse a manual run whose named event no trigger hears on a flow with a check
commits.body:
fix(workflows): refuse a manual run whose named event no trigger hears on a flow with a check

Review of #1921:
- Without a triggerId, a NAMED event that no trigger listens to, sent to a flow
  that has a check-only trigger (e.g. `antecipacao.desembolso.Conferir`,
  `antecipacao.qualquer` on the disbursement flow), used to fall back to the
  oldest trigger — the authorization — and run as a payment. It is now refused
  (409 MANUAL_RUN_EVENT_NOT_HEARD) before anything is emitted or run. Generic
  runs (`manual` / no event) keep the fallback, minus check triggers.
- `requireListener`: the credit desk's generic execute route requires a trigger
  that listens to the event it names — no fallback at all.
- Removed the unreachable check-event branch of resolveManualTrigger

feat(service-attestations): bloco novo — atestados de serviço lidos da fonte de escala (MOCK + fonte-escalas)

Quem antecipa o repasse de um prestador precisa saber se o serviço foi prestado e quanto o
pagador vai pagar. Hoje é um PDF do cedente. Este bloco lê o sistema de escala e repasse de quem
paga (fonte-escalas; simulado até a credencial existir) e guarda o que a fonte afirmou, com versão
e hash, avisando por evento quando nasce, muda ou some. Agnóstico: não sabe de antecipação.

- Porta `AttestationProvider` + fábrica (switch) + `MOCK` determinístico por organização e
  cenário (12 profissionais com CPF/CNPJ válidos, setores de hospital, repasse mensal = soma dos
  plantões, pago no dia 20 útil do mês seguinte; `mockOverrides` cancel/amount; cenários
  empty/unavailable/partial).
- Driver `fonte-escalas` (doc v1.7): token password grant com Basic, renovação < 60 s, 401 → renova
  uma vez, refresh POST → GET → login, 204 vazio, fornecedores paginados, lista de leitura que
  recusa escrita antes do envio, campos fora da doc no bruto, externalId sem CPF.
- Conexão por organização com credencial cifrada (nunca sai), teste, leitura agora e agendada.
- MOTOR genérico em `src/service-attestations/sync/` (trava por conexão, SyncRun, upsert com
  contentHash/version, sumiço em leitura completa = cancelado, hooks de evento, agendador
  LockedPass), sem referência ao domínio — teste garante. Corte para o bloco irmão de rastreio;
  sobe a `src/shared` quando ele existir.
- Eventos `service-attestations.attestation.confirmed|changed|cancelled` e `.sync.failed`, sem
  PII; concessão do simulado no stream do operador; mapeamento no audit-trail.
- Rotas do contrato com Zod e escopo por organização; trava do simulado em produção (concessão do
  operador ou lista de reserva).
- Ligação: ModuleNames/porta 3042/prefixo, container, app monolito, standalone, build, package,
  aliases, deploy-swarm, deploy-guard, stacks, compose, permissões, secret-keys, INDEX, openspec.
- Migration idempotente (aplicada duas vezes num Postgres 16 limpo).

Testes: 32 novos (mock, leitura, motor genérico, driver contra servidor HTTP falso, rotas e
escopo, credencial, trava). Suítes shared/iam/audit-trail/webhooks-engine: 2440 passam; a única
falha (env.test WPP_SESSION_WORKER_ENABLED) falha igual na base. tsc: os mesmos 9 erros da base.

N1 the signer is re-read INSIDE the signing lock (ALREADY_SIGNED), SIGNED and
   esignature.signer.signed are written inside it, and the SIGNING revert is a
   conditional update (status = 'SIGNING'): a concurrent SIGNED never regresses.
N2 ADD VALUE 'SIGNING' moved to its own migration 20261017125000 (the Launch
   verifier does not see ADD VALUE; alone it is "indeterminada"), with a test
   over the previous state (120000 applied, data in it) and idempotent re-apply.
(a) refresh moves a stuck SIGNING back to SENT only with the engine readable,
    no Signed entry, no lock held and SIGNING for more than 10 minutes.
(b) residual window documented.
(c) OPENSIGN_ALLOWED_HOSTS takes scheme://host:port (IPv6 in brackets); a bare
    hostname opens https on the default port only; http needs an explicit port.
(d) evidence claim older than 5 min with no hash is claimed again.

feat(calc,baas): BULLET com juros capitalizados e pagamento de boleto no sandbox

Motor de cálculos: `bulletConfig: { capitalizeInterest, compoundingPeriods? }` no
BULLET. Com uma parcela, `compoundingPeriods` é o prazo: 350.000 a 1,4% a.m. em
12 meses passa de 354.900 (um mês de juros, medido no painel em 16/10) para
413.545,70. Sem `bulletConfig` o BULLET de sempre não muda; configuração que não
fecha é 400, nunca ignorada.

BaaS: o aviso `boleto.settled` do banco caía no `default` do processamento de
webhooks — o título nunca liquidava e ninguém era avisado. Agora o handler casa
o título (id do banco, ou nosso número), reivindica a liquidação e publica
`baas.boleto.settled` a cada aviso (`firstSettlement`, `previousStatus`). No
MockBank, `POST /boletos/:id/sandbox/pay` simula o pagamento: liquida, credita a
conta do beneficiário e avisa pelo MESMO webhook de um banco real.

Provedor em cache: conferido que não existe — o provedor é construído do
registro a cada operação; teste prende isso. A armadilha real do PATCH é
`settings` substituir o objeto inteiro.

fix(build): alias the createRequire banner — a source import of the same name broke the e-signature bundle

The esbuild banner declares `createRequire` at the top of every bundle. #633 made
src/e-signature/routes/sign-page.router.ts import `createRequire` from 'node:module' itself; the
bundle is one ESM module, so the name was declared twice and Bun refused to load
dist/e-signature/main.mjs ("createRequire has already been declared"). In staging the new
e-signature replica crash-looped on boot and the deploy of bf4d5c3f never promoted (16/10/2026).

The banner now imports it as __bbCreateRequire. Checked: with the old banner `node --check`
rejects dist/e-signature/main.mjs (SyntaxError: Identifier 'createRequire' has already been
declared); with the new one all 41 dist/*/main.mjs pass `node --check`, and bun parses e-signature.

commits.title: feat(e-signature): OpenSign local engine signs to COMPLETED via SignatureApplier (#632)
commits.body:
feat(e-signature): OpenSign local engine signs to COMPLETED via SignatureApplier (#632)

* feat(e-signature): OpenSign local engine signs to COMPLETED through the block

The OpenSign self-hosted provider now drives the local engine (behind the
X-OpenSign-Gate) end to end: one technical owner per organization kept in
the config settings, one contact per signer per document, one signature
widget per signer, and a SignatureApplier that draws the PNG and the footer
stamp with pdf-lib, calls functions/signPdf with X-Signer-Ip, and on the last
signer archives the sealed PDF and the certificate in file-storage, marks
COMPLETED, publishes esignature.request.completed and captures evidence.

COMPLETED now comes from IsCompleted (the engine never writes Status); the
fake SignedUrl, "the first contracts_Users", contact reuse by e-mail and the
side-effect resend are gone. Every refusal/failure of the signing path
publishes an event.

Proven against the real engine (image of panel PR #1975 at 9629f8fe).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(e-signature): harden the OpenSign local signing path (adversarial review)

A1 PNG size read from the IHDR (<= 2000x1000) before pdf-lib or the engine.
A2 signer goes SIGNING before signPdf; a failed/timed-out call re-reads the
   engine until the signer's Signed entry shows up (reconciled) or the deadline
   passes; unreadable engine keeps SIGNING (503 SIGNATURE_UNCONFIRMED).
A3 engine host allowlist OPENSIGN_ALLOWED_HOSTS (unset -> refused); gateToken
   rotation plan in the README.
M1 every document read checks the organization's owner; extUserId and
   extUserOrganizationId are block-owned in provider-config create/update.
M2 no engine body echoed (status + Parse code only), testConnection included.
M3 lock only around the engine step, heartbeat + compare-and-delete (Lua);
   COMPLETED and evidence claimed by conditional update; certificate wait capped;
   evidence reuses the archived bytes.
M4 evidence only over an archived certificate (refresh captures it later).
M5 OUT_OF_ORDER for sequential requests.
M6 fileBase64 max, 500 pages, download size capped while streaming.
Low: widget bounds, duplicate signer e-mail, validated IP in the stamp,
   original hash from the stored original, ensureAccount converges on the
   oldest owner, settings merged over the current copy, cancel keeps DECLINED.

Migration: SignerStatus gains SIGNING (ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS).

PROVIDER_CONFLICT, OUT_OF_ORDER, IMAGE_TOO_LARGE, ... and the failures

* fix(e-signature): same-signer race, SIGNING migration of its own, refresh/allowlist hardening

N1 the signer is re-read INSIDE the signing lock (ALREADY_SIGNED), SIGNED and
   esignature.signer.signed are written inside it, and the SIGNING revert is a
   conditional update (status = 'SIGNING'): a concurrent SIGNED never regresses.

(c) OPENSIGN_ALLOWED_HOSTS takes scheme://host:port (IPv6 in brackets); a bare

fix(e-signature): follow-ups of #632 (#635)

1. Inside the signing lock the applier re-reads the ENVELOPE too: DECLINED,
   CANCELLED, EXPIRED or COMPLETED meanwhile -> refused with the reason
   (REQUEST_DECLINED...). PARTIALLY_SIGNED and COMPLETED are written only from an
   open status (updateStatusIfOpen / claimCompleted), so a decline that lands
   during the engine call is never overwritten.
2. refresh releases a stuck SIGNING with updateIfStatus(id, 'SIGNING',
   {status: 'SENT'}, updatedBefore) - the age limit is in the WHERE; a SIGNING
   signer the engine reports DECLINED takes the engine status.

   applies an "indeterminada" migration by itself; confirm SIGNING in pg_enum).
   The migration itself is untouched: it is already applied in staging.
4. OPENSIGN_ALLOWED_HOSTS entries in the old host:port format: warning at boot,
   explicit refusal message (ALLOWLIST_LEGACY_FORMAT), and POST
   /provider-configs/:id/test answers success:false with message and code.

commits.body:
fix(e-signature): hosted page review — OTP limits decided in the database, single-use sign token, engine refusals in pt-BR

Revisão adversarial do #633:

1. Limites do código no banco (updateMany condicional + count): envio (espera, trava,
   teto) e cada tentativa são reivindicados antes de comparar; pedidos paralelos não furam.
   Tetos na vida do link: 15 tentativas e 10 envios (otp_attempts_total, otp_sends_total);
   atingido, o link trava (link_locked_at) até a casa reemitir no reenvio.
2. O /verify devolve um token de uso único (scope esignature:sign, 30 min, do signatário
   que conferiu); /sign o exige e consome o jti. GET /:code/state não diz mais 'conferido'.
3. O /decline exige o mesmo token e corre sob o lock do applier da F2
   (esignature:signing:<requestId>); SIGNING fica fora do notIn.
4. Recusas do motor (details.reason: BUSY, OUT_OF_ORDER, REQUEST_EXPIRED, ALREADY_SIGNED,
   IMAGE_TOO_LARGE, PROVIDER_CONFLICT) em pt-BR, com reload só quando o estado mudou; o
   desenho e o aceite ficam na tela e o token volta a valer nas passageiras. Estado SIGNING.

Também: HKDF separa a chave da cópia do código e a do HMAC do OTP; PDF original e logo

commits.body:
feat(antecipacao): cedente PF por padrão, termo modelo 3 qualificado e e-mail do signatário conferido (#1947)

* feat(antecipacao): accept an individual assignor (CPF) in counterparty mode

Owner's decision (15/10/2026): with counterparty mode on, the fund also
acquires from an individual. `ensureForLead` used to refuse anything that
was not a 14-digit CNPJ with a 409.

- ensureForLead: the document is classified with check digits. A valid CPF
  creates-or-recognizes the PERSON in `people` (externalRef = lead id, the
  lead's e-mail as contact) and records `identidade.tipo = 'pessoa'` with
  ids only; a CNPJ follows the company path as before (now tagged
  `tipo: 'empresa'`). Anything else is a 409 in plain pt-BR. A 409 from the
  block (same lead, another CPF) becomes a human sentence.
- statusForLead: an individual shows name + CPF, no company/representative;
  the only pending item is the e-mail the term goes to.
- CessionSignatureService.request: an individual signs in her own name —
  no `companies.evaluate`; the record says why (`reason
  CEDENTE_PESSOA_FISICA`, `modo proprio`, role `titular`). The envelope,
  W8's event and the per-line are the same code as for a company.
- gerar-termo (model 2): the assignor line of a CPF reads "pessoa física,
  CPF 000.000.000-00"; a company's line is unchanged (same text and hash).
- Desk: register form takes CPF or CNPJ, the PF badge is no longer red and
  an individual can be enabled; the identity card shows the individual.

Money path untouched: the disbursement still goes to the assignor's Pix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* feat(antecipacao): PF by default, fully qualified term (model 3), checked signer e-mail

Owner's decisions (15/10/2026) and the review of #1947.

D1 - every receivables product accepts an individual by default
(exigeCedentePJ: false in the catalog and in the policy seed). Requiring a
legal entity is the house's call and a floor: the policy's true wins over
the product (ladder FLOORS only-on), a product may only tighten it. The
decision table 1.4.0 drops the general PF refusal (the score turns the
requirement into an impediment, which the table refuses); the bank channel
extension is dispensed on a table without that refusal (whenAnchorAbsent:
'not-needed') and still applies to tenants on 1.2.x.

D2 - term model 3: the assignor fully qualified (PF: name, CPF,
nationality, marital status, profession, address; PJ: corporate name, CNPJ,
seat) and the place of the deed. Anything missing means no term
(SEM_QUALIFICACAO_DO_CEDENTE with semTermo.faltando, or
SEM_LUGAR_DA_CELEBRACAO). Stored model-2 terms keep their text and hash.
The desk form and the bank channel ask for the fields (GET/PUT
/credit-channel/v1/assignor-profile, ASSIGNOR_PROFILE_INCOMPLETE before the
analysis).

B1 - the term classifies the assignor like assignorDocumentOf: PF only on
^\d{11}$ of the unmasked document; an alphanumeric CNPJ is a company.
B2 - exigencias[act].pessoa ('declared' | 'verified'); verified requires an
e-mail whose possession people proved (POST /people/contacts/resolve).
R1 - identidade is compared through the real deepMergeJson; null only to
delete a key the record has; an individual record has no company keys.
R3/R7 - the envelope goes to the LEAD's e-mail, checked against people;
a different proven e-mail is a pending item, nothing is sent.
R5 - the desk offers "Habilitar" to an individual only when the house
policy does not require a legal entity, with matching hints.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* feat(antecipacao): gradual model 3, debenture keeps PJ, legacy PJ default migration

Owner's decisions (16/10/2026):

- Term model 3 is GRADUAL: fully qualified (assignor + place of the deed)
  gives model 3; anything missing gives model 2 byte for byte (pinned
  against the generator on origin/master) with termo.qualificacaoPendente,
  qualificacao and a QUALIFICACAO_INCOMPLETA warning in preco.avisos.
  No proposal is held. The desk shows the gap on the assignor's page and on
  the proposal (ficha and queue).
- receivables-generic-debenture keeps exigeCedentePJ: true (the issuer has
  to be a corporation); every other product accepts an individual.
- The installer turns the OLD seed's exigeCedentePJ: true off only when it
  is provably untouched (published by the seed, no snapshot of the policy);
  otherwise it reports REVIEW_ASSIGNOR_PJ ("Revise Exigir cedente PJ") to
  the house and changes nothing.
- The bank channel never holds the request: ASSIGNOR_PROFILE_INCOMPLETE is
  gone from POST /applications. A missing e-mail leaves the SIGNATURE
  pending: the acceptance answers SIGNATURE_PENDING (409, details.missing)
  from a typed SignaturePendingException; GET /assignor-profile still says
  what to complete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(antecipacao): fail closed on unreadable signature mode; migration order; term refinements

Second review of #1947.

- B3: the PJ-default migration runs BEFORE the house inputs (which
  republish the policy as a person). "Seed's" = the whole history
  (snapshots + active) with the same value, published only by the seed or by
  package installations, never by the desk's screen. Runs for the bank
  channel package alone too; a document without version is a pendência; a
  concurrent installation that already wrote false is not; the wording of a
  failed write says what happened.
- Fail closed: an unreadable counterparty switch (policy or tenant key) is
  `indeterminado`, never "off". The acceptance is refused with 503 "tente de
  novo" (UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE on the bank channel, not stored as the answer),
  also for counterparties on without e-signature. The desk front no longer
  treats a 5xx as hash mode.
- Score and dossier classify the document like assignorDocumentOf: an
  alphanumeric CNPJ is PJ (own check digits), never "PF with invalid CPF".
- Term model 3: marital status agrees with `genero` or is said neutrally
  (never "(a)"); a company is "neste ato representada por" its registered
  representative (missing -> model 2 with the warning); the assignee is
  qualified too (CNPJ and seat of the fund or creditor) as a model-3
  condition. Policy screen gains the seat fields.
- Desk form: per product, with the LIVE parameter, whether it requires PJ,
  and the house's switch; optional gender field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(antecipacao): no unsigned operation with counterparties on, from any door

Third review of #1947.

- Assignor portal BFF (apps/antecipacao): the hash acceptance runs only
  when the panel said `modo: 'hash'` successfully. A 5xx (the new 503), the
  panel down, a 404 of a route an older panel lacks, or an unknown answer
  is "tente de novo" (503) — never the hash. Pure gate (cession-gate.mjs)
  with node tests.
- Server side: the acceptance validator (antecipacao-validar-aceite) reads
  the house policy and the signature records of the proposal (W8 passes
  them). With counterparties on it opens the operation only for a signed
  record of THIS proposal, envelope and term (ASSINATURA_EXIGIDA /
  ASSINATURA_NAO_ENCONTRADA / ASSINATURA_NAO_CONFERIDA otherwise). Proven
  by running W8 directly on the real executor.
- Who published a policy version is a server-written field
  (`origemPublicacao`): package-seed (W0), package-install (installer),
  desk (forced by the Data Store proxy), assistant. The PJ-default
  migration trusts it; legacy versions only by the server's exact texts.
- Desk hints treat exigeCedentePJ 'true' (text) as true.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(antecipacao): the acceptance gate lives on the server, closed for every tenant

Fourth review of #1947: the gate failed open (a policy read that failed gave
"no counterparties"), trusted a tenant-writable record and lived only in
each tenant's copy of W8.

- Validator: a policy answer that is not a successfully read, non-empty list
  is ASSINATURA_NAO_CONFERIDA (every installation creates the policy).
- Server gate: WorkflowExecutionService.execute — the one door every
  execution passes — asks AcceptanceGateService (registered at boot) before
  anything runs or is recorded, for any flow listening to
  antecipacao.proposta.aceita. Counterparty mode unreadable → refused; off
  → allowed (hash); on → only a signed record of THIS proposal and envelope
  AND the e-signature block saying the envelope is COMPLETED with
  businessId cessao:<docId>:<hash>. A block that does not answer → refused.
  Closes tenants that never reinstalled.
- cessoes_assinatura is server-owned: the Data Store proxy, the workflow
  handlers (insert/update/ensure/delete) and the assistant's tools refuse to
  write it; only CessionSignatureService does.
- origemPublicacao is stamped by the workflow Data Store handlers too
  (`workflow`, or `package-seed` for the seed's own ensure) and snapshots
  carry who took them (snapshotOrigem); the PJ migration checks both.

commits.title: fix(decision): decision-pedir and decision-mesa read what the blocks answer, through the same action
commits.body:
fix(decision): decision-pedir and decision-mesa read what the blocks answer, through the same action

decision-pedir read the outcome at decidir.output.output.resultado (every
request went to the desk) and registered the analysis with key and data,
which the ensure handler refuses (docKey and defaultData): the analysis was
never registered and the routing that depends on it never ran. The ensure
now creates the analysis and a merge UPDATE writes the execution, so a new
attempt of an existing analysis carries the new executionId.

decision-mesa read acharAnalise.output.data[0].leadId/analiseId over a
query: the verdict was recorded without its analysis and the card never
moved.

Both use decision-result-compose, now with each input optional: the
execution only (pedir), the query only (mesa), or both (resultado).
EXECUTE_DECISION_CONFIG returns the trace when the block sends it, so the
synchronous outcome follows the outcomeOf rule too.

fluxos.flow.spec.ts (renamed from resultado.flow.spec.ts) runs each of the
three flows end to end against the real answers, graph and dag; against the
previous pedir and mesa 12 of their cases fail. mesa-verdict-flow spec moved
to the new output shape.

fix: review findings on #1976 — captcha ready on remount, safe redirect, transient acceptance refusals as 503

- Register: mark the captcha ready on `onReady` too. @hcaptcha/react-hcaptcha 2.0.2 fires
  `onLoad` only when it downloads api.js; on a second mount (window.hcaptcha present) it only
  renders and fires `onReady`, so the form sat in 'loading' until the 10 s timeout and failed.
  Transient hCaptcha errors (network-error, rate-limited, challenge-expired, challenge-closed)
  no longer lock the form: back to 'ready' with a retry sentence.
- safeRedirect util shared by Login and Register: internal paths only — refuses backslash,
  control characters and a leading `//` (also after one percent-decoding) and requires
  `new URL(r, origin).origin === origin`. Register no longer forwards an external redirect.
- AcceptanceRefusedExceptionFilter: transient codes (ACCEPTANCE_GATE_FAILED,
  ACCEPTANCE_GATE_NOT_REGISTERED, *_UNREADABLE, ESIGNATURE_UNAVAILABLE) answer 503 with the
  neutral message; definitive ones stay 409. Nothing is written when headers were already sent.

  lead's e-mail as contact) and records `identidade.tipo = 'pessoa'` with

  `tipo: 'empresa'`). Anything else is a 409 in plain pt-BR. A 409 from the
  block (same lead, another CPF) becomes a human sentence.
- statusForLead: an individual shows name + CPF, no company/representative;
  the only pending item is the e-mail the term goes to.
- CessionSignatureService.request: an individual signs in her own name —
  no `companies.evaluate`; the record says why (`reason
  CEDENTE_PESSOA_FISICA`, `modo proprio`, role `titular`). The envelope,
  W8's event and the per-line are the same code as for a company.
- gerar-termo (model 2): the assignor line of a CPF reads "pessoa física,
  CPF 000.000.000-00"; a company's line is unchanged (same text and hash).
- Desk: register form takes CPF or CNPJ, the PF badge is no longer red and
  an individual can be enabled; the identity card shows the individual.

Money path untouched: the disbursement still goes to the assignor's Pix.

commits.title: feat(opensign): mutual TLS on the engine's port — the docker runtime hides the origin
commits.body:
feat(opensign): mutual TLS on the engine's port — the docker runtime hides the origin

Owner's decision (16/10): "Fazer o mTLS antes de prod". Measured in staging: inside the Launch
docker runtime every connection reaches the container from 172.17.0.1 (docker-proxy), from outside
and from the e-signature LXC alike, so an origin allowlist cannot work here.

- Caddy on 8090 is TLS only, client_auth require_and_verify against OUR CA; the gate header stays
  (defense in depth). Material comes from the service env (base64 PEM) and the entrypoint writes it
  0600; SERVER_URL must be https.
- scripts/opensign/emitir-tls.sh: EC P-256 CA (key never leaves the operator's machine) + server cert
  (SAN = mesh host) + client cert CN=bb-e-signature (clientAuth). Idempotent.
- deploy-opensign.sh: no HTTP health (healthPath empty → liveness by the container, no public route
  or name), --recriar, mTLS material into the service env and into opensign-local-<env>.env, the locks
  checked over mTLS (gate token via a 0600 header file, not argv), 1 h wait for the image pull.
- prova-assinatura.mjs over node:https with the client cert and the CA pinned.

Proof against the built image: PROVA OK 15/15 — plain HTTP 400 without reaching Parse; no client cert →
ERR_SSL_TLSV13_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED; cert without gate 403; cert + gate 200 over TLSv1.3; signPdf →
COMPLETED with hash, certificate and the signer's ip. Also refused: a client cert from another CA
(curl 56), the server cert used as client (56), and a client that does not pin our CA (60).

commits.title: fix(workflows): an execution never starts inside the rewrite in place (P6, CBP review)
commits.body:
fix(workflows): an execution never starts inside the rewrite in place (P6, CBP review)

The check for executions in flight and the rewrite run in one transaction,
but an execution could start between them: its running row did not exist
when the check counted, and it read the old steps. Both sides now take one
advisory lock per workflow (definition-lock.ts): the rewrite takes it
exclusive before counting; an execution takes it shared to write its running
row, and reads the layout again under it. The check also counts a wait state
just resolved whose execution is still suspended (the resolver flips the wait
state before it marks the execution running).

Integration spec (real Postgres, 20/20): an authorization dispatched while the
rewrite holds its transaction starts only after the commit and runs the new
steps (without the lock it starts in the window, on the old steps); a resolved
wait not yet resumed leads to a new copy; the acceptance flow rewritten in
place keeps its id and trigger, the event matcher finds that one flow, and the
real AcceptanceGateService still refuses an unsigned acceptance on it.

fix(decision): the async result finds the analysis and reads the outcome as the rest of Decision

decision-resultado read the analysis at acharAnalise.output.data[0].id and
the outcome at lerExecucao.output.output.resultado. The query answers items of
{ id, version, attributes } and a policy answers a scalar or, with several
outputs, an object with outcome (the package's starter answers
{ outcome, motivo }): the analysis was never written and every async result
went to the desk with an empty outcome.

A JavaScript custom action, decision-result-compose (sandbox, no network),
takes the whole items and the whole execution, picks the analysis of that
execution and reads the outcome by the rule of outcomeOf (last trace step,
its output named outcome, the output if scalar, its field named outcome). A
delivery with no analysis writes nothing and asks no desk. gravar keeps
merge: true (#1964).

resultado.flow.spec.ts runs the flow with the real executor, handlers,
interpolation and sandbox against the answers of the Data Store and the
platform block, in graph and dag mode; against the previous template 10 of

commits.title: fix(antecipacao): trava de recebíveis no handshake do banking (BB #629) — proposta declara, aceite leva o lienId
commits.body:
fix(antecipacao): trava de recebíveis no handshake do banking (BB #629) — proposta declara, aceite leva o lienId

The banking block creates the lien BEFORE calling the acceptance, so the CCP side follows its handshake:

- GET proposal answers `repaymentLock { amountCents, destinationAccountId, sourceDocuments, externalReference,
  expiresAt, payerName? }` — exactly `CreditRepaymentLock`, deterministic, reference `credit-proposal:<id>`.
  A lock that cannot be formed (no fund account UUID, payers without document, >20 payers) is not offered.
- POST acceptance takes `repaymentLock { lienId, externalReference }` (declared in the DTO: the whitelist pipe
  would drop it). A lock proposal without it, or with another reference, is refused 409 with a neutral sentence
  (the bank undoes the lien); a lien sent for a non-lock proposal is refused too. No echo in the answer.
- The lien is stamped on the proposal (`travaBanco`) before W8; validar-aceite refuses without it
  (TRAVA_AUSENTE) and copies it to the operation (`trava`, no `trava_pendente`) and every title
  (`lienId`, `lienExternalReference`).
- antecipacao-trava-baas resolves the proposal reference to the operation (by propostaId); `created` before the
  operation is a no-op; NEW `baas.lien.capture.failed` (holdLeftActive) stamps `trava.alertaMesa` and audits
  `trava.captura.falhou`; events without an operation alert. W10 subscribes the new event in its own
  subscription (no double delivery for tenants that already have the lien one). W7 untouched.
- Contract test copies the banking types and shape check (credit.facade, http-credit.facade, banking-core).

commits.body:
feat(antecipacao): PF by default, fully qualified term (model 3), checked signer e-mail

Owner's decisions (15/10/2026) and the review of #1947.

D1 - every receivables product accepts an individual by default
(exigeCedentePJ: false in the catalog and in the policy seed). Requiring a
legal entity is the house's call and a floor: the policy's true wins over
the product (ladder FLOORS only-on), a product may only tighten it. The
decision table 1.4.0 drops the general PF refusal (the score turns the
requirement into an impediment, which the table refuses); the bank channel
extension is dispensed on a table without that refusal (whenAnchorAbsent:
'not-needed') and still applies to tenants on 1.2.x.

D2 - term model 3: the assignor fully qualified (PF: name, CPF,
nationality, marital status, profession, address; PJ: corporate name, CNPJ,
seat) and the place of the deed. Anything missing means no term
(SEM_QUALIFICACAO_DO_CEDENTE with semTermo.faltando, or
SEM_LUGAR_DA_CELEBRACAO). Stored model-2 terms keep their text and hash.
The desk form and the bank channel ask for the fields (GET/PUT
/credit-channel/v1/assignor-profile, ASSIGNOR_PROFILE_INCOMPLETE before the
analysis).

B1 - the term classifies the assignor like assignorDocumentOf: PF only on
^\d{11}$ of the unmasked document; an alphanumeric CNPJ is a company.
B2 - exigencias[act].pessoa ('declared' | 'verified'); verified requires an
e-mail whose possession people proved (POST /people/contacts/resolve).
R1 - identidade is compared through the real deepMergeJson; null only to
delete a key the record has; an individual record has no company keys.
R3/R7 - the envelope goes to the LEAD's e-mail, checked against people;
a different proven e-mail is a pending item, nothing is sent.
R5 - the desk offers "Habilitar" to an individual only when the house
policy does not require a legal entity, with matching hints.

commits.title: feat(e-signature): OpenSign provider speaks mutual TLS to the engine
commits.body:
feat(e-signature): OpenSign provider speaks mutual TLS to the engine

Owner's decision (16/10): "Fazer o mTLS antes de prod". The engine (panel repo docker/opensign, #1981)
requires a client certificate signed by our CA on its only port; inside the Launch docker runtime
every connection comes from 172.17.0.1, so the lock is WHO, not where.

- engineTlsFromEnv(): OPENSIGN_TLS_CA_PEM_B64, OPENSIGN_TLS_CLIENT_CERT_PEM_B64 and
  OPENSIGN_TLS_CLIENT_KEY_PEM_B64 from the SERVICE env (never a tenant's ProviderConfig); all three or
  none — a partial or broken set throws instead of talking without a certificate.
- Every request to the engine (REST, PDF upload, file download) carries Bun's fetch `tls` option
  {ca, cert, key}: our CA pinned, the client certificate presented.
- With mutual TLS configured an http baseUrl is refused (ENGINE_TLS_REQUIRES_HTTPS), never downgraded;
  material from the env outside Bun fails loud (ENGINE_TLS_RUNTIME: Node would drop `tls` in silence).
- Boot logs whether mutual TLS is on and errors loud on a broken set. README: the three variables.

Tests: tests/unit/e-signature 30 files, 363 passed (7 in opensign.mtls.test.ts; the fake PEM key is
assembled at run time so the secrets scanner does not see a literal header).
Runtime proof (Bun 1.4, the real provider against the engine image with mTLS): with cert + CA →
ensureAccount OK; nothing → refused; CA pinned without client cert → refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.title: fix(e-signature): falha do file-storage é logada e publicada, nunca null calado (#638)
commits.body:
fix(e-signature): falha do file-storage é logada e publicada, nunca null calado (#638)

* fix(e-signature): file-storage failures are logged and published, never a silent null

The proof in staging (17/10) found the signing page answering 503 DOCUMENT_UNAVAILABLE and the sealed
PDF/certificate never archived, with nothing in the log pointing at why: bb-e-signature ran WITHOUT
MODULE_FILE_STORAGE_URL, and documentBytes returned null on every path without a word.

- documentBytes(signer, ctx): every failure is logged with where and why (source file-storage|engine;
  reason no_document / download_url_refused + code / no_url / http_error + status / unreachable), no
  document data, and published as esignature.signer.document_unavailable when there is a request context
  (the page and the sign flow pass it).
- The file-storage store() messages name the category instead of "temporary copy" for every file, so a
  failed archive of the sealed PDF reads as what it is.
- Boot (standalone): error when MODULE_FILE_STORAGE_URL is not set, warning when it lacks the
  /file-storage module prefix (the block serves under it; without it every call is 404).

Tests: tests/unit/e-signature 30 files, 364 passed (new: the three failure paths of document.pdf → 503,
event payload, three warn lines, no PDF bytes in logs).

commits.body:
fix(opensign): --recriar guarded by the e-signature DB, owners reset after it; review of #1981

Blocker from the review: recreating the engine wipes its volume (documents in flight and each
organization's technical user), and the ProviderConfigs would keep pointing at owners that no longer
exist.

- --recriar refuses while there is an OpenSign request open (DRAFT/SENT/VIEWED/PARTIALLY_SIGNED) or
  COMPLETED with the sealed PDF or the certificate not archived; production also needs
  APAGAR_VOLUME_PROD=sim. The counts come from the blocks DB through a detached worktree of
  building-blocks-v2 origin/main (its launch lib; URL in a 0600 file, nothing printed).
- After recreating, settings.extUserId/extUserOrganizationId of the OpenSign ProviderConfigs are
  cleared; the provider recreates each organization's technical user on its next call.
- emitir-tls.sh: reissues the server leaf when the SAN asked differs, warns on certificates that
  expire within 30 days.
- Dockerfile header and README updated (mTLS, and the switch-over order).

Checked in staging (read only): the open / pending-archive counts and the reset's target query run
(0 / 0 / 0 today; updated_at exists). emitir-tls: a changed SAN reissues, the same SAN keeps the cert.

commits.title: feat(opensign): TLS mútuo no portão do motor (o runtime docker esconde a origem) (#1981)
commits.body:
feat(opensign): TLS mútuo no portão do motor (o runtime docker esconde a origem) (#1981)

* feat(opensign): mutual TLS on the engine's port — the docker runtime hides the origin

Owner's decision (16/10): "Fazer o mTLS antes de prod". Measured in staging: inside the Launch
docker runtime every connection reaches the container from 172.17.0.1 (docker-proxy), from outside
and from the e-signature LXC alike, so an origin allowlist cannot work here.

- Caddy on 8090 is TLS only, client_auth require_and_verify against OUR CA; the gate header stays
  (defense in depth). Material comes from the service env (base64 PEM) and the entrypoint writes it
  0600; SERVER_URL must be https.
- scripts/opensign/emitir-tls.sh: EC P-256 CA (key never leaves the operator's machine) + server cert
  (SAN = mesh host) + client cert CN=bb-e-signature (clientAuth). Idempotent.
- deploy-opensign.sh: no HTTP health (healthPath empty → liveness by the container, no public route
  or name), --recriar, mTLS material into the service env and into opensign-local-<env>.env, the locks
  checked over mTLS (gate token via a 0600 header file, not argv), 1 h wait for the image pull.
- prova-assinatura.mjs over node:https with the client cert and the CA pinned.

Proof against the built image: PROVA OK 15/15 — plain HTTP 400 without reaching Parse; no client cert →
ERR_SSL_TLSV13_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED; cert without gate 403; cert + gate 200 over TLSv1.3; signPdf →
COMPLETED with hash, certificate and the signer's ip. Also refused: a client cert from another CA
(curl 56), the server cert used as client (56), and a client that does not pin our CA (60).

commits.body:
fix(cession): keep the signing link, e-mail it, close signatures within a minute (#1982)

* fix(cession): keep the signing link, e-mail it, close signatures within a minute

Smoke of 17/10 on the real signature path:
- the signer's link vanished from the 2nd request on (view built without the
  envelope just read); every view now carries signers[].signingUrl from the block
- nobody sent the link: the panel e-mails it (system sender, house brand, first
  name only) on envelope creation and on an explicit resend
  (POST /assignor-identity/leads/:leadId/cession/resend); cessoes_assinatura.convite
- minute sweep for pending envelopes opened in the last 2 h (page of 20)
- the operation keeps termo.aceitoEm = the COMPLETED instant from the record,
  plus termo.envelopeId
- a term changed after the signature is `termo_alterado`; asking again opens an
  envelope for the current term; same term no longer asks for a second signature

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(cession): resend records the attempt first, 503 when nothing went out; link only to the assignor

Adversarial review of #1982:
- resend writes convite.tentadoEm BEFORE asking the block (conditional write:
  the lock between replicas and clicks); the 1-min wait counts from it; at most
  5 attempts per envelope per day; nothing delivered -> 503 in pt-BR
- liveSignerOf: order AND e-mail must match when the block brings an e-mail;
  e-mail alone only when unique; trim + lowercase
- the signer's link only reaches the assignor's channel (machine token); the
  desk (JWT) never gets it, and the envelope's generic viewUrl is never a link
- only https links on the signing host are e-mailed
- every invitation send goes to the tenant's EmailLog (no body)
- definitive refusals after the signature are terminal (no endless retries);
  the desk reads the reason

commits.title: fix(antecipacao): webhook subscriptions unique per tenant + re-point on 409; lien events of another tenant ignored quietly
commits.body:
fix(antecipacao): webhook subscriptions unique per tenant + re-point on 409; lien events of another tenant ignored quietly

The webhooks-engine enforces a unique subscription NAME per IAM organization (409
'Subscription name already exists'), and CREATE_WEBHOOK_SUBSCRIPTION speaks with the
platform key, so every panel tenant lands in the same organization. The W10 installer
(and the boleto/esignature ones) used fixed names: the second tenant got a 409, stored
subscriptionId null and its antecipacao-trava-baas never received a lien event (staging
smoke, 19/10).

- CREATE_WEBHOOK_SUBSCRIPTION `scopeToTenant`: name gets ` · <tenantId>` (stable, <=100
  chars); a 409 means the tenant's own subscription: found by name and re-pointed (PATCH
  endpointUrl, eventFilters, x-webhook-secret), real id returned; other refusals fail loud
  instead of writing an empty id. Enabled on the 3 W10 subscriptions, boleto and esignature.
- ENSURE_TENANT_WEBHOOK_SUBSCRIPTION: name scoped per tenant; TenantWebhookSubscriptionService
  re-points on 409 only when the name carries THIS tenant (never touches another tenant's).
- antecipacao-trava-baas reads the proposal in this tenant (lerProposta) and credit-lien-apply
  returns REFERENCIA_DE_OUTRO without alert when there is no operation AND no proposal; the
  OPERACAO_AUSENTE alert stays for this tenant's proposal without operation.

commits.title: fix(workflows): P6 review — unique step names, no layout loop, resume never restarts a flow
commits.body:
fix(workflows): P6 review — unique step names, no layout loop, resume never restarts a flow

- replaceDefinition refuses a definition with an unnamed or repeated step before any write, and consumes each old
  step once matched; a kept step keeps the house's on/off. calculateNodeLevels stops with WorkflowGraphCycleError on
  a self-loop or reachable cycle instead of spinning at 100% CPU. Catalogue guard: every template names its steps
  uniquely.
- In-flight check counts a `running` execution resumed from a wait state in the last 24 h (its startedAt is the
  original one), and only LIVE wait states (execution suspended, deadline not >10 min gone).
- resumeExecution reads steps/layout and writes `running` under the shared definition lock; a waited step that is
  no longer active fails the execution with a clear error instead of slice(0) re-running from step 1.
- No swallowed query inside the lock transaction; the shared-lock transaction gets maxWait 15 s / timeout 40 s.
- Schedule (cron) jobs re-synced on this replica after the switch commits.
